# Tails & Scales: final refactor specification (multiplayer-ready)

Status: final, for the lead engineer to implement. It supersedes the four proposals (netcode-first, testability-first, content-first, experience-first) and `design/pre-multiplayer/experience-first.md`.

Code references are to HEAD `861a1eb`. In this checkout the determinism commit is `44cf4b2`; the brief calls it `ebfcd56`.

---

## 0. Thesis, base, and the decisions that settle the disagreements

**Thesis.** A battle is a pure function of `(setup, accepted command log)`.

- **The core is a synchronous reducer.** It applies a command, runs on to the next decision a human must make, and pushes plain-data events. It never awaits anything.
- **The view replays those events.** A presenter plays them at animation pace.
- **Online play shares one Automerge document.** It holds the lobby and an append-only command log. Every peer folds the log through the same core, and the AI runs inside that fold.
- **Every mode is one `Session` over a store.** vs-AI, hotseat, watch, online play, spectating, rejoin, scrubbing and replays all work this way. The store is a `LocalStore` (a plain array) or an `AutomergeStore`. Automerge is only the transport and persistence for the log. It never holds game state.

**Base.** The structure and test backbone come from **testability-first**, the winner for two of the three judges. Its strengths are a lean pure core, flags-not-hooks race data, merge-sim, property tests and a widened corpus.

The **match layer comes wholesale from netcode-first**. It is the only fold that stays correct under concurrency:
- seat and device checks;
- per-seat heads for simultaneous decisions;
- `h` checked only where a single seat is being waited on, and checked before `legal()`;
- `ImmutableString` entries;
- size caps and a tamper check.

Specific ideas are grafted from content-first and experience-first. They are named where they appear.

### 0.1 Facts this spec stands on (all verified)

| Fact | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Today's `main.js` runs unmodified in Node under the scratch fake-DOM/three-shim harness, and reproduces the browser baselines byte for byte | I re-ran seed 64 / dice 89 this session: identical, 0.7 s. The judges ran all 12. |
| No logic runs while a visual is being awaited, so replacing each `await` with an emitted event in the same position keeps the logic-RNG order | Input is gated (`S.busy`, `phaseResolve`, `myTurn` 1348). Per-frame code only reads state. Tween callbacks touch only visuals or `Math.random`. Scenery `hurt`/`destroy`/`collapse`/`topple` change logic state instantly. The walk's smashing is path-sampled (529-545). |
| The AI is part of the dice stream | Its tie-break `rng()*0.05` per valid lattice cell (ai.js 133) accounts for most of the 3.3-4.8k draws per battle. |
| None of the 12 baselines ends in a wipe-out. The "can't find a way" charge branch (977) is unreachable. | Both callers check `chargePlan` first (click 1384, ai.js 270), and `doCharge` recomputes the same plan. Keep the branch as defensive code; it needs no coverage. |
| `freeSpot` returns cell centres | 367-382. So `place {u, c}` reproduces deployment exactly. |
| Deploying both sides at once leaves the trace unchanged | No trace line sits between the two "deploy your army" logs (1933-1944). Placements commute: the zones are at least 24" apart, and the clearance is only 0.4". |
| `ImmutableString` is exported by `@automerge/automerge` 3.5.0 | Checked. Plain strings in a list are collaborative text and can be edited character by character (`judge-str.mjs`). |
| Approximated `Math.*` calls in logic files | main.js: hypot 20, sin 25, cos 8, atan2 11. scenery: hypot 11, sin 14, cos 12, atan2 2, atan 1 (a hedgerow's yaw, 482). ai: hypot 12. nav: hypot 7, sin 1, cos 1. Some of these are view code that still lives in those files. `exp` (2) is view-only. |
| `npm run verify` builds nothing and accepts extra files under `dist/<slug>/` | scripts/verify.mjs. A `.wasm` asset is fine. |
| Node's and Chromium's builds of V8 disagree in the last bit of `Math.sin`/`cos` for ~3% of inputs and `pow` for ~10%; `atan`, `atan2`, `exp` and `hypot` agree | Found at R0 over 100k samples. Node 20, 21 and 22 (V8 11.3 to 12.4) agree with each other on all seven; Chromium 141 (Playwright 1.61's `chromium-1194`) differs. So the split follows Chromium's build of V8, not the V8 version (a newer Chromium was reported to change `atan` too). Terrain built with sin/cos then sits an ULP apart in the two engines: 31 of the 40 R0 battles have a different Chromium shadow while their traces match byte for byte. So "the V8" is two engines: the parity shadow is compared per engine (`webShadow`), `pairs.json` names the Node and the Chromium that recorded it (`engines`), and a Chromium (Playwright) upgrade is followed by `parity.mjs --browser`, then `--record --browser` if only `webShadow` moved. (N0) The split is the implementation: Node's V8 runs fdlibm's sin and cos (its `src/base/ieee754.cc`), Chromium's build its own. `core/dmath.js` ports fdlibm's sin, cos, atan and atan2: Node's bits, the same in Chromium (`sim/dmath-check.mjs`), so the corpus's shadow is every engine's and `webShadow` is retired. |

### 0.2 Conflict resolutions

| # | Topic | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Layout | Consensus code lives in `core/` and `data/`. `match/` is the pure netplay rules. `net/` is the only code that imports Automerge, and it is reached only through `import()`. Node-only code lives in `sim/`. | The boundary is enforceable by directory. The two-peer tests can import everything except the wasm bootstrap. |
| 2 | Fold check order | envelope → duplicate → turn (seat is pending) → device → `prev` → `h` → `legal()` | Hash before legal: a desynced peer's command is *reported*. With legal first (testability-first) it is silently rejected, its successors go stale, and the game stalls with no report. Judge 3 preferred legal first to stop a forged entry freezing the match. I rejected that: at trust level L0 a forger can already play a *legal* move for the victim, which is worse than a freeze. Signatures (N4) are the real fix. |
| 3 | Scope of `h` | Required on single-seat decision kinds (`phase`, `chargeEnd`). Never present on simultaneous kinds (`deploy`, `roundLimit`) or out-of-band entries. The rule is by decision **kind**, not by how many seats are still pending. | Otherwise every concurrent online deployment raises a false desync. Keying it to the remaining seat count would break when one seat finishes deploying first. |
| 4 | Entry encoding | Canonical JSON (sorted keys, integers and booleans only) inside `A.ImmutableString` | Atomic and about 4× cheaper to append than objects. Fields of objects can be mutated after acceptance. Plain strings are editable text. |
| 5 | Command vocabulary | Specific `t` names (`move`, `shoot`, …). The fold never switches on `t`, except for `open`, `start`, `concede` and `desync`. | Readable, one legality rule per name. New actions such as `burrow` are core changes plus a `CORE_VERSION` bump. The wire format and the fold stay the same, which is what content-first's generic `act` was meant to buy. |
| 6 | `concede`, `desync` | **Out-of-band** entries: no `prev`, valid at any time after `start` from a seated human seat's device, terminal at their position in fold order | Fixes netcode-first's "any seat, any time" contradicting its own seat gate. |
| 7 | Who appends `start`; where the seed commitment lives | The creator. The commitment is the immutable first log entry `open {commit}`, not a mutable lobby field. | The creator holds the reveal `a`. A last-writer-wins lobby field could be overwritten after the fact. |
| 8 | Seeds | The board seed is the creator's visible choice, as the title screen's "New battlefield" is today. The dice seed is a joint commit-reveal. | The board is not hidden information. Only the dice stream must be grind-proof. |
| 9 | AI in online games | Runs inside the fold on every peer. AI seats append nothing. `hold` is internal to the AI and never on the wire. | All 12 traces stay valid, no host has to be online, and nobody can play the AI for their own benefit. Cost: AI code is rules code. |
| 10 | dmath timing | The two-argument `hypot` (V8 formula port, proven trace-neutral on 12/12 and 5M samples) lands at R1. Three-argument `hypot` lands at R1 only if it matches V8 exactly, otherwise at N0. `sin`/`cos`/`atan`/`atan2` land at **N0**. | Single-engine parity doesn't need them. Netplay across engines does. **Cross-engine determinism only requires dmath to be pure JS over exact IEEE operations. Matching V8 bit for bit only avoids one re-baseline.** If a V8-exact port proves elusive, take `CORE_VERSION 2` and re-record once, in a commit of its own. |
| 11 | Nav cache | Explicit `refreshNav(G)` at exactly today's call sites (477, 572, 816, 939, 999, plus setup at 1897). No lazy cache. | testability-first's lazy cache claim is unproven. `inCover` reads `nav.cover`. |
| 12 | Forking and fixtures | Refold `(setup, entries.slice(0, k))`. `structuredClone(G)` is not required, so `G` may hold `NavGrid` and `Terrain` instances. Invariant: **between commands, `G` holds no in-flight control state** (no promises, generators or pending closures). (R4) Two I/O fields are not match state and are exempt: `out`, the event array, and `onTrace`, the sim/debug observer (R0 notes), which never draws, mutates or is read by rules ((R7b) and the page's in every battle: it takes the unit card's facts at each `act` line, §2.4, reading only, with the dice locked). `stateHash`, `shadowState` and the §2.6 adapter skip both, and a refold passes its own. (R6a) A third, `strict`, a plain boolean (createMatch's option, §2.2): the AI's commands are checked with `legal()` before they are applied, which can only throw, never change play; skipped likewise. No other closure lives in `G`, its `Terrain` or its `NavGrid`. | Event sourcing gives forks for free, in at most 0.3 s. |
| 13 | Abilities | Flags on data, each read by exactly one rules module, plus a lint. content-first's hook and registry framework is deferred. | 4-6 new mechanics don't justify a framework inside the parity window. Hooks would also have to reach `expected()` and the AI. |
| 14 | `RULES_ID` | Adopted from content-first: a hash of the rule-bearing data, carried in `start` | A stat retune then makes old matches visibly incompatible instead of silently desyncing. |
| 15 | Display positions, event-driven labels/flags/VP | From **R5**, the first step where actions become synchronous, not at the view decomposition | `animateUnits` lerps toward `u.pos` (1961-1965), and `animateObjectives` polls `controlOf` (2020). Without this, figures glide straight to the end of a move through walls. |
| 16 | Human-path baselines | Recorded at **R0** from the legacy code, in the netplay command format (netcode-first M0). Recording uses an aggressive wipe-seeking policy, a widened AI corpus, admission only when Node and Chromium agree, a swapped-die mutation check, and a full-precision shadow snapshot (judge 3). | Every risky step, including the charge split and simultaneous deploy, is then checked on human flows against pre-refactor behaviour. |
| 17 | Engine rewrite | Built beside the old loop. Switch only when the headless fold matches every baseline. | R6 is the riskiest step. |
| 18 | Preview safety | `legal()`, hover previews and the HUD model run under `rng.lock`, where a draw throws. A property test checks that `rngState` never moves. | The strongest guard against UI code shifting the dice. |
| 19 | Feature 4 semantics | `setup.overtime: 'never' \| 'vote'`. It is absent, meaning `'never'`, in every baseline and in `?watch`. Voters are the human seats. AI seats follow. Continuing needs a unanimous `more`. The vote is asked after every round ≥ `rounds`. A wipe is final. Watch mode has no overtime in v1. | Keeps parity, and keeps `start` free of a seat −1 "host voter". |
| 20 | Presence | Who is here (seat or spectator), `{head, hash}` and current selection, sent on change plus a 5 s heartbeat. No cursor streaming. | Cross-checks spectators. 10 Hz through a public server is waste. |
| 21 | Fold slicing or Worker | None in v1. The worst case is about 1 s on a phone for a whole AI battle, shown behind a "Setting up the battle" veil. | Simplicity. Results never depend on slicing, so it can be added later. |
| 22 | State in the doc | None: no snapshots, no derived state | Unvalidatable, forgeable, and it bloats the doc. |
| 23 | Test location | `packages/tails-and-scales/sim/`, never bundled (Vite only follows `index.html`'s graph), run by hand like thumbnails | CI stays `npm run verify` only (CLAUDE.md). |

**(V2) The figures, as built.** Two figure styles (`view/models/cache.js`'s `STYLES`), each a set of
kits by the name a race's look gives its models: **new**, the default (the Coil of Ssithra smooth and
glossy, `view/models/serpent.js` over `view/models/gloss/`, moved from `proto/scales/`; the Bushtail
Clans with splat fur, `view/models/squirrel.js` over `view/models/splat/`, the next note), and **classic** (the R7 figures, `view/models/classic/`, unchanged but for their import paths),
kept for comparison and as the fallback. A page draws one: `app/boot.js` calls `setFigureStyle` before
any figure is built, from `?models=new|classic` (for development) or else what the title's **Figures**
link kept in this browser (`localStorage['tails-and-scales:models']`; a click keeps the other style and
reloads the page, since the page's query string never reaches a published single-file page; round 2:
where the browser keeps nothing, the click writes `#models=<style>` into the fragment, which does reach
it, and reloads); the
templates, and the far stand-ins' shapes, are keyed by style too. Every glossy figure is built at one
level of detail, **0.5** (serpent.js's header): one template per unit serves the 28 px classic table and
the 140 px close look alike, the claws, catchlights and the hood's banding kept, the shader's own
footprint level of detail calming the gloss at 28 px; against detail 1, the mean colour difference over
a figure's pixels is 6.1, 5.2 and 4.7 levels at ~140, 60 and 28 px (0.3: 9.1, 7.5, 6.4), and the classic
army's 24 Ssithra are 137k triangles (detail 1: 617k; 0.3: 72k; the classic figures 64k). **The bake**
(`view/models/bake.js`) took the prototype's three changes, each a no-op for a plain part: its class key
keeps every old field and appends a glossy part's finish (gloss.js's physical fields and shader
parameters); a part's own vertex colours are read (times its material colour) only when its material has
`vertexColors` on, a skin part's `plain` colour with them, both flipped with their corners on a mirrored
part; a glossy class is drawn with gloss.js's `classMaterial`. `sim/bake-check.mjs` holds every classic
figure's bake to R7a's, node for node. The far stand-in (F8b's `lodOf`) needed nothing: a glossy class's
colours are in its vertices under a white material. gloss.js's env map is made with the first glossy
material, never as the module loads (three.js draws `Math.random` for a texture's uuid, and the title's
table is painted from `Math.random`), so a page drawing the classic figures draws its table as before.
Two view changes came with it: the idle breath (`view/units.js`, `view/diorama.js`) scales a figure's
height about its own built scale (`userData.sy`), where it had set the scale itself and so drew the
brute (built at 2.15), the hierophant (1.32) and the elder (1.28) about 1 high, squashed, in every style;
and **the perf overlay** (`ui/perf.js`): the stage's `probe` (`view/stage.js`, null while it is off, so
off it costs nothing) is handed the table's render (renderer.info right after it, the sun's shadow pass
counted too: while the probe is on the stage resets the counts itself) and each frame's start
and end, and about twice a second it writes the fps, the frame interval's average and worst, the frame's
CPU time, draw calls, triangles, splats (`view/stats.js`'s `drawStats`, which the splat Bushtails
feed, beside their budget), the canvas's pixels and pixel ratio, shadows, the figure style and the
milliseconds its figures took to build; switched in the page by the
title's **Perf overlay** link and the battle's 📈 tool (kept in `localStorage['tails-and-scales:perf']`)
or by `?perf`, never under `?fast` (round 2, below: six short lines, at the right under the battle log on
a wide screen and at the left under the roster's head on a phone, a tap on it the next quality).

**(V2) The splat Bushtails, as built.** The 'new' style's Bushtail Clans are `proto/splat/`'s look,
moved into the game: each squirrel's fur Gaussian splats, everything it wears or carries meshes from
`view/models/kit.js`, fitted to the splat body. `view/models/splat/fur.js` is generated by
`proto/splat/make-bushtail.py` from the splat-squirrel project's `src/squirrel.js` (kept beside the
script); `view/models/splat/splats.js` is the runtime (proto/splat's `splat-three.js`);
`view/models/squirrel.js` the kit (its `bushtail-kit.js`), on the game's figure contract. **One fur a
unit:** made the first time the unit is built (seven furs for six units: the trebuchet's two crewmen
are two), at density 0.05 (about 8,300 splats; the prototype's 0.1 made 11,800 in twice the time and
can't be told from it at 60 or 28 px, `make-bushtail.py` lowering the generator's floor to 0.04 for it),
in progressive order, baked at four levels of detail, **800, 1,500, 3,000 and 6,000** splats (`lodSlice`:
a prefix, its splats enlarged so the coat still covers), all four packed into one float texture (five
texels a splat) under one `ShaderMaterial`, a level being a range of it that the draw order addresses
(one texture and one material a fur, where one a level would be four of each to bind and free for the
same draws). Every figure of the unit draws it, the template cache's template and clones and every
trebuchet (built afresh for its heap of acorns, its crew's furs not), and no figure owns a GPU buffer.
**Each render** of a scene that shows figures (the table's, a race picker window's) starts with
`prepareSplats(camera, renderer, lightDir, scene)`, as the scene's `onBeforeRender` (three calls it once
the world matrices and the camera, the shake's offset in it, are current, before it lists what to draw:
the last moment an instanced attribute can change for that render). For every registered figure in that
scene, shown (no hidden ancestor: a far stand-in hides its figure) and in the frustum (its fur's bounding
sphere), it picks **a level**, from the figure's height on screen in CSS pixels (n ≈ 1.7 px², the
prototype sheet's rule at DPR 1: 1,500 at 28 px, 6,000 from about 60 px; CSS so a phone's DPR doesn't
ask four or nine times the splats for a figure the same size to the eye), the smallest level holding
it, with 15% hysteresis; if the render's figures would draw more than **150,000** (`SPLAT_BUDGET`, shown
in the perf overlay; round 2: a frame's, the quality's, shared by the table and the race picker's
windows), the farthest step down a level, then the next farthest, a pass at a time, until
they fit; and **a draw order**, without sorting: the camera's direction in the figure's own frame (Aᵀ of
its world matrix's linear part times the camera's offset: what orders by depth under a breath's or a
keel's transform) picks a view bin, 32 azimuths by 6 elevation bands of 30° (the table's 44° camera sits
at a band's middle), and the fur keeps a draw order per (level, bin), the level's splat centres sorted by
their dot product with the bin's middle direction (a counting sort, 16 bits as first built and 12 since
round 2, made the first time a figure is seen from that bin), as a Uint16 instanced attribute (three r160 hands an unnormalised
`UNSIGNED_SHORT` to `in float` exactly) in an `InstancedBufferGeometry` of the fur's own that every
figure seen from that bin draws: a figure turning, or the camera orbiting, swaps which geometry it
draws. A bin's geometry is counted by the figures holding it, and one none holds and none has drawn for
90 preparations is freed with its order (made again if the bin is seen again), so a battle's turning
leaves nothing on the title. Measured against an exact sort for each view (a nutkin about 120 px tall,
an orbit every 4° at 20°, 44° and 70° up; an elder every 6°), the binned order differs by 0.3-1.1 colour
levels in 255 on average over the figure's pixels, 0.05-0.22% of them by more than 24; finer bins (64
azimuths, or 12 bands) moved those by less than they differ between elevations, the rest being the
perspective across a close figure, so the bins stay coarse. Figures register as `cache.js` builds or
clones them and unregister as `disposeFigure` frees them (a template never stands on a table, so it is
never prepared). **In the scene graph**, a squirrel's splat mesh lives inside `root.userData.fig`, so the
view's hop, breath, lean, flinch, keel and sink, and a glider's lift and stand, move it unchanged; it is
`userData.keep` (bake.js leaves a kept subtree whole, and a splat mesh has no children), its `clone()`
draws the same fur, its `raycast()` meets its fur's box (the race picker's `unitAt`), and `cache.js`
never sets its `castShadow`. **Shadows** (as first built; round 2 merges the proxy into the figure's one
shadow caster, below): each squirrel casts the classic figure's body
(`view/models/classic/squirrel.js`'s `squirrel()`, exported for it; no hat, the kit's meshes casting
their own), posed roughly as its fur (a raised arm; a glider's arms wide and its membrane's two quads
each side), an invisible proxy: a kept subtree on `SHADOW_LAYER` (1) alone, which bake.js now bakes on
its root's layers (a fourth change, a no-op for every other figure) and a clone keeps. The sun's shadow
camera enables the layer, and since three r160's shadow pass tests a caster's layers against the camera
the scene is drawn by, not the shadow camera's, `view/stage.js` wraps the renderer's shadow pass to
enable it on the drawing camera too, and set it back after: the scene's render lists what it draws
before the shadow pass, so a proxy is drawn into the shadow map and nowhere else. The fur takes no
shadow. **The far stand-in** (`lodOf`) merges every mesh but the splats: the proxy's body in its fur
colours and the kit, so a far squirrel keeps its hat and its halberd (round 2: the fur itself instead of
the body, below). **userData.anim** is as the
classic figures': kind `'squirrel'`, `body` (the squirrel's group), `head`, `tail`, `armL`, `armR`
(groups riding those bones, the kit on them baked into the figure, as the classic ones'), a glider's
`lift`; the elder's `gem` a kept mesh that spins and that the thorns' motes rise from; the trebuchet's
the classic machine's own (`'machine'`, `wheels`, `throwArm`, `rest`, kept). A squirrel stands 0.03
higher in its miniature than `cache.js` lifts it, its feet in the base's flock. **Load** (Chromium,
SwiftShader, desktop): a unit's figure built first on a fresh page (`proto/splat/viewer.html`, its fur
and kit, the JIT cold) takes 122-224 ms, a median of about 142 (a trebuchet, two furs, 223; at density
0.1 it was 136-297, median 180; a classic figure 14-39). The title builds every unit of both races
before its first frame: the perf overlay's `built in` (`view/stats.js`) reads 657-668 ms in the 'new'
style over three loads (Node, in the title's order: the Bushtails 427-476 ms, the first, the nutkin,
136 of it with the JIT warming; the glossy Ssithra 212-235) against 53-92 ms classic, and the page boots
in 8.5-8.7 s against 5.5-6.2 (SwiftShader's shader compiles are most of both). At a phone's four times
slower that is about 2.6 s of building against 0.3: the overlay shows a real phone's. Of the Bushtails'
time the generator is 44% (its body's distance field the most of it), the four levels 18%, the meshes'
bake 11%, the progressive order 8%; the cheap wins were taken (density 0.05, about half the generator's
time; no closure or view a splat in the bake and the packing); building the levels lazily would save
part of the 18% and less on the title, which draws the finer levels, so it is not done. A later trebuchet
is built in 7-8 ms (its crew's furs kept). **Drawn** (1280×800 unless said, the overlay's counts): the
title, 29 squirrels prepared, 150,000 splats (the budget binding: 8 at 3,000, 21 at 6,000), 595 draw
calls in the main pass and 1,222 with the shadow pass (classic: 883), 984k triangles counting a splat's
two (classic 447k); a watched battle at round 3 from its own camera, 17 squirrels and 42,100 splats
(mostly 3,000 each), 471 calls; a close look at a grenadier squad, 66,000-78,000; a phone (390×844, DPR 3,
the canvas 780×1688 at the stage's DPR 2), the title's 16 squirrels in view 93,000, a battle's 24 at 800
each, 19,200, about 1,040 calls with the shadow pass. The entry chunk is 313.8 kB gzipped (the glossy
half's 287.8).

**(V2) Round 2: the figures' cost, cut for phones.** The first round's verification measured the 'new'
figures at 1.3-1.4× classic's draw calls (half of them the sun's shadow pass, which draws every figure
whatever the camera sees: a glossy figure cast with all its 6-10 baked classes), splats drawn per render
rather than per frame (the race picker's windows on top of the table's 150,000), a phone's splat fill
growing with its pixel ratio squared, `?lowfi` not reducing the splats, and no way to try the cheapest
knobs on a phone, whose page never receives its query string. What changed:
- **One shadow caster a figure** (`view/models/cache.js`'s `casterOf`, the 'new' style's `ONE_CASTER`):
  the miniature's meshes merged in its space, positions only, clustered to 0.012" (finer than a shadow
  texel), under one double-sided material on `SHADOW_LAYER` alone (so the stage's shadow-pass wrapper
  draws it and no camera does), made with the template and copied by its clones; the miniature's own
  meshes cast nothing, a kept subtree on three's own layer (a machine's arm and wheels, a gem: they move)
  casts as ever, a squirrel's shadow proxy is merged in, and the base casts by its plinth's class alone.
  A figure is two calls in the shadow pass (the glossy ones made 9 to 13, the classic 6 or 7); the
  classic style casts as it always did.
- **A quality** (`view/stage.js`'s `QUALITY`): `high` (the page as it always drew: a pixel ratio up to
  2, a 2048 shadow map, 150,000 splats a frame), `medium` (1.5, 1024, 60,000) and `low` (1, no shadows,
  30,000); `auto`, the default, is `medium` where the pointer is coarse (a phone, a tablet) and `high`
  elsewhere. In the page: the title's **Quality** link and a tap on the perf overlay step it, kept in
  `localStorage['tails-and-scales:quality']`; `?quality=` (or `#quality=`) for development. It changes
  the stage at once (`setQuality`: the ratio and the canvas; the shadows by the sun's `castShadow`,
  which changes the lights' state, so three makes each lit program again; the map remade at its size).
  `?lowfi` stays what it was (a ratio of 0.5, no shadow map), and draws `low`'s 30,000 splats a frame
  whatever the quality (the harnesses' mode).
- **A frame's splat budget** (`splats.js`'s `setSplatBudget`, the quality's): the table's render begins
  the frame (`prepareSplats`' role `'table'`), each race picker window draws what it left (`'window'`),
  and while a window shows (the battle-setup panel or a lobby card over the table) the table's figures
  all draw their coarsest level, so the windows' figures, the ones looked at, get the budget. A figure's
  level is chosen from the drawing buffer's height under a pixel ratio below 1, so `?lowfi` (0.5) draws
  a quarter of the splats. A draw order's counting sort has 4,096 buckets, not 65,536 (the fill and
  prefix sum over them were most of a small level's sort).
- **See-through things in the air** (an explosion's flash and smoke, `view/effects/fx.js`) take the furs'
  `FUR_ORDER` (10), so they and the furs are drawn back to front together: a puff before a squirrel
  veils its fur as it veils its cap (a fur writes no depth, so whatever see-through was drawn after it
  covered it, and three sorts by renderOrder first). The smoke pool sorts at the middle of its live
  puffs. Two groups that set their renderOrder on the group (a blast template, the group order's flag)
  now set it on their meshes: three sorts a group's order before any mesh's, which drew them over the furs.
- **The far stand-in** (F8b's 60" switch): a squirrel's keeps its fur. It merges the base and the kit as
  before, and holds a splat mesh of each of the figure's furs where the figure at rest holds it, which
  `prepareSplats` gives its level as any figure's (the coarsest, mostly, at that distance), and its
  shadow proxies merged, on `SHADOW_LAYER`, for its body's shadow: two calls a far squirrel where it
  was one. As first built it merged the classic body in the fur's place, which turned darker, harder
  and curled-tailed at the switch (a first fix, the body painted from the splats' colours, still left
  its shaded side 2.5-4.7× darker than the fur's, which a splat's two-tone shading keeps light). Every
  stand-in is now made with its figure at rest (a figure first asked mid-hop or mid-keel no longer
  freezes its stand-in there) and draws a double-sided part (a robe, a breastplate) from both sides.
- **The perf overlay**: six short lines (fps and frame time, CPU and calls, triangles and splats of the
  budget, pixels, ratio and shadow map, the quality, the style and its build time), at the right under
  the battle log on a wide screen and at the left under the roster's head on a phone (at the top over a
  phone's title; none over its battle-setup panel, whose race windows would show it through), no longer
  over the score; a tap steps the quality.
- **render-bench** counts the splats apart from the triangles (a budget decision: renderer.info counts a
  splat, an instanced quad, as two triangles, but its cost is four vertices and its fill; §4.2.1's
  triangles row is the meshes', and a splats row holds them to the `high` quality's 150,000).
- **The harnesses**: play-check's waits for the table (the camera at rest, a placed unit's label) span
  drawn frames as well as time (under SwiftShader a frame of the 'new' figures could take longer than the
  800 ms it waited, so the camera was taken for at rest mid-swing); every harness's page load waits
  `IDLE_MS` (the boot builds the figures before the load event, longer in the 'new' style).

Measured (SwiftShader, a loaded machine; counts don't depend on it): render-bench's classic frame, main
calls 722 (1.20×, as before), shadow calls 639 → 280 (classic style 459), mesh triangles 335 K (0.84×),
splats 83 K (0.56×); Grand, every figure a stand-in, 438 (0.73×: a far squirrel's fur is a call of its
own), 336 (its body's shadow another), 268 K and 70 K (87 furs at 800 splats). The built page at
1280×800, calls with the shadow pass: the title 1,255 → 857 (classic style 920), a watched battle at
round 2 787 (classic 935); the setup panel's table 23,200 splats at the coarsest behind its two windows
(150,000 before, the windows' on top). At the 60" switch, through a narrow lens so a unit fills the
frame, the mean colour over a squirrel unit's pixels is within 0.87-1.14× of the figure's (linear),
where the painted body was 1.2-4.7× darker and the first version's darker still. A cold build of every
unit in Node (one process, the title's order): about 1.3 s 'new' against 0.15 s classic, the casters'
clustering a few per cent of it (a string grid key had cost it a tenth; it is a number now). What is
left of the boot is the Bushtails' generator (44% of their build, fur.js, generated) and the first
frame's shader programs (27 on the title, 40 in battle, against 19 and 27): building fur levels lazily
would save little on the title, which draws the finer levels, and compiling off the first frame
(`compileAsync`) would move the first frame, which sim/title-shot.mjs and the 1200 ms title checks hold;
both are left for a phone's numbers to justify.

### 1.2 Layer rules, enforced by `sim/boundaries.mjs`

`sim/boundaries.mjs` walks the static import graph and greps tokens.

| Layer | May import | Must not contain |
|---|---|---|
| `core/`, `data/` | each other | `three`; `@automerge`; `document`, `window`, `location`, `localStorage`, `requestAnimationFrame`; `async`, `await`, `Promise`; `Math.random`, `Date`, `performance`; ((R6b's fixer, round 3) what else the host lends that differs from run to run: `Math` other than as `Math.<member>` (`Math['random']`, `const { random } = Math`, an alias, `Math` passed on), the timers and task queues (`setTimeout`, `setInterval`, `setImmediate`, `queueMicrotask`, `requestIdleCallback`), `crypto`, `process`, `globalThis`); module-level mutable state (ids, rng, counters); approximated `Math.*`: `hypot` from R1, `sin\|cos\|tan\|atan\|atan2\|exp\|pow\|log` from N0; tests on unit key, race key, ability text or `fx` (`.key ===`, `startsWith(`, `.fx`: `sim/flag-lint.mjs`'s patterns, with its allow-list) |
| `match/` | core (`index.js` only: (R6b's fixer, round 2)), data | three, DOM, Automerge, `async`/`await`; importing `core/rng.js` ((R6b's fixer), §4.1 rule 1); ((R8) the Folder's verdicts depend on the entry list alone) the host's tokens the consensus code is denied: `Math.random`, `Date`, `performance`, the timers, `crypto`, `process`, `globalThis`, `Math` other than as `Math.<member>` (an entry id's random part is handed to the Session by the app); ((R8's fixer, round 2) several Folders share a process, every peer of `sim/merge-sim.mjs`, §4.1 rule 13) module-level mutable state, as for `core/` |
| `present/` | core (read-only queries: (R6b's fixer, round 2) `queries.js`, `rules.js` but `d6`/`roll`, `index.js` but `createMatch`/`apply`), match | three, DOM; importing `core/rng.js` ((R6b's fixer)) |
| `net/` | match, core ((R6b's fixer, round 2) `index.js` but `createMatch`/`apply`), `@automerge/*` | three, DOM rendering; importing `core/rng.js` ((R6b's fixer)) |
| `view/`, `input/`, `ui/`, `app/` | everything above; core through its surface ((R6b's fixer, round 2): `index.js` but `apply`, `queries.js`, `rules.js` but `d6`/`roll`, `match.js`, `nav.js`, `dmath.js`, `util.js`, `terrain/recipes.js`) | a **static** import of `net/` (it is reached only through `import()`); importing `core/rng.js` |

(R6b's fixer) So no layer but `core/` and `data/` imports `core/rng.js` (§4.1 rule 1, §2.2's preview). (R6b's fixer, round 2) Nor any other module of the core that draws: above the consensus code each layer imports from `core/` only the modules of its row (its **surface**), and not the names its row excepts, nor all of such a module (`import *`, `export * from`, `import()`). `core/rng.js`, `engine.js`, `commands.js`, `actions/` and `ai/` are on no layer's surface; of `index.js`, `createMatch` and `apply` fold commands and so draw: `apply` is the Session's (`match/`), and a match is created by `match/` or by the view (the title's backdrop, a match of its own that never rolls). The surface's modules, and `data/` (which the view imports whole), are its **doors**: a door passes on none of `rules.js`'s dice, nothing of the modules that draw but the queries the check lists (`queries.js`'s `moveMode`, `forbidMask`, `movePlan`, `validEnd`, `nearestValid`, `canShoot`, `shotInfo`, `shootTargets`, (F17) `rangeOf` and `lobbed`, `canCharge`, `chargeTargets`, `chargePlan`, `chargeSpots` and `rngState`; `index.js`'s `legal`, which runs locked, and (R8) `KINDS`, `commands.js`'s frozen list of the command kinds, which `match/envelope.js` decodes no other than), and all of a module only if that module is a door too; no module of `core/` or `data/` passes on anything of `core/rng.js` but `rngState`. A new query that crosses from an action into a door is added to that list, which is the review it deserves. The check follows a binding through `export {…}` (with or without `from`, across lines), `export const x = name` (or `ns.name`, any declarator), `export default name` and a module-level `const x = name` alias. What it can't see is code: a door's function that wraps a draw (`export const f = (G) => d6(G)`). That, and any stray draw from above the core through the surface it is allowed, only parity catches (a draw shifts every later die), on the paths the corpus runs. The module-level mutable state `sim/boundaries.mjs` looks for in `core/` and `data/`: a `let` or `var` (exported or not), and as any declarator of a one-line module-level `const`: a `Map` or `WeakMap`, an empty `Set` or `WeakSet` (`new Set()`, `new Set([])`), an empty array or object literal, a bare `Object.create(null)`.

## 2. Interfaces

### 2.1 Core state

```js
G = {
  setup,                   // frozen: { board, dice, terrain:'classic', rounds:5, overtime:'never'|'vote', diceMode:'shared',
                           //           seats:[{ race, ctrl:'human'|'ai', dev?, name?, nonce? }, …] }  (+ core, rules from `start`)
  rng: { a, n, h, locked },      // createRng(setup.dice); rngState(G.rng) prints exactly today's `${count}#${hash36}`
  seats: [{ seat: 0, race: 'squirrel', edge: -1, ctrl }, { seat: 1, race: 'serpent', edge: +1, ctrl }],  // edge fixed by seat
  units: Unit[], nextUnitId,     // army order, seat 0 first; ids 1..N, reset per match
  objectives: [{ i, x, z }],
  terrain: Terrain,              // chunk logic data, per-match chunk ids
  nav: NavGrid,                  // derived cache; not hashed; refreshed only at today's refreshNav sites
  turn: { stage: 'deploy'|'battle'|'over', step, round, t, first, active, ph, vp: [0, 0], wiped: -1, result: null, overtime: 0 },
                                 // (R4) R4-R5: { stage: 'title'|'deploy'|'battle'|'over', round, active, first, phase, vp, wiped }
                                 // (R6a) this shape in both loops: main.js's old one sets ph (no phase), leaves step null and t 0,
                                 // and keeps stage 'title' for its per-table G until R6b; the key is phaseKey(G) (queries.js)
                                 // (R6b) one loop, the engine's; newState starts the turn at stage 'deploy', step 'rolloff'
                                 // (the title screen holds no match, so 'title' is only the mirror's stage for the backdrop)
  pending: Decision | null,      // (R6a's fixer) only ever a human seat's decision: runAI never stores the AI seat's (§2.2);
                                 // null from newState on (never missing, so a hash or a check of it reads every G alike)
  journal: { trace: [], pendingLog: [] },
  out: Event[] | null,           // null = quiet fold (catch-up, scrub, peers); [] when someone will present
  onTrace: ((line, G) => void) | null,  // (R4) sim/debug observer of trace lines (R0 notes); (R7b) and the page's in every battle (app/flow.js: the unit card's facts at each act line, reading only, the dice locked); I/O like out: unhashed, never read by rules (§0.2 #12)
  strict: boolean,               // (R6a) sim/'s P-prop: every AI command checked with legal() first (§2.2 runAI); I/O, like out
}
Unit = { id, side /* = seat */, race, key, t, pos: { x, z }, r, alive, lost, mesmerized,
         flags: { moved, advanced, advRoll, fellBack, shot, charged, chargeTried, chargeTarget, fought },
         models: [{ w, alive, ox, oz }] }
Decision = { k: 'deploy',     seats: [s…] }                          // simultaneous: one head per seat
         | { k: 'phase',      seats: [s], phase: 'move'|'shoot'|'charge' }
         | { k: 'chargeEnd',  seats: [s], u, tg, rolled, cell }     // cell = the shortest-move spot (plan.cell)
         | { k: 'roundLimit', seats: [s…], votes: { [s]: bool } }   // simultaneous
```

**`turn` through R5 (R4).** R4 gives `G.turn` the shape today's loop can run on: `{ stage, round, active, first, phase, vp, wiped }`. `phase` is the phase key, which `canAct` reads. `stage` starts at `'title'`, because through R5 `setupTable` builds a G for the table the title screen shows before any mode is chosen; the battle is begun on it by the transitional `startMatch`. R6's step machine replaces `phase` with `ph`, the index into `PHASES`, whose key `canAct` and the `?debug` `S.phase` then derive (`PHASES[ph].key`), so `phase` does not survive R6. R6 also adds `step`, `t`, `result` and `overtime`. `'title'` goes with `createMatch` (R6), which starts at `'deploy'`.

Every view field leaves the unit and goes to `view/units.js`: `mesh`, `ring`, `hit`, `label`, `facing`, `moving`, and per model `x, z, yaw, lunge, lungeDir, lift, flash, dying, look, flying, fleeing`. `u.facing` has one logic read (532), which can never fire because `walk` returns early when the path is under 0.05" (519).

`edge` replaces every hard-wired side. Seat 0 → −1 reproduces today's numbers exactly.

| Site | Lines | Becomes |
|---|---|---|
| facing | 293 | `-edge·π/2` |
| `freeSpot` zone | 369 | `[edge·W/2 … edge·(W/2−deploy)]` |
| deploy | 386, 399 | `sx = edge`, z flip `-edge` |
| flee exit and yaw | 1133, 1137 | `edge·(W/2+3)` |
| zones | 158-170 | by edge |
| title drift | 2045 | camera preset (R7) |

Death voice and gore colours (892-897) come from race `look`. A mirror match uses `look.alt` for seat 1.

### 2.2 Commands and the engine

**Command bodies.** Units are addressed by per-match id. Places are addressed by nav cell index on the half-inch grid (80×56 = 4,480 cells). Bodies carry only integers and booleans. ((R6a's fixer) `legal()` also refuses a body carrying any field its kind doesn't take, so the seat travels beside a body, never in it: `sim/run.mjs` splits a corpus log entry's `s` off before it asks, and R8's Folder hands it `bodyOf(e)`, the entry without its envelope fields (§2.6's (R6a) note).) The client snaps clicks with the same core queries the UI uses today (`nearestValid`, `freeSpot`, `nearestSpot`), so a float from the view never enters the log.

| `t` | Body | Legal when (`core/commands.js`; the source of today's check) | Logic draws |
|---|---|---|---|
| `place` | `{u, c}` | `deploy` pending for seat; `u` is the seat's unit; `placeOk(G,u,c)`: inside the edge's zone, `standable(c, r, 'walk')`, no other unit within `o.r+u.r+0.4` (deployClick 1392-1411, freeSpot 367-382). The 2.5" click tolerance is UI only. | – |
| `deployed` | `{}` | `deploy` pending for seat (`#endPhase` in deploy, 1786) | The last one closes deployment, then the roll-off (1207-1213) |
| `advance` | `{u}` | `phase:move`; own unit; alive, `!moved`, `!advanced`, `!isEngaged` (1723) | 1 D6 |
| `move` | `{u, c}` | `phase:move`; own, alive, `!moved`; `validEnd(movePlan(G, u, advanced ? advRoll : 0), c)` (1372). Also covers advance moves and falling back. ((R5c's fixer) core's `doMove(G, u, c)` remakes that plan itself when handed none, and main.js hands it none, so parity holds every corpus move made on the remade plan to the old move, made on the plan its cell was picked from; a one-off probe at R5c also found the two plans deep-equal) | – |
| `shoot` | `{u, tg}` | `phase:shoot`; own; `canShoot(u)`; `tg` is an alive enemy; `shotInfo(u, tg).ok` (1380). ((F18) A target locked in combat is no longer refused, for any ranged weapon: shotInfo's "locked in combat" is gone; the shooter itself still may not shoot while engaged, `canShoot`) | yes ((F18) into a fight, a volley's stray draws: §4.1 rule 27) |
| `charge` | `{u, tg}` | `phase:charge`; own; `chargeTargets(u).includes(tg) && chargePlan(u, tg)` (1384) | 2D6 |
| `chargeEnd` | `{c}`, `-1` = shortest | `chargeEnd` pending for seat; `c === -1 \|\| chargeSpots(chargePlan(u,tg), rolled)[c]` (1035) | – |
| `end` | `{}` | `phase` pending for seat | Only the charge-phase `end`, which runs fight, morale, scoring and the next turns, AI included |
| `auto` | `{}` | `phase` pending for seat | AI policy for this phase, then `end` (1798-1811) |
| `vote` | `{more}` | `roundLimit` pending; seat hasn't voted | – |
| `concede` | `{}` | out-of-band: any seated human, any time after `start` ((R6a's fixer) until the battle is decided: refused once a side is wiped out mid-phase, which has decided it though the battle only ends at the phase's end) | – |
| `hold` | `{u}` | **internal to the AI**, never legal on the wire (ai.js 109-110) | – |

```js
// core/index.js: the only API that match/, sim/ and the UI call
export function createMatch(setup, { out = null, onTrace = null, strict = false } = {})  // onTrace(line, G): sim/debug (R0 notes, §4), (R7b) and the page's in every battle (app/flow.js: the unit card's facts at each act line, reading only, the dice locked); (R6a) strict: P-prop
                                                        // terrain, units, deployArmies; logs "deploy your army" per human seat
                                                        // (seat order); pending = deploy(humanSeats) or straight on: an all-AI
                                                        // match runs to 'over' inside this call
export const pendingSeats = (G) => [...(G.pending?.seats ?? [])]  // (R6a's fixer) a copy: editing it leaves the decision be
export function fullSetup(setup)                        // (R6a) the setup with its defaults filled in (its own fields first, in its
                                                        // order); throws unless the rules can play it (createMatch calls it): seeds
                                                        // 0 to 2^32 − 1, rounds 1 to MAX_ROUNDS = 99 ((R6a's fixer) so no setup makes
                                                        // createMatch play an all-AI battle as long as a typo asks; F4's vote adds
                                                        // overtime a round at a time), overtime 'never' until F4, shared dice
export function legal(G, seat, body)                    // → null | 'why'; runs under rng.lock; pure; may refreshNav (idempotent)
export function apply(G, seat, body) { HANDLERS[body.t](G, seat, body, 'seat'); advance(G) }  // precondition: legal
export function stateHash(G)                            // (R8) cyrb53 → base36 over canonical pre-state (§2.6) ((R8) built: core/hash.js)
export function shadowState(G)                          // (R8) debug: full-precision superset of traceState (not the parity shadow, §2.6)
export const CORE_VERSION, KINDS, canonicalJSON, cyrb53 // (R8) the rules code's number; the command kinds (match/envelope.js decodes no other); sorted-key JSON (how an entry is written); the string hash (the Folder's head after a simultaneous decision closes)
export * as q from './queries.js'                       // read-only, for previews and the ?debug __ts surface
export function preview(G, fn)                          // (R6a) fn(G, q) with G.rng locked: tools, HUD, the Session's preview (match/ may not import rng.js)
```

`q` covers every query the `__ts` contract names (R0 notes, §4), so `app/` can serve that surface without importing anything it may not: `queries.js` re-exports `movePlan`, `validEnd`, `nearestValid` (`actions/move.js`), `freeSpot` (`deploy.js`), `shootTargets`, `shotInfo` (`actions/shoot.js`), `chargeTargets`, `chargePlan`, `chargeSpots` (`actions/charge.js`) and a read-only `rngState(r)` from `core/rng.js`, which `app/`, `view/`, `input/` and `ui/` never import (§1.2). The `?debug` block maps it as `rngState: () => q.rngState(G.rng)` and never rebuilds the `n#h36` format from `G.rng`'s fields itself. (R4) A query that reads the match takes `G` first; one that reads only its arguments takes no `G`: `alive`, `dist`, `gap`, `mx`, `mz`, `eyeY` and `chestY` (the last two until F7's `groundY`, §2.10), and `actions/move.js` `moveMode`. `queries.js` holds a superset of what `q` must cover: it also re-exports `moveMode`, `forbidMask`, `canShoot` and `canCharge`, which the plans, `canAct` and the AI read and the `__ts` contract doesn't name.

**Step machine.** `battle()` and `playerTurn()` (1201-1264) are unrolled into resumable steps. The statement order is unchanged, so the trace lines up line for line:

```js
function advance(G) {
  const T = G.turn
  while (!G.pending && T.stage !== 'over') switch (T.step) {
    case 'rolloff':   T.stage = 'battle'; emit(G, 'stage', { stage: 'battle' }); emit(G, 'objectives', { owners: ownersOf(G) })  // (R5a) as battle() today: the stage (the mirror's only source of it) and the flags, then the roll-off
                      rollOff(G); T.round = 1; T.t = 0; T.step = 'turnStart'; break   // do…while as 1208-1213
    case 'turnStart': T.active = (T.first + T.t) % 2; resetTurn(G, T.active); T.ph = 0; T.step = 'phase'; break  // 1228-1231
    case 'phase': {
      const ph = PHASES[T.ph].key; emit(G, 'phase.start', { side: T.active, phase: ph, round: T.round }); T.step = 'phaseEnd'
      if (ph === 'fight') { if (G.units.some((u) => alive(u) && isEngaged(G, u))) fightPhase(G, T.active) }
      else if (ph === 'morale') moralePhase(G)
      else if (!anyCanAct(G, T.active)) emit(G, 'pause', { s: 0.2 })
      else if (ctrl(G, T.active) === 'human') G.pending = { k: 'phase', seats: [T.active], phase: ph }
      else runAI(G, T.active, ph)
      break
    }
    case 'phaseEnd':  traceState(G, `phase ${T.active}:${PHASES[T.ph].key}`); checkWipe(G)
                      if (T.wiped >= 0) { gameOver(G); break }                     // skips the mesmerism reset, as 1257
                      T.step = ++T.ph < PHASES.length ? 'phase' : 'turnEnd'; break
    case 'turnEnd':   endMesmerism(G, T.active); T.step = ++T.t < 2 ? 'turnStart' : 'score'; break  // 1259-1263
    case 'score':     scoreRound(G)                                                 // 1266-1281
                      if (T.round < G.setup.rounds) { T.round++; T.t = 0; T.step = 'turnStart' }
                      else if (G.setup.overtime === 'vote' && humanSeats(G).length) G.pending = { k: 'roundLimit', seats: humanSeats(G), votes: {} }
                      else gameOver(G)
                      break
  }
}
```

**Handlers.**

- `end` clears `pending` (the step is already `phaseEnd`).
- `auto` runs `runAI(G, seat, phase)`, then clears `pending`.
- `deployed` removes the seat from `pending.seats`. When none are left, it clears `pending` and sets the step to `rolloff`. ((R6a) `createMatch` sets the step to `rolloff` up front, so `deployed` only clears `pending`.)
- `vote` records the vote. When every seat has voted, all `more` means `T.round++; T.overtime++; step 'turnStart'`, and anything else means `gameOver`.
- `concede` ends the game for the other side.
- (R6a) Built in `core/commands.js` with `legal()`'s table (`RULES`: the decision each kind answers, the phase it belongs to, its integer fields, its rule). `legal()` and `preview()` save and restore the lock, so they nest. `concede` is judged out of band (any human seat, until the battle is over or, (R6a's fixer), a side is wiped out). `vote` is F4's: `createMatch` refuses `overtime: 'vote'` until then (`fullSetup`), and the score step keeps the `roundLimit` shape. `move`, `shoot`, `charge` (on a miss, or the AI's) and `chargeEnd` end the action (`finishAction`) in the handler, not in the action, so main.js could keep calling the actions until R6b; (R6b) approved and kept so (the charge's (R6a) note below).

Actions inside a phase leave `pending` as the phase decision. `charge` may replace it with `chargeEnd`, and `chargeEnd` restores it.

**The charge splits at today's `await pickChargeSpot` (996). It draws nothing between the two halves.**

- `declareCharge(G, u, tg, via)` runs 972-994 unchanged (plan, `chargeTried`, 2D6, failure → `finishAction`; success → flags, "Contact!" log). (R6a) As built, the `charge` handler opens the decision: `declareCharge` still returns `{plan, rolled}` for a seat's contact (main.js calls it until R6b), and the handler turns that into `pending = {k:'chargeEnd', …}`, or ends the action on a miss or the AI's charge; `chargeEnd` calls `finishCharge`, gives the seat its phase back, then `finishAction`. Proposed to stay so at R6b (the actions never touch `G.pending` and never call `finishAction`), which supersedes this bullet's "failure → `finishAction`" and the two sub-bullets marked (R6a) below. If the lead rejects it, R6b moves the `pending` write and `finishAction` into the actions (the R6a notes, "What R6b must do", item 2).
  - If `via === 'ai'` (an AI seat, or a human's Auto; this replaces `auto || !human(u.side)`), it calls `finishCharge(G, u, tg, plan.cell)`.
  - Otherwise it sets `pending = {k:'chargeEnd', seats:[seat], u, tg, rolled, cell: plan.cell}`. (R6a, approved: the `charge` handler sets it, from `declareCharge`'s `{plan, rolled}`.)
- `finishCharge` walks, calls `refreshNav`, then `finishAction`. (R6a, approved: `finishCharge` walks and refreshes the nav, and the `chargeEnd` handler, or the `charge` handler for the AI's, calls `finishAction`.) The `act` trace line comes after the walk in both paths, exactly as today.
- `chargeEnd` recomputes `chargePlan(G, u, tg)`. That is pure over unchanged state: nav is never dirty at a command boundary, because every action ends with `refreshNav`.
- (R5b) Built in `core/actions/charge.js` with the step machine's parts left to R6: through R5 neither half calls `finishAction` (main.js's until R6's `core/engine.js`), which main.js calls once the charge's events have played, so the `act` line is never written while the view is behind (R5b notes). There is no `G.pending` yet, so `declareCharge(G, u, tg, via)` returns what the seat picks from, `{plan, rolled}`, or null once the charge is over (a miss, or `via` `'ai'`, which has gone on to `finishCharge` itself); main.js holds the pick (`S.chargePick`, `placeCharge`, Shortest move) until R6's `chargeEnd`. `finishCharge(G, u, tg, cell, plan = chargePlan(G, u, tg))` takes the plan the AI path already has, and remakes it after a human's pick, as R6's `chargeEnd` will (P-human holds the remade plan to the old code's at every pick in the corpus). It walks through `actions/move.js`'s `resolveWalk` (§2.3), which lands with it, ahead of R5c. `chargeSpots(plan, rolled)` reads only its arguments and takes no `G`: a `Uint8Array` with a 1 per nav cell the roll reaches (the old `pickChargeSpot`'s mask, 1009-1011).

**AI inside the fold.**

```js
function runAI(G, seat, phase) {
  for (const cmd of aiPhase(G, seat, phase)) {        // generators keep `mine` and `claimed` as today (ai.js 57-114)
    if (SIM) assertNull(legal(G, seat, cmd))          // property: the AI never issues an illegal command
    HANDLERS[cmd.t](G, seat, cmd, 'ai')
  }
}
```

Inside the generators:
- `await api.doAdvance(u)` becomes `yield {t:'advance', u}`, after which the roll is read back from `u.flags.advRoll`.
- `await wait(s)` (ai.js 112, 256, 287) becomes `emit(G, 'pause', {s})`.
- `api.focus` becomes `emit(G, 'focus', …)`.
- Every tie-break draw stays between the same yields.
- (R6a) Built: `core/ai/policy.js` (`ORDER`, `aiPhase` and its three generators) and `core/ai/score.js`, ai.js moved verbatim. `hold` is not yielded: the generator calls `hold(G, u)` itself (no command, no event), so `legal()` knows no `hold`. (R6a's fixer) `runAI` leaves `G.pending` as it found it (nothing for an AI seat, the seat's own for an Auto), so it only ever holds a human seat's decision, at every point and after a throw; under `strict` each AI command is judged by `legalFor(G, seat, cmd, decision)` (`core/commands.js`, not in the API: `legal()` against a decision passed in), with the phase decision the seat would hold were it a human's (`{k:'phase', seats:[seat], phase}`), so exactly as a seat's; a command that leaves a decision open throws. `if (SIM)` is `G.strict`. main.js's old loop drives the same generators (`aiTurn`), so the shipped game and the fold run one AI.

### 2.3 Events

`emit(G, t, payload)` pushes `{t, ...payload}` onto `G.out` when it is non-null. Building an event never draws and never mutates. Every pure wait in today's code becomes a `pause {s}` at the same spot: damage 0.25, fight end 0.3, a morale flee 0.5, a blast with no victims 0.25, a skipped phase 0.2, AI waits 0.05/0.1, and (R5a) the 0.06 after each wound allocated, so a unit's last model falls and its "destroyed" text shows in the same moment, as today. Every visual await becomes the semantic event below. (R5a) `core/journal.js` also has `emitTo(out, t, payload)`, the same rule onto an array the caller passes (the `Terrain`'s reports), `drain(G)` (every event since the last drain, taken out of `G.out`; `[]` for a quiet run; (R6b's fixer) gone with its last caller: the Session takes each entry's events out of `G.out` itself, §2.6), and `log(G, side, html, cls)`/`flush(G)`, which trace a battle-log line and emit its `log` event, then the held-back lines' (`traced: false`).

| Group | Events |
|---|---|
| Flow | `phase.start {side, phase, round}` ((R5a) `round`, the mirror's) · `pause {s}` · `focus {x, z}` ((R5b) the fight emits one per fight, unconditionally: the old test, `human(u.side) \|\| human(target.side) \|\| S.follow`, was true whenever `focus()` did anything, and the view's follow setting decides) · `round.scored {round, held, vp, owners}` · `objectives {owners}` (at every action end; (R5a) also at the battle's start, after a damage that slew, and after a morale flight; (R5b) and at the end of a `resolveWalk`, where the old walk turned a flag the frame it crossed) · `status {engaged: [ids], mesmerized: [ids]}` (at action end; labels; (R5a) also at the end of every damage, of a morale flight, of the fight phase and of a turn's mesmerism; (R5b) and of a `resolveWalk`, which is where a charger's ⚔ now comes from, in the frame `finishAction`'s brought it) · `act {tag, proj?}` (after `traceState('act')`; `proj` = `mirror.project(G)` in sim only: (R5a) under `?debug`) · (R5a) `check {proj}` (`?debug` only: main.js's `checkpoint()` puts one after each action's events (`played()`) and after main.js's own `stage` events (each deployment's; the battle's start, with its `objectives`); `proj` being `project(G)` as the match then stood; P-present's checkpoint between acts, §2.4; the view plays it as nothing; through R5b it also came at the old walk's end with `keys: ['owners']`, holding only those fields of the mirror; (R5c) that field went with the old walk, and P-present reads none) · `stage {stage}` ((R5a) the mirror's stage, and its only source (`phase.start` does not set it), where the loop sets `G.turn.stage`: deploy, battle, over) · `pending {k, seats}` ((R6a) at the end of every `advance()` that stops at a decision, so after each command inside a phase too) · `game.over {win, why: 'score'\|'wipe'\|'concede', vp, rounds}` ((R6a) `rounds` the rounds played: (R6a's fixer round 2) the one under way counted: the last round on the score, the round it ended in for a wipe-out or a concession mid-round, 0 for a concession in the deployment (where `G.turn.round` already says 1); the end screen words its line from `why`) |
| Tray and log | `tray.open {title}` · `dice {label, dice, need, sum, pass, note, save}` · `log {side, html, cls, traced, at}` (`at`: trace length when logged or flushed) |
| Units | `unit.move {u, path: [{x,z}], L, speed, fly, smashes: [{s, ev: [terrain events]}]}` ((R5b) and `to: {x, z}`, where the unit stands: the k=1 lerp, so neither the mirror nor the view redoes the walk's arithmetic to find it; the mirror folds the smashes' events with it, the view plays each as the walker passes its `s`; (R5c) and `stomp`, a presentation flag like `speed` and `fly`, which the caller says: a wrecker setting off on a move of more than 0.1", whose old `sfx.boom(0.4)` the view plays as the walk starts; a charge's walk never stomped) · `unit.place {u, x, z}` ((R5a) a deployment placement, R6's `place`; and, until R5c's `resolveWalk`, each frame of the old walk; (R5c) a placement only) · `unit.face {u, tg}` · `unit.wound {u, m, dmg}` (the model stands) · `unit.slain {u, m, by, dmg}` ((R5a) `dmg`: the number shown, the wounds it had left) · `unit.flee {u, m}` · `unit.formation {u, offs, r, pos}` ((R5a) emitted by `closeRanks` after the relayout and any pile-in; `offs` holds `[ox, oz]` for every model) · `unit.destroyed {u, by}` (`by` an id, or null for a morale flight) |
| Attacks | `volley {u, tg, fx, n}` ((R5c) `n` the shots thrown, `attackCount`; the view flies `min(10, n)` of them, as the old `volleyFx` did) · `blast.aim {x, z, r}` · `blast.scatter {from, to, d}` · `blast.fire {u, to, fx}` · `blast.land {x, z, r, fx}` · `spell.cast {u}` · `spell.fizzle {u}` · `spell.thorns {u, x, z, r}` · (R5c) `spell.fade {u}` (after an eruption's template: its thorns sink back, which the old `thornburst` started once its `blastLands` was done) · `spell.gaze {u, tg}` · (R5c) `spell.mesmerized {u, tg}` (the "Mesmerized!" over `tg`, after the mesmerize's damage and its `status`) · `melee {u, tg, hits}` ((R5b) `{u, tg, n, hits}`: `n` attacks thrown, `hits` of them landing; emitted after the hit roll and before its `dice`, where the old code lunged, and its handler throws the sparks as that row settles, `PACE.dice(n)` later, where the old code threw them) · `charge.result {u, tg, ok}` · (F19a) `keg.fuse {id, x, z}` (a powder keg set off: chunk `id`, at its place, after the traced line "The powder keg goes up!" and straight before its blast's `blast.land {x, z, r, fx: 'keg'}`, whose victims and scenery follow as a template's do; the keg's own `terrain.destroy` came earlier, with whatever broke it. The view fizzes its fuse a beat (`PACE.cost`'s half second, a hold in an attack batch), then plays the blast as the keg's own bang; the camera's `pointsOf` and the courtesy fog take it as its blast's landing; the mirror folds nothing for it) |
| Terrain | `terrain.clear {}` (a new table) · `terrain.add {def}` (every chunk, the board's included: rubble piles and fallen logs too; `def.look` included, a fallen log's being `{piece: 'fallen', tree, dx, dz}`, so the fall plays from its add and there is no topple event) · `terrain.hurt {id, from, at}` · `terrain.destroy {id, kind, from, at}` (before its consequences; (R4) `at` is the chunk's place `{x, y, z}` when it was hit) · `terrain.collapse {drops: [{id, dy}], by}` · `terrain.rubble {id, from}`. The view never reads the live chunk: it keeps each chunk's `x`/`z` from its `terrain.add {def}` (a chunk never moves sideways; a collapse only lowers it), and reads `alive` and `y` from the mirror (§2.4). (R4) A hurt or destroyed chunk's debris reads its place from `at`, so those handlers need no mirror lookup; the mirror, folded in event order, holds the same place at that event, so `at` is a convenience, not a second source of truth. The collapse handler's dust, which today reads the block's live place when its fall tween ends (a later blast in the same volley may have lowered it again by then), reads the block's resting place after its drop from the mirror instead, captured when the event is played: cosmetic, and different from today only in that case. (R5a) Done: the `Terrain` reports these `id` events (`def` = `{id, kind, shape, look}`, `shape` a copy taken as the chunk joins), still into the `out` its caller passes per call, which is `G.out` in play (the R5a notes say why). |

`m` is a model index. `fx` and `look` values are presentation keys only; rules never read them.

**`resolveWalk`.** It samples exactly as 522-533:
- one sample every 0.25" for a wrecker, plus the end point;
- `smashAround` runs per sample, in order, and its `terrain.*` events are captured with that sample's `s`;
- the unit is then placed at the **k=1 lerp** (`seg.find(d <= s+l)`, `lerp`, 536-539), not at `pts.at(-1)`;
- a path under 0.05" moves nothing and smashes nothing (519);
- finally it emits `unit.move`.

### 2.4 The core/presenter boundary

```js
// view/player.js
export class EventPlayer {
  constructor({ handlers, mirror, onIdle })
  push(events) { this.q.push(...events); if (!this.running) this.run() }        // never blocks the fold
  async run() { this.running = true
    while (this.q.length) { const e = this.q.shift(); this.mirror = applyEvent(this.mirror, e)
      this.catchUp(); await (this.handlers[e.t] ?? this.handlers.fallback)(e, this.mirror) }
    this.running = false; this.onIdle() }
  get idle() { return !this.running && !this.q.length }
  backlog()                    // seconds queued at the current speed, estimated from PACE and unit.move L/speed
  snap(G) { this.q.length = 0; this.mirror = project(G); this.view.rebuild(this.mirror); this.onIdle() }
}
```

- (R5a) **The transitional player** (`view/player.js`, built at R5a) has `push`, `play(events)` (resolves once everything queued has played; (R6b's fixer) gone with its last caller: the Session's sink `push`es each entry's events), `idle`, `onIdle`, the mirror, and an `observer` (`?debug` only). A handler returns a promise when the next event must wait for it; events whose handlers take no time play inside `play()`, so main.js's own events (a terrain call's reports, a figure placed, an action's end) are shown straight after the code that emits them, as before. Until R7's `TerrainView.sync` exists it has `reset(mirror)` instead of `snap(G)`: a new table resets the mirror to `project(G)` and then plays the board's `terrain.clear` and adds. `backlog()` and catch-up are N2's.
- (R7a) **The snap, as built:** `snap(G, shown = project(G))` starts a new table (a handler's promise from the last one, a dice row or a pause, resumes nothing when it settles), drops the queue, makes `shown` the mirror, calls `view.rebuild(G, shown)`, resets the `?debug` observer to `shown` and calls `onIdle({ snap: true })` ((R7a's fixer, round 2) so main.js's `idled` leaves an open card as it was after a snap, as before R7: R7a notes). `rebuild` reads `G`, not the mirror: the meshes need each chunk's def (shape, look), which the mirror doesn't hold, and a snap is only taken where the two agree (an idle player, a new table, a battle's start). It is `TerrainView.sync(G.terrain.chunks)`, `UnitViews.sync(G.units, edgeOf)` (`edgeOf(seat)`, the seat's edge, which a view is made for; each kept figure's pose reset, a war machine's arm at rest and its globe back on: R7a's fixer), `Shots.clear()` (the template's marker, the thorns) and fx's `clearDecals()` ((R7a's fixer, round 3): the scorch and acid marks, which only `showTable` cleared, after its snap, so a snap back to an earlier point, or onto another match, would have kept them); `rebuild(G, M)` doesn't read `M`: the views read the mirror themselves (their `mirror()`, the player's, set to `M` before `rebuild` is called); the `?debug` snap check makes its fresh snap with this same `rebuild`, into views off the table. `shown` is the backdrop's projection at the stage `'title'` for both the title's snap and a battle's start, the table as the title showed it, so the battle's own `stage` events (its deployment's first) take the mirror on from there and P-present holds each (snapped at the backdrop's own stage, `'deploy'`, a dropped deployment `stage` passed it: its `--self-test` caught that). `reset` is gone: the backdrop is drawn by a snap (`showTable`), and a battle starts with one of its own table as it stood before anything happened (`start()`), replacing R6b's dropped board events and `bindViews`; the battle's board events then play, and their adds take back the meshes on show (§2.9's (R7a) note). Held by `sim/snap-check.mjs` in Chromium: at every drained queue and every P-present checkpoint the table as built is a fresh snap's, and a kept table synced again, and (R7a's fixer, round 3) at each battle's end the page's own table, snapped where it stands, is a fresh snap's with none of fx's marks left (the R7a notes).
- **Handlers hold today's visuals verbatim.** `dice` → `tray.row` (1605-1638); `unit.move` → the old tween (535-545), driving a per-figure display position and replaying each smash's events as the walker passes `s`; `unit.slain` → the `killModel` tween chain (898-907).
- **Unknown events go to a fallback.** It floats `e.text` if present, then waits `e.beat ?? 0.3` s (content-first), so a new keyword can ship rules before art. (R7b) Built as the `EventPlayer`'s own default `handlers.fallback` (`view/player.js`), the text said through the view's `text` (`view/index.js`, fx's floating text), so a player made without one still plays an unknown event; handlers that bring their own replace it.
- **`present/pace.js` holds every fixed duration** ((R5a) `PACE.phaseStart(local, stage)`, `PACE.dice(n)`, `PACE.pause(s)`, `PACE.beat` for the fallback)**:**
  - `phase.start`: 0.9 s when the seat is local or the stage isn't battle, otherwise 0.6 (1779);
  - `dice`: `0.38 + min(n,14)·0.035` (1637);
  - `unit.wound`/`unit.slain`: 0.06; (R5a) no: they take no time of their own, and the 0.06 is a `pause` the core emits after each wound allocated (§2.3), as today's code waited;
  - `pause`: `e.s`.
  Animation handlers keep their tween lengths.
- **The view never reads `G` while events are queued.** One `end` can compute a whole AI turn before the first die is shown. Labels, rings, flags, VP, round and figure positions read the **mirror**: `present/mirror.js`, a pure fold of events into `{units: {id → pos, r, models, alive, mesmerized, engaged}, chunks: {id → alive, y}, owners, vp, round, active, phase, stage}`. (R5a) Pure in what it reads (the event, never `G`, no rendering), but `applyEvent` folds in place and returns `M`: a caller that keeps a mirror across events copies it, and whoever is handed the player's mirror (a handler, the `?debug` observer) reads it and never folds into it. (R5a) Rings: their place and size (the ring and hit cylinder) read the mirror; their highlight (selected, can act, a target) reads `G` while the player is idle, as input does, and comes from the HUD model from R7. (R5a) What the pointer finds and names reads the mirror too, since it works while the player is behind (on the opponent's or the AI's turn): the hit test (`pick()`) takes the units the mirror shows standing, and the tooltip's unit line and the unit card take their models, wounds, mesmerized and in combat from it. The card's moved/shot/charged and cover still read `G` (no mirror field; R7's `ui/card.js` moves them onto the HUD model), as do the move, shot and charge previews, which show only on a local seat's own idle turn. (R6b's fixer, round 2) So the card shows them only while `player.idle`: while the player is behind it leaves them off (from R6b one `end` computes a whole AI turn and a watched battle is computed whole at its start, so they would tell of moves and dice the table hasn't played; a watched battle's cards show none until its end, an accepted change), and a card still open as the player goes idle is redrawn, catching up with the table (a phase's start and the selection still close or replace it, as before). Cover is not recomputed from the mirror's place either: `G.nav.cover` may already reflect terrain the match smashed later. R7's HUD model should give them a shown source (a view-only per-unit record of what each seat's action did, set by its `act` and cleared by its seat's `phase.start`, or mirror fields P-present holds to `project(G)`), and the cover the mirror's chunks (`TerrainView.sync`). P-present holds every unit's card to the mirror at every checkpoint (the `?debug` block's `present.card`; its self-test's `card-reads-match`). (R7b) Built as the view-only record: every battle's `onTrace` (the flow's, `app/flow.js`, no longer `?debug` only) takes each unit's facts (`present/hud-model.js` `factsOf`: moved, fell back, advanced and its roll, shot, charged, and `inCover(G, u)`, read through the core's `preview`, the dice locked) as the match writes each `act` line, the sink hands each `act` event its own (`facts`), and the `act` handler makes it the card's record; (R7b's fixer) and at each stop, where the match waits on a decision after an entry, the sink hands the entry's `pending` event (its last: `advance` emits one as it stops) the match's facts as they stand, which the table shows exactly once it has played that far, and the `pending` handler makes them the record (so a deployment's placements, which write no `act`, are in it through the roll-off, the first banner and an AI's first walk, and the record each entry's playback starts from is what the idle card showed); a seat's first `phase.start` clears its units' deeds (`turnBegun`, as `resetTurn` does), and a snap takes the record from the match snapped to. So the cover is the match's at the last action's end or stop the table has played, not recomputed from the mirror's chunks (which would need the nav grid as shown); what a fight or a morale phase changes without an `act` (a pile-in, a model slain or fled) reaches the record at the next action's end or stop, an accepted lag. While the player is idle the card reads `G` as before (through the preview too). P-present's card check holds the record too, to facts it takes from a quiet fold of the same battle through the core alone, an `act` line and an entry at a time (`card-facts-stale`, `card-stop-stale` and `card-turn-kept` in its self-test, `card-reads-match` retargeted to `ui/card.js`).
- **Input, the HUD model and previews read `G` only when `player.idle`** and the pending decision belongs to a local seat. At that point mirror and `G` agree.
- **Instant replay and catch-up.**
  - Rejoin, late join, rollback and scrubbing all fold quietly (`G.out = null`) and then `snap(G)`.
  - (R5c's fixer) The view's rebuild on `snap` also removes what the view holds outside the mirror: a template's marker (main.js's `blastMarker`) and an eruption's thorns (`spikesOf`), since a snap drops the queued `blast.fire` or `spell.fade` that would have taken them away (`setupTable` clears both for a new table today); (R7a's fixer, round 3) and fx's scorch and acid marks, which no event takes away and which a snap back to an earlier point, or onto another match, would otherwise keep from a timeline it left.
  - Live backlog is handled elastically (experience-first): above 8 s at the current speed, play at 2×, then 4×. Above 30 s, or while `document.hidden`, snap and toast a summary such as "Caught up: Ann moved 3 units, shot twice". The log keeps every line.
  - The fold is driven by store change events, never by `requestAnimationFrame`, so background tabs stay current.
- **Checks.** `sim/present-check.mjs` asserts `applyEvent*` equals `project(G)` at every `act` of every log, so a missing event is a failing test, not a ghost unit ((R5a) built: it taps the page's player through the `?debug` block's `present.listen`, and its `--self-test` drops one event at a time). (R5a) An action's end emits `objectives` and `status` straight before its `act`, so at an `act` the flags and labels are always fresh, whatever the action emitted on the way. P-present therefore also holds the mirror to `project(G)` at each `check {proj}` (§2.3), after each converted action's events, so an `objectives` or `status` an action forgets (after a kill, a flight, a damage's end) fails too; the self-test drops each of those and checks they are caught, and that they are not without the checks. The same `check` follows the `stage` events main.js emits itself (each deployment's, the battle's start), which the next stage event would otherwise put right before any `act`, and held the flags (`keys: ['owners']`) at the old walk's end, which its action's end would otherwise re-emit, until R5c retired that walk (a move's flags now turn at its `resolveWalk`'s end, held by the move's own `check`). Not covered: main.js's own `status` events outside a converted action (a mesmerism's, a turn's end), which the next action's end repeats before any checkpoint; they move into core at R6 (R5b left them: neither is the fight's or the charge's), inside a checked action. (R5b) Nor the fight phase's own closing `status`, which repeats the last fight's damage's (every fight ends in a damage), so dropping it changes no check (probed); and the fight runs whole inside one `played()`, so its checks come once per fight phase, not once per fight's damage as before (P-present's checks fell from 4,033 to 3,728 with the fight alone): a damage's flags or labels dropped mid-phase are caught only when no later fight in the phase puts them right, and the self-test's damage drops are still caught (by a shooting damage's own check, or a fight phase's). The charge's events that change nothing the mirror holds (`charge.result`, `unit.face`) and the fight's (`melee`, `unit.face`, `focus`, the tray, the pause) are held instead to their order as the player plays them (R5b's fixer, `present-check.mjs`'s `eventOrder`): a fight is `unit.face`, `focus`, `tray.open`, `melee`, then straight on to its hit row (`n` dice, `hits` passing), one `melee` before each fight line, for the pair it names and the hits it counts, and the 0.3 s `pause` after it; a charge is `tray.open`, its `dice`, `unit.face`, `charge.result`, then straight on to its line, agreeing with `ok`. The self-test drops or moves each (a lunge, a lunge after its row, either turn to face, the beat after a fight, either verdict), and the run fails if the corpus held no fight or no charge line. So P-present fails on code older than R5b. (R5c) The move's and the shot's own events likewise: a move line (`move`, `advance`, `fall back`) is followed, past the held-back lines it shows, by its walk, as long as the line says (none for 0.0"), `stomp` set exactly for a wrecker's move of more than 0.1" (never for a charge's walk); an advance line comes straight after its tray and its one-die `Advance D6` row; a shot's tray straight after the shooter's `unit.face`; a `volley` straight after the tray and straight before its hit row (`n` dice), one before each shooting line for the pair it names; a template is `blast.aim`, straight on to its one-die hit row, on a miss the `Scatter D6+1` row straight on to `blast.scatter` from the aim (`d` the die plus one), then `blast.fire` to where it was aimed or scattered to, straight on to `blast.land` there, and no template is aimed while one is in the air; a cast row straight on to `spell.cast` or `spell.fizzle` as it passed or not, a fizzle line straight after its `spell.fizzle`, a cast straight on to the gaze or the eruption's line, which comes (past held-back lines) to its `spell.thorns`, straight on to a `blast.land` under them, and `spell.fade` before the action ends; a gaze straight on to its `Mortal wounds D3` row, and the mesmerize line straight after `spell.mesmerized`, which comes straight after the gaze's `status`, one with the target mesmerized (the damage's own `status` just before it has the target as it was). The self-test drops or moves each (sixteen edits, among them the volley after its row and the gaze's `status`), and over the whole corpus the run fails if it held no line or template of any of these kinds. So P-present fails on code older than R5c. (R5c's fixer, round 2) And the look fields the view reads off those events: every walk has `fly` exactly when its unit flies and goes at 7"/s for a move, 11 for a charge; each `blast.land` (a template's or an eruption's) comes straight on to its first victim's wound row, or to the 0.25 s `pause` when it caught nobody; the volley and each template's `blast.fire` are the shooter's (the unit that turned to face before the tray), and `volley`, `blast.fire` and `blast.land` carry that shooter's weapon's `fx`. The self-test bends each (a flier's move on the ground, a move at a charge's pace, the beat dropped, a template thrown by its target, a volley and a landing in the wrong look), and the whole corpus must hold walks of fliers and templates that caught nobody.
