(R5c's fixer) A run on a selection (`--only`) only notes the kinds it held none of, since one battle may have no fizzle, gaze or eruption; and the self-test first runs the check unmutated on the same battles, stopping if that fails, and counts a mutation caught only when a battle fails on the mirror, the act events or the event order. Nor, in practice, the flags at the battle's start: a check follows them, but no corpus battle deploys a model within reach of an objective (the deployment zones end at |x| = 12 and the flank objectives stand at |x| = 9, with a 3" reach plus the base), so they are always nobody's there and dropping them changes nothing a check sees; covering them needs a human log that deploys onto an objective, a corpus change for the lead. Under `?debug` the browser diffs the drained view against a fresh `snap(G)`. (R6b) Over the Session the checkpoints have a new source, since the core can't project: the `?debug` block's `onTrace` takes `project(G)` as the match writes each `act`, `phase` and `over` line, where it stands in the events emitted so far (`G.out.length`), and the sink puts a `check` there before the player gets the entry's events (after an action's own events and before its end re-reports the flags and labels, as R5's `played()` check stood; after a fight or a morale phase; before the end), gives each `act` event its act line's projection, and ends each entry's events with a `check` of the match as it stops (after the deployment's stage, a placement, a charge declared, an advance: the checks main.js's own stage events had). The mirror P-present folds starts from the one the player is reset to as a battle starts (the backdrop's, which is the battle's table before anything happens, `start()`), and at the end it must equal `project(G)` round included, the engine's round never running one past the last. Still not covered: the `status` after a turn's mesmerism wears off, which the next action's end repeats unless the next turn's first phase has nothing to do (its `phase` line's check comes first then). (R6b's fixer) The roll-off's tray and dice rows, new in the stream, are held to their order like an action's own events (`eventOrder`): the tray straight after the battle's `stage` and its `objectives`, one-die rows in pairs (seat 0's, then seat 1's, labelled as the first pair), every pair but the last a tie, then straight on to the line naming the higher roller of the last; the self-test drops seat 1's row (`no-rolloff-row`), and over the whole corpus the run fails if it held no roll-off.
- **`?fast`** keeps `clock.speed = 1e4` and no render (legacy behaviour), so `sim/chromium.mjs` keeps working.

### 2.5 Controllers

| Source | Where it runs | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| **Local human** (`input/human.js`) | the client holding the seat | The mode is derived, never stored: `mode = player.idle && session.decisionFor() >= 0 ? G.pending.k : 'watch'`. That replaces `S.busy`, `S.auto`, `S.waiting`, `phaseResolve`, `S.deployDone`, `S.chargePick` and `myTurn()`. Tools turn a pick into a body (`tools/move`: `{t:'move', u, c: nearestValid(plan, x, z)}`; Advance: `{t:'advance', u}`; Shortest: `{t:'chargeEnd', c:-1}`). The tool previews with `session.preview(fn)` (rng locked), then calls `session.submit(seat, body)` only if `legal` passes. |
| **AI** (`core/ai/policy.js`) | inside `apply`/`advance`, **on every peer** | Generators yield commands, so an AI seat appends nothing. A human's `auto` runs the same generator. |
| **Remote human** | none on this client | Its entries arrive through the store and fold like anyone's. |
| **Script** (`sim/`) | Node | Replays recorded bodies. Human baselines, peer tests and the netplay log share one format. |

Hotseat is two local seats. During a simultaneous deploy, `submit` takes an explicit seat, and the UI deploys seat 0 then seat 1 as today. A spectator is `localSeats = []`.

(R6b) As built, in main.js until R7's `input/human.js`: `localSeat()` is `session.decisionFor()`, `localDecision()` the pending decision when it is a local seat's, `deploySeat()` the seat deploying here (a placement plays at once, so the deployment doesn't wait on `player.idle`, as the old `deployClick` never waited on `S.busy`), `myTurn()` `player.idle` and a local `phase` decision, `picking()` `player.idle` and a local `chargeEnd` decision (the pick, `input/tools/charge-end.js`: the `chargeSpots` mask of the plan made again under `session.preview`, cached per decision, Shortest move `-1`). Every click and button is a body through `send(seat, body)`, which asks `session.legal` first and sends nothing it refuses: a deployment click `place {u, c}` (freeSpot's cell, within the 2.5" UI tolerance), Begin battle `deployed`, a move click `move {u, c}` (`nearestValid` on the selected unit's plan), Advance, a shot, a charge, a charge's end `chargeEnd {c}`, End and Auto. The tools' previews (the move plan, its path and inches, a shot's odds, a charge's plan and spots, `freeSpot`, the rings' highlights, the Advance button's test) all go through `session.preview`. The HUD's End, Auto and Advance show while a local seat's phase decision is the one the table shows (the mirror's stage, seat, phase and round, once the table has played a `phase.start` since its last `stage` event: (R6b's fixer) until then the mirror's turn fields are a table's before the battle, seat 0's movement in round 1, so through the roll-off End, Auto and the hint showed seat 0's movement whoever was to move first; main.js's view-only `phaseShown`, kept out of the mirror, which P-present holds to `project(G)`; the "(AI) are taking their turn…" hint waits for it too), are disabled whenever the player is playing, and keep what they showed while it plays, so they never read `G` before the table has caught up; they hide once the decision moves on (an End or an Auto hands the phase over). (R6b's fixer, round 3) A charge that makes contact is the seat's own action too, though the decision it holds is its `chargeEnd` until the end is placed: End and Auto stay up, disabled, through its roll and its walk (main.js's view-only `buttonsUp`, set when the player catches up to the seat's phase and cleared once the decision is neither that phase nor that seat's `chargeEnd`), and hide only while the pick itself waits, Shortest move in their place; until then they vanished at the roll and came back only once the walk had played. When the player goes idle, the selected unit stays selected while it can still act (an advance), and a charge waiting for its end shades its spots. (R6b's fixer) A click on the board during the pick ends the charge only on a spot the roll reaches (`nearestSpot` within 2.4"); a click outside the orange area does nothing, as before R6b (its `-1` for "no spot" is also the wire's Shortest move, so `placeCharge(c)` takes only a reached cell and the Shortest move button has its own path, `takeShortest()`). Each button's handler returns why it sent nothing (null once sent), for the `?debug` hooks that press them.

(R7b) As built in `input/human.js`: the `Human` holds the selection (`sel`, `reach`, `hover`, `hoverPick`, `mouse`, and `pickShown`, the charge whose spots are shaded) and derives the rest from the Session and the player: `mode()` is the row above's (`player.idle && session.decisionFor() >= 0 ? G.pending.k : 'watch'`), `myTurn()` its `'phase'` and `picking()` its `'chargeEnd'` (the charge-end tool's pick), `deploySeat()` the seat deploying here (not gated on the player, as before), `state()` what the HUD model reads of it. The tools are `input/tools/deploy.js` (`spotAt`, freeSpot's cell within the 2.5" tolerance; `placeAt`), `move.js` (`planOf`, `cellAt`, `preview`: the path and its inches; `moveTo`, `advance`), `shoot.js` (`preview`: the odds, `ui/tooltip.js`'s `oddsText`; `shootAt`), `charge.js` (`preview`: the roll needed; `chargeAt`) and `charge-end.js` (R6b's); a hover asks the one tool its phase names inside one `session.preview`, as before. `input/picking.js` (`Picker`) finds the unit and the ground under the pointer. The buttons (`ui/actions.js`) are intents into the `Human` (`end`, `auto`, `advanceSel`, `takeShortest`), still returning why they sent nothing. `app/flow.js` calls `Human.idled()` (the selection kept while it can act, a charge's spots shaded) from its own `idled`.

### 2.6 Match layer: envelope, fold, stores, session (pure)

**Envelope.** One per log entry, stored as canonical JSON:

```js
{ id: 'k3f9.17.x2', s: 0, d: 'k3f9', p: 'p2x1.16.q0', h: '1u8kq0d', t: 'move', u: 3, c: 1234 }
// id: `${dev}.${counter}.${rand}` (unique) · s: seat (−1 for open/start) · d: device · p: prev (the head this seat saw)
// h: stateHash(author's pre-state), only on single-seat decision kinds · then the body
```

`decode` rejects anything that is not an object with known `t`, integer fields, or more than 1 kB. The log is capped at 5,000 entries; past that the status becomes `full` and the match freezes. (R8b) Settled for the large battles (§2.6's (R8b) note): `KINDS` stays `core/commands.js`'s `RULES`' keys; `decode` takes any safe whole number or boolean in any field of a known kind, none of them required, and no array (`legal()` is the one judge of a body, and nothing in `match/` reads a kind's fields, so F4's `opt` and `bools` need no change here); no field of any kind may be named as an envelope key (`id`, `s`, `d`, `p`, `h`) or `t` (a lint); `MAX_BYTES` is one constant, at least 1,024, for every kind; the cap counts junk; and the count is exposed (`folder.count`, `session.count`, a report's `count`).

(R6a) **`legal()` and `apply()` take the body, never the envelope.** `legal()` refuses a body carrying any field its kind doesn't take (§2.2's command bodies), so handed a whole entry it would refuse every one (`takes no field "id"`) and the match would never leave `start`. `match/envelope.js` therefore exports `ENVELOPE_KEYS`, `['id', 's', 'd', 'p', 'h']`, the one list that names the envelope's own fields (`encode` and `decode` use it too, so a field the envelope gains later joins it there and nowhere else), and `bodyOf(e)`, a new object holding every key of `e` but those. It strips by that fixed list, not by the kind's fields: a stray field that is neither an envelope key nor one the kind takes stays in the body, and `legal()` refuses the entry for it, alike on every peer, so the strict check stays the one place a body's fields are judged (§4.1 rule 12) instead of a filter that would quietly drop them. `decode` adds no key to an entry it accepts; one it refuses it marks `bad`, which `push()` rejects before any body is taken. The Folder (`push()` and `outOfBand()`, below), the Session's own checks and `sim/merge-sim.mjs` hand `legal()` and `apply()` only `bodyOf(e)`, as `sim/run.mjs` already hands them a corpus log entry without its `s`. The entry kinds the Folder handles itself (`open`, `start`, `desync`) never reach `legal()`.

**stateHash.** It is cyrb53 → base36 over a canonical string, a superset of `traceState`:
- turn: stage, step, round, t, first, active, ph, vp, wiped, overtime;
- pending;
- every unit: id, `pos.x`/`pos.z` printed with `String(n)` (ES `Number::toString` is spec-exact on every engine), r, alive, lost, mesmerized, flags in sorted keys, models `w/alive/ox/oz`;
- every chunk: id, alive, hp, `shape.y`;
- `rngState` plus the generator word.

(R8b) It stays extensible, and its format is versioned. A unit field a feature adds (F9's `aboard`) is named in `core/hash.js`'s `UNIT_EXTRAS` with the value a unit that never uses the feature holds, and is printed after the unit's models as a sorted `key=value` list only where it differs from that (`[aboard=2]`), so a match that never uses the feature hashes exactly as before. Any change to what `shadowState` prints for some match bumps `CORE_VERSION`, or an older online log would freeze as `desync` instead of opening as `skew`: `sim/data-check.mjs` pins today's hash of a few corpus matches under today's `CORE_VERSION` (8 states of 3 battles under 1), so an accidental change fails there loudly. Derived caches (the nav, the LOS bins, a plan memo) and `G.board` stay out.

`shadowState` is the same string, for debugging. It is **not** the parity shadow. The shadow hashes in `sim/baselines` are `sim/oracle/shadow.mjs`'s legacy format, frozen at R0 and taken at every state line of the trace, not only at `act`. From R4/R6, `sim/` keeps a G → legacy-shadow adapter beside the `__ts` one. It reproduces that format's quirks, which the header of shadow.mjs lists: the last phase run on `round` lines, the round overshoot and stage `battle` on a non-wipe `over` line, `wiped` printed `-` rather than −1, false flags dropped, chunks by array index. The same adapter rebuilds the third parity stream, the battle log as written (`written`: each `#logList` entry as `@<trace length> <class>: <html>`), from `G.journal` once the core has no DOM; it is what pins the destroyed-unit lines that are written but never traced (§4.1 rule 8). (R6a) Built from the `log` events instead (`sim/run.mjs`), each with its `at`, the trace's length as it was written (§2.3): `G.journal` keeps only `trace` and `pendingLog`. So a quiet fold (`G.out` null: a catch-up, a scrub, a peer, R8's `reset` snap) has no battle log, and the trace's `log` lines lack the destroyed-unit lines. R6b's Session and R8's snap must keep the log from the events they present, or a view that snaps after a quiet refold shows an empty log; or `log`/`flush` also append `[side, html, cls, at]` to an unhashed `G.journal.written`, which draws nothing (for the lead). (R8) Deferred to N2, for approval: no mode played on one device refolds, so R8's snap (the flow's `sink.reset`) keeps the battle log as it was shown, the undone entries' lines included; N2's refolds and catch-ups take one of the two ways above.

```js
// match/fold.js: pure, synchronous; the replicated authority; knows nothing about Automerge
const SIMULTANEOUS = new Set(['deploy', 'roundLimit'])
export class Folder {
  constructor({ out = null } = {})        // status 'lobby' until a valid start
  get G(); get status()                   // 'lobby' | 'live' | 'over' | 'desync' | 'skew' | 'full' | 'tamper'
  get accepted(); get rejected()          // ids in fold order · [{ id, why }]
  head(seat)                              // simultaneous decision: this seat's last accepted entry in it, else the entry that opened it;
                                          // otherwise the last accepted entry overall
  push(e) {
    if (e.bad || this.seen.has(e.id)) return this.reject(e, 'envelope')
    this.seen.add(e.id)
    if (this.status === 'lobby') {                                        // online logs open with `open`; local logs start with `start`
      if (e.t === 'open' && !this.openBy) this.openBy = e.d
      return e.t === 'start' && (!this.openBy || e.d === this.openBy) ? this.begin(e) : this.inert(e)
    }
    if (this.status !== 'live') return this.inert(e)                       // over or frozen: later entries are inert
                                                                            // (R8's fixer, round 2, for approval: over, but for a seat's desync
                                                                            // and a seat's hashed command on the final head: the (R8) note)
    if (e.t === 'concede' || e.t === 'desync') return this.outOfBand(e)    // seated human seat + device; terminal
    const P = this.G.pending
    if (!P?.seats.includes(e.s))               return this.reject(e, 'turn')
    if (e.d !== this.G.setup.seats[e.s].dev)   return this.reject(e, 'device')
    if (e.p !== this.head(e.s))                return this.reject(e, 'stale')    // first valid extension of the head wins
    if (!SIMULTANEOUS.has(P.k) && e.h !== stateHash(this.G)) return this.freeze(e)  // desync: never a rejection
    const body = bodyOf(e)                                                  // (R6a) the command alone, never the envelope
    const why = legal(this.G, e.s, body);  if (why) return this.reject(e, why)
    apply(this.G, e.s, body); return this.accept(e)                         // updates heads; records decision openers
  }
  sync(entries)                           // → { events, reset }
}
```

- **`outOfBand(e)`.** (R6a) A `concede` is judged by the seat and device checks and then by `legal(this.G, e.s, bodyOf(e))` alone (§2.2's table: any seated human, until the battle is decided), never by the turn, `prev` or hash checks, and is played with `apply(this.G, e.s, bodyOf(e))`. A `desync {at, mine}` carries strings, so it never reaches `legal()`: it is the Folder's own kind, judged by seat and device alone.
- **`begin(e)`.** If `e.core !== CORE_VERSION || e.rules !== RULES_ID`, the status becomes `skew` (read-only). Otherwise `G = createMatch(e.setup, {out, onTrace})` ((R7b) with the Session's `onTrace`, handed to the Folder: the page's, which takes the unit card's facts at each `act` line and feeds `?debug`'s trace, app/flow.js; a quiet refold passes its own), the deploy decision is opened by `start.id`, and the status becomes `live` (or `over` for an all-AI match).
- **`sync(entries)`.**
  - If the entries already pushed are a prefix of `entries`, it pushes the tail and events flow.
  - Otherwise (a concurrent insert landed *before* entries already applied, as the research measured), it refolds quietly. If the old accepted list is a prefix of the new one, nothing shown is undone: it refolds quietly up to the old count, then pushes the rest with events. Otherwise it returns `reset: true`, the view snaps, and a "History changed: N moves undone" toast appears. This happens only with two devices on one seat, or with tampering.
- **Why `prev` is required.** Automerge orders concurrent list inserts arbitrarily but identically on every peer, and the higher actor id goes first. It can insert *before* entries a peer has already applied. With `prev`, every peer accepts and rejects the same entries, whatever their arrival order. The prototype showed both an out-of-turn append and a same-seat fork.
- **Why per-seat heads are sound during `deploy` and `roundLimit`.** Their commands commute: zones are at least 24" apart, and votes are per seat. (R8, for approval: it was "the entry that closed it") When the decision closes, the global head is a digest of every seat's head in it (each seat's last accepted entry in the decision, else the head that opened it; in seat order, cyrb53 in base 36, so it fits an envelope's 64-character `p`), not the closing entry alone. The seat that closes it extends only its own branch, so a second device on another seat whose branch lost (a same-seat fork: two tabs placing a unit apart) would otherwise write on after the close with the losing placements in its `h`, which every peer holding the winner finds a desync of the whole match; with the digest that entry is stale, and the losing tab's peer resets. A decision opened by the entry that closed the last (F4's vote) opens with that digest as its head.
- **The fold depends only on the entry list.** Never on wall time, arrival order, who is online, or local settings.
- **On a desync**, `freeze(e)` records `{at: e.id, theirs: e.h, mine}`. The session then appends an out-of-band `desync {at, mine}` (seated clients only) so the author's client freezes too: its own hash matched, so it would never notice otherwise. Spectators only show a banner. (R8's fixer, round 2, for approval) The author's client freezes on it even when its match is over by then: the entry found apart may be the one that ended the match there, or the desync may land after the end (a lower actor's insert sorts after the author's entries). And a seat's command that names the head an over match ended at, with a hash that isn't that match's, freezes it as a hash mismatch: the author's match went on where this one ended (the Folder's (R8) note).

**Stores and session.**

```js
// match/store.js
/** MatchStore: { entries(): Entry[] (decoded, list order), append(entry): void, subscribe(fn): () => void, kind: 'local'|'automerge' } */
// (R8's fixer, round 2) append(entry | text): the Session hands over the text it has checked decode takes, kept as it is;
// entries(): the same object for the same entry, cached per list element or text, never per index alone (an insert shifts indices)
export class LocalStore { constructor(entries = []) }    // vs AI, hotseat, watch, sim; export → a replay JSON of about 6 kB
// match/session.js
export class Session {
  constructor({ store, localSeats, dev, sink })           // sink: { events(evts), reset(G, info), status(s, info) }
                                                          // (R8b) + settled(session), dropped(seat, body, why, session): the single flight
  get G(); get status()
  decisionFor()                                           // first seat in pendingSeats(G) ∩ localSeats, else -1
  preview(fn)                                             // fn(G, q) under rng.lock (overlays, odds, hud)
  submit(seat, body) {                                    // throws unless seat ∈ localSeats ∩ pendingSeats
    const P = this.G.pending
    this.store.append(envelope(body, { s: seat, d: this.dev, p: this.folder.head(seat), id: this.nextId(),
                                       h: SIMULTANEOUS.has(P.k) ? undefined : stateHash(this.G) }))
  }                                                       // store change → onChange (synchronous for both store kinds)
  onChange() { const { events, reset } = this.folder.sync(this.store.entries())
               reset ? this.sink.reset(this.G) : this.sink.events(events); this.sink.status(this.folder.status) }
}
```

Every mode goes through this. From R8, single-player and hotseat exercise the same validator that guards online play.

(R6b) Built without envelopes or the Folder, which R8 puts between the store and the core. `match/store.js` `LocalStore(entries = [])`: `kind`, `entries()`, `append(entry)` (its subscribers hear it synchronously, before `append` returns), `subscribe(fn)` → unsubscribe, and `export()` (the log as JSON, a replay). An entry is plain data: the first `{s: -1, t: 'start', setup}` (the whole setup, createMatch's), then each command `{s, …body}`, the seat beside the body. `match/session.js` `Session({store, localSeats, sink, onTrace})` folds the store at construction and on every append: the start is `createMatch(setup, {out: [], onTrace})` (a setup the core refuses leaves the status `'refused'`, with `error`), and each later entry is split into its seat and body and judged as the Folder will (out of band for a concession, else the seat held to `pendingSeats`, then `legal()`), then `apply`, or recorded in `rejected` (`{at, why}`) and skipped. After each entry it drains `G.out` into `sink.events(events, session)`, so the match keeps no event between entries. `status` is `'lobby'` (no start yet), `'live'`, `'over'` or `'refused'`; `decisionFor()`, `preview(fn)` (`core.preview`) and `legal(seat, body)` (a local seat, waited on unless conceding, then `legal()`) are as sketched; `submit(seat, body)` throws unless `legal` passes, then appends `{s: seat, …body}`. No `dev`, `head` or `h` until R8. main.js builds a `LocalStore` and a Session per battle (`start(mode)`), `localSeats` the mode's human seats; the battle log's lines come from the events it presents (no Session folds quietly yet: a catch-up, a scrub or a snap must keep the log, §2.6's (R6a) note, at the step that adds one).

(R8) Built as sketched, the Folder between the store and the core in every mode; what the sketch left open, as built (the R8 notes):
- **The envelope** (`match/envelope.js`). `decode(text)` takes the stored text and refuses it unless it is the canonical JSON `encode` would write (sorted keys: equal entries are equal text), at most 1 kB of UTF-8, with `id` and `d` names (at most 64 characters), `p` and `h` names where present, a whole seat from −1; then either a command kind (core's `KINDS`) for a seat from 0, every field beside the envelope's and `t` a safe whole number or a boolean (§4.1 rule 12; a stray field of that type passes, for `legal()` to refuse), or one of the Folder's kinds with exactly its fields: `open {commit}` and `start {core, rules, setup, a?}` for seat −1, `desync {at, mine}` for a seat. A refused text comes back `{bad, id}` (the id when it names one), an accepted one deep-frozen, no key added; `decode` never throws, whatever string it is handed (a number past the double range, `1e999`, parses to `Infinity`, which has no canonical text: refused as `not canonical JSON`, R8's fixer), so one peer's junk is refused alike everywhere instead of crashing every peer's fold. `newEntryId(dev, n, rand)` is `` `${dev}.${n in base 36}.${rand}` ``, `n` the log's length as written and `rand` the caller's (match/ draws nothing); `bodyOf` builds own properties, so a field named `__proto__` stays a field for `legal()` to refuse.
- **The Folder** (`match/fold.js`). `push()` checks in the sketch's order, the cap first (the list's 5,001st entry freezes a lobby or live match `'full'`). A rejection is `{id, why}`, the `why` led by the check that refused it: `envelope`, `turn`, `device`, `stale`, `illegal` (then `legal()`'s why), `seat` (out of band from a seat no human plays), `start`, `skew`, or `inert` (before a start, after the end, after a freeze: recorded, so every peer lists the same rejections). A hash mismatch is neither accepted nor rejected: the match freezes there. (R8's fixer, round 2, for approval) After the end, two entries still freeze the match, since each says a peer's match went apart from it: a seat's `desync` (the entry found apart may be the one that ended it here, or the desync may land after the end), and a seat's hashed command (not a concession) from its own device on the very head the match ended at whose `h` isn't the over match's (a hash freeze: its author's match went on where this one ended; an honest author's ends there too and writes nothing more, and a stale or forked entry never names that head). Still not caught, for N2: a drift inside the final entry's application that leaves every match over (only pre-states are hashed), and a peer whose match went on waiting on a seat whose match is over (it stalls); N2's closing check, each seated device appending its post-state `stateHash` out of band at `over` for every Folder, live or over, to compare. The Folder reads `h` only where it checks one, and neither `p` nor `h` out of band: §0.2 #3's and #6's "never present" are the writers' rule (the Session's, which P-merge holds every accepted entry to, by the kind of decision it answered), not a refusal (for approval). An online log's `open` is accepted (the head a start then carries as `p`); a start from another device than the opener's is inert ((R8's fixer, round 3) with `error` saying so, which the Session's lobby reports); a second start is refused (`turn`). `begin` refuses a start whose setup the core refuses or whose human seat names no `dev`, or (R8's fixer, round 3) a `dev` no entry can carry as its `d` (envelope.js's `isName`: at most 64 characters; no peer would decode that seat's entries, so the match would wait on it for ever) (`error` says why; the log stays in its lobby for a good start): the Session's R6b status `'refused'` is gone. A start under another `CORE_VERSION` or `RULES_ID` is rejected (`skew`) and the status is `'skew'`, with no match. A simultaneous decision stays the same one while the turn's clock (stage, step, round, t, ph, overtime) stands still, so F4's vote that closes one round limit and opens the next in one entry starts fresh heads. When one closes, the head is the digest of every seat's head in it (the bullet on per-seat heads above; R8's fixer), which also opens the next one. `SIMULTANEOUS` is a frozen array (`.includes`), not the sketch's Set. A seat's `desync {at, mine}` is accepted and freezes with `{at, theirs: mine, mine: the h of entry at, by: its id}`; a hash freeze records `{at, theirs: e.h, mine: stateHash(G), by: 'hash'}`. The report adds `status`, `core`, `rules`, `setup`, every entry pushed, `accepted`, `rejected`, the last 50 trace lines and `state` (`shadowState`); the entries are decoded, so a refused text's own text is the store's (§2.7's "raw entries": N2's dialog adds the store's texts, `LocalStore.export()` or the Automerge strings). `sync(entries, each)` hands each accepted entry's events to `each(events, e)` as it goes (the Session's sink still gets one batch per entry, R6b's P-prop rule) and returns `{events, reset, undone}`; it tells a prefix by identity, then by content. A refold becomes this Folder the moment it is shown again (before the first event it hands on, or at a reset), so whoever is handed an entry's events reads the match they lead to: the Session's `G`, `preview`, `accepted` and the Folder's `head` (R8's fixer: the page's sink takes `session.G` and `preview` there). An accepted id gone from the list is `'tamper'`, and the freeze holds for the Folder's life, whatever later lists hold (N3 keeps the accepted ids across reloads); (R8's fixer, round 2) so is an accepted id whose first good entry in the list is no longer the one accepted (another body under it, in its place or inserted before it), which a check by ids alone refolded silently into another match, the view never told; (R8's fixer, round 3) and so are the accepted entries out of the order they were folded in (each id's first good entry by its place in the list): a copy of an accepted entry's very text inserted before the head it was written after is stale there and makes the entry itself a second copy, undoing it and everything after it as deleting it would, but quietly (a reset, not a freeze). An insert never moves an element already in the list, and an honest copy is written by a peer holding the original, so it lands after it: neither check fires in honest play. (R8's fixer, round 3) `sync` is not reentrant: it throws when `each` asks for another fold (the rest of the list would be pushed twice, this peer's `rejected` and `pushed` apart from every other's, its cap reached early), and frees itself when `each` throws; the Session never trips it (below).
- **A reset is also two seats' simultaneous entries in another order.** The sketch's "this happens only with two devices on one seat, or with tampering" doesn't hold: two seats deploying at once can be folded interleaved one way, then the other once a concurrent insert lands, and the old accepted list is no prefix of the new one. The strict rule is kept (the view snaps, to the table it shows already: the placements commute), and the sink's `reset(G, session, {undone})` says how many entries shown the new match no longer accepts at all: 0 for such a reordering (N2's "History changed: N moves undone" toast only for more), a same-seat fork's losers otherwise. (R8's fixer, round 2) With one device per seat a reset undoes nothing but entries an out-of-band concession or desync made inert by sorting before them (a concession racing a move: N2's toast then counts the move the concession cut off); P-merge holds a plain scenario's resets to undoing nothing.
- **`stateHash`** (`core/hash.js`) is `cyrb53(shadowState(G))` in base 36, `shadowState(G)` the lines `turn` (stage, step, round, t, first, active, ph, vp, wiped, overtime), `pending` (canonical JSON), `units` (each id, `pos.x`, `pos.z`, r, alive, lost, mesmerized, its flags in sorted keys, an undefined one skipped, each model's w/alive/ox/oz), `chunks` (id, alive, hp, `shape.y`) and `rng` (`rngState` and the word `a`); numbers by `String(n)`, so an indestructible chunk's hp prints `Infinity`, which canonical JSON can't carry, and `-0` as `-0` (`String(-0)` is `0`, and the rules tell them apart: `atan2(0, -0)` is π; R8's fixer). `G.out`, `onTrace`, `strict`, the nav, the journal and the setup stay out (§0.2 #12); `sim/data-check.mjs` holds each listed field to moving it (each of the turn's, the decision's kind and seats, a unit's and a model's, a chunk's, the dice's; and a slot at `-0` apart from `+0`) and the I/O fields, a trace line and the nav to not. Not the board's geometry beyond each chunk's height: a chunk's `x`, `z`, yaw and extents, built with `sin`/`cos`/`atan2`, are fixed at the start and hashed only through what they move (N0's note, R8 as built).
- **The stores and the Session.** `LocalStore` keeps each entry as its text (`encode`d, or a text given as it is: a replay, junk) and hands out what `decode` makes of it, once per place (safe only because it never inserts: a store that does caches per list element or per text, never per index, §2.7's (R8) bullets); `export()` is the texts as JSON (13 kB for a 110-entry hotseat log: the envelopes' weight). `Session({store, localSeats, dev = 'local', rand = () => '0', sink, onTrace, strict})` folds through a `Folder({out: [], onTrace, strict})`: `start(setup)` appends `{t: 'start', core, rules, setup}` from this device (the caller names the device on each seat played here: app/flow.js's `DEVICE`, `'local'`); `legal()` also asks that the seat is played from this device; `submit()` writes `p: head(seat)`, and `h` exactly where one seat is waited on; an entry it writes is appended as its text only if `decode` takes it (at most 1 kB, names of at most 64 characters, numbers JSON can write): `submit()` throws why, and a start no peer could decode is never appended, the log left in its lobby with `session.error` saying why, as for a start the Folder refuses (R8's fixer); `status`, `error`, `report`, `accepted` and `rejected` are the Folder's; `sink.events(events, session)` is handed each entry's events with the session already the match they lead to (above); `sink.reset(G, session, {undone})` only with a match (a refold that leaves none, its start made inert, is told by `sink.status`) and `sink.status(status, session)` are called as named; a desync this device found itself is appended once, out of band, from the first seat played here (a spectator only shows it). (R8's fixer, round 3) The Session's fold is not reentrant either: a change made while one is being folded (a sink's `submit` from the events it is handed, an autopilot's) is appended at once and folded once the change in hand is done, in another pass, so every entry is pushed once, in list order, as on every peer. Such a command is written on the match as it stands after the entry whose events the sink was handed, so it is stale when a later entry of the same change (a sync message, a reload, a refold) moved its seat's head; refused, it hands on no events, so a sink that answers decisions answers every batch it is handed (the last of a change is on the head the change ends at, and stands); and a second submit in one call, on the same head, is stale too (one command a call). The flag drops even when a sink throws; `sink.status` is called once a change, after its passes, and the desync is said after the flag drops (its append a change of its own). (R8b, superseding this sentence: the status is told, and a desync this device found is said, inside the single flight, one thing at a time with the passes, the queue and `settled`; a sink that throws no longer ends the loop: its first error is kept and thrown once every queued body has been written or dropped and `settled` told, R8b's review.) `start(setup, {a})` carries N2's seed reveal when one is given; `session.error` says nothing once a start has begun the match (why this device's own start was never written is cleared then), and in a lobby it says why a start was refused, an online log's start from a device other than its opener's included. The flow's sink takes `reset` as a snap; `status` is N2's (the desync dialog, the read-only screen). (R8b, superseding round 3's sentences on a sink's submit: §2.6's (R8b) note) A submit from a sink's callback is queued, never appended there and then.

(R8b) What the large battles need of these seams (the large-battle design's "R8 must allow" list), as built (the R8b notes):
- **The single flight.** The Session folds a change whole before it writes anything. A `submit` (or a `start`) made while a change is being folded, from any sink callback (`events`, `reset`, `status`, `settled`, `dropped`) or the match's `onTrace`, is queued as its body and never appended there and then; `submit` still throws on a body `legal()` refuses as it is called. Once the change is folded (its status told, a desync this device found said), the queue drains one body at a time: each is held to the Session's `legal()` again on the match as it then stands and either dropped, `sink.dropped(seat, body, why, session)` saying why, or written, its envelope (the id, the seat's head as `p`, the match's hash as `h`) built then, from that match, and folded before the next is looked at. So a queued command is never stale for what its own change still held, a second one from the same callback is written on the head the first left, and every entry is pushed once, in list order. A change that reaches the store meanwhile is folded first, in another pass. `Folder.sync` still throws when entered again, and so does `Folder.push` (from the match's `onTrace`, or from the events `sync` hands on: an entry would land in the middle of a fold every other peer makes whole).
- **`sink.settled(session)`**, approved by the lead: called once a change is folded and nothing else is to be (no entry left to fold, nothing queued), so changes that arrive or are queued while one is folded settle with it; the match there is the one the store's whole list leads to. It is the place to answer a decision (F10's autopilot, an auto-End): a submit there is queued, written and folded, a change of its own, which settles again. A sink answering from `events` instead may have a command written that a later entry of the same change made needless but not illegal (a second End: `legal()` is all a queued body is held to), so decisions are answered in `settled`.
- **The per-entry cost.** Per entry the Folder does its checks, `stateHash` where one seat is waited on, `legal()` and `apply()`, and O(1) besides; per change, one pass of identity compares over the entries pushed (the prefix check). Nothing per entry decodes, copies or stringifies the list: a store tells its `length`, `LocalStore.entries()` hands out its own array (decoded once per text, read-only, never copied), the Session numbers its ids from a counter of its own (from the log's length as it is made, so past every number this device wrote before), and `sync` reads the list as it stood when it began. The refold stays behind one seam, `Folder.refoldFrom()` (a fresh Folder from the list's start today; S6's checkpoints start it from a copy later). `sim/fold-cost.mjs` holds a 5,000-entry log's fold to linear. (F12) Beside `accepted` the Folder keeps each accepted entry's place in `pushed` and the dice counter `G.rng.n` after it (`placed`, `dice`: a number each, pushed in `accept()`, carried by a refold's show() with the rest of the Folder; derived, never hashed, never in the log), which the page's local undo reads (F12's notes, §4).
- **Out of band.** `concede` and `desync` only (`match/fold.js`'s `OUT_OF_BAND`; data-check asserts it, and that `concede` is the one kind of core's answering no decision).
- **Not changed, as the list asks.** The `h` rule and the per-seat heads stay keyed on the pending decision's kind; events per entry stay uncapped; a sink may read `session.G` and `preview`. The setup's key whitelist (the list's item 8) is deferred to F8a or F11, when the mission's and the army's keys land.

| Mode | Seats 0 / 1 | Store | `localSeats` | AI runs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| vs AI | human / ai (or ai / human) | Local | `[0]` or `[1]` | in-fold, here |
| Hotseat | human / human | Local | `[0, 1]` | – |
| Watch | ai / ai | Local | `[]` | in-fold |
| Online | human / human | Automerge | `[mine]` | – |
| Online vs AI, or spectating | human / ai | Automerge | `[0]` or `[]` | in-fold on every peer |

### 2.7 Automerge document and network layer

**Document.** It holds commands, never state.

```js
{
  app: 'tails-and-scales', schema: 1,
  lobby: {                                    // mutable, last-writer-wins; the fold ignores it once `start` exists
    host: 'k3f9',                             // creator device
    board: 1234, terrain: 'classic', rounds: 5, overtime: 'vote',      // creator edits until start
    fog: false,                               // (F16) the courtesy fog of war: the creator's, a change un-readying both seats; never in the start
    seats: { s0: { ctrl: 'human', dev: 'k3f9', name: 'Ann', race: 'squirrel', ready: true, nonce: '' },
             s1: { ctrl: 'human', dev: 'p2x1', name: 'Ben', race: 'serpent', ready: true, nonce: '9f…' } },
    next: null,                               // rematch documentId
  },
  log: [ ImmutableString(json(entry)), … ],   // append-only by convention; one A.change per entry
}
// log[0]  { id, s:-1, d:host, t:'open', commit: hex(sha256(a)) }       a = 16 random bytes kept in the host's localStorage per doc
// start   { id, s:-1, d:host, p:openId, t:'start', core, rules, a,
//           setup:{ board, dice, terrain, rounds, overtime, diceMode:'shared', seats:[{race, ctrl, dev, name, nonce}…] } }
```

- (F16) **`fog`** is the courtesy fog of war (§5): the host's switch beside the battle, shown to the guest before its Ready, a change un-readying both seats (so both Readys agree to it); the start never carries it and the fold never reads it: each page reads it from the lobby as its battle begins and hides in its own view what its one seat can't see (F16's notes).
- **Seat claims** use map keys `s0`/`s1`. Concurrent claims resolve last-writer-wins, and the loser sees the conflict through `getConflicts` ("seat taken").
- **The dice seed** is `dice = u32be(sha256(a ‖ ':' ‖ documentId ‖ ':' ‖ nonce0 ‖ ':' ‖ nonce1))`, where an AI or creator seat contributes `''`.
- **`net/seed.verifyStart(doc)`** runs once, asynchronously, outside the fold. It checks that `sha256(start.a) === open.commit`, that `setup.dice` re-derives, and that this client's own nonce appears in its seat. On failure the match is read-only, with the message "seed check failed". (N2, as built: this client's whole seat against every lobby record it readied, the N2 notes.)
- **Local matches** have no `open` and no `a`. Their log is `[start, …]`, with `dice` from `?dice=` or `Math.random` at the app level.

**Lobby flow (`net/lobby.js`, `ui/screens/lobby.js`).**

1. Title → Play online → pick a race in the diorama and a battlefield.
2. `repo.create(lobbyDoc)`, append `open`, and the URL becomes `…/tails-and-scales/#m=<documentId>`.
3. The page shows Copy link and Open second tab. The second tab syncs over BroadcastChannel, which helps testing.
4. The joiner opens the link and claims the free seat with its device id, name, race and a fresh nonce.
5. Both press Ready. The host's client appends `start` (setup frozen, `a` revealed). If the host is offline, the lobby says "waiting for host".
6. Anyone who arrives once the seats are full is a spectator.
7. Rematch creates a new doc with the same seats and races, and sets `lobby.next`.

**Identity and URLs.**

- A device id lives in `localStorage['ts.dev']`: 8 random base36 characters.
- `#m=<id>&dev=<dev>` is a "continue on another device" link for the same seat.
- `#m=<id>&sync=<wss url>` carries a non-default sync server.
- The fragment never reaches GitHub Pages, so no routing is needed.

**Lazy loading.** This is the research's verified recipe. It needs no Vite plugin and no change to the shared config.

```js
// net/repo.js: reached only from "Play online" or a #m= URL via import('../net/repo.js'); prefetched when the Online panel opens
const [{ Repo, initializeWasm }, { default: wasmUrl }, { WebSocketClientAdapter }, { BroadcastChannelNetworkAdapter },
       { IndexedDBStorageAdapter }] = await Promise.all([
  import('@automerge/automerge-repo/slim'), import('@automerge/automerge/automerge.wasm?url'),
  import('@automerge/automerge-repo-network-websocket'), import('@automerge/automerge-repo-network-broadcastchannel'),
  import('@automerge/automerge-repo-storage-indexeddb')])
await initializeWasm(wasmUrl)
export const repo = new Repo({ storage: new IndexedDBStorageAdapter('tails-and-scales'),
  network: [new BroadcastChannelNetworkAdapter(), new WebSocketClientAdapter(syncParam() ?? 'wss://sync.automerge.org')] })
```

- **Cost:** about 68 kB gz of JS plus a 3.64 MB `.wasm` file (1.14 MB gz), fetched on demand. GitHub Pages serves it as `application/wasm` with gzip. The single-player entry stays at 169 kB gz and holds no Automerge code and no modulepreload of it; N2 checks this with a grep of the entry chunk.
- **Pin exactly**, with `--save-exact`: `@automerge/automerge@3.5.0` and every `@automerge/automerge-repo*@2.5.6`. npm's `latest` tag for automerge-repo points at `2.6.0-alpha.3`. `…-network-messagechannel@2.5.6` is a devDependency for the tests.
- **`ImmutableString`** is imported from `@automerge/automerge/slim`, the same module instance the repo initialises. Verify this in N1.
- **Repo cost:** `dist/` is committed, so the wasm enters git once per Automerge version.

**`net/automerge-store.js`.** `new AutomergeStore(handle)` implements `MatchStore`:
- `entries()` decodes `String(imm)` with a per-index cache;
- `append(e)` is `handle.change((d) => d.log.push(new ImmutableString(encode(e))))`;
- `subscribe` wires up `handle.on('change')`.

(R8's fixer, round 2: the MatchStore contract R8 built, §2.6, replaces the first two bullets)
- `append(x)` is `handle.change((d) => d.log.push(new ImmutableString(typeof x === 'string' ? x : encode(x))))`. The Session hands it the canonical text it has checked `decode` takes; encoding that again would write a JSON-quoted string, which every peer's `decode` refuses as "not an object", so the start and every command would be junk online.
- `entries()` returns `decode` of the list as it stands now, cached by the element's text (a Map from text to decoded entry: `decode` depends only on the text, and every text carries a unique id) or by list element, **never by index alone**. Automerge inserts before entries a peer has folded (merge-sim: about 6,000 such inserts a run), which shifts every later index; an index-only cache then hands back the old entries at shifted places, the Folder takes the list for a prefix (it tells a prefix by identity first) and never folds the inserted entry, and the peers split. Prefer the text key: Automerge may not keep the same `ImmutableString` object for an element from one version of the doc to the next, so a WeakMap keyed by it would miss every time. The cache is an optimisation only: `same()` falls back to the id and content, so fresh objects are correct, only slower (merge-sim's self-test fails a store that caches by index).

- (R8b) `length` is the log's length, read without decoding anything (the Session numbers its ids from a counter, never from `entries()`); `entries()` may hand out a fresh array or its own (read-only, never kept by the Folder past a sync), and returns the same decoded object for an element that hasn't changed, as `LocalStore` does, so the Folder's prefix check stays an identity compare and never falls back to JSON (`sim/fold-cost.mjs` counts what a fold decodes, stringifies and copies, run against LocalStore; N1 runs it against this store).

It never initialises the wasm, so `sim/peers.mjs` imports it under Node's `node` export condition and hands it handles.

**Transport.**

- `wss://sync.automerge.org` stores and forwards, so asynchronous play and late joins work. Its terms: "as-is", for prototyping, no privacy (the URL is the capability). See open question 2.
- BroadcastChannel covers tabs in the same browser.
- `?sync=ws://127.0.0.1:3030` points at a self-hosted `@automerge/automerge-repo-sync-server` (0.3.0). That is the escape hatch, and also the browser test rig. ((N2) As built, the rig's server is `sim/sync-server.mjs`, the same thing from the pinned packages; the N2 notes.)
- IndexedDB keeps the doc locally, so reload and rejoin work offline.

**Presence (`net/presence.js`).** `handle.broadcast` sends `{dev, seat|-1, name, head, hash, sel?, tg?}` on change and every 5 s, and is never persisted.

- **Net badge:** "online · 2 watching", "reconnecting", or "offline · your moves will sync".
- **Opponent ghost:** the opponent's selected unit gets a dashed ring in their colour, with a line to their chosen target.
- **Hash cross-check:** spectators compare `{head, hash}`. That is the only cross-check in an all-AI match, where no `h` ever flows.

**Joining, rejoining, spectating.**

- **Load:** from IndexedDB, or `await repo.find(url)`. An unknown doc rejects with "unavailable", shown as "Match not found; is the host online?".
- **Then:** `verifyStart`, a quiet fold (0.25-0.28 s of logic for a whole AI-heavy battle), and `snap`. Join time is dominated by baking figures, which the template cache addresses.
- **Spectators:**
  - get the broadside camera and their own speed control;
  - can scrub history by refolding `start + accepted[0..k]`, with "watch from the start" as a replay;
  - get a JSON replay export from the log.

**AI in online games.** Every peer runs it, with no host required (§0.2 row 9).

**Validation and authority.** This is the Folder in §2.6. Rejected entries stay in the log, inert, and every peer rejects the same ones.

**Desync.** The match freezes on all seated clients, through the out-of-band `desync` entry. A dialog offers a downloadable report containing:
- setup;
- raw entries;
- accepted and rejected entries;
- the entry where it diverged, and both hashes;
- the last 50 trace lines;
- `shadowState`;
- user agent, `CORE_VERSION`, `RULES_ID` and the URL.

(R8's fixer, round 2) The Folder's `report` holds the entries decoded; the dialog adds the store's raw texts. A client whose match is over by then still freezes (§2.6's (R8) note). For N2, a closing check: each seated device appends its post-state `stateHash` out of band once its match is over, and every Folder, live or over, compares it, which catches what the pre-state `h` can't (a drift inside the final entry's application, and a live peer waiting on a seat whose match is over; online against the AI, the AI's whole final turn).

**Versioning.**

- **`CORE_VERSION`** is a manual integer, bumped whenever consensus behaviour changes. The parity suite forces the bump, because any such change breaks a baseline.
- **`RULES_ID`** is computed at module load: cyrb53 over canonical JSON of the rule-bearing data. That is every race field except `name`, `short`, `abilities`, `icon`, `look` and `fx`, left out at every level (so a unit's or a weapon's rename doesn't move it), plus the `PHASES` keys (their names are banner copy), the constants and, from R3, `SETS`, and (R4) from R6 the mission (`data/mission.js`, its row), so the objectives join the hash ((R6a) done: `rulesData({ missions })`, `1ugu9b3oztd`).
- **A mismatch with `start`** opens the match read-only: "This battle was made with a different version of the game". A deploy therefore orphans matches in progress (open question 4).

**Tamper detection.** Accepted ids are cached per doc in IndexedDB. If a previously accepted id vanishes from the list, the status becomes `tamper` and the match freezes with a report. An entry that becomes rejected after a concurrent insert is legitimate and is not tamper.

**Dice fairness: v1 is "friendly".**

- The seed is public but jointly derived, so nobody can grind it.
- Anyone with devtools can predict hypothetical rolls. The active player could fork `G` and search action orders, and the advance roll is visible before its move by the rules.
- `setup.diceMode: 'fair'` is reserved. It means per-command hash-chain reveals from both players, about 70-90 round trips a battle, both players online, and its own baselines. It may only reseed `G.rng` at a command boundary.
- This is open question 1.

### 2.8 Race, unit, weapon and ability data

**Abilities are flags on the data.** Each flag is read by exactly one rules module. Card text is never read by rules.

- Stat lines stay flat, so `u.t.M` still works.
- `name`, `short` and weapon `name` are copied verbatim, because they appear in traced log lines.
- `look`, `icon`, `abilities` and `fx` are presentation.

```js
// data/schema.js
defineRace({ key, name, short, icon, look: { team, dark, alt, gore: [a, b], voice, models, anim }, army: [unitKey…], units: { [key]: UnitDef } })
UnitDef = { name, short, role: 'Troops'|'Elite'|'Fast'|'Hero'|'Monster'|'Artillery', models, base, pts, ai: 'melee'|'raider'|'line'|'shooter'|'hero'|'artillery',
            stats: 'M7 WS4 BS4 S3 T3 W1 A1 Ld6 Sv6 OC2', ranged: Weapon|null, melee: Weapon, abilities: [text…],
            fly?, wrecker?, big?, hero?, chargeAfterAdvance?, noCharge?, brawler?, burrow?, swarm?: {min}, swoop?: {chargeS} }
Weapon  = { name, range?, shots?, S, AP, D, assault?, heavy?, indirect?, blast?, scenery?, poison?, corrodes?, spell?, mesmerize?, fx }
// derived (each overridable): M…OC from stats · move = fly ? 'fly' : wrecker ? 'wreck' : burrow ? 'burrow' : 'walk'
//   brawler = !ranged || wrecker  (reproduces ai.js 204: oakguard and sidewinder have ranged:null)
//   noCharge = role === 'Artillery' (924) · hero from role 'Hero' · deployRow = Artillery ? back : hero ? mid : front (388-391)
//   eye = big ? 1.9 : fly ? 1.5 : 0.95 · chest = big ? 1.0 : fly ? 1.0 : 0.55 (410-411)
```

| Flag | Read only by |
|---|---|
| `fly` | `moveMode`, `inCover`, derived eye/chest |
| `wrecker` | `moveMode`, `resolveWalk` smashing, derived `brawler`; (F19a) the AI's keg terms (`kegDanger`, `kegWalk`) |
| `big` | `blastLands` (`ceil(d6/2)+1` hits, 799), eye/chest |
| `hero` | `leadership` aura, `deployRow` |
| `chargeAfterAdvance` | `canCharge` (was `startsWith('Sidewind')`, 925); the Advance button text (was 1725) |
| `noCharge` | `canCharge` |
| `assault` | `canShoot`, AI advance choice |
| `heavy`, `indirect` | `shotInfo`, AI `shotValue` |
| `blast`, `scenery` | `blastVolley`, `blastLands`; (F19a) the AI's keg terms (`kegDanger`; `kegGain`, through `Terrain.blastDamage`) |
| `poison` | `woundNeed` (and so `expected`, the AI and the odds, all through the same function) |
| `corrodes` | `blastLands` → `terrain.blast({acid})` (was `w.fx === 'acid'`, 814); (F19a) `kegGain`, the same `acid` |
| `spell`, `mesmerize` | `doShoot`'s branch |
| `burrow`, `swarm`, `swoop` (F5) | `moveMode`/nav, `fight` wound re-roll, `fight` strength bonus on the charge turn |

```js
// data/races/squirrel.js: plain data; data/schema.js runs defineRace over each race file as it builds RACES
```

`sim/data-check.mjs` deep-equals the normalised types against legacy `TYPES` (minus `side`, plus the derived fields). It also checks that `RULES_ID` changes when a stat changes and does not change when a name changes.

(Large battles, §4.2.8 and §4.2.5) F11a gives every unit `cost` and every race `roster` and `armies`. F9 adds the `Vehicle` role, the `transport` record, the `vehicle` and `climb` flags, and (F9b) `footprint`.

(F19a) **Hazards** (`data/hazards.js`): consensus data beside the races and the missions, a map keyed by name, each record a hazard's hit points and the profile of what it does when it breaks, in a template's numbers as `blastLands` reads them: `keg: { name: 'Powder keg', hp: 2, S: 5, AP: 1, D: 2, blast: 3, scenery: 4, fx: 'keg' }`. `name` is the battle log's ("Powder keg hits Nutkin: …") and `fx` the view's, so `RULES_ID` hashes each record less those two (`rulesData`'s `hazards`, stripped as a unit's presentation is); `checkHazard` refuses a broken record as the module loads (hit points and S, D and scenery whole numbers above 0, AP 0 or more, a blast radius above 0, no other field). `core/terrain/recipes.js` reads `hp`; `core/actions/shoot.js` the profile; the AI's keg terms the profile and `blast`.

### 2.9 Terrain: recipes, sets, meshes

```js
ChunkDef = { id, kind: 'block'|'tree'|'hedge'|'rock'|'crate'|'mushroom'|'floor'|'rubble'|'log' (+ 'deck'|'stair' F7, 'keg' F19a),
             hp, maxHp, destructible, alive, navKind: 'hard'|'soft'|'diff'|null, los: 'block'|'obscure'|null, cover,
             shape: { x, y, z, hx, hy, hz, yaw, reach }, nav?, coverShape?, level?, trunkH?, trunkR?,
             col?: { blocks: [chunk…], x, z, yaw, style, by, rubble, w, t },   // a wall column, shared by its blocks
             surface?: { y, ramp?: { axis, y0, y1 } }, supports?: [id],          // F7
             look: { piece, chip?, leaves?, …what the layout stream decided for that piece } }
// look.piece: box | log (a wall block) · cap · tree (its trunk: { h, r }) · hedge · boulder · crate | barrel | sack · mushroom · floor
//             · rubble { style } · fallen { tree, dx, dz } (a toppled tree's log: the tree's own mesh, keeled over)
//             · keg { color, yaw } (F19a: a powder keg's barrel, its staves' colour; chip '#7a4c2a')
// look.chip: the debris colour (a block's colour; '#9a7048' for a crate) · look.leaves: what bursts from it
// core/terrain/sets.js: the selection table is data; recipes stay code
export const SETS = { classic: { centre: [['tower', 0.55], ['rockbox', 0.8]], kinds: [['ruin', 3.2, 4], ['wall', 3.6, 2], ['forest', 3.2, 3],
  ['hedgerow', 3.4, 2], ['rocks', 2.0, 2], ['barricade', 2.0, 2], ['mushrooms', 2.0, 1.5], ['obelisk', 1.6, 1]],
  pairs: [6, 3], attempts: 1200, mirror: 'point', margin: 0.5, selfGap: 1.4, deployMargin: 1, bigNotInDeploy: 2.1,
  notInDeploy: ['forest'], objectiveGap: 2.2, gap: 2.1 } }   // F7 adds `fortified`; `classic` is frozen; recipes.js checkSet runs on each at load
```

- **The trap.** `generate` draws visual values from the same `mulberry32(seed)` stream as the layout: colour picks and scale jitter (170-174), canopy blobs (206-235), berries, moss. `recipes.js` must make **every** `rng()` call in the same order and **record** the results in `look`. `view/terrain.js` then builds meshes with no randomness.
- **Purely cosmetic randomness stays in the view, on `Math.random`:** rubble pieces (648-659), shudder (577) and leaves. The rubble piece count `r.pieces` is visual only.
- **Destruction is already instant in logic.** `collapse` lowers `shape.y` (624), and `topple` adds the log chunk (691). They now emit events where today they create tweens.
- **Iteration semantics are preserved.** `smashAround` walks the **live** chunk array, so a fresh log can be smashed in the same sweep. `blast` walks a copy (548). Chunk ids are per match.
- **Adding a kind to `classic` would change every classic board's draws**, so new pieces only ever go into new sets, selected by `setup.terrain`.
- **(F19a) The powder keg** (`recipes.js` `powderKeg`, `CENTRES.keg`; `sets.js` `keg`). A chunk of kind `keg` an inch across and 1.2" tall (`hx`, `hz` 0.5, `hy` 0.6), with the hazard's 2 hit points (`data/hazards.js`), `soft` (walkers go round it, a wrecker through it), no sight or cover; its look `{ piece: 'keg', color, yaw }`. It is a centre piece: the `keg` set, classic's table (its features, counts and spacing rules) with `centre: [['keg', 1]]`, a threshold above every draw, stands it at exactly (0, 0) on every board, its yaw and then its staves' colour drawn from the layout stream, its footprint keeping the features `KEG_R` (1") off; it is its own point mirror. The terrain breaks a keg as a crate (it bursts, its staves for debris) and never sets it off: what broke is in a blast's list (`blast`'s) or a wrecker's walk's (`smashAround` now hands `hurt` the walk's list), and the rules read the kegs out of it (`kegsIn`) and set them off (`core/actions/shoot.js` `kegsGoOff`, §4.1 rule 28). `Terrain.blastDamage(c, x, y, z, r, dmg, acid)` is `blast`'s own arithmetic for one chunk (the damage, or null out of reach), which `blast` now calls and the AI asks (would a template landing there set a keg off?). No other set has a keg, so every classic, open and fortified board draws as it did (rule 11).
- **The same seed gives the same defs**, so the title, lobby and battle reuse one `TerrainView` with no rebuild flash. (R7a) As built: `TerrainView.sync(chunks)` draws the chunks as they stand, keeping each mesh whose def and standing match (a dropped block or cap only moved to its height, its fall cut), a fallen tree drawn keeled over from its log's def, a rubble pile with a fresh cosmetic spill; `clear()` keeps the meshes it takes off as spares, and an add finds its untouched spare of the same def (its height too) and puts it back instead of building it: so a battle's board, played on its own table's snap, rebuilds nothing. (R7a's fixer) A spare must hold a mesh (a broken chunk's item from a sync holds none, and its add builds it), and `sync` re-keys a block it sets lower to the def at that height (an add of the block where it first stood builds it rather than taking it back down there); `sim/terrain-check.mjs` plays a board's adds again on a table synced to its wrecked chunks, fresh and kept, against a fresh sync. `dispose()` frees all of it (a new table), and an item off the table frees what only it used (its geometry but the shared box and log shapes, a scuffed chunk's own material, a felled canopy). `sim/terrain-check.mjs` holds `sync` to the view built event by event, and a view kept and synced again, on every board.

### 2.10 Navigation and LOS, ready for elevation

`scenery.los` is already a 3D segment-versus-oriented-box test (522-540, 702-721). Elevation needs correct heights, not a new LOS model.

```js
nav.hasHeight                        // false on every classic board → every height branch is skipped (a separate path, not "+0")
nav.floor: Float32Array              // walkable height per cell
nav.cliff: Float32Array              // distance to the nearest neighbour step > STEP (0.3"); built only when hasHeight
nav.standable(i, r, mode, forbid)    // + cliff[i] ≥ r − 0.06: a base never straddles a ledge
nav.reach(sx, sz, { r, max, mode /* walk|wreck|fly|burrow */, forbid })   // + step allowed iff |Δfloor| ≤ STEP (stairs are ramps); cost += |Δfloor|
nav.path / walkable                  // + no string-pull across a level change
q.groundY(G, u, m)                   // floor under the model; 0 when !hasHeight
q.sight(G, a, b, from)               // eye.y = groundY(a) + t.eye; target.y = groundY(b, m) + t.chest
q.gap / engagement                   // + |Δy| ≤ 1.2" to count as engaged
inCover                              // a cover raster applies only at its chunk's base level (a parapet covers the deck, not the ditch)
```

`burrow` mode (F5) gets its own clearance field. It passes under soft and difficult scenery, and must end on a cell that is standable on foot. Commands stay a single cell index `c`, because a 2.5D heightfield has exactly one floor per cell. Bridges are a non-goal.

(Large battles) The F7 sketch in §2.9 and this section is superseded by §4.2.4: `STEP` 0.4", stairs rising 0.5" per inch and 4.5" wide, floors quantised to 1/64", ladders as nav links rather than ramps, parapets with `navKind` null, and `kind` gains `ladder`, `parapet` and `post`.

### 2.11 Camera presets and HUD model

```js
// present/camera-presets.js: pure, unit-tested
export const PRESETS = { title: { orbit: { centre: [-5, 0, 0], radius: 25, y: 13, speed: 0.035 } },          // 2044-2049
  broadside: { azimuth: 0, elevation: 0.77, fit: 'length' },                                              // seat 0 (west) left
  behind: (edge) => ({ azimuth: edge < 0 ? -Math.PI / 2 : Math.PI / 2, elevation: 0.9, fit: 'width' }) }
export const battleView = ({ localSeats, edges }) => localSeats.length === 1 ? PRESETS.behind(edges[localSeats[0]]) : PRESETS.broadside
```

- **The preset keys off the seats on this client**, never off a count of human players. Two online players each get their own `behind` view. Spectators, watch mode and hotseat get the broadside.
- **`CameraRig.fit(preset, aspect)`** solves the distance from fov and aspect, with HUD padding. Maximum distance is per preset: a portrait broadside needs about 86", above today's fixed 75 (line 56). This replaces `defaultView` (2065-2068).
- **Follow policy:** never during the local player's own decision (1173-1174, generalised). ((F14) An action played alone is cued too, a seat's command never followed for a seat played here: F14's notes in §4.)
- **The view-cycle button** switches between behind-me, broadside and top, local only and remembered in `localStorage`. Hotseat can opt in to "swing to the active side".
- **`hudModel({ G, mirror, session, input })`** is pure, and reads `G` only when idle. It returns:
  - `sides: [{name, who: 'You'|'AI'|name|'name · offline', active, vp}]`;
  - `round: 'Round r / R'`, or `'Round r · overtime'`;
  - `end: {show, label, busy: !idle, ready: mine && pending.k === 'phase' && !anyCanAct(G, seat)}`;
  - `advance`, `auto`, `shortest`, `hint`, `rings`, and `waiting: '<name> is choosing a charge spot…'`.
- **`ui/theme.js`** sets `--s0`/`--s1` and the glow colours from the seats' race `look`, using `alt` in a mirror match.
- **Frame budget** (experience-first). Cache each figure template per (race, unit, colour) and clone it: about 12 bakes instead of 52, against about 400 ms today. Dispose per-game geometry; today `clearUnits` (357-364) and `Scenery.clear` leak it. Use one renderer, with the diorama drawn into a scissor viewport. (R7a) As built: a template per (models kit, unit), since the miniature doesn't depend on the colour (only the base's rim does, and the base, whose flock falls at random, is made per figure); a builder that draws `Math.random` (the trebuchet's acorns) makes no template and is built afresh each time. A new table frees the last one's figures (their bases; a template's geometry is shared and kept) and meshes; `sim/rematch-memory.mjs` holds renderer.info and the heap flat over a battle and 5 rematches. (R7a's fixer, round 3) Freeing is weighed against linking: three.js drops a shader program once the last material using it is freed, and links it again (a stall on the frame that first draws it) when one draws again, so a material made per use and freed after it is shared instead when nothing else holds its program (a glowing projectile's: one per colour, kept, as the kit's are). `sim/rematch-memory.mjs` notes every program linked, and none may be linked twice between a title and a battle's end; the one a new table links again (the units' rings, whose materials it frees, are the only holders of theirs on a watched battle's table) is one link a table, next to a table's rebuild.
- (R7b) **The HUD model as built** (`present/hud-model.js`): `hudModel({ G, mirror, session, input, hud })`, `G` the match the table shows (the battle's, or the title's backdrop), `input` the `Human`'s `state()`, `hud` the HUD's own state (`phaseShown`, `buttonsUp`, the hint as shown, each seat's look; the flow keeps all of it, the hint too, (R7b's fixer) never read back from the page). It is R6b's `refreshUI` and `refreshRings` rule unchanged, returned as slices that `ui/hud.js` (the score, the round, the phase, the active seat, the hint), `ui/actions.js` (End, Auto, Advance, Shortest move: `{ show, label, busy }`, a null `show` or `label` leaving the button as it was, which is how they keep what they showed while the table plays) and the view (`zones`, `rings`: `ringLooks`, by unit view) put on the page, plus the next `buttonsUp`. (R7b's fixer, round 2) The slices as built: `vp` ([seat 0's, seat 1's], the mirror's), `round` (`'Deployment'` or `'Round r / R'`), `phase` and `active` (the mirror's, null and -1 outside the battle), `end`, `auto`, `advance`, `shortest`, `zones` (each seat's zone's opacity), `hint`, `rings` and `buttonsUp`. There is no `sides` slice: the score and the seat to play are `vp` and `active`, and each seat's name and look come in through `hud.sides` (`ui/theme.js`), which `ui/hud.js` reads; N2 adds `sides[].who` (or a slice like it) when it has something to show there. And "reads `G` only when idle" holds for what the model asks of the match (End's readiness, Advance, the hint's engaged test and the rings, through the preview), not for what says which decision the table is on: the decision pending (the input's `decision`), the turn's round, each seat's controller (the AI's turn hint) and `G.setup.rounds` are read while the table plays, as R6b's rule read them. `end.ready` is computed (`mine && idle && !anyCanAct(G, seat)`, asked through the Session's preview) and not shown: F3 lights End by it. (R7b's fixer) `sim/hud-check.mjs` holds it to the match (`?debug`'s `hud`, the model last put on the page) after each snap in a phase and at every frame the player is idle on a local seat's phase. Not built: `sides[].who`, `round`'s overtime and `waiting` (nothing shows them today: N2's and F4's). `afterSnap(M)` is the HUD's state a snap leaves: a phase shown once the snapped mirror's stage is `'battle'`, no buttons up until the player idles on a local seat's decision; `app/flow.js`'s `snapped(G)` (G the match snapped to, which the player passes its `onIdle`: `{ snap: true, G }`) applies it, (R7b's fixer, round 2) takes the local human's selection again from G (the unit picked up by id, its move's plan and what the pointer is over found afresh: N2's snaps onto a freshly folded match would otherwise leave them on the old match's unit objects), clears the overlay (a charge's shaded spots and its ghost: the input shades them again as it catches up, if a charge waits on its end), takes the card's record from G, and shows the end screen when the snapped mirror's stage is `'over'` (`resultOf(G)`: the result, score and rounds `game.over` would have carried). `sim/hud-check.mjs` snaps mid-battle (in the roll-off, in a seat's phase while the table still shows the other seat's turn, past `game.over`; (R7b's fixer, round 2) and in the deployment and at a charge's end, the player held a frame at the checkpoints there, since `?fast` plays a placement and a charge's roll through at once, and at a charge's end again once the spots are shaded) and holds End and Auto up for the seat's phase, Begin battle and the deploying seat's zone in the deployment, Shortest move and the charge's spots shaded orange at its end (End and Auto down), and the end screen up past the end, worded as the match's own `game.over` (taken from the player's queue before the snap drops it; until round 2 it was worded by `resultOf`'s own formula); and `sim/property.mjs` (its rule 10) holds `resultOf(G)` to the match's `game.over` at the end of every corpus battle, random game and out-of-band concession. The card's facts (`factOf`, `factsOf`, `turnBegun`, `cardStatus`): §2.4's (R7b) note.
- (R7a) **The presets as built** (`present/camera-presets.js`, `sim/camera-check.mjs`): `PRESETS.title` (the orbit, with its start angle), `landscape` and `portrait` (today's `defaultView`, chosen by aspect), `broadside` and `behind(edge)` (built with `max`, 86 and 75, chosen by nothing yet); `battleView({localSeats, edges, aspect})` returns today's view (landscape or portrait) until F1/F2 make the choice above; `fovFor(aspect)` (`fitFov`), `orbitPose`, `follows(…)` (the follow rule) and `fitPose(preset, aspect)` (the distance at which the board's corners fit with padding, at most `max`: `CameraRig.fit`, pure). (R7a's fixer, round 2) The `fit: 'length'|'width'` of the block above is not built (the presets carried it, read by nothing): `fitPose` fits the whole board, all four corners with 12% padding each way, whichever way it lies across the screen. On a narrow portrait phone both presets stop at their `max` with the board's ends past the screen's sides (the broadside below an aspect of about 0.55, `behind` below about 0.47): F1/F2's to tune, adding a fit across one of the board's sides, with a `sim/camera-check.mjs` case for it, if they want one. `CameraRig.fit(preset, aspect)` is `fitPose`, and `CameraRig.goTo(preset)` (R7a's fixer) fits the preset through it and tweens there as `defaultView` did; when the preset's `max` is beyond the dolly limit (`maxDistance` 75, which OrbitControls clamps to every frame) it raises the limit to it, and the title puts it back. So F1/F2 change only `battleView`, and `sim/camera-check.mjs`'s "battleView chooses by the screen's shape" checks (its header and lines 95-96), which pin today's choice, change with it in the same step (all it checks besides, today's landscape and portrait poses, the title's orbit, `fitPose` and `CameraRig.goTo`, must still hold); `start()` passes the match's edges by seat (`edgeOf`). The landscape test is `!(aspect < 1)`, today's `innerWidth >= innerHeight` (a 0×0 screen's NaN aspect is landscape, as before). The view-cycle button is F1/F2's.

**Additions from the large-battle design (§4.2), row by row.**

- **The Automerge multiplayer row** (headed "R0: Automerge multiplayer": N1-N3): N2's lobby seat record is `{ctrl, dev, name, race, ready, nonce}`, and from F11b `army`.
  - **Names and nonces** (the start's byte budget, §4.2.1). A display name is normalised (NFC, with control characters and lone surrogates removed, then trimmed). It is capped at 24 characters **and** at 48 bytes of canonical JSON, `utf8Length(canonicalJSON(name)) − 2 ≤ 48`. A nonce is exactly 16 hex characters.
  - **The whole seat.** `net/seed.verifyStart` checks this client's **whole seat** in the start, not only its nonce. Every field of the client's own lobby seat record except `ready` must equal the start's seat as written: `race`, `ctrl`, `dev`, `name`, `nonce`, and from F11b `army`. A field absent on one side must be absent on the other. A host that changed any of them, for instance flipping a guest's `ctrl` to `ai` or swapping its `dev` for the host's own, gets a read-only match with "The start changed your seat (ctrl)".
  - **Presence** keeps `sel` as the lead unit's id. F10a adds the selection under a new key, `sels` (up to 120 ids), and F10c adds the order badges as `ords`. A tab still on an older build ignores keys it doesn't know.
  - N1 runs `sim/fold-cost.mjs` against the AutomergeStore (R8b's per-entry rule).
- **F1, F2:** `fitPose(preset, aspect, rect)` and `battleView({…, board})` take the board as a rectangle `{cx, cz, w, h}`, never `BOARD` (`present/` may not import `data/`). Classic passes today's numbers, so camera-check's other rows hold. The view-cycle gains **Overview** (the whole board, also the Home key), which is a no-op on classic.
- **F3:** From F10c, `end.ready` counts **manual** units only. Units whose standing order covers the phase count as handled, and so do riders in the movement phase, since disembarking is optional.
- **F4:** `legal()`'s field schema gains `opt` (optional integers) and `bools` (booleans), §4.2.6; `vote {more}` is the first `bools` field and F9b's heading `f` the first `opt` field. The result screen stops offering Keep playing at ≥ 80% of `MAX_ENTRIES`, read from the Folder's entry count (R8b's `count`). This is a UI rule: a vote past it is still legal, and the cap still freezes the match.
- **F5:** Split in two (the designer's choice, open question 27).
  - **F5a, the races**, after F9c (moved there after F8a, the user's call; first planned right after F11a): the insectoids (burrow, swarm) and the bird-people (fly, swoop). Each race brings its builder data (§4.2.8): a `roster`, a `cost` per unit fitted by `army-sim --fit` at Skirmish against both existing races, and its classic `army`. It must pass army-sim's gates for every race pair. Its Field and Grand presets come with F8b, which writes them for every race.
  - F7a lands after F5a. It makes `burrow` treat a deck's footprint as hard (no tunnelling under fortifications), and its data-check lists any unit with r above `CLIMB_R` (1.22, §4.2.4) as a non-climber.
  - **F5b, their vehicles**, after F9c (§4.2.5). The insectoids' Brood Beetle runs on F9b's footprint engine and is data only. The bird-people's Sky-Basket is a flying hull that may land on deck tops (~40 lines of rules, open question 24). Each has its `cost` fitted, and both must pass army-sim's gates.
- **F6:** It stays right after N3, where this table has it. F6 introduces the **battle-setup panel** that a mode button opens: each seat's race in the picker, with defaults read from `?races=`. The panel gains a terrain line at F7a, a battle size at F8b and an army line at F11b. N2's lobby seat cards, built before F6, offer a plain race list until F6 gives them the picker.
  - **Harnesses.** The panel puts one click between a mode button and the battle. F6 therefore ports, in the same step, every Chromium harness that starts a battle from the title to press the panel's Start: `sim/chromium.mjs` (parity `--browser`, P-browser, and self-test's mutant-title row), play-check, snap-check, hud-check and rematch-memory. P-browser then re-runs over the whole corpus. There is no `?quick` path around the panel: the checks press what a player presses.
  - The diorama uses today's template cache (about 12 figures), not F8b's LOD bake. The title's first frame doesn't change.
