## 4. Migration plan

**Gates.** Every step leaves the game playable and must pass its gate. Each shipping step ends with `npm run build && npm run verify` and a commit of `dist/` (CLAUDE.md). Lockfile changes always go in their own commit.

| Gate | What it checks |
|---|---|
| **P-ai** | 12 existing plus ~12 widened AI baselines: trace **byte-identical**, the shadow snapshot at every state line identical (until N0 per engine, in Chromium against `webShadow` where the corpus recorded one, since the engines' sin/cos differ, §0.1; (N0) since then every engine against `shadow`), and every battle-log write identical (`written`, which includes the destroyed-unit lines the trace never shows) |
| **P-human** | the human command logs: trace, shadow and battle log (per engine, as P-ai) |
| **P-browser** | `node sim/parity.mjs --browser`: a fresh build of the code under test in Chromium (`sim/chromium.mjs`), every battle started from its title-screen button; the whole corpus, AI pairs and human logs, or `--only` a few; at milestones only |
| **P-terrain** | ChunkDefs for board seeds 1-500 against legacy `scenery.js`, which imports in Node with a no-op fx proxy |
| **P-present** | mirror equals `project(G)` at every `act` of every log; (R5a) and at every `check`, after each converted action's events (§2.4); (R6b) over the Session: a `check` where each `act`, `phase` and `over` line was written and as the match stops after each entry, from the `?debug` block's `onTrace` (§2.4) |
| **P-prop** | `legal`/previews ((R8) and `stateHash`) never move `rngState`; the AI never issues an illegal command; random legal play never throws; (R6a) two matches in one process never touch (§4.1 rule 13), and a quiet fold (`G.out` null) of every corpus battle plays the same battle as its presented one; (R6a's fixer) the engine's own events, folded into the mirror, equal `project(G)` at every `act`, every decision and the end, in every corpus battle and random game (P-present's rule, for the core's stream until R6b's Session); `legal()` refuses a body with a field its kind doesn't take, and a concession once a side is wiped out; (R6a's fixer round 2) a concession out of band (from the seat not waited on, in a hotseat match) is legal, applied, and folded by `sim/run.mjs` `foldJob`, which refolds every random game's log to the same trace; asking emits no event; `game.over` says the result and the rounds played; (R6a's fixer round 3) `createMatch` refuses each setup the rules can't play (`fullSetup`'s battery: seeds, rounds outside 1 to 99, F4's vote, other dice, seats, races, controllers) without crashing, and `G.pending` is null, never missing, through an all-AI battle; (R6b) every corpus battle played through a `Session` over a `LocalStore` (and a spectator Session on the same store) writes foldJob's trace, refuses nothing, hands the sink every event ((R6b's fixer, round 3) the very batches the same log folded straight through the core leaves in `G.out`, after the start and each entry) and leaves `G.out` empty, refuses a body the match refuses before appending it, and replays its log with junk entries slipped in, refusing exactly those; (R7b's fixer, round 2) the end screen after a snap past the end, `present/hud-model.js` `resultOf(G)`, says what the match's own `game.over` said at the end of every corpus battle, random game and out-of-band concession; (R8) every corpus fold, quiet fold and refold through the Folder, every entry an envelope, a quiet fold's `stateHash` before every entry the presented fold's, and the Session's envelopes (device, head, hash where one seat is waited on) and its exported log replayed; (R8b) every one of those folds held to the Folder (`via: 'folder'`: the presented, the quiet, every refold), and three rules of the Folder's held at the Session over replays (an entry answering one seat's decision with no hash freezes the match; after the end, a hashed command on the final head is inert from a spectator's device and freezes it from the seat's; a start under an older or newer `CORE_VERSION` is `skew`) |
| **P-merge** | merge-sim agreement ((R8) built: `node sim/merge-sim.mjs`, K peers over an RGA list ordered as Automerge orders one, ops delivered causally in a seeded random order, every corpus human log played by its seats' peers and a spectator in three scenarios (plain, a same-seat fork, a concession out of band) with junk, duplicates, stray fields, stale heads, out-of-turn and wrong-device entries and spoofed out-of-band ones slipped in, the AI pairs, the cap, the Folder's edges, (R8's fixer) same-seat forks in the deployment and the desync drills ((R8's fixer, round 2) early and late, the late ones finding a match over); all agree on `{accepted, rejected, stateHash}`, the single-process fold's, which traces the corpus log's own fold; each peer's view is its match; (R8's fixer, round 2) every accepted entry carries `h` where §0.2 #3 says, by the decision's kind, and the cap is the spec's 5,000; `--self-test`: ((R8's fixer, round 3) 41) broken match layers and a store caching by index caught, (R8's fixer, round 3) a Session or Folder that folds again from a sink's submit among them; the R8 notes; (R8b) a reenter scenario per human log, each seat answering only from its Session's sink (events, reset, settled), every entry it writes appended once the change is folded on the head and hash as they then stand, and the single flight's edges; the no-guard mutant `no-queue` among the self-test's; the R8b notes) |
| **P-peers** | real Automerge two- and three-peer runs ((N1) built: `node sim/peers.mjs`, every corpus human log played by its seats' peers over automerge-repo, as a pair, a trio and, hotseat, a same-seat fork, and three AI pairs; every peer's document, fold and view agree with a fresh fold and the corpus battle; `--self-test` breaks the store four ways) |

Everything runs by hand with `npm run parity -w @vibe-dump/tails-and-scales` (and `test`, `peers`). The parity harness runs the **working tree's** `main.js` under the fake-DOM harness through R5, and the pure core with no shims from R6 ((R6a) `parity.mjs --core`, beside the page's default until R6b switches it; `sim/run.mjs` refuses three.js and the fake DOM as it loads the core, and `mutation.mjs --core` holds that gate to a swapped die; (R6b) the pure core is the default, `--page` keeps the page under the fake DOM, through sim/oracle's driver, for the PIN, the references and the code older than R6, and P-browser plays the page in Chromium). A failure prints the first diverging line with context; a Node battle that never finishes is stopped at a deadline (`ORACLE_TIMEOUT_MS`, 60 s) and named. `node sim/self-test.mjs [--browser]` checks the harness itself catches what it must.

For the browser half, the `?debug` block implements the R0 `__ts` surface over the Session, so `sim/oracle` and `sim/chromium.mjs` run unchanged (one driver for the PIN and the working tree): the input hooks become promise-returning wrappers that build a body and call `session.submit(seat, body)`, settling once `player.idle` again (`doMove(u, c)` → `{t:'move', u:u.id, c}`, `placeCharge(c)` → `{t:'chargeEnd', c}`, `deployClick` keeps its select-then-place pair ending in `{t:'place'}`, `endPhase` and `autoPhase` likewise; `doCharge`'s promise stays pending until the `chargeEnd` is placed, as today). The block derives the rest: `select(u)` sets `S.reach` to a plan `validEnd(plan, i)` accepts; `phaseResolve` is truthy iff a local seat holds a `phase` decision in `G.pending` and `player.idle`; `chargePick` is `{u, plan:{cell}, ok}` from a pending `chargeEnd` (ok a per-cell boolean array); `S.busy` and `S.auto` read `!player.idle`; `S.deploySide` comes from the pending deploy seat; the turn fields, `units` and `scenery.chunks` keep the legacy shapes, and the shadow and battle log come from the G adapter (§2.6). (The legacy double advance after Advance-then-Auto was fixed before the corpus was recorded, commit 33946a4, so P-prop's "the AI never issues an illegal command" holds without exception.) (R5a) The browser half also inherits R5a's trace hold (the R5a notes): under `?debug` the page's trace keeps the player's pace, so a trace line written while the player is behind waits to join it, and sim/oracle takes a state line's shadow from the live match as the line joins. From R6 one `end` computes a whole AI turn before its first die is shown, so many state lines wait, and the block must carry the state with each: snapshot what the shadow reads (the turn fields, `units`, `scenery.chunks`, `q.rngState()`) as a state line is written, and serve that snapshot through those members while the line is pushed. Until then a waiting state line throws as it joins if the match has moved (R5a's guard), so this cannot pass silently; and P-browser, which reads the page through this hold, is R6's own gate. **R0 as built.**
- **Corpus.** `sim/baselines` commits inputs and hashes only: `pairs.json` (seed and dice, plus `engines`: the Node and the Chromium that recorded the corpus) and `human/*.json` (`{setup, bot, why, n, trace, shadow[, webShadow], written, entries}`), with a 10-hex hash per trace line, per shadow snapshot and per battle-log write. Full texts are regenerated from the PIN code on demand (`node sim/parity.mjs --pin --dump <dir>`). `sim/corpus.mjs` rebuilds it, seeded. Chromium runs a fresh build of the PIN code for admission, and nothing is written unless the run is complete: every original admissible, every quota and coverage target met (`--no-browser` only previews). It holds the 12 originals plus 12 AI pairs, and 16 human logs: 4 per vs-AI seat and 8 hotseat. Six end in a wipe-out: by the AI's shooting, in a fight, by a human's shot, and by a human's own friendly fire. The logs cover deployment, advances, falling back, both charge ends, a failed charge, Auto first and after acting, and the AI advancing an already-advanced unit again after Auto.
- **Three streams, per engine.** Admission means the Node and Chromium **traces and battle logs** agree. The shadow is compared within one engine: Node against `shadow`, Chromium against `webShadow` where the corpus records one (§0.1). (N0) Retired: every engine computes Node's shadow now, and is held to `shadow`. The battle log (`written`) is every entry put into `#logList`, which pins the destroyed-unit lines the trace never shows.
- **The PIN.** `sim/oracle/PIN` names two commits. The PIN is the one whose code produced the committed hashes; references and failure context come from it. `hooks` is the commit that added the `?debug` hooks, which `hooks-inert.mjs` checks by default. After the R0 commit, both are set to its sha in a commit of their own. A deliberate re-record (`--record` then `--record --browser`, N0's `CORE_VERSION 2`, the F4, F5 and F7 baselines) moves the PIN, and only the PIN, to the commit whose code produced the new hashes, in the same push; `node sim/parity.mjs --pin` must pass after it. Until it does, parity shows hashes instead of stale context and `mutation.mjs` reports inconclusive. Revisit this rule at R6, when `sim/run.mjs` regenerates references. (R6b) Revisited, and kept: the PIN still names the one commit whose code produced the committed hashes, moves only on a deliberate re-record, in the same push, and `node sim/parity.mjs --pin` must pass after it. What changes is the runner the references come from: the PIN's own, its pure core folded headless (`sim/run.mjs`) when the PIN names a commit that has one (`core/index.js`), its page under the fake DOM when not (`sim/lib.mjs` `runnerOf`). Today's PIN, the R0 commit, has no core, so references stay the page's; the next re-record (N0's `CORE_VERSION 2`, F4, F5, F7) moves the PIN to a commit with a core, and from then references come from the fold, in about 0.2 s a battle, with no fake DOM. Recording follows the code under test's runner the same way (the pure core by default, `--page` for the page; `--record --browser` still takes only Chromium's shadow). The PIN file's header (sim/oracle, frozen) still says to revisit; this note is the decision. (F4) The PIN moved to F4's commit, the first refactored code it names: no hash changed (`--pin` passes 40/40 through the fold), and F4's two logs that vote were recorded on it. The page runners stopped refusing setups the R0 page's URL couldn't carry (`legacyMode`, retired): each starts a log from its title-screen button with the setup's seeds, races and overtime on the URL (`oracle/human-bot.mjs`'s `pageStart`), then holds the battle the page started, `G.setup`, to the log's, field for field but the devices (`playedAs`), so a setup the page can't make fails where it is played. New logs are added with `sim/corpus-add.mjs` (a mode, a policy, a setup and what each log must show; the corpus's admission), which a step that lets logs hold something new (F5's races, F7's terrain) uses the same way.
- **The `__ts` contract.** The comment at the top of main.js's `?debug` block lists everything the parity driver reads (`sim/oracle/*` and `sim/chromium.mjs`, which the PIN and the working tree share): the `S` fields, `trace`, the unit, chunk and nav fields, `validEnd`, `phaseResolve`, `chargePick`, `start`, the input hooks, and the ten `q` members (`alive`, `isEngaged`, `canAct`, `movePlan`, `freeSpot`, `shootTargets`, `shotInfo`, `chargeTargets`, `chargePlan`, `rngState`) with today's arity and the result fields `sim/` reads: `shotInfo().ok`; `chargePlan()` null when unreachable, else a plan with `.need`; `freeSpot()` null or `{x, z}`; `movePlan()` the plan `validEnd` takes; target lists holding the unit objects themselves. Replaying a log depends on the hooks, `alive`/`isEngaged`/`canAct`, `shotInfo().ok`, `chargeTargets`, `chargePlan`'s null and `rngState()`. `.need`, `freeSpot` and `movePlan` feed only the corpus policies, so parity alone won't catch a reshape of them. R2-R7 keep the surface working inside that block, mapping members in place (`rngState: () => q.rngState(G.rng)`, §2.2; from R6 derived from the Session). Outside `__ts`, `sim/` wraps `#logList`'s `prepend` and, in Chromium, presses `#title`'s `[data-mode]` buttons. The oracle refuses code older than the hooks commit (it has no hooks), and (F4) holds the battle each page started to its log's setup (`oracle/human-bot.mjs`'s `playedAs`): a setup the page can't make fails where it is played, so a step that adds logs of a new kind (F5's races, F7's terrain) makes the page able to start them. Other `sim/` tools may read more of `__ts`, and nothing promises them those members: `sim/terrain-shots.mjs` (R3's screenshot diff) also reads `clock.speed` and `clock.time`, `S.titleSpin`, `camera`, `renderer`, `scenery.scene` and `scenery.blast` (R3 notes; until R4 also `units[].models[].mesh`, which R4's port replaced with the figures' own mark: R4 notes). `sim/rematch-check.mjs` (R4) reads `G` (it requires `G.out` empty after every frame; (R5a) after every frame on which `player.idle`, which it reads too) and `S.seed`, and presses `#again`, `#reroll` and `#seed` (its `onchange`), so the step that changes what lands in `G.out` (R5), retires the per-table G (R6) or moves the screens (R7) keeps it working or ports it, as R4 did `terrain-shots`. (R5a) `sim/present-check.mjs` reads `present.listen`, `G` (it folds its mirror from `project(G)` as the page loads and at each new table, and holds it to `project(G)` at the game's end) and `player.idle`, so R6 (no per-table G; the Session's G) and R7 (the rebuilt player) keep those or port it.
- **The driver** checks what the UI's own gates check before each entry: the seat holds the pending decision, the command answers that kind of decision and belongs to the current phase, then the per-command query. A log that breaks one stops with an error naming the entry.
- **Checks.**
  - `sim/mutation.mjs` swaps one die. It exits 2, inconclusive, when the swap changes nothing.
  - `sim/hooks-inert.mjs` compares everything outside the `?debug` block's body by parsing. It also compares every other source file at any depth, `vite.config.js`, `package.json` outside `scripts` and `gallery`, the root shared config and the locked `three`. Its `--self-test` shows it catches edits before the block, after it, in an `else`, in a second block, in another module, in a new subdirectory, in the Vite config and in a dependency, and that it passes a scripts-only edit.
  - `sim/self-test.mjs` shows the harness refuses wrong-phase commands and runs through a symlinked path. It stops a battle that spins forever (`ORACLE_TIMEOUT_MS`) and names it, and fails a build that drops the destroyed-unit lines. With `--browser`, it fails a title screen whose buttons start nothing, on one watch and one hotseat battle it picks from the corpus by mode. (It named `hotseat-late-3` until R2, which is not in the corpus, so `--browser` exited 2; R2 fixed this harness bug.)
- **Spec changes made at R0 (approved by the lead).** Beyond R0's own row, R0 changed:
  - §0.1: the per-engine trig fact; `atan` added to the logic `Math.*` list, N0's dmath list and the lint.
  - §2.2: `q` re-exports the whole `__ts` query set, `rngState(r)` included.
  - §2.6: the parity shadow is `shadow.mjs`'s legacy format, not `shadowState`. A G adapter keeps its quirks through R8 and rebuilds the battle log from `G.journal`.
  - The gate rows: P-ai and P-human snapshot every state line, check the battle log and compare per engine. P-browser is the whole corpus on a fresh build, started from the title buttons.
  - R0's checkpoint: the hooks-inert criterion, and admission on traces and battle logs.
  - R4 and R6: the `__ts` obligation, which R6 meets by deriving the surface from the Session.
  - N0's target, and §4.1's statement of who enforces what.

  The lead's decisions on the three open choices:
  1. **Shadows at every state line: kept.** It is the stronger check. The G adapter keeps the round, phase and stage quirks through R8.
  2. **The double advance: fixed, not pinned.** A human's Advance followed by Auto let the AI advance the same unit again (a second D6). That is a rules bug, so it was fixed in its own commit (33946a4: the AI moves an already-advanced unit on its existing roll) before the corpus was recorded. The same commit ends a blast volley whose own unit is wiped out by its first template, which used to crash and soft-lock the game. Neither path occurs in an AI-only battle; the 12 original battles replay identically across it.
  3. **`shadowState` as the parity shadow: no.** The legacy `shadow.mjs` format stays the parity shadow, through the G adapter. `shadowState` remains a debugging aid.
- **Two hooks later steps need (from the R0 review).**
  - **The battle log's position stamp.** The corpus's `written` stream records, for each line put into `#logList`, the trace length at the moment it was written. From R5 the log is an event played later by the presenter, when the trace has run ahead, so that stamp would drift. The `log` event therefore carries `at` (the trace length when the line was logged or flushed, §2.3). `ui/log.js` (and R5's transitional log handler) puts it on the entry as `data-at` under `?debug`, and the instrumentation reads `data-at`, falling back to the live trace length for the PIN code, which has none. No re-record is needed. (R5a) The handler writes `data-at`, but `sim/oracle/shadow.mjs` reads only the live trace length, and sim/oracle is not edited for the working tree; so the `?debug` block's page trace keeps pace with the player instead, and every entry lands at its `at` (the R5a notes).
  - **Seeing trace lines as the core makes them.** From R4/R6 there is no `__ts.trace.push` to wrap. `createMatch(setup, { out, onTrace })` takes a sim/debug-only callback that `journal.js` calls synchronously with `(line, G)` on every trace push. It never draws, is not part of G's hashed state, and sits beside `out` (so §0.2 #12's "no pending closures in G" still holds; from R4 #12 names both as exempt I/O fields). The `?debug` block keeps `__ts.trace` as one page-lifetime array fed by it.

**R1 as built.**
- **`hypot3` landed with `hypot`.** V8's three-argument formula matched `Math.hypot` on 5M board-scale samples, 5M more shaped like `distToBox`'s (non-negative, often zero on an axis) and the edge cases (zeros, NaN, Infinity, extremes); the two-argument one did too. So N0's list is `sin`/`cos`/`atan`/`atan2` only.
- **Every rules call measures with dmath.** main.js 16 sites, ai.js 12, nav.js 7, scenery.js 10 (`distToBox` uses `hypot3`). `Math.hypot` stays only in view and input code: the camera follow, the drag threshold, the deploy click's snap tolerance and the figures' walk speed in main.js, the rubble spill in scenery.js, and fx.js.
- **`G` is `{ rng }` until R4.** It is created at load on a `Math.random` seed, which nothing draws from before a battle, and `start` replaces the generator with `createRng(S.dice)`. The AI reaches it as `api.G`. `lock`/`unlock` exist, but nothing locks until R6.
- **`sim/perturb.mjs --fn <names>`** preloads `sim/oracle/perturb-preload.mjs` into every oracle child, which moves each result of the named `Math` functions one ULP away from zero, and replays the corpus (the AI pairs by default). It runs the same nudge on the PIN code first as a control, and is inconclusive if nothing moves there. For `hypot`: the PIN code moves 24/24 AI battles; R1 moves 0/24 AI and 0/16 human. N0 uses the same probe with `--fn sin,cos,atan,atan2`.

**R2 as built.**
- **Races are data.** `data/races/squirrel.js` and `serpent.js` are plain definitions in the §2.8 shape, names, shorts, weapon names and ability text verbatim. `data/schema.js` checks and normalises them into the frozen `RACES` registry. A race file exports its definition rather than calling `defineRace` itself: schema.js imports the race files to build the registry, and that import cycle would reach `defineRace` before its tables exist. Every flag is a boolean on the normalised type, beside the derived `move`, `deployRow`, `eye`, `chest`, `brawler`, `noCharge` and `hero`. Rules code reads them: `moveMode` reads `t.move`, `eyeY`/`chestY` read `t.eye`/`t.chest`, and `deployArmies` reads `t.deployRow`. `RACES` and each race's `units` have no prototype, so a race or unit name such as `toString`, `constructor` or `__proto__` (from a URL now, from a lobby a peer writes at N2) finds nothing instead of an `Object.prototype` member. Race and unit keys are lower-case letters, digits and dashes. `RACES` is `raceRegistry([squirrel, serpent])`, which refuses two races with one key (a race file copied as the start of another and left with the old key would otherwise hide one of them); a new race file is added to that list. Every table `core/` and `data/` export is frozen, deeply where it nests (`BOARD`, `PHASES`, `CONSTANTS`, `EDGES`, the schema's vocabularies, `RACES`, the compat views), so no importer can change what a later match reads (§4.1 rule 13).
- **Flags replace tests.** `canCharge` reads `noCharge` and `chargeAfterAdvance`, which also drives the Advance button's text. `blastLands` passes `corrodes` to `scenery.blast`. The AI reads `t.ai` instead of `ROLE[u.key]`, and `t.brawler` instead of its key test. `brawler = !ranged || wrecker` covers Oak Guard and Sidewinders because both have `ranged: null`; `sim/data-check.mjs` checks this. Rules code may test `t.role` (the AI still favours Artillery targets): role is rule data, which RULES_ID hashes.
- **Seats.** `core/match.js` has `makeSeats(races, ctrl)`, `raceOf`, `edgeOf` and `ctrl`. `G.seats` is built at load, and `start()` rebuilds it from `S.control`, which stays because `sim/chromium.mjs` reads it. The races are fixed at load because `setupTable` builds the armies on the title screen; `start()` changes only the controllers (`seatPlayers()`). So `?races` is read at load, not in `start()` as the R2 task note had it: applying it in `start()` would seat races whose armies the title-screen table doesn't hold. `human()` reads the seat. Every site in the §2.1 table now reads the edge: facing, the `freeSpot` zone, the deploy x and z flip, the flee exit and yaw, and the zones. The title drift stays for R7.
- **Presentation by seat.** `data/compat.js` `sidesFor(seats)` builds the old `SIDES` records (name, short, icon and colours) for whoever is playing, and main.js's `SIDES` is that view. A mirror match (`isMirror`) gives seat 1 `look.alt`, a hue well away from `team` (blue for the Coil, violet for the Bushtails; both stay apart under red-green colour blindness), because the models are the same for both seats and the base rims, label borders, zones and objective flags are the only cues on the table. `killModel`'s voice and gore come from the unit's race (`RACES[u.race].look`). main.js writes a `<style>` that sets `--s0`/`--s1` and the active seat's glow (`--s0-glow`/`--s1-glow`, which style.css's `:root` defaults to the classic pair) for the HUD, labels, log and card, and fills in the HUD's names and icons. In a mirror match the two seats' names read the same. Of the texts that name a seat outside the HUD, labels, log borders and card, only the turn banner and the end screen's title take the seat's colour (inline, and only in a mirror match; otherwise they keep the stylesheet's); the rest are listed below.
- **Left for R7/F6.** The title screen's copy, its `.m0`/`.m1` mode buttons and their classic colours (`index.html`, `style.css`); the HUD's VP pill ink (`#2a1404`/`#05220f`, dark inks picked for orange and green, still legible on the alt colours); seat names in mirror-match text, which stay the same for both seats and carry no seat colour (the dice tray's roll-off rows, the log's roll-off, deploy and end-of-round lines, the AI hint, the card and the end screen's reason); and a stronger mirror cue on the table than a coloured base rim (a thicker or filled rim, a label background). Any qualifier must be mirror-only: the classic lines are traced, and the oracle records every battle-log entry's HTML, so even a classic line's markup must not change.
- **`?races=<seat 0>,<seat 1>`** picks the seat races for the page (case and spaces ignored). It is URL-only. A value naming no two races makes the page warn, say why on the title card and play the classic matchup (`?debug` or not, so there is no second `?debug` test outside the hooks block); `sim/mirror-check.mjs` fails any run whose log shows other races than it asked for. An oracle job takes an optional `races`, which becomes that parameter in Node (`run-legacy.mjs`) and in Chromium (`sim/chromium.mjs`). Jobs without it run exactly as before. (F4) A job's `races` now takes the place of its setup's seat races (`oracle/human-bot.mjs`'s `jobSetup`), and every page runner puts a setup's races on the URL and holds the page to them, so a race log can hold its races in `setup.seats` as the core's runner does.
- **`RULES_ID`** (`core/version.js`) is cyrb53 over `canonicalJSON`, printed in base36; `cyrb53` and `canonicalJSON` are in `core/util.js`. The hash covers the races minus `name`, `short`, `icon`, `look`, `abilities` and `fx` as fields of any record (a race, a unit type, a weapon), never as keys of the race and unit maps (a unit keyed `fx` is rules like any other), plus the six constants and the phase keys. Phase names are banner copy, so they are left out. The terrain sets join the hash at R3, and the mission's objectives join when they move to `data/`. `CORE_VERSION` still lands at R8.
- **The ruleset is `core/rules.js`** (the constants, `PHASES` and the dice maths), so `data/` and `core/version.js` import only `core/`. The root `rules.js` re-exports it for main.js and ai.js until R4-R6 move their rules code.
- **Checks.**
  - **The legacy anchor.** `sim/data-check.mjs` and flag-lint's `--self-test` read the legacy code from the R0 commit, named as `LEGACY_REF` in `sim/lib.mjs`, not from the PIN. The R0 commit is the first with the hooks; it, like every commit before R2, holds `TYPES`, `SIDES` and `ARMIES` in `rules.js` and the tests the flags replaced in main.js and ai.js. The PIN moves at every deliberate re-record (N0's `CORE_VERSION 2`, the F4, F5 and F7 baselines, a Chromium-upgrade `--record --browser`) to code that has none of this; those re-records leave `LEGACY_REF` alone. `legacyDir()` refuses an anchor whose `rules.js` has no `TYPES`.
  - `sim/data-check.mjs` compares each type with the R0 code's `TYPES`. It computes the expected flags with the legacy tests themselves, and those tests must appear verbatim in the R0 source.
  - It also checks the races against `SIDES`/`ARMIES` and killModel's voice and gore (by the R0 text); that every race's voice is a sound `sfx.js` plays (its proxy would turn a missing one into silence); that `defineRace` refuses fourteen kinds of broken data (an army listing `constructor` or `__proto__`, a unit keyed `Brute` or `__proto__` among them) and the registry two races with one key; that `makeSeats` seats every race in either seat with the edge by seat, and refuses `toString`, `__proto__`, `constructor`, `hasOwnProperty`, `valueOf` and `''` in either seat; 16 changes that must move `RULES_ID` (a retuned unit keyed `fx` and race keyed `look` among them) against 8 that must not; and that every table `core/` and `data/` export is deeply frozen.
  - `sim/flag-lint.mjs` covers main.js, ai.js, rules.js, `core/` and `data/`. It flags tests on a unit or race key (strict or loose comparisons, a table keyed by either or by a bare `key` other than the `RACES` and `race.units` lookups, list membership, `in`, `switch`, text methods such as `includes` or `localeCompare` on a key, a regex `.test` of one), on a name or short, on text (`startsWith`/`endsWith`), and reads of ability text or `fx`, also by another route: a race named through the registry (`RACES.serpent`, `RACES['serpent']`), a banned field read by its string name, destructured, or aliased into a variable. Its allow-list names the presentation sites, each with a reason; an allowed text excuses only itself, and the rest of its line is linted again. Its `--self-test` must flag every legacy test in the R0 code, and a set of lines that must be flagged (race tests the R0 code can't show, loose, method and regex key tests, tests smuggled beside an allowed one) or must pass (`RACES[u.race]`, `race.units[key]`, the mirror check, role and flag reads).
  - `sim/mirror-check.mjs` plays serpent v serpent, squirrel v squirrel and the swapped seats, three battles each, AI v AI and hotseat with the aggressive bot in both seats, each twice. Every run must reach game over with identical traces, shadows, logs (and bot entries), and its log must show the races it asked for. Every unit still unmoved in the first full-precision snapshot must sit on its seat's edge (seat 0 west, seat 1 east, at least one unit each), and the bot must place at least half of each seat's units. An edge taken from the race instead fails all 18 runs; determinism alone passes it. The classic matchup asked for by URL must replay the 24 AI pairs. With `--browser`, each matchup's first AI battle also runs in Chromium and must trace and write its log as Node did.
- **Transitional.** `compat.js` (`CLASSIC`, `TYPES`, `ARMIES`, `SIDES`, `sidesFor`, `isMirror`) goes at R6. main.js reads `sidesFor`, `isMirror` and `CLASSIC` from it (and `RACES` from `data/schema.js`); the three legacy-shaped views, and `CLASSIC` for the legacy side-to-race pairing, serve data-check. At R6 (see its row) `sidesFor` and `isMirror` move to view code, `CLASSIC` becomes the setup's default seat races ((R6b's fixer, round 3) as built, the page's: main.js names them in each title-screen mode's setup, and no setup takes them by default), and data-check builds its legacy-shaped views from `RACES` itself, still against the fixed R0 commit.
- **Spec changes made at R2 (for lead approval).**
  - §1.1 `core/match.js`: the seat helpers are `makeSeats`, `ctrl`, `edgeOf` and `raceOf`. `makeSeats(races, ctrl)` is R2's transitional builder; from R4 `newState(setup)` folds over `setup.seats`.
  - §2.8: a race file exports a plain object, and `data/schema.js` applies `defineRace` as it builds `RACES` (the import cycle above).
  - §2.7: `RULES_ID` hashes the phase keys only, and leaves `name`, `short` and `fx` out of every record, so unit and weapon renames don't move it. `SETS` joins at R3.
  - §1.1 `data/compat.js`: main.js reads the seat-based `sidesFor`, `isMirror` and `CLASSIC` from it, and `RACES` from `data/schema.js` directly; the legacy-shaped `TYPES`/`ARMIES`/`SIDES` views serve only data-check. Still deleted at R6, whose row now names where each export goes.
  - §4 F5 row: a new race file is added to `data/schema.js`'s `raceRegistry([…])` list (a consequence of the §2.8 change above).
  - §2.1's table: the title drift is left to R7's camera presets; every other site in it reads the edge at R2.
  - R2's row: `?races` is read at load, not in `start()` (see **Seats** above), and it is a URL parameter, not `?debug`-only.
  - §2.8: the mirror `alt` colours are `#4aa8e8` (Coil) and `#c75ad6` (Bushtails) instead of `#a6e05a` and `#f2c14e`, which sat too close to their `team` colours to tell the armies apart on the table.

**R3 as built.**
- **The split.** `core/terrain/terrain.js` is `Terrain`: the chunks, `add`, `generate`, `los`, `blast`, `hurt`, `destroy`, `collapse`, `rubble`, `topple`, with no three.js, clock or randomness of its own. `generate` is `clear` plus `recipes.js` `scatter`, so the layout policy (the centre rule, the pair count, the spacing rules, the point mirror) is not in the class, and a set with another placement rule (F7) changes `scatter`, not `Terrain`. `recipes.js` holds the seven modules, the nine features (`FEATURES`) and the two centre pieces (`CENTRES`) as ChunkDef producers, with every layout-stream draw in the old order and its visual result recorded in `look`; it also holds `STYLES`, `LEAVES` and `WOOD`, `scatter` (the set's own draws: centre, pair count, then per attempt the feature, its place, its turn and its seed) and `checkSet`. `sets.js` holds `SETS.classic`, and `geom.js` holds `segmentHitsBox` and `distToBox`. `view/terrain.js` is `TerrainView`. It builds each mesh from the chunk's `look` plus its place (`shape.x`/`z`, and `shape.y` for a wall block or cap) and nothing else, and it plays the terrain's events with the old visuals unchanged: shudder, debris, the fall, the topple and the rubble pieces, all on `Math.random`. `scenery.js` is now a facade over the API main.js uses: `generate`, `chunks` (the Terrain's live list), `dirty` (read and written through to the Terrain's), `los`, `blast`, `hurt` and `onBreak` (reaching the view), so main.js is untouched; also `clear`, `features` and `group`, and `scene`, `view` and `terrain` for `sim/`. The old public `destroy`, `collapse`, `rubble` and `topple` are gone from it: main.js never called them, and they are the Terrain's own steps now, so a caller from outside would get the logic without the view's part (a tree toppled that way would keep its canopy). `mulberry32`, `lerp`, `pick`, `rr` and a `deepFreeze` live in `core/util.js`. The root `util.js` re-exports `lerp` (main.js's only use of them) and wraps `pick` to default to `Math.random` for the view, while core's always names its stream; nothing outside `core/` and `data/` needs the others. `data/schema.js` freezes with the same `deepFreeze` (it had its own copy). `generate` tests a set name with `in` on the prototype-less `SETS`, not `Object.hasOwn`, which Vite's default ES2020 target leaves to the engine and older Safari and Chrome builds lack.
- **Logic to view, synchronously.** The Terrain reports through `sink`, a function the facade wires to `TerrainView.apply`. Each event is reported as it happens, never awaited:
  - `terrain.clear`
  - `terrain.add {c}`
  - `terrain.hurt {c, from}`
  - `terrain.destroy {c, from}`, before its consequences
  - `terrain.collapse {drops: [{c, dy}], by}`
  - `terrain.rubble {c, from}`

  These are §2.3's terrain events, names and order, except that they carry the chunk itself (`c`) where §2.3's carry `id` (and `def` on an add), and the view reads the live chunk as each one comes. R5 turns them into §2.3's id-addressed events in `G.out`, the view then keeping each chunk's `x`/`z` from its add and reading `alive` and `y` from the mirror. There is no topple event. A felled tree's log is added with `look: {piece: 'fallen', tree, dx, dz}`, and the view plays the fall on that add, reusing the tree's own group as the log's mesh as before.
  - **The sink is R3's only.** It is a closure stored on the Terrain, which §0.2 #12 forbids in `G` (G holds no pending closures, so `stateHash` and refolding see plain data). So at R4, when `G.terrain` is the Terrain, its reports go through `emit(G, …)` into `G.out` (or an `out` passed per call) instead (R4's row). Queuing them is not a drop-in change for the view: it reads the live chunk (a scuffed block's place, for its debris) when each event comes, and a later collapse in the same blast can lower that block, so queued events need their values in the payload or the mirror (§2.4).
  - **TerrainView is built only by replaying events** from a table's `terrain.clear`: a fallen log is its tree's group keeled over (the add finds the tree's mesh), and a collapsed block is wherever its tween left it. Built from the chunks as they stand, it would draw dead chunks as alive. A snap (R5's EventPlayer `snap`, R7's `?debug` snap-equivalence diff, N3's rejoin and scrub) needs `TerrainView.sync(chunks)`: live chunks at their current `shape`, dead ones skipped, a fallen log built from its tree's look already keeled over without its canopy, a rubble pile with a fresh cosmetic spill. It is R7's (its row), or the first step that snaps the view ((R7a) built: §2.9's (R7a) note). Destruction stays instant in the logic: `collapse` lowers `shape.y` and `topple` adds the log. `smashAround` (main.js) still walks the live list and `blast` a copy (§4.1 rule 6). main.js's break sound plays on `terrain.destroy`, which is in the same tick as before but now comes ahead of the collapse and rubble visuals rather than after them. Once audio is unlocked, the sound's noise draws `Math.random`, so the rubble pieces after it draw different values from the same state. That changes nothing that can be observed: `Math.random` is never seeded in play, and no rule reads a rubble piece.
- **Looks.** Each mesh kind has one `look.piece`:
  - `box` and `log`: a wall block (a fallen tree is `fallen`, so a log wall's blocks can't be mistaken for one);
  - `cap`, `tree`, `hedge`, `boulder`, `mushroom`, `floor`, `rubble`;
  - `crate`, `barrel` and `sack`: the three crate variants.

  A look records exactly what the layout stream decided: colours, scale and rotation jitter, the canopy, tufts and berries, moss, the crate's variant and stack, the acorns, the mushroom's spots as (azimuth, elevation) and its tilt, and the forest floor's 23 rim factors. A tree's look also has `trunk: {h, r}`, the same draws as its `trunkH` and `trunkR` (which stay chunk fields: a felled tree's log is shaped from them), so the view reads the look alone, the fallen log's tumble included. The view does the rest of the old arithmetic. The old chunk fields that were presentation moved into `look`:
  - `color`, the debris colour (a block's colour, or `'#9a7048'` for any crate), is now `look.chip`;
  - `leaves` is now `look.leaves`;
  - a cap's `capH` is now `look.h`. Nothing ever read `capH`.

  `col` stays a shared column record, `{blocks, x, z, yaw, style, by, rubble, w, t}`, where `style` is a `STYLES` key. There is no `canopyN`: use `look.canopy.length`.
- **Ids.** Chunk ids come from a per-Terrain counter that restarts at 1 on every new table (`clear`). Only the view's map and a fallen log's `look.tree` read an id, and the parity shadow prints none.
- **SETS.** `SETS` follows §2.9, plus the numbers `generate` used to write inline: `attempts` 1200, `margin` 0.5, `selfGap` 1.4, `deployMargin` 1, `objectiveGap` 2.2 and `gap` 2.1. It has a null prototype and is deeply frozen, like every table `core/terrain` exports. `generate(seed, objectives, deployDepth, set = 'classic')` refuses an unknown set. The centre rule names centre pieces from `recipes.js` `CENTRES` (`tower`, `rockbox`), which keep their footprints (4.6, and 1.8 per rock pile) in code. `sets.js` runs `checkSet` on every set as it loads, the way `data/schema.js` checks a race: each feature (`kinds`, `notInDeploy`) is in `FEATURES` and each centre piece in `CENTRES`; radii and weights are numbers above 0; centre thresholds are in (0, 1] and rise; `pairs` is two whole numbers and `attempts` one; `mirror` is `point`, the only one `scatter` knows; the spacing rules are finite; and no field is missing or unknown. A slip in a new set then fails at load, not only on the boards whose draws reach the bad entry.
- **`RULES_ID`** now hashes `SETS` whole (`rulesData({ sets })`): `eypwgs6v2u`, up from R2's `18vs5wwhm0w`. data-check checks that it moves on a feature's weight, its footprint, the table order, the centre rule, the pair count, a spacing rule, `notInDeploy` and an added set. As a control, an unchanged copy of the sets must hash the same. The recipes' own numbers (`STYLES`' hit points and sizes, the modules' shapes) count as code: changing them is CORE_VERSION's business from R8, and P-terrain catches a change until then.
- **Checks.**
  - `sim/terrain-check.mjs` (P-terrain) builds every board twice, with the R0 code's `scenery.js` (`LEGACY_REF`, real three.js and a no-op fx that records its calls) and with the working tree's facade. It compares them exactly, with `Object.is` on every number:
    - every layout stream's seed and draw count, in order;
    - every chunk's logic fields (id order, kind, shape including `reach`, hp, `maxHp`, `destructible`, `alive`, `navKind`, `los`, `cover`, `nav`, `coverShape`, `col`, `level`, `trunkH`, `trunkR`), and that no field on either side is unaccounted for;
    - each old mesh against the new one: object type, position, rotation, quaternion, scale, shadows, children, geometry type and parameters, every vertex attribute value, material settings and colour, and which meshes share a geometry or material;
    - the whole scenery group.

    Then it runs the same seeded destruction on both, 8 operations per board: blasts (some acid) and wrecker sweeps over the live list, with the tweens stepped to the end and `Math.random` seeded alike. After every operation it compares the chunks, what `blast` returns, `dirty` and every fx call. At the end it compares the whole group (rubble pieces, fallen logs, collapsed blocks) and line of sight. Boards 1-500 match. `sim/terrain-hooks.mjs` counts the draws by wrapping `mulberry32` in memory as each `util.js` loads, so neither checkout is edited on disk. `--self-test` applies nine edits one at a time, and each must fail the check: two draws swapped, one dropped, a look value, a material, `blast` walking the live list, a log's shape, the rubble's spill, a set's gap, and one draw too many at the end of an obelisk, which no chunk, mesh or later draw shows (the next feature reseeds), so only the draw count can catch it. It refuses a run that checks nothing, and bad arguments (an unknown option included), with exit 2: `--seeds` is `N` or `A-B` with A ≤ B, `--ops` and `--max` whole numbers, at least one board compared, and with `--ops` above 0 at least one destruction op run.
  - `sim/terrain-shots.mjs` is the screenshot diff. It makes fresh builds of the R0 code and the working tree and opens each with a seeded `Math.random`. Through the `__ts` both builds already expose, it stops the clock at 0, sets one camera pose and reads back one frame per board, of the table as generated and again after the same blasts on both. It hides the tufts, flowers and figures. Since R1, main.js draws one `Math.random` at load after painting the mat, which shifts every later cosmetic draw by one against R0. `--ref HEAD --full` draws everything, for a ref with the same draws at load. main.js needed no new hook. The default boards are 1, 4242, 90210, 411 (log walls, trees, mushrooms) and 22392 (hedges, trees).
    - **Determinism.** SwiftShader's WebGL draws identical draw calls identically, but Chromium's accelerated canvas 2D raster does not rasterise main.js's mat identically on every page load, though `paintMat` is the same code in every build since R0. One gate run failed on that alone: board 4242's frames differed from R0's by 8,554 and 8,733 pixels, at most 2 per channel, all on the mat, and the same code matched on every later run. A probe hashing the canvas textures over 8 loads of each build saw the mat differ on 1 load in 16 on the accelerated path, and 16 loads in 16 the same with canvas 2D on the CPU. So the gate launches Chromium with `--disable-accelerated-2d-canvas --disable-gpu-rasterization` (its own launch only: parity compares no pixels), and the mat, the wood and fx's decals stay in the comparison. As a control, a board whose shots differ is shot again on both sides in fresh pages, up to twice. A difference in the code is deterministic and repeats on every pass, so the board fails. One that goes away is printed as noise, with how far each side's frames moved against its own first pass, and is not counted. Each run builds into its own temp dir, so runs side by side don't share builds.
    - With those flags, all 10 shots are pixel-identical to R0 on the first pass, in 3 runs out of 3, and all 10 with `--full` are identical to the R2 commit (5f3df5b), figures and tufts included. Identical is not enough on its own, since two blank canvases are identical too. So every frame must hold at least 1,000 distinct colours (a real one holds tens of thousands), the blasts must break something, and each side's wrecked frame must differ from its own table frame by at least 2,000 pixels; otherwise the board fails as vacuous. A board whose page fails to load or throws is reported as not run and counts as a failure, and the run goes on. Page loads wait `IDLE_MS` (`sim/chromium.mjs`, 120 s) rather than Playwright's 30 s, which a busy machine can exceed.
  - **Both tools are R0-R3 only as they stand.** They drive the working tree through the `Scenery` facade, which goes at R4. `terrain-check` imports `scenery.js` and calls `new Scenery`; `terrain-shots` uses `__ts.scenery.scene` and `.blast`. `terrain-shots` also reads view members the `?debug` contract (main.js; R0 notes) does not promise: `clock.speed` and `clock.time`, `S.titleSpin`, `camera`, `renderer` and `units[].models[].mesh`. R7 moves the camera and clock. So R4 (its row) ports P-terrain to `Terrain` and `TerrainView` directly, since it is a standing check (§1.1's `sim/` list), and ports `terrain-shots` to what the `?debug` block then exposes, or retires it explicitly. If R7 wants a pixel diff as a gate, R7 adds it to its gate column and puts the members it reads into the contract comment then, marked screenshot-only (comment-only, so hooks-inert holds). Nothing promises them from R3 on.
  - `sim/data-check.mjs` section 7: `checkSet` passes `classic` and refuses 18 broken sets, one field at a time (a feature or centre piece that doesn't exist, `toString` as a feature, an entry without its weight, a footprint of 0, a weight that is a string or negative, no features, a threshold above 1, falling thresholds, fractional or missing pairs, infinite attempts, an unknown mirror, a NaN gap, `notInDeploy` naming no feature, a misspelt field, a missing one).
  - **No banned token in `core/`, even in comments.** §1.2's `boundaries.mjs` (R6) greps tokens, and `core/` had none of them before R3. R3's comments say "the engine's own unseeded random" and "no randomness but the layout stream", and the tower's window flags are `glazed`, so `Math.random` and `window` appear nowhere in `core/`.
  - Coverage: none of the corpus's 40 boards has a log wall, so parity never builds one. P-terrain's 500 boards build 1,148 log-wall blocks, among 38,258 chunks in 1,243,066 layout draws. Its 4,000 destruction runs break 8,682 chunks and fell 115 trees. 36 of those logs are smashed in the same sweep that felled them (the live list), and 67 lie within the blast that felled them and are spared (the copy).
- **Spec changes made at R3 (for lead approval).**
  - §2.9: the ChunkDef `look` is per piece (above); `col` is a shared record and there is no `canopyN`; `SETS` carries the inline numbers; the centre rule's pieces are `CENTRES` in `recipes.js`.
  - §2.3: the Terrain row now lists R5's target as R3 found it: `terrain.clear`, a `terrain.add` for every chunk (the board's too) whose `def.look` carries a fallen log's `{tree, dx, dz}` so the fall plays from the add and there is no topple event, `kind` on `terrain.destroy`, `by` on `terrain.collapse`, and the view keeping each chunk's `x`/`z` from its add and reading `alive` and `y` from the mirror. R3's sink events are those, carrying the chunk itself (`c`) instead of `id`/`def`; R5 converts them (above).
  - §1.1 and §1.3: `Terrain.generate` is `clear` plus `recipes.js` `scatter`, which makes the set's own draws; `recipes.js` also holds `FEATURES`, `CENTRES`, `STYLES`, `LEAVES`, `WOOD` and `checkSet`; `core/util.js` holds `deepFreeze`; `sim/` gains `terrain-hooks.mjs` and `terrain-shots.mjs`.
  - §2.9: a tree's `look.trunk`; every set is checked at load (`checkSet`).
  - The R0 `__ts` contract and §1.3's boot row: the `?debug` comment lists what the parity driver reads (`sim/oracle/*`, `sim/chromium.mjs`), not everything `sim/` reads; `terrain-shots` reads more, unpromised.
  - R4's row: the facade goes; the Terrain reports into `G.out`, not a stored callback; P-terrain is ported to `Terrain` + `TerrainView` and gates R4; `terrain-shots` is ported or retired. R7's row: `TerrainView.sync`.
  - §1.3, the scenery.js rows (main.js 229-234's row edited): the break sound still goes through the facade's `onBreak` (main.js's hook) until R7 moves it into `view/terrain.js`.
  - §2.7: `RULES_ID` hashes `SETS` from R3, as planned.

**R4 as built.**
- **The match state.** `core/match.js` `newState(setup, { out, onTrace })` builds G: `setup` (a frozen copy), `rng` (`createRng(setup.dice)`), `seats`, `units`, `nextUnitId`, `objectives` (`{ i, x, z }` from `OBJ_POS`, which moved there from main.js), `terrain` (the `Terrain` itself), `nav`, `turn`, `journal: { trace, pendingLog }`, `out` and `onTrace` (the two I/O fields §0.2 #12 now exempts: neither is match state). It scatters the board into `out`, refreshes the nav grid (the setup site), makes both armies (`core/units.js` `makeUnit`, ids from `G.nextUnitId`, which starts at 1) and deploys them (`core/deploy.js` `freeSpot`, `deployArmies`). `refreshNav(G)` runs at exactly the old sites: the new table, `movePlan`, `chargePlan`, and the end of `doMove`, `doCharge` and `blastLands`.
- **A G per table, started by `start()`.** The title screen shows the table before a mode is chosen, so `setupTable` (load, a new seed, Again) builds the G: the board seed, the races, the title's provisional controllers and a placeholder dice seed (`TABLE_DICE`, drawn once at load where R1-R3 drew their placeholder stream, so the view's own `Math.random` draws at load keep their order; nothing draws from it). `start(mode)` calls `startMatch(G, { dice, ctrl })`: a new frozen setup, a fresh `createRng(dice)` and the seats with the mode's controllers. Every battle is preceded by a `setupTable`, so every battle has a G of its own, and `startMatch` refuses a table whose battle has begun. `setupTable` builds the new G before it takes the old table's figures away, so a throw leaves the last table whole and the frames running; `start()` refuses an unknown mode before it touches `S`, and sets `S.dice` and `S.control` only once `startMatch` has accepted them. Building G in `start()` instead (R6's `createMatch` from the whole setup) would either rebake every figure at the click or need the view reuse §2.9 describes; R6 takes that on with `createMatch`, and its row now names what it retires (this `startMatch`, `TABLE_DICE`, the stage `'title'`, the per-table G). The `setup.rounds` the table is built with (`ROUNDS`, its default) is the one the battle loop, the HUD's round and the end screen read.
- **`G.turn`** is `{ stage, round, active, first, phase, vp, wiped }`, as far as today's loop allows: `phase` is the phase key (R6's step machine brings `step`, `t` and `ph`, which replaces it: §2.1), `stage` starts at `'title'` (the table before a start; §2.1's stages begin at `deploy`), and `wiped` is −1 until a side is wiped. `battle()`, `playerTurn()`, `scoreRound()` and `gameOver()` run on it unchanged, so the shadow's quirks (the round overshoot, the last phase on `round` and `over` lines, stage `battle` on the `over` line) come out as before.
- **Queries.** `core/queries.js` holds `alive`, `enemiesOf`, `friendsOf`, `dist`, `gap`, `engagedWith`, `mx`/`mz`, `isEngaged`, `eyeY`/`chestY`, `inCover`, `sight`, `leadership`, `controlOf`, `canAct` and `anyCanAct`. Those that read the match take `G` first; those that read only their arguments (`alive`, `dist`, `gap`, `mx`, `mz`, `eyeY`, `chestY`, and `moveMode` below) take no `G`. `canAct` needs the shoot and charge queries, so their read-only halves moved now to the files §1.1 gives the actions: `core/actions/move.js` (`moveMode`, `forbidMask`, `movePlan`, `validEnd`, `nearestValid`), `shoot.js` (`canShoot`, `shotInfo`, `shootTargets`) and `charge.js` (`canCharge`, `chargeTargets`, `chargePlan`). `queries.js` re-exports them with `freeSpot` and `rngState`, a superset of §2.2's `q`. The actions themselves (`doMove` … `moralePhase`) stay async in main.js, awaiting their tweens as before (R5). `core/journal.js` holds `trace(G, line)` (into `G.journal.trace`, then `G.onTrace`), `traceState` and `traceLog`; `emit` comes with R5's events. main.js reads `rngState` through `core/queries.js` (§2.2's `q`); its one import of `core/rng.js` left is `draw`, for the blast's aim, which moves into `core/actions/shoot.js` at R5 (§1.2). `nav.js` moved to `core/nav.js` (it imported only dmath), with `gridSize` for the overlay texture, which is sized before any match exists. The root `rules.js` re-export and `scenery.js` are gone.
- **The AI** imports the core queries and takes `G`; it acts through `act = { doMove, doAdvance, doShoot, doCharge, focus }`, main.js's own actions. The `api` object is gone (§1.3's row 1189-1197); its generators are R6's.
- **Units, logic and view.** A unit is §2.1's record (it lost `name`, which nothing read). Its view is main.js's `views` map, keyed by unit id: `{ facing, moving, ring, hit, label, models }`, where `models[k]` draws the unit's `models[k]` (`mesh`, `x`, `z`, `yaw`, `lunge`, `lungeDir`, `lift`, `flash`, `dying`, `look`, `flying`, `fleeing`). The rules read none of it. `moveUnit` (the rules' `setUnitPos`, then the ring and hit cylinder) and `syncView` (after `relayout`) keep the view's disc with the unit. A walk still moves `u.pos` along its path inside its tween, as before (R5's `resolveWalk` makes it synchronous). The dead `u.facing` read in the walk is gone: a path of 0.05" or more always has a last segment.
- **Terrain reports go into an `out` passed per call.** The Terrain stores no sink: `clear`, `add`, `generate`, `blast` and `hurt` (and the `destroy`, `collapse`, `rubble` and `topple` they call) take the `out` array to report into; `generate` hands the recipes a `T.add` bound to it. main.js passes `G.out` and plays it into the view (`TerrainView.play`) straight after each terrain call: the board in `setupTable`, each smashed chunk in `smashAround`, the blast in `blastLands`. The break sound is `terrainView.onBreak`, set by main.js. `terrain.hurt` and `terrain.destroy` carry `at`, the chunk's place when it was hit, and the view's debris reads that. The R3 note's hazard cannot arise with classic's recipes, though. A blast walks a column's blocks lowest first (they are added bottom up, and a collapse keeps their order), and a collapse closes every gap in the column, so it lowers a block only when a gap lies beneath it: the broken block's, which is above every block walked before it, or a recipe hole (the window at level 1 that some wall, ruin and glazed-tower columns leave). Classic's holed columns are three high with no cap, so one block stands above the hole and it is the column's last: no block scuffed earlier in a blast is lowered later in it. A taller holed column would still be safe: a column keeps its holes only until its first break (that collapse closes them), and until then a blast never takes more from a block than from those below it, since they share one footprint and are at least 0.5" tall, the height a blast is measured from (classic's are 0.56" and 0.72"); so every block has at least the hp of those below it, and a higher block cannot break in a blast that only scuffs a lower one. A cap above a hole (the cap has a footprint of its own) or blocks under 0.5" could reach it, which F7's sets may build; `at` already covers that. A probe over boards 1-500, 40 blasts each (73,986 events, 7,513 hurts, 700 blasts with a hurt before a collapse), found every carried place equal to the live one when the call's events were played. So `at` changes nothing today. It is kept because it makes the hurt and destroy events self-contained for R5, whose view must not read the live chunk; the mirror, folded in event order, would give the same place (§2.3). One live read is later than the call and stays as it always was: the collapse's dust reads the block's place when its fall tween ends, and a later blast in the same volley may have lowered the block again by then. It is cosmetic. R5 replaces it with the resting place from the mirror (§2.3, R5's row), and `core/terrain/terrain.js`'s header says so.
- **The `?debug` surface**, adapted in place (sim/oracle untouched): `S` is a Proxy over main.js's `S` whose `stage`, `round`, `active`, `first`, `phase`, `vp` and `wiped` read the current `G.turn` (`wiped` undefined while −1) and refuse writes, and which lists and copies as a plain object would, turn fields included (`Object.keys`, `{...S}`, JSON; `structuredClone` refuses it, as it does any Proxy); `units`, `nav` and `scenery.chunks` are getters over the current G; `validEnd` and the ten `q` members keep today's arity (`q.canAct: (u) => canAct(G, u)`); `setUnitPos` is `moveUnit`. `trace` is one array for the page's lifetime, fed by each match's `onTrace` (under `?debug` main.js gives every match a forwarder to the block's listener, so `G.onTrace` is never set from the block; without `?debug` it is null, as §2.1 has it) and emptied when `start()` begins a battle: right after `startMatch`, `start()` calls the listener's `begin` (nothing without `?debug`), where R0-R3's `start()` emptied it, so between Again and the next start the trace still holds the last battle, as it always did. Not promised: `G`, for the console and `sim/rematch-check.mjs` (`G.out`; it also presses `#again`, `#reroll` and `#seed`: R0 notes), and for `sim/terrain-shots.mjs` `scenery.scene` and `scenery.blast` (a blast played as `blastLands` plays one: reports drained, nav refreshed), beside `clock`, `camera`, `renderer` and `S.titleSpin`, which stay where they were.

  - `core/journal.js`: `emit(G, t, payload)`, `emitTo(out, t, payload)` (the same rule onto an array the caller passes), `drain(G)` (all three function declarations, hoisted, so no module reading one as it loads can meet it uninitialised should `journal.js` join an import cycle), and `log(G, side, html, cls)`/`flush(G)`, which trace a battle-log line and emit its `log {side, html, cls, traced, at}` event, then a `traced: false` event per held-back destroyed-unit line, `at` being `G.journal.trace.length` (§4.1 rule 8's order). main.js's own `log()` is that plus a synchronous `show()`.
  - `present/mirror.js`: `project(G)` in §2.4's shape (owners -1 before the battle, as the flags showed), `applyEvent(M, e)` (folds in place and returns `M`; events that change nothing shown leave it), and `blankMirror()` for `sim/terrain-check.mjs`. `present/pace.js`: `PACE` (`phaseStart`, `dice`, `pause`, `beat`).

The converted actions write only `log` lines while the player is behind (morale's; damage writes none), so no state line waits and every shadow is taken against the state it always was. That a state line never waits is guarded, not assumed: a state line that waits keeps a fingerprint of what sim/oracle's shadow reads (the turn, `rngState`, every unit's place, radius, counts, flags and models, every chunk's `alive`, `hp` and shape), and joining the trace throws, naming the line, if the fingerprint has moved or the table has been replaced. R5b converts actions that write state lines (an `act`) while the player is behind; it must keep such lines from waiting, or carry the state with the line, which R6 must do (its row).

- **Spec changes made at R5a (for lead approval).** Each is applied in the body and marked "(R5a)" there.

  - R5's row: the three-pass split.

R6's step-machine sketch: `rolloff` sets the stage and emits `stage` and `objectives` before the roll-off, as `battle()` does today (it set the stage after). The transitional player's `reset` drops the old table's playback.

**R5b as built.** The second of R5's three passes (its row): `core/actions/fight.js`, then the charge split in `core/actions/charge.js`. Shoot and move still run the old async way in main.js until R5c, though the charge's move already walks the new way (below).
- **The fight.** `fight(G, u)` and `fightPhase(G, active)`, synchronous, in the old statement order: each `await` is an event in its place (the hit, wound and save rows as `dice`, the 0.3 s after a fight as `pause`), each visual a §2.3 event where the old code made it (`unit.face`, `focus`, `tray.open`, `melee`), the wounds and deaths `damage.js`'s as before, the battle-log line a `log`, and the alternation keeps its guard of 30 (§4.1 rule 6). main.js runs the phase as `await played(fightPhase(G, side))`, so the phase's `phase` state line is written after everything it emitted has played. Three choices:
  - `melee` carries `n` as well as `hits` (spec change below): the old code lunged before the hit roll and threw the sparks once its row had waited, so the event goes after the roll and before its `dice` (the lunge and the row share a frame, as before), and its handler throws the sparks `PACE.dice(n)` later, as that row settles. Nothing logic moves: only the lunge's visual statements cross the roll.
  - `focus` is emitted on every fight. The old test (`human(u.side) || human(target.side) || S.follow`) was true whenever `focus()` would do anything (it returns at once unless `S.follow`), so the view's own follow setting decides; `focus()` and `face()` read the stage, the seat to act and the places from the mirror, not G.
  - The phase's closing `status` stays (the old code refreshed every label there), though it repeats the last fight's damage's, which every fight ends in: a probe dropping it leaves P-present passing 40/40, so it is not among the self-test's mutations (§2.4).
- **The charge.** `chargeSpots(plan, rolled)` (the pick's mask, out of main.js's `pickChargeSpot`), `declareCharge(G, u, tg, via)` and `finishCharge(G, u, tg, cell, plan = chargePlan(G, u, tg))`, in the old order: the plan, `chargeTried`, the tray, the 2D6 and its row, the turn to face, then `charge.result` (the old "Charge failed" or "CHARGE!", where each was shown) and the log line; on contact the flags before the result, as before. `via` `'ai'` (an AI seat, or Auto; main.js passes `auto || !human(u.side)`, the old test) goes straight on to `finishCharge` with the plan in hand. A human's seat gets `{plan, rolled}` back, and main.js opens the pick as before (`S.chargePick`, a click through `nearestSpot`, `placeCharge`, Shortest move), then calls `finishCharge` with the cell, which remakes the plan from the unchanged match, as R6's `chargeEnd` will: P-human holds that to the old code at every one of the corpus's 125 human charge ends (50 Shortest move, 75 spots picked), so R6's recompute is already proven. `finishCharge` takes the shortest route to the cell, walks it (`resolveWalk`, next) and refreshes nav. No pile-in, though the step's brief named one: the old charge ended at its walk, and the only pile-in is `damage.js` `closeRanks`'s, after losses (§1.3's `relayout` row).
- **The act line never waits (the R5a follow-up).** Neither half ends the action: main.js's `finishAction` (the `act` state line, the flags, the labels, the `act` event and its `?debug` projection, the wipe check) still does, and only once the charge's events have played (`await played(declareCharge(…))`, then the pick and `await played(finishCharge(…))`, then `finishAction()`). So a charge's `act` line is written with the player idle and joins the `?debug` trace at once, its shadow taken against the match as it always was, and the hold's guard never sees a state line wait. The trace and the battle log come out in the old order: the "Contact!" and "Failed." lines are written while the player is behind, wait in the hold, and join at their `log` events. This is §2.2 with its step machine left to R6: from R6 the engine's `finishAction` is core's and the halves call it (R6's row), and then the `act` lines do wait, which R6's row already makes it carry the state for.
- **The walk, brought forward from R5c.** `finishCharge` walks (§2.2), and a core action cannot await the old tween, so `resolveWalk(G, u, pts, {speed, fly})` and `smashAround(G, u, sample, out)` moved into `core/actions/move.js` now. `resolveWalk` takes the old walk's samples (every 0.25" for a wrecker, plus the end point, in order, each smashing the live chunk list), keeps each sample's terrain events with its `s` (only when someone presents: a quiet run, `G.out` null, builds no event, as the fixer's round made it), and puts the unit at the k=1 lerp, exactly the old last frame (§4.1 rule 7); `unit.move` carries `to`, that place (spec change below). It then emits `objectives` and `status`: the flags and labels as the walk left them, where the old walk turned a flag on the frame it crossed and the ⚔ came with `finishAction` (in the same frame: the walk's handler ends with the old 0.15 s breath, and `finishAction` follows at once). main.js's `walked` handler is the old tween verbatim (and, like the fight's sparks, does nothing more once its table is replaced), moving a display place (`v.at`) that the ring, hit cylinder, figures and label follow until the walk ends (the mirror already holds the end), and playing each smash's terrain events as the walker passes `s`. The movement phase's `doMove` keeps the old walk until R5c; that walk now smashes through core's `smashAround` too (main.js's `smashNow`), and keeps its per-frame flags and its `checkpoint(['owners'])`.
- **What looks different from R5a** (none of it rules): a charging unit's objective flags turn as its walk ends rather than on the frame it crosses (a move's still turn mid-walk until R5c); a collapse inside a charge's walk raises its dust where the mirror has the block after the whole walk rather than after that drop (it differs only for a block dropped twice in one walk); the fight's sparks and lunges are timed by the handler rather than by the code around them, at the same game time.

- **Spec changes made at R5b (for lead approval).** Each is applied in the body and marked "(R5b)" there.

**R5c as built.** The third and last of R5's three passes (its row): the movement phase's actions in `core/actions/move.js`, then the shot in `core/actions/shoot.js`, then P-browser over the whole corpus. No rules action awaits anything now: main.js calls each as `await played(fn(G, …))` and then ends it (`finishAction`), and the AI still reaches them through `act`, main.js's wrappers, so its draws stay between the same awaits (§4.1 rule 10).
- **The move.** `doMove(G, u, cell, plan)` (the old `doMove` without its awaits: the path, `moved` and `fellBack`, the line with the route's length, the walk, `refreshNav` at its old site, §4.1 rule 9) walks through R5b's `resolveWalk`, so a move, an advance's move and a fall back are one `unit.move` each, played back by main.js's `walked`, as a charge's has been since R5b. `doAdvance(G, u)` is the tray, the D6 and its row, the flags and the line, and returns the roll; it writes no `act` line (§4.1 rule 8), and its wrapper ends nothing. `hold(G, u)` is the AI's spent move for an advanced unit it leaves standing (ai.js's direct `u.flags.moved = true`, §1.3), no event and no line, as before. Gone with the old walk: main.js's `walk` and `smashNow`; `moveUnit`'s per-frame `objectives` (it is a deployment's placement and `?debug`'s `setUnitPos` only now; (fixer round 2) in battle, which only `setUnitPos` reaches, it emits the flags and labels after the placement, as a walk does); the walk's `checkpoint(['owners'])`, so `checkpoint()` takes no `keys`; and present-hooks' `no-walk-owners`. `no-place` stays, re-aimed: it drops a deployment's placement, which the battle's start `check` catches in every human log that deploys.
- **The stomp.** The old `doMove` played `sfx.boom(0.4)` between its line and its walk when a wrecker set off on more than 0.1", and the charge never did. The core says so on the walk, `unit.move`'s `stomp` (spec change below), beside `speed` and `fly`, the other two things the caller says about how the walk looks; `walked` booms as it starts, in the frame the old code did.
- **The shot.** `doShoot(G, u, target)`, `blastVolley`, `eruption` (was `thornburst`), `blastLands` and `mesmerize`, synchronous, in the old statement order, each wait a `dice` or `pause` in place, each visual a §2.3 event where the old code made it: the turn to face (`unit.face`), the volley (`volley`, before its hit roll), each template's marker (`blast.aim`, before its hit roll), the marker's slide on a miss (`blast.scatter`, after the scatter row), the throw (`blast.fire`), the landing's explosion, boom and ring (`blast.land`, at `blastLands`' head), the cast's sound (`spell.cast`), the fizzle (`spell.fizzle`), the thorns (`spell.thorns`) and the gaze (`spell.gaze`). §4.1 rule 4's orders are kept exactly, each with its comment: per template the shooter's own unit, then the target (after the first), the aim's angle then offset, the hit roll, on a miss the scatter's D6 then angle; `blastLands`' victims all found first, in unit order, a big one's D6 before its wound roll; the gaze's D3 after the cast. Rule 5's no-save rolls still roll. The aim's `draw` moved with the volley, so main.js imports nothing of `core/rng.js` (§1.2). Two events beyond §2.3's list (spec change below): `spell.fade`, emitted when an eruption's template is done, where the old `thornburst` started its spikes sinking once `await blastLands` returned; and `spell.mesmerized`, the "Mesmerized!" over the target, after the gaze's damage and its `status`, where the old code floated it. `fx` (the weapon's look) rides in `volley`, `blast.fire` and `blast.land`, so `core/actions/shoot.js` reads `w.fx` to carry it, never to test it: flag-lint allows that one text there (`fx: w.fx`, three lines), and its self-test now also flags a test of `w.fx` beside it in core and an alias of it.
- **The handlers.** main.js's `volley` (the old `volleyFx`: a handful of projectiles, `min(10, n)`, from the figures standing), `aimed`, `scattered`, `fired` (the old `artilleryFire`, then the marker away), `landed`, `thorns` (the gem's motes, the spikes rising, their explosion; the spikes kept by caster until `faded` sinks them), `gaze` (the beam, then the rings) and the `spell.*` one-liners hold the old visuals verbatim, `projectileStyle` and `projGeo` unchanged. They read the mirror (`standing`, `top`, `shown`), never G. The marker and the spikes of a table replaced mid-shot (no path does that) are cleared by `setupTable` with the decals. (fixer round 2) And a handler that goes on after a wait (`volley`, `fired` and its throw, `thorns`, `gaze`) does nothing more once its table is replaced, as `walked` and `lunge` since R5b, so no scorch mark or projectile of the old table lands on the new one.
- **Display.** Every unit's place on the table now comes from the events: the mirror's (a placement, a formation, a walk's end) or, while a `unit.move` plays, `walked`'s display place (`v.at`). The old per-frame walk and its hacks are gone. What reads G is what acts only while the player is idle, as before (the input branches and previews, the range ring, the rings' highlight, the card's moved/shot/charged and cover). **R6a as built.** The first of R6's two passes (its row): the pure core, built beside main.js's old loop, which still plays the shipped game, and proved headless. Nothing in play changed: the page replays the corpus 40/40 as before, and the pure core folds the same 40 battles headless, 40/40.
- **The engine.** `core/engine.js`: `advance(G)`, §2.2's step machine (`rolloff`, `turnStart`, `phase`, `phaseEnd`, `turnEnd`, `score`), with `rollOff`, `resetTurn`, `endMesmerism`, `finishAction`, `checkWipe`, `scoreRound`, `gameOver(G, conceded)`, `runAI` and `humanSeats`, each the old loop's statements in their old order, so the trace lines up line for line. What the old loop showed itself is events now, at the same places: the stage and the flags at the roll-off, the roll-off's tray and dice rows (main.js's `battle()` still writes those to the tray directly), `phase.start`, the 0.2 s beat of a phase with nothing to do, the `status` after a turn's mesmerism wears off, `round.scored`, `act` (without `proj`: below), `stage` over and `game.over {win, why, vp, rounds}` ((fixer round 2) `rounds` the rounds played, the one under way counted: the last round on the score, the round it ended in for a wipe-out or a concession mid-round, and 0 for a concession in the deployment, where it had sent 1, the turn's round from the start (§2.3)), the result also in `G.turn.result`. The battle log's lines are the old ones, the names and shorts from the seats' races (`raceOf`), which is what `sidesFor` gave main.js. The step machine's `round` stops at the last round, where the old `for` loop left it one past; the G adapter (below) puts that quirk back for the shadow. `advance` ends with a `pending {k, seats}` event whenever it stops at a decision.
- **Commands.** `core/commands.js`: `HANDLERS` and `legal(G, seat, body)` for `place`, `deployed`, `advance`, `move`, `shoot`, `charge`, `chargeEnd`, `end`, `auto` and `concede` (§2.2's table; `vote` waits for F4). `legal()` asks, in order: a known kind; a seat that exists; no field but the kind's ((fixer round 1): a log entry's seat travels beside its body, so `sim/run.mjs` splits a corpus entry's `s` off) and those whole numbers; the battle not over; then (`concede` apart, which any human seat may send until the battle is decided: (fixer round 1) not once a side is wiped out mid-phase, where the battle only ends at the phase's end and a concession would have handed the win to an army with nothing standing) the seat holds the pending decision, the kind answers it, and inside a phase belongs to that phase; then the kind's own rule, the old click handler's check (and human-bot's): `placeOk` for a placement (freeSpot's cell test, pulled out into `core/deploy.js` with its checks in the same order), the unit the seat's own and standing, `!moved`, `!advanced` and `!isEngaged` for an advance, `validEnd` on the plan the move itself will make (from the unit's flags) for a move, `canShoot` and `shotInfo().ok` for a shot, `chargeTargets().includes` and a `chargePlan` for a charge, and for a picked end `chargeSpots` of the plan made again. It runs with the dice locked (`core/rng.js` `lock`: a draw throws) and leaves the lock as it found it. The handlers are §2.2's, the action's end (`finishAction`) in the handler, so main.js could keep calling the actions themselves until R6b; and the `charge` handler opens the charge's decision from `declareCharge`'s `{plan, rolled}`. (R6b) Approved, and so as built: the handlers own the decision and `finishAction`, and main.js calls no action.
- **The API.** `core/index.js`: `createMatch(setup, {out, onTrace, strict})`, `pendingSeats`, `legal`, `apply` (a handler, then `advance`), `preview(G, fn)`, `q` and `RULES_ID`. `fullSetup` fills a setup's defaults (the classic terrain, the mission's rounds, overtime `'never'`, shared dice; (fixer round 1) also for a field given as null or undefined, as a form's empty field is; (fixer round 2) keeping the setup's key order, its own fields first and then the defaults it left out, where it had put the defaults' keys first) and refuses seeds outside 0 to 2^32 − 1, rounds under 1 ((fixer round 3) or over `MAX_ROUNDS`, 99: `createMatch` plays an all-AI battle to its end before it returns, and one neither army wipes out lasts its rounds, so a typo or a peer's setup asking for a million would block every fold of it), `overtime: 'vote'` (F4) and any other dice mode. `pendingSeats` answers a copy ((fixer round 1): sorting or editing it leaves the match's decision be). ((fixer round 2) §2.2's API block lists `fullSetup` and the copying `pendingSeats`; (fixer round 3) `core/index.js`'s header lists `fullSetup` too, and §2.2's `stateHash` and `shadowState` lines and §1.1's `stateHash, shadowState, CORE_VERSION` are marked (R8), when they join.) (fixer round 3) `newState`'s G holds `pending: null` and `strict: false` from the start, in §2.1's order, so `G.pending` is never missing (an all-AI match had run without the key until `gameOver` set it, and R8's `stateHash` hashes `pending` as canonical JSON, which drops an undefined key and keeps a null); `createMatch` still sets `strict`. `createMatch` logs "deploy your army" for each human seat in seat order and opens one `deploy` decision for all of them (§0.1: the trace and the battle log are the old sequential deployments', since a placement neither traces nor draws); with no human seat the whole battle runs inside the call. `preview(G, fn)` is new: `fn(G, q)` with the dice locked, which R6b's `Session.preview` is (nothing above core/ may import `rng.js`, §1.2).
- **One AI.** `core/ai/policy.js` (`ORDER`, `aiPhase` and its move, shoot and charge generators) and `core/ai/score.js` (`worth`, `meleeValue`, `shotValue`, `bestSpot`, `score`) are ai.js moved verbatim into §2.2's generators, and ai.js is gone. `await act.doX(…)` became `yield {t, …}`, the advance's roll is read back from `advRoll`, `act.focus` became a `focus` event and the waits `pause` events (0.05 s after each unit's move, 0.1 s after a shot or a charge); `hold` is called by the generator itself, never yielded. main.js's old loop drives the same generators (`aiTurn`, also behind Auto): each command through the wrappers a click uses, its events played before the generator is asked for the next, the generator's own events played before each command and after the last. So the shipped game and the fold cannot run two AIs. P-present counts the same 3,309 acts and 4,400 checks as at R5c (the `focus` and `pause` events change nothing the mirror holds, and its event-order rules still hold).
- **The turn, §2.1's in both loops.** `newState` builds `G.turn` with `step`, `t`, `ph` (in place of `phase`), `result` and `overtime`. `phaseKey(G)` (`core/queries.js`) is the phase's key, clamped to the last phase once `ph` runs past it (the engine's turn end and score, where the legacy shadow and the mirror still say `morale`). main.js's loop sets `ph`, every read of the key is `phaseKey(G)`, `present/mirror.js` projects it, and the `?debug` `S.phase` derives it (sim/oracle unchanged). main.js's per-table G keeps stage `'title'`, `step` null and `t` 0 until R6b.
