- **P-prop.** `sim/property.mjs` (its header says it all): (1) at every decision (each entry of every corpus human log, each decision of 32 random games) `legal()` judges a battery of commands (every kind, for both seats and seats that don't exist, junk bodies, `hold`, `vote`) and the previews a seat's tools run go through `preview()`: nothing may throw, move the dice, change the match (the full shadow, the turn, the decision, the journal, the nav's dirt) or leave the dice locked, and the probed corpus folds must still replay their recorded streams; a draw while locked throws, and `legal()` and `preview()` restore the lock as they found it. (2) Everything folds `strict`, so every AI command of every AI phase and Auto is held to `legal()`. (3) Random legal play (random seeds, races with mirror matches and swapped seats, every seat mix, 1 to 10 rounds; half the games aggressive, which is what wipes an army out) never throws, ends, keeps the invariants between commands (waiting exactly while not over, on human seats only; the nav never dirty; standing units on the table; the dice unlocked; trace and dice forward only; no closure, promise or generator in G but `out` and `onTrace`), and ends with the result its score, wipe-out or concession says. (4) Two games with human seats, interleaved command by command in one process, each trace as alone (§4.1 rule 13). R6 is complete: the shipped page, every mode, plays the pure core through one Session, and the old loop is gone. - **Every mode one Session.** `match/store.js` and `match/session.js`, as §2.6's (R6b) note has them (a `LocalStore` of plain entries, `{s: -1, t: 'start', setup}` and then `{s, …body}`; a `Session({store, localSeats, sink, onTrace})` that folds each entry as it is appended, hands its events to the sink and keeps none in `G.out`). main.js's `start(mode)` builds the whole setup (the title's board seed, a fresh dice seed or `?dice`, the races at the table, the mode's controllers), a `LocalStore` and a Session whose `localSeats` are the mode's human seats, and appends the start: the match runs on at once, to the human seats' deployment or, watching, to its end, and the table plays it from there. Retired from main.js: `battle()`, `playerTurn()`, `scoreRound()`, `gameOver()`, `finishAction()`, `checkWipe()`, `aiTurn` (the engine's `runAI` drives the generators inside the fold), the action wrappers (`doMove`, `doAdvance`, `doShoot`, `doCharge`), `pickChargeSpot` and its promise, `phaseResolve`, `S.busy`, `S.auto`, `S.waiting`, `S.deployDone`, `S.chargePick`, `S.deploySide`, `moveUnit`, and main.js's own events (it imports neither `core/journal.js` nor `core/rng.js` nor any action). The view learned the core's events: `stage` (the zones, the selection), `phase.start` (the banner, which the table waits on, `PACE.phaseStart` from the mirror's seat and stage), `round.scored` (a ring on each objective its owners hold, the score's banner), `game.over` (the end screen, worded from `why` and `rounds`: "Final score 7 – 10 after 5 rounds.", "… have been wiped from the table in round 3.", "… conceded in round 3." or "in the deployment.") and `pending` (nothing: the table asks once it has played everything); the roll-off's `tray.open` and `dice` go through the tray's handlers.
- **The title's backdrop.** No match exists before a mode is chosen: on the title `session` and `G` are null. `showTable(board)` draws a backdrop instead: a match on the board seed that is never played (`createMatch` with both seats human, so it stops at its deployment having drawn nothing; its dice, 0, are never rolled), its board played from its terrain events (the rest of what it reported, its deployment's lines, dropped), figures made for its units. It is kept only to be drawn, for the card's cover on the title, and for its nav grid's geometry, which sim/oracle's driver captures as the page loads. `start()` then resets the player to a copy of the mirror on show and asks the sink to drop the battle's board events (its `terrain.clear` and an add per chunk, which come first): the same seed gives the same defs (§2.9), so the backdrop's `TerrainView` already shows them, and `bindViews` points each figure's view at the battle's unit of the same id (the same type and seat: `newState` is a function of the setup, and neither the controllers nor the dice move a unit before the battle), making the figures afresh only if they ever differ. So one `TerrainView` from the title into the battle, no rebuild flash, no figure rebaked, and P-present holds the shown table to the battle's match at every checkpoint. `TABLE_DICE` went (main.js draws one `Math.random` fewer as it loads: view only); `core/match.js` `startMatch` went, and `newState` starts the turn at stage `'deploy'`, step `'rolloff'` (`'title'` is now only the mirror's stage for the backdrop). A second `start()` without the end screen's Back draws a fresh backdrop first. (R7a) The backdrop is now a quiet match (`out: null`: nothing it does is reported) drawn by a snap, and `start()` snaps the table to the backdrop, the battle's table as it stood before anything happened (the same board, terrain and races; `sameUnits` checks the battle's units against it), in place of the dropped board events and `bindViews` (§2.4's (R7a) note).

The page now takes each seed `>>> 0`, which is what mulberry32 and `createRng` always did with one, so every input draws the board and dice it did before: a watched battle on `?seed=-5`, `1.5`, `5000000000` and `?dice=-3`, `2.5`, `5e9` traced exactly as at HEAD (R6a, under the fake DOM). They now stay up, disabled, while the table plays the seat's own actions, a charge's roll and walk included, and hide only while the pick waits (§2.5's (R6b's fixer, round 3) note: a view-only `buttonsUp`, set once the player has caught up to the seat's phase and cleared when the decision is neither that phase nor that seat's `chargeEnd`). **R7a as built.** The first of R7's two passes (its row; the lead's split): the view. Every three.js object the page draws is now made and played by `view/`'s modules, and the camera's poses come from `present/camera-presets.js`; main.js keeps the input, the HUD, the tray, the log, the card, the screens, the flow and the `?debug` block (R7b's), and makes the view's modules in their old order (2,357 lines to 1,648 after R7a's fixer, round 3). No logic touched: `core/`, `data/` and `match/` are unchanged (the view needed nothing beyond `sim/boundaries.mjs`'s `SURFACE`), the corpus replays 40/40 through the core, on the page and in Chromium, and the title at 1200 ms is HEAD's pixel for pixel with the figures hidden.
- **The modules** (§1.1's (R7a) marks). `view/stage.js` (`Stage`: the renderer, the scene and its fog, the labels' layer; `light()`; `run({parts, rig, shake})`, the frame loop, with `?fast`'s clock speed and no drawing); `view/clock.js` (util.js's clock, tweens, waits and easings; util.js deleted, its `lerp` and `pick` `core/util.js`'s); `view/camera.js` (`CameraRig`: the camera and its orbit controls as they were set up, follow, the title's spin and angle, the panel shift, the panning keys, `fit(preset)`, `goTo(preset)`, `toTitle()`, `focus(x, z, …)`, and the shake's three draws a frame); `view/table.js` (`Table`: the mat, the wood, the board, the zones, the tufts and flowers; `paint`, `zones(opacity)`, `scatterTufts`); `view/objectives.js`; `view/overlay.js` (the reach texture, the range ring, the path line, the ghost); `view/units.js` (`UnitViews`, below); `view/effects/fx.js` (fx.js moved) and `view/effects/shots.js` (`Shots`: the volley, the projectile styles, a blast's aim, scatter, fire and landing, the artillery's arc, the spell's cast, fizzle, thorns, fade, gaze and mesmerism, `clear()`); `view/models/` (models.js split: `kit.js` the parts and materials, `squirrel.js` and `serpent.js` each kit's builders, `bake.js`, `cache.js` the templates, below); `view/sfx.js` (sfx.js moved; a race's cry is `VOICES[look.voice]` through `sfx.voice(name)`, where data-check now reads the voices); `view/terrain.js` (`TerrainView` gains `sync`, its spares, `dispose` and `free`: §2.9's (R7a) note). The handlers main.js gives the player are one-liners into these.
- **The snap** (§2.4's (R7a) note). `EventPlayer.snap(G, shown)` rebuilds the table from `G` as it stands: `TerrainView.sync(chunks)`, `UnitViews.sync(units, edgeOf)` (`edgeOf(seat)`, each seat's edge, which a view is made for), `Shots.clear()` and `fx.clearDecals()` ((R7a's fixer, round 3): fx's scorch and acid marks). `UnitViews` keeps the views by unit id, each holding only what doesn't change (its type, seat, edge and colour) and reading the mirror for the rest; `sync` keeps a view whose four match and makes the others, and for each model: a dead one's figure off the table and freed; a live one's rebuilt if it was dying, fleeing or carried off; its pose reset (yaw, look, lunge, lift, flash); then its disc, stand and label. `showTable` draws the backdrop with a snap (a quiet match, `out: null`, at the stage `'title'`; the battlefield synced, then the tufts strewn, then the snap, the order its draws always came in), and `start()` snaps the table to the backdrop, the battle's table as it stood before anything happened (the same board, terrain and races: the backdrop stands in for the battle's match, which has already run on by the time the sink sees it), at the title's stage too (`onTitle`: the battle's deployment `stage` then moves the mirror on, as P-present requires), in place of R6b's dropped board events and `bindViews`: the battle's board events (its `terrain.clear` and an add per chunk) now play, and the adds take back the meshes on show, untouched and of the same def, so nothing is rebuilt; the sink checks that the battle's units are the table's (`sameUnits`, by type and seat: the battle's `G` has run on past its start when the sink first sees it, a watched battle's to its end, so where its units stood then is no longer in it) and throws if not. P-present therefore folds 65,996 events, 3,090 more than at R6b: the corpus battles' boards.
- **The template cache** (§2.11's (R7a) note). A figure is a base made for it (its seat's colour on the rim, its flock at random) carrying a miniature built and baked once per (models kit, unit) and then cloned, sharing the template's geometry and materials; a builder that draws `Math.random` itself (a kit's `DRAWS`: the trebuchet's acorns) is built afresh every time. A figure leaving the table for good frees what only it used (`userData.own`: its base; a drawn miniature too), and a template's geometry is kept for the next table. Cosmetic consequence: three.js draws four `Math.random` for every object it makes (its uuid), and a unit's first figure now makes more objects than a build did (the template, then its clone) and each later one fewer (a clone), so the bases' flocks and the idle phases fall from another point of the stream than before (later at first, earlier from about a unit's third figure on). Unseeded in play, so nothing observable; under a seeded stream (`sim/title-shot.mjs`) the title differs in the figures' flocks and idle phases only (about 25,000 pixels of 1,024,000 on each of three seeds), every figure in its place, its miniature vertex for vertex (the trebuchet's, drawn at random, mesh for mesh).
- **Load order and `Math.random`.** For the same reason what the view makes as the page loads, and in which order, decides every cosmetic draw on the title: the mat's paint, the wood, the tufts, the flowers. The modules are made in main.js's old order, and the shapes several views share are made with the view or when first needed rather than as their module loads (the projectiles' with the shooting's view, `Shots`, where main.js made them before; the rings, the hit cylinders and the thorns at their first use) (made at load they shifted the board's paint: a first title shot differed in 83% of its pixels). `sim/terrain-shots.mjs` holds the five boards to R0 pixel for pixel, and `sim/title-shot.mjs` the title at 1200 ms to HEAD with the figures hidden.
- **A dropped block falls to where the match puts it** (changes a player can see, for approval). R0's collapse tween dropped a block by the drop from where the block was drawn as the collapse began; when two blocks under it broke in one blast or sweep, the second fall started where the first had begun, and the block came to rest a level or more above its place in the match (board 1's chunk 38: a cap drawn at 1.88", resting at 0.44"), a floating block until the next table. Each fall now runs from where the block is drawn to the height the match gives it, and a newer fall cuts an older one off. `TerrainView.sync` found it (a table built from the chunks disagreed with the one the events built). `sim/terrain-check.mjs` holds the working tree to R0's code with the same rule made in R0's tween (`sim/terrain-hooks.mjs`'s `R7_FALL`, as R5's dust edit was): over boards 1-500, 3,602 of 8,287 falls began while the block was still falling. And a hurt block's shudder is now sideways only, giving back only the place it shook: R0's held the block at the height it was hit at for its quarter second and then put it back there, so a block the same blast dropped and then hurt hung at its old height while it shook, and stayed there when its fall had ended in the same frame as the shudder (`?fast`, or a long frame at 4×). The snap check found it, on 64886-198528 (the table as played kept the block 1.44" above its place). R0's shudder draws the same `Math.random` in the same order, so nothing else moves; terrain-check, whose clock steps a frame at a time, never let a fall end in the shudder's frame, and passes either way.
- **The camera** (§2.11's (R7a) note). `sim/camera-check.mjs` (266 checks since R7a's fixer) runs R0's `defaultView`, `fitFov`, the camera as made, the title's angle and spin and the focus rule, taken from the R0 main.js's text, against the presets (on 13 screens, a 0×0 one among them), holds them frozen, and holds `fitPose`'s promise (every board corner in frame with its padding, at most `max`); and (R7a's fixer) it makes the `CameraRig` itself in Node over a stand-in canvas and swings it with `goTo` onto every preset (landscape, portrait, broadside, behind either edge) on four screens, the tween run out and the controls updated: each comes to rest where `fitPose` puts it (a pose preset exactly where it says, a portrait broadside 77" and 86" out, past the old limit), and back on the title the dolly limit is 75 again. As first built, `goTo` took only a pose (pos and target), so a fitted preset threw, and the controls would have pulled a broadside back to 75.
- **The `?debug` surface.** sim/oracle and `sim/chromium.mjs` unchanged. It splits: the view's own table, exported by `view/` beside `rebuild` (a facade module, say `view/index.js`, that makes the view's modules in their order and hands out `{ handlers, rebuild }`; `rebuild` then lives in `view/`, not `app/`, and takes away what the view holds outside the mirror as it does now: the shooting's marker and thorns and, since R7a's fixer, round 3, fx's scorch and acid marks, which N2's snaps mid-battle depend on), and the UI's and the flow's, which `app/flow.js` merges in before it makes the player. A snap mid-battle (N2's rejoin, scrub, catch-up) would leave them stale: snapped after the battle's `stage` and before its first `phase.start` has played, a local seat holding its phase decision gets no End and no Auto (`refreshUI`'s `mine` is false) and no hint; snapped past `game.over`, `#over` (and Back to the war room on it) never shows, nor the banner or the log. `present/hud-model.js` derives them from the mirror and the pending decision (a phase has been shown once the mirror's stage is `'battle'` after a snap, `project(G)` carrying the turn fields; the buttons up once the player is idle on a local seat's decision), `ui/screens/result.js` shows the end screen whenever the mirror's stage is `'over'`, and the flow resets what is left when a snap idles (`onIdle({ snap: true })`). A check snaps mid-battle (in the roll-off, in a local seat's phase, past `game.over`) and asserts End and Auto up for the seat's phase and the end screen up (in `sim/snap-check.mjs`, or a check of its own).

Heap snapshots on the title after battle 1, 5 and 9 of one page (a scratch probe, as `sim/rematch-memory.mjs` plays them): the title's heap grows 797 KB from battle 1 to battle 9 (633 KB to battle 5, 164 KB more to battle 9: slowing), of which 687 KB is V8's compiled code and 50 KB its internal lists (`WeakArrayList`), 41 KB the browser's performance timeline (event and long-animation-frame entries, bounded buffers), and a few KB of the page's own objects, up and down. So the title retains nothing of the game's: the growth is the engine warming up (more of the code compiled, and optimised, the more battles run), and there is nothing to free. `sim/rematch-memory.mjs` therefore judges the page's own heap instead of a flat 2 MB allowance on all of it: on each title after a battle it takes a heap snapshot and sums what the page holds, V8's code, hidden lists and shapes and the performance timeline left out, and fails when that grows by more than 16 KB a rematch (the least-squares slope); the heap in use is reported, not judged. **R8 as built.** The last refactor step (its row): the netplay seams, pure. Every mode now plays through the Folder, the replicated authority of §2.6, with envelopes written, stored as text and decoded as a peer's would be, so a game played alone exercises the validator that guards online play; and the gates hold the Folder to it under concurrency with no Automerge in the package. Nothing in play changed: the corpus replays 40/40 through the Folder (parity's default), on the page under the fake DOM, and in Chromium over the whole corpus.
- **The seams** (§2.6's (R8) note has each as built). `core/hash.js`: `shadowState(G)`, §2.6's list as one string (numbers by `String(n)`), and `stateHash(G)`, its cyrb53 in base 36. `core/version.js`: `CORE_VERSION = 1`. `core/index.js` exports them, and `KINDS` (`core/commands.js`'s command kinds, which the envelope decodes no other than: a name `sim/boundaries.mjs`'s doors list now lets `index.js` pass on) and `canonicalJSON` (how an entry is written), and (R8's fixer) `cyrb53` (the Folder's head after a simultaneous decision closes); core's code otherwise unchanged (additions only: the exports and `KINDS`). `match/envelope.js`: `ENVELOPE_KEYS`, `MAX_BYTES`, `newEntryId`, `envelope`, `encode`, `decode`, `bodyOf`, and (R8's fixer, round 3) `MAX_NAME` and `isName`. `match/fold.js`: the `Folder` (`SIMULTANEOUS`, `MAX_ENTRIES`): the checks in §0.2 #2's order, the heads, `h` by kind, out of band, the cap, the desync freeze with a report, `skew`, `tamper`, `sync` with a quiet refold and `reset`. `match/store.js`: `LocalStore` keeps texts and hands out decoded entries. `match/session.js`: the Session over a Folder, `start(setup)`, the device, the head and the hash on what it writes, a desync it finds said out of band.
- **Every mode through the Folder.** `app/flow.js`'s `start()` names this device (`DEVICE`, `'local'`) on each human seat of the setup, makes the Session with it and calls `session.start(setup)`; a start the core refuses leaves the log in its lobby (`session.error`), where R6b's Session said `'refused'`, and the flow draws the title's table again as before. The Session still hands the sink one entry's events at a time, so the card's facts pair with each entry's `act` events and its `pending` takes the match's facts as before (What R8 inherits, R7b), and the Folder passes the flow's `onTrace` to `createMatch` (the card's facts, `?debug`'s trace). The sink gains `reset(G, session, {undone})`, a snap to the match (never called in a game played alone, whose log only grows at its end). No other file of the page changed: input, the HUD and the `?debug` block ask the Session as before (`legal`, `submit`, `preview`, `decisionFor`, `G`, `localSeats`).
- **Parity through the Folder.** `sim/run.mjs` `foldJob` writes each battle's log as a device would (device `sim`, named on each human seat of the start; each entry after its seat's head, with the hash where one seat is waited on; a concession out of band), encodes and decodes each entry and pushes it through the code under test's own Folder (`loadMatch(dir)`); its result says `via: 'folder'` only when that Folder accepted the start and every entry played and its match is the one traced (R8's fixer: it said so whenever the code had a Folder), `'bypassed'` otherwise, and `'core'` for code older than R8, folded as R6a did. `node sim/parity.mjs` says it folds "through its Folder, every entry an envelope" and fails a battle of code with a Folder that went another way (a scratch copy whose Folder leaves its `end`s out of `accepted` fails hotseat-late-8 so). P-prop's corpus folds, its quiet folds and its refolds of random logs go through it too.
- **P-merge** (`sim/merge-sim.mjs`, new; its header says it all). No Automerge: a shared append-only list whose ops name the element they follow and carry a Lamport stamp, ordered on every peer as Automerge orders a list (RGA: concurrent inserts after one element, highest stamp first, the higher actor winning a tie), delivered causally in a seeded random order (a random linear extension of the appends' causal DAG; each peer holds a causally closed subset at every moment) in batches of one to three, each batch one notice to the peer's Session, as a sync message. Every corpus human log is played by its human seats on peers of their own (seat *s* from device `d<s>`; the lowest human seat writes the start), with a spectator, each seat sending the log's next command for it whenever its own view waits on it (so the two deployments interleave), while every peer slips in, a few times a battle, what must be refused alike: junk texts (not JSON, an array, an empty object, an unknown kind, a fraction, a string field, keys out of canonical order, over 1 kB, no id, a start with a stray field, a desync carrying a number, and (R8's fixer) a start whose setup holds `1e999`), a duplicate of an entry's text, the seat's next command with a stray top-level field, after an older head, while the other seat is waited on, or from a device not the seat's, and a spectator's concession or desync for a seat it doesn't play. Three scenarios per log (`--seeds`, default 3): plain; fork (a second peer on seat 0's own device playing the same commands: same-seat forks); concede (a seated peer concedes out of band at a random moment). The AI pairs run as a start with spectators slipping junk in. At the end, every op on every peer: the same list, status, `accepted`, `rejected` (ids and whys) and `stateHash` on every peer, each the single-process fold of the final list (a fresh Folder); each peer's match traces that fold, and, unless a seat conceded, the corpus log's own single-process trace (`foldJob`, held to the baseline first); each peer's view (its sink's events folded into a mirror, snapped to the match on a reset) is `project(G)`, and (R8's fixer) at every batch its sink is handed the Session is already the match the events lead to (its `preview` works, its decision is the batch's last stop, the view is `project(session.G)`, a refold's included); no two accepted commands of a seat after one head; every slipped-in entry refused for a reason its kind allows and every honest one accepted (in a fork scenario stale or, past the fork's winner, not its turn); a reset with one device per seat undoes nothing (in a plain scenario: R8's fixer, round 2, §2.6's (R8) note on a concession racing a move); (R8's fixer, round 2) every accepted entry carries `h` exactly where §0.2 #3 says by the kind of decision it answered (the spec's `phase` and `chargeEnd`, never the code's `SIMULTANEOUS`) and an out-of-band one neither `h` nor `p`, each kind met over the run; and over the run each kind meets its own reason, sync refolds quietly, resets, and undoes a fork's loser. Three more: **cap** (a spectator floods past 5,000 entries while a seat plays on: both peers `'full'` at the list's 5,001st entry, agreeing; (R8's fixer, round 2) the spec's 5,000, never the code's `MAX_ENTRIES`), **edges** (one process: a start under another `CORE_VERSION` or `RULES_ID` is `'skew'` with no match, later entries inert; a start naming no device for a human seat is refused and a good one then begins the match; an online log's `open` names the one device whose start counts, the start after it; a second start is refused; an accepted entry gone from the list is `'tamper'`, reported, and (R8's fixer) stays so when it comes back after an insert; decode refuses each junk text and throws on none; an entry with another match's hash and a body this match refuses freezes it, never a rejection (the hash before `legal()`); a Session with a page-like sink, reading `session.G`, `preview` and `accepted` at each batch, through a first match that arrives by a refold (junk first, its start inserted before it) and through a refold that catches up and then shows the next entry; a start no peer could decode, over 1 kB, holding `NaN` or from a device whose ids run past 64 characters, never appended, the Session in its lobby saying why) and (R8's fixer) **forks** (one process, each hotseat log: a same-seat fork in the deployment, the losing tab first placing a unit on another cell, the other seat closing the deployment having seen neither branch; in the losing world the first single seat's decision is answered, by the forked seat and, the fork on the other seat, by the seat that saw only the loser; on the final list that answer is stale, never a desync, the winning world's answer is played, the match live; a Folder that showed the losing world resets, undoing the loser's entries and the answer; one that showed the winner's refolds without a reset; all agree with the single-process fold).
- **The desync drill** (six of merge-sim's scenarios in the final tree: the three `hypot` drills here, the third R8's fixer's, and R8's fixer's round 2's two `late` drills and a `deaf` one, below): hotseat-aggressive-103 and -125, each seat on its own peer and a spectator, one seat's peer (seat 1 of -103, seat 0 of -125, and seat 0 of -103) running a copy of the code whose two-argument `hypot` answers an ulp high (`r + r * Number.EPSILON`). Its match drifts at once (a unit's radius is a `hypot`), so the first entry written for one seat's decision is found apart by `h`: that peer freezes at it (`by: 'hash'`) and appends a desync out of band; the other seat's peer freezes on that entry; the spectator by the hash or the entry; all three at the same entry, each with a report (setup, entries, accepted, rejected, both hashes crossed between the seats, the last 50 trace lines, the state). In the first two the drifted peer writes that entry and the spectator finds it apart by its own hash; in the third an honest seat writes it, the drifted peer finds it apart, and the spectator, whose match is the author's, freezes on the drifted peer's desync entry; the run requires both.

- **R8's fixer, round 1.** The four confirmed findings, fixed at the root:

- **R8's fixer, round 3.** The confirmed finding and the three rules the independent gate mutants found unguarded, fixed at the root:
  - *The Session and the Folder were not reentrant.* A sink that submitted while a change of several entries was being folded (from the events it is handed: an autopilot, an auto-End; N2's rejoin and sync messages fold many entries in one change) made the Session fold the store again inside the fold under way, and the outer fold then pushed the same entries a second time, each refused as `envelope: an id seen before`: this peer's `rejected`, `report.entries` and `pushed` apart from every other peer's and the single-process fold's, its cap reachable early (reproduced: a store of 8 entries pushed 14 times, six spurious refusals). `match/session.js`'s `onChange` is not reentrant now: a change made while one is folded sets a flag and returns, and the fold under way takes another pass once it is done (`do … while (again)`), so a sink's entry is folded right after the change in hand, stale when a later entry of that change moved its seat's head, as on every peer; the flag drops in a `finally` (a sink that throws no longer leaves the Session deaf to every later change); `sink.status` is called once a change, after its passes (a nested fold could tell one change twice); the desync is said after the flag drops (its append a change of its own). `Folder.sync` refuses reentry loudly (it throws, and frees itself when `each` throws; `show()`'s swap keeps the flag), so N1/N2 code that calls it directly fails at once instead of splitting `rejected` silently. The Session's header and §2.6's (R8) note say what a sink's submit means: written on the match after the entry whose events it was handed, folded after the change, one command a call; a sink that answers decisions answers every batch it is handed (a refused answer hands on no events), the last of a change standing. Held by edges' five new cases, each Session judged against a fresh Folder over its store's final list (accepted, refused, status, and as many entries pushed as the list holds): a sink submitting on the start's events as the Session is made over a store of seven entries; one submitting while a refold shows what follows (junk inserted before folded entries); an autopilot answering every batch, which plays the log on to its end through one change after another, the corpus battle traced and never `'full'`; a sink that throws, the Session folding the next change; `Folder.sync` entered again from its own `each`, which throws, and folds on after a sink that throws. Mutants `session-reentrant` (caught by the Folder's throw), `sync-reentrant` and `session-no-finally`.
  - *Three Folder rules no gate held* (the independent gate mutants `missing-h-accepted`, `over-any-device` and `core-newer-only` passed P-merge and P-prop; merge-sim's honest writers always write `h`, its `device` kind plays only while the match is live, and edges tried only a newer `CORE_VERSION`). Edges now pushes a phase entry with no `h` (a desync by the hash, `theirs` null, never accepted), a hashed `end` on an over match's final head from a spectator's device and from one the seat isn't played from (inert, the match still over; then the same from the seat's own device, a desync by the hash) and a start under an older `CORE_VERSION` (skew); the three are merge-sim mutants now, caught by the edges.

- **Spec changes made at R8 (for lead approval).** Each is applied in the body and marked "(R8)" there.
  - §2.6: the envelope's, the Folder's, the stores' and the Session's settled details (its (R8) note): decode refuses non-canonical text; the Folder's own kinds' fields; the reasons' words, inert entries listed as rejections; the `open` accepted; a refused start leaves the lobby (`'refused'` gone); a human seat must name its device; the "same decision" by the turn's clock; the report's fields; `sync(entries, each)` and `{events, reset, undone}`; tamper within a Folder's life; the Session's `start`, `dev`, `rand`, `strict` and sink signatures.
  - §2.6: **a reset is also two seats' simultaneous entries in another order**, not only a same-seat fork or tamper; the strict rule kept, with `undone` (0 then) for N2's toast.
  - §1.2's match/ row: the host's tokens the consensus code is denied are denied to match/ too (the Folder's verdicts depend on the list alone); the doors list: `index.js` passes on `KINDS`.
  - §1.1 and §2.2: `index.js` also exports `KINDS` and `canonicalJSON`.
  - The battle log through a refold or a reset is not kept or rebuilt yet (N2's, §2.6's (R6a) note, marked there): no mode played on one device refolds.
  - (R8's fixer) §2.6, the per-seat heads: **when a simultaneous decision closes, the head is a digest of every seat's head in it**, not the closing entry (it opens the next one too); a same-seat fork's losing world writing on after the close is then stale, not a desync of the whole match. §1.1 and §2.2: `index.js` also exports `cyrb53` for it.
  - (R8's fixer) §2.6's (R8) note: a refold is swapped into the Folder before any of its events is handed on (the sink reads the match they lead to); `decode` never throws; the tamper freeze holds for the Folder's life; the Session appends only what `decode` takes (a start it can't write leaves the lobby with `error`) and calls `sink.reset` only with a match; `-0` prints apart in `shadowState`; `SIMULTANEOUS` is an array.
  - (R8's fixer, round 2) §2.6, the sketch's "over or frozen: later entries are inert" and the "On a desync" bullet: **after the end, a seat's `desync` and a seat's hashed command on the final head still freeze the match** (the (R8) note); the closing hash is N2's (§2.7's desync note).
  - (R8's fixer, round 2) §2.6's (R8) note: an accepted id whose first good entry is another body is tamper; the Folder reads `h` only where it checks one and neither `p` nor `h` out of band (§0.2 #3's and #6's "never present" a writers' rule, which P-merge holds); the report's entries are decoded, the dialog adding the store's texts; a reset with one device per seat may undo a move a racing concession cut off.
  - (R8's fixer, round 2) §2.6's and §2.7's `MatchStore`: `append(entry | text)`, the text pushed as it is; `entries()` cached per list element or text, never per index alone (§2.7's `AutomergeStore` bullets, marked (R8)).
  - (R8's fixer, round 2) §1.2's `match/` row: module-level mutable state is denied to `match/` as to `core/`.
  - (R8's fixer, round 3) §2.6's (R8) note: **the Session's and the Folder's folds are not reentrant**: a sink's submit while a change is folded is appended at once and folded once that change is done (stale when a later entry moved its seat's head; one command a sink call), and `Folder.sync` throws when entered again; the accepted entries are held to the order they were folded in (a copy inserted before its own head is tamper); a human seat's device must be a name an entry can carry; an online log's start from another device than its opener's sets `error`; `session.error` is cleared once a start begins the match; `Session.start(setup, {a})`.
- **The refactor ends at R8: its three claims, confirmed.**
  - *The core runs headless in Node.* Parity's default runner folds the corpus through the pure core with three.js and the fake DOM refused as it loads (`sim/run.mjs`'s guard); P-prop, P-merge, the drill and data-check run it in plain Node too.
  - *Every mode goes through one Session and Folder.* `app/flow.js`'s `start()` is the only place a battle is made, every mode by its title-screen button, through a Session over a LocalStore whose Folder folds the start and every command (`?debug`'s hooks send through the same Session); the title's backdrop is a quiet match no one plays (`createMatch` for the table's look, R6b), no battle. sim/'s folds (parity's, P-prop's, P-merge's) go through the Folder too.
  - *Every seam R0 needs exists, and is tested in Node without any Automerge dependency.* Commands, `legal`, the `Folder`, `MatchStore` (`LocalStore`, and merge-sim's store over its RGA list), the `Session`, `stateHash`, `CORE_VERSION`, `RULES_ID`, the per-match dice and dmath; the package names no `@automerge/*` and `sim/boundaries.mjs` holds match/ to no package at all.
- **What N0, N1-N3 and F4 inherit.**
  - N0: `stateHash` prints every unit position, radius and model slot to the last bit (`String(n)`, `-0` apart), so a peer on an engine whose `sin`, `cos` or `atan` differ freezes the match at the first single-seat entry after a formation built with them: the drill's path. Not so for the board (R8's fixer): a chunk's `x`, `z`, yaw and extents (core/terrain/recipes.js, a toppled log's placement) are built with `sin`/`cos`/`atan2`/`hypot` and are not hashed (only id, alive, hp and `shape.y`), so two engines that build the board an ulp apart hash alike until the difference moves something hashed, possibly never. N0 can't rely on the drill for terrain: `perturb.mjs` is its check there (or, for approval, chunk geometry joins `shadowState`, Node and Chromium then freezing at once until N0's dmath lands). Cross-engine play needs N0's dmath first.
  - N1: the `MatchStore` contract (§2.6; (R8's fixer, round 2) §2.7's (R8) bullets): `entries()` decoded, the same object for the same entry across calls, decoded once per list element or per text, never per place (a store that inserts shifts places; `LocalStore`'s per-place cache is safe only because it never inserts; the Folder tells a prefix by identity first, an optimisation only, since it falls back to the id and content), `append(entry | text)` (the Session hands it the text it has checked `decode` takes: pushed as it is, never encoded again), subscribers told synchronously on a local change; `AutomergeStore` is that over `ImmutableString(text)`, and merge-sim's self-test fails a store that caches by index. A store that inserts (as Automerge does) makes the Folder refold often (merge-sim: 6,044 ops landing before folded entries); the sink is handed each entry's events with the Session already the match they lead to, so `session.G`, `preview`, `accepted` and `head` may be read there (merge-sim's sink holds it at every batch). `sim/peers.mjs` can reuse merge-sim's judgement (`judge`, the fates, the mirror view, the drill) with real Automerge docs in place of its RGA list; the actor ids swapped both ways as merge-sim's random actor names do.
  - N2: a device id per browser (localStorage) in place of `DEVICE`, and `rand` from `crypto` (match/ draws nothing); the lobby's seat claims fill each seat's `dev`; `open {commit}` before the start (the Folder takes it). The flow's `sink.reset` is a snap: add the "History changed: N moves undone" toast when `undone > 0`, keep the battle log and `?debug`'s trace through a refold, and take the local selection again from the new match (a refold that undid nothing still swaps G's objects: `snapped(G)` does this for a snap only). It is called only with a match (a refold that leaves none, its start made inert by an `open` from another device or a start under other rules, is `sink.status`'s: the lobby or skew screen); a reset onto another table (two starts from the opener's device, on another board) must draw that table afresh first, which `sameUnits` refuses today (it throws). `sink.status` and `session.report` (plus the browser, URL and time) are the desync dialog's; `session.error` the skew screen's. Elastic catch-up: a Session over an online store folds quietly to the head first.
  - (R8's fixer, round 2) N2 also: the closing check, each seated device appending its post-state `stateHash` out of band once its match is over, every Folder, live or over, comparing it (a drift inside the final entry's application; a live peer waiting on a seat whose match is over; online against the AI, its whole final turn); the desync dialog adds the store's raw texts to `session.report` (whose entries are decoded); the toast's count of a reset may include a move a racing concession cut off (§2.6's (R8) note). `session.accepted` and `rejected` are the Folder's own arrays: read them afresh after each change, never keep or edit them.
  - (R8's fixer, round 3) N2 also: the lobby's start goes through `Session.start(setup, {a})`, which writes the seed reveal (never a start appended beside the Session); a sink that answers decisions (an autopilot, an auto-End) answers every batch it is handed, since its submit is folded once the change in hand is done and is stale when a later entry of that change moved the seat's head (or, for approval, a `sink.settled(session)` call once a change is folded, the one place to answer a decision); `Folder.sync` is called from one place only (the Session's fold: it throws when entered again).
  - N3: the tamper alarm across reloads seeds the Folder with the accepted ids kept in IndexedDB (and, (R8's fixer, round 2), keyed by content too: an accepted id whose first good entry is another body is tamper within a Folder's life already; (R8's fixer, round 3) and by order: the accepted entries' first good occurrences must keep the order they were folded in, or a copy inserted before its own head undoes the entry quietly); a scrub to k is a Folder over a LocalStore of the start and the first k accepted entries.
  - F4: `vote {more}` joins `KINDS` with `commands.js`'s RULES and decodes already (booleans pass); `roundLimit` is in `SIMULTANEOUS` (no `h`, per-seat heads), the "same decision" rule by the turn's clock starts fresh heads for a round limit opened by the vote that closed the last, opened by the digest of the closed one's heads; bump `CORE_VERSION`; merge-sim wants vote scripts and concurrent-vote scenarios.

**R8b as built.** The consolidation after R8 (its row, added by the lead): what the large battles need of the netplay seams (the large-battle design's "R8 must allow" list), R8's critic lows, and the refactor's closing verification. Nothing in play changed: the corpus replays 40/40 byte-identically through the Folder, on the page and in Chromium; `CORE_VERSION` stays 1, `RULES_ID` is R8's, and `stateHash` of every pinned corpus state is R8's (computed on R8's commit and on this tree alike).
- **The review's fix (the lead's, after one code review).** A sink that threw ended the Session's loop at once, so a body it (or an earlier callback) had queued stayed in the queue with nothing to drain it until some unrelated change came, that change never settled, and a later submit from outside any callback could be written ahead of the older queued body. Now every sink callback, and each pass that runs them, goes through `call()`: its first error is kept and thrown once the loop is done, after every queued body has been written or dropped and `settled` told, and `submit()` drains a queue left over before writing its own body, so the log keeps the order the bodies were made in. merge-sim gains the edge case (a sink that queues a body and then throws: the body written, the change settled, the error still surfacing) and the `call-rethrows` mutant its self-test catches.

- **(A) What R8 must allow**, item by item (§2.6's (R8b) note has the contracts):
  1. *The single flight* (`match/session.js`). A `submit` (or `start`) made while a change is being folded, from any sink callback or the match's `onTrace`, is queued as its body, never appended there and then; once the change is folded (its status told, a desync said) the queue drains one body at a time, each held to the Session's `legal()` again on the match as it then stands and dropped (`sink.dropped(seat, body, why, session)`) or written, its id, `p` and `h` built then, and folded before the next. `onChange` is now one loop doing one thing at a time (a pass of `sync`, the status, the desync, the next queued body, `settled`) under the single-flight flag, held across all of it (R8's dropped it before the status and the desync). `Folder.sync` still throws when entered again, and `Folder.push` is guarded too (a `busy` flag held while an entry is judged and while its events are handed on: from the match's `onTrace` or from `sync`'s `each` it throws). merge-sim: a **reenter** scenario per human log (each seat's peer answers only from inside its Session's sink, from `events` and `settled` half the time each, from `reset` and after a drop always, one command queued at a time, deliveries slowed so the two deployments interleave and resets find a seat still deploying; every entry its Session writes is vetted as it is appended: never while its Folder syncs, on the seat's head and the match's hash as they then stand, the very command it queued; `settled` only with the whole list pushed and nothing of its own queued; nothing queued at the end), the edges' round-3 reentrancy cases rewritten for the queue (a sink's submits during a change of several entries: one the match moved past dropped and reported, two from one callback written in turn on the heads they find; a submit from a refold's tail; a submit from a reset; an autopilot in `settled` playing the log to its end; a change that reaches the store mid-fold folded in the next pass; a start made from `settled` queued; `sync` and `push` entered again throwing), and six mutants: `no-queue` (the no-guard mutant: R8's append there and then; caught by the edges and by the reenter scenario's vetting alone), `drain-unchecked`, `drop-silent`, `settled-early`, `no-settled`, `push-reentrant`. Every scenario now also requires every peer's Folder to have pushed each entry of the list once.
  2. *`sink.settled(session)`* (approved by the lead): once a change is folded and nothing else is to be, so a burst of changes (a sync message's entries, what the sink queued meanwhile) settles once, with the store's whole list folded; the one place to answer a decision. Found while building the edges' autopilot: an autopilot answering from `events` had a queued `auto` written that the change's own later entries had made needless but not illegal (`legal()` is all a queued body is held to), which played the AI's phase for it: so decisions are answered in `settled`, as the Session's header and §2.6 now say.
  3. *Kinds and fields.* Already so, now held: `KINDS` is `RULES`' keys (`core/commands.js` exports `RULES`, deeply frozen, for the lints only: no layer above the core imports it); `decode` takes any safe whole number or boolean in any field of each kind, none of them required, and refuses an array, an object, a string, a fraction, 2^53 and null; no module of `match/` reads `RULES` or a kind's field lists (data-check's section 10).
  4. *Reserved names.* data-check's section 10: no field of any kind (its `fields`, and F4's `opt` and `bools` when they come) is named `id`, `s`, `d`, `p`, `h` or `t`; the lint is shown to find two planted in a copy.
  5. *Sizes.* `MAX_BYTES` one constant, 1,024, and the only size in `match/envelope.js` but `MAX_NAME`; every kind's entry decodes at exactly 1,024 bytes and is refused a byte over (no cap by kind); the cap counts junk (a start and 4,999 junk entries leave the match live, the next freezes it `full`); the count exposed as `folder.count`, `session.count` and a report's `count`.
  6. *Per-entry cost.* `LocalStore` tells its `length` and hands out its own decoded array (no copy per change); the Session numbers its ids from a counter (`this.n`, from the store's length as the Session is made, so past every number this device wrote; a game played alone writes R8's very ids); `sync` reads the list as it stood when it began (a store's own array may grow meanwhile); the refold is behind one seam, `Folder.refoldFrom()`. New `sim/fold-cost.mjs`: hotseat-late-8 padded to 1,250 and 5,000 entries (placements in the deployment, hashed commands `legal()` refuses at single-seat decisions, every tenth junk), folded played an entry at a time and reloaded whole; the marginal cost per added entry at 5,000 is that at 1,250 (time within ×2, the fastest of five folds each in a fresh process; JSON.parse calls exactly one per entry; JSON.stringify calls and array elements copied within ×1.5); its self-test catches a store that copies its list every change, one that decodes its whole log every change, and a prefix check by content.
  7. *`stateHash` extensible and versioned* (`core/hash.js`). `UNIT_EXTRAS` (frozen, empty today; F9's `aboard: 0` the first) and `unitExtras(u)`: a unit's extras printed after its models as `[k=v,…]`, sorted, only where they differ from their defaults, so `shadowState` prints exactly R8's string today. data-check pins 8 states of 3 corpus battles (64-89's end; hotseat-late-8 before entries 0, 20 and 60 and at its end; serpent-random-2 before 0 and 10 and at its end) under `CORE_VERSION` 1, failing with "shadowState's output changed, which bumps CORE_VERSION" on any change, and shows with a doctored table that a unit at its default (or without the field) hashes as before and one off it moves the hash.
  8. *The setup's key whitelist* is deferred to F8a or F11, when the mission's and the army's keys land (noted in data-check's header, §2.6 and F8a's inheritance below).
  9. *No new out-of-band kinds.* `match/fold.js` exports `OUT_OF_BAND` (`concede`, `desync`) and routes by it; data-check pins it, checks that `concede` is the one kind of core's answering no decision and `desync` the one Folder kind a seat sends, and that in a hotseat battle every kind from the seat not waited on is refused as not its turn but those two.
  The design's item 4 (`h` and the heads by the decision's kind) and item 10 (events per entry uncapped, the sink reading `session.G` and `preview`) needed no change; P-merge already holds every accepted entry's `h` to the decision's kind.
- **(B) R8's critic lows.** P-prop holds each of its folds to the Folder for code that has one: the presented corpus fold (R8 only refused `'core'`, so `'bypassed'` passed), the quiet one and every random game's and out-of-band concession's refold must say `via: 'folder'`; two mutations show each check is needed (`quiet-accepted-short`: a quiet Folder leaves its Ends out of `accepted`, caught only by the quiet fold's check; `concede-accepted-short`, caught only by the refolds'). P-prop's Session check (9) gains the Folder rules R8's gate mutants found unguarded, over replays of every corpus log: an entry answering one seat's decision with its `h` taken out freezes the match there by the hash (`theirs` null); after the end a hashed End on the final head is inert from a spectator's device and freezes the match from the seat's own; a start under `CORE_VERSION` − 1 or + 1 is `skew` with no match; `missing-h-accepted`, `over-any-device` and `core-newer-only` are P-prop mutations now. The rendered lanes are committed as `sim/play-check.mjs` (R6b-R8's scratch script, ported onto `sim/lib.mjs`'s build): in the bushtail, serpent and hotseat lanes each seat played here picks units up by clicking them and puts them down by clicking the ground in its zone, each landing seen as its label moving, before Begin battle (hotseat: seat 0, then seat 1), and a lane fails if a seat placed nothing.
- **Found on the way.** R8's round-3 mutants `session-reentrant` and `sync-reentrant` went uncaught in the first self-test run: a sink's submit no longer re-enters the Session (it is queued), and `Folder.push`'s new guard threw first where `sync` was re-entered, which the edges' case accepted as any "not reentrant". Fixed by an edges case for what still re-enters a Session (a change reaching the store mid-fold, here a sink appending to the store itself, as a sync message landing mid-change would) and by holding each guard to its own message.
- **What N1, N2, F4 and the large battles inherit.** N1: the `MatchStore` contract gains `length` (the Session refuses a store without one), and `entries()` may be the store's own array but must keep handing out the same decoded object for an unchanged element (§2.7's (R8b) bullet; run `sim/fold-cost.mjs` against `AutomergeStore`). N2: decisions an autopilot or an auto-End answers go in `sink.settled`; a lobby's start may be made from a callback (queued); `sink.dropped` says why a queued command was never written; `session.count` for the HUD and F4's offer cap. F4: `vote {more}`'s boolean and any `opt`/`bools` need nothing in `match/`; the reserved-name lint covers their lists. F8a/F11: the setup whitelist (`fullSetup` refusing unknown top-level and seat keys). F9: `aboard` joins `UNIT_EXTRAS` with default 0 and needs no bump for the field alone; any other change to `shadowState`'s output bumps `CORE_VERSION` and re-pins data-check's hashes. S6: checkpoints start a refold from `Folder.refoldFrom()`.

- Every shipping step ends with `npm run build && npm run verify` and a commit of `dist/`.
- Lockfile changes and baseline re-records each go in a commit of their own.
- Bumps come at F4, F10b, F8a, F11a, F5a, F7a, F7b, F7c, F8b, F9a, F9b, F9c, F5b and F9d (and at N0 only if its V8 match fails), and at the October playtest's rules changes, F17, F18 and F19. None of N1-N3, F6, S0-S3, V1, F10a, F10c, F11b, F12 or F15 bumps. A price retune is data only: `RULES_ID` moves, with no bump.
- **What moved, and why.**
  - **From the user's answer 6:** everything from S0-S3 on follows N3.
  - **Kept from the earlier plan:** F6 right after N3.
  - **The designer's choices:**
    - F11a needs F8a's `setup.mission`, whitelist and `checkMission`. F11b needs F6's panel and N2's lobby.
    - **F5 splits.** F5a follows F11a, so the builder is priced for two races and each new race brings prices fitted against the others. (Revised after F8a by the user: F5a follows F9c, the big boards and vehicles first; the builder is still priced for two races first, and the new races bring their Field and Grand presets with them.) F5b follows F9c, because the Beetle runs on F9b's engine and both hulls want firing decks. The cost: the new races arrive seven steps later than the earlier "F6 → F5" (open question 27).
    - Fortifications follow the builder. Field and Grand switch on with orders, lists and fortifications in hand. Vehicles follow the boards they need (none in Skirmish), and firing decks wait for both ground shapes.
- **If selection and autopilot are wanted sooner**, F10a-F10c (with V1) can move ahead of N1. Their online checkpoints then move to N2: F10a's group move in the two-tab rig, F10c's orders at End online, and the presence keys `sels` and `ords`. Nothing else in them depends on N1-N3 or on S0-S3.

**N0 as built** (consensus hardening; no bump, no re-record):
- **Which engine.** Node's: its V8 runs fdlibm's `sin`, `cos`, `atan` and `atan2` (V8's `src/base/ieee754.cc`), and Chromium's build of V8 runs its own `sin` and `cos` (about 2.5% of a probe's inputs differ in the last bit; `atan` and `atan2` agree). `core/dmath.js` gains fdlibm's four, in plain JS over exact IEEE operations: the argument reduction (with the large-argument `__kernel_rem_pio2`, from 2/π's 24-bit chunks), the kernels and their coefficients, built from their exact hex words. The words of a double come from one 8-byte scratch `DataView`, written and read inside each call (a register, not state: §4.1 rule 13).
- **No battle changed.** dmath equals Node's own Math bit for bit, so every trace, shadow and battle log is the corpus's: P-ai and P-human 40/40 in Node, and P-browser 40/40 in Chromium against Node's `shadow`, where until now 32 battles (20 AI pairs, 12 human logs) needed their own `webShadow`. So the branch "match Node's and retire `webShadow`" was taken, and `CORE_VERSION` stays 1.
- **Every call site.** `core/units.js` (formation rings, the relayout sort), `core/nav.js` and `core/terrain/geom.js` (box yaw), `core/terrain/recipes.js` and `terrain.js` (the scatter's angles and yaws, the hedgerow's `atan`), `core/actions/move.js` (the walk's heading, the smash point behind it) and `shoot.js` (the blast's aim and scatter) take `sin`, `cos`, `atan` and `atan2` from dmath.
- **The ban.** `sim/boundaries.mjs` bans, in `core/`, `data/` and `match/`, every Math function the engines approximate (`sin`, `cos`, `tan`, their inverses and hyperbolics, `atan2`, `exp`, `expm1`, `log`, `log1p`, `log2`, `log10`, `pow`, `cbrt`, and `hypot` as before) and the `**` operator (pow by another name, which the engines also round their own ways); the count it used to report is gone. Its self-test gains seven edits (six caught, one not: dmath's `sin` beside `Math.sign`, `Math.sqrt` and names that only begin like a banned one).
- **The checks.** `sim/dmath-check.mjs` (new, a standing check) holds dmath to Node's Math over a few hundred thousand inputs per range (angles, small, medium, huge, subnormal, raw bit patterns, the special values) and, with `--browser`, to the same bits in Chromium, the inputs built from exact bit patterns (never `**`); flipping the leading sine coefficient's last bit, a cosine coefficient's, or the reduction's `z ≥ 0.5` test each fails it (the lowest coefficients' last bits change no result). `node sim/perturb.mjs --fn sin,cos,atan,atan2`: the PIN code moves 24/24 battles, the working tree 0/24 (the design's "11/12 to 0/12", over today's 24 AI battles).
- **`webShadow` retired.** `verdict` holds every engine to `shadow`; `parity.mjs --record --browser` refuses (there is nothing of Chromium's own to record), and a shadow-only failure in Chromium says it is code older than N0 (the PIN still is: it differs there by an ULP of terrain, as before); `corpus.mjs` writes no `webShadow`; the corpus files drop the field in a commit of their own (data only).

**F1 and F2 as built** (view only; no consensus change; together, since both are the battle's opening view):
- **Which view.** `present/camera-presets.js` `battleView({ localSeats, edges })` opens behind the one seat played here (`PRESETS.behind(edge)`: its own army in front, whichever edge it holds, so the serpents' player looks out from the east), and broadside for no seat played here or two (a watched battle; hotseat, where neither player is favoured): one army left, one right. The screen's shape no longer decides it; `fitPose` fits either to the screen. The `landscape` and `portrait` presets stay (the camera made at load, `fovFor`), still the R0 code's.
- **Fitting.** `fitPose(preset, aspect, rect)` takes the board as a rectangle `{cx, cz, w, h}` (`BOARD_RECT`, classic's, by default; F8 passes a mission's) and looks at its centre. The presets' maxes grow so the whole classic board shows on every screen down to a 412×915 portrait phone: broadside 105 (a phone needs about 104), behind 80 (about 78). On a landscape screen the behind view stands about 61" off (the board's 40" running away from the player sets it), against today's 43" broadside; on a phone the broadside is small (the 40" board across 412 px), which the view button answers.
- **The view button.** `PRESETS.overview` (the whole board from nearly overhead, elevation 1.45); `viewsFor({ localSeats, edges })` lists a battle's views, its own first: behind the seat played here, broadside, behind the other army, overview (a watched or hotseat battle: broadside, behind the west, behind the east, overview). The CameraRig's `setViews` swings onto the first as the battle starts (app/flow.js), `nextView` steps round (the HUD's 🧭, `#view`, and V) and `toOverview` goes to the last (Home); `toTitle` clears them, so neither does anything on the title. The Rules panel says so; the title card is unchanged (title-shot, the thumbnail).
- **The check.** `sim/camera-check.mjs` (425 checks): the landscape and portrait presets are still the R0 code's views by shape; `battleView` is behind the one local seat's edge (either edge) or broadside, on every screen; `viewsFor` lists its views in order; every fitted preset, the overview included, sees the whole board at its elevation down to the 412×915 phone (and stops at its max only below it); `fitPose` of classic's rectangle is its default, and of a 60×40 board off centre looks at its centre and sees it whole; the rig rests where `fitPose` puts it for every preset, overview included, and `setViews`, `nextView` (round again) and `toOverview` step through a battle's views, doing nothing on the title.
- Under SwiftShader the game clock runs about a fifth of real time, so the swing onto a battle's view takes some 8 s of wall time in the sandbox's Chromium: a screenshot taken sooner catches it mid-swing.

**F3 as built** (view only; no consensus change):
- **The model.** `present/hud-model.js`'s `end` slice gains `lit`: `ready` (nothing left to do in the seat's phase: the core's `anyCanAct`, asked through the Session's preview with the dice locked, once the table has caught up), or the deployment, where Begin battle is the only way on.
- **The page.** `#endPhase` loses its fixed `primary` class (index.html) and is an ordinary button while units can still act; `ui/actions.js` toggles `.ready` by `end.lit`, which is today's primary look plus a glow that breathes (1.6 s), held still under `prefers-reduced-motion` and stopped while the button is disabled (the table playing).
- **The check.** `sim/hud-check.mjs` holds the page, not only the model: at every frame idle on a local seat's phase, End lit exactly when `ready` is (and `ready` exactly when no unit can act), and Begin battle lit wherever it shows in the deployment. Its self-test gains three edits, each caught: End never lit on the page (`lit-never`), Begin battle unlit (`deploy-unlit`) and End unlit when ready with Begin battle still lit (`ready-unlit`, which only the phase check can see).
- F10c's change (manual units only, §3's additions) comes with F10c.

**F4 as built** (consensus: `CORE_VERSION` 2; baselines unaffected):
- **The rules.** `fullSetup` takes `overtime: 'never' | 'vote'` (anything else is refused, as before). Under `'vote'`, the `score` step of a round at or past `rounds` logs "Round r is over: play another round?" and opens `{ k: 'roundLimit', seats: humanSeats(G), votes: {} }` (§0.2 #19: the human seats vote, the AI seats follow, a wipe is final since it ends the battle before `score`). `vote {more}` (`core/commands.js`) records the seat's say in `votes`, emits `vote`, and drops the seat from `seats`; the last say closes it, logging every say in seat order (the seats vote at once, so the battle's log is the same whichever say folds first; the panel shows each as it comes, from `G.pending.votes`): every `more` plays round r+1 (`T.round++`, `T.overtime++`, step `turnStart`, logged "Overtime: round r+1"), anything else is `gameOver` on the score. The vote is asked again after every overtime round. `CORE_VERSION` is 2 (the rules take a command they refused), and `sim/data-check.mjs` pins version 2's `stateHash`es to version 1's: no corpus state changed, since no corpus setup asks for the vote.
- **`legal()`'s schema** as §4.2.6 sketched it: a RULES entry may list `opt` (optional whole numbers, none yet: F9b's `f` is the first) and `bools` (required booleans: `vote`'s `more`); a key outside `t`, `fields`, `opt` and `bools` is refused as before. `vote` answers a `roundLimit` decision only (the turn rule: a seat that has had its say is no longer in `seats`).
- **Who gets the vote.** `app/flow.js` asks for it in every battle with a human seat (the title's three human modes), never in a watched one; `?overtime=never` turns it off, which is how `sim/`'s page replays play the logs recorded before F4 (`sim/chromium.mjs` and `sim/oracle/run-legacy.mjs` put the log's own `overtime` on the URL; the PIN's code ignores it).
- **The panel.** The end screen (`ui/screens/result.js`, `#over`) doubles as the vote: "Round r is over", who leads and by how much, "Play another round? It takes everyone's yes.", each human seat's say so far (keep playing, end it, or deciding…), and Keep playing / End the battle. `app/flow.js` shows it while a seat played here is still to vote and the table has caught up, and takes it down as play goes on; the end screen replaces it when the vote ends the battle. Its buttons vote for every seat played here that is still to vote (hotseat's two players share one screen and so one say; online, N2's, each device votes its own). Keep playing is held back once the Folder's log holds 80% of `MAX_ENTRIES` (`Session.count`, 4,000 entries), with a line saying this round is the last: a UI rule, so a `more` past it is still legal and the cap still freezes the match. The HUD's round reads "Round r · overtime" past the rounds (`present/hud-model.js`).
- **The netplay.** `roundLimit` was already in `SIMULTANEOUS` (no `h`, per-seat heads, R8), so two seats' says written at once on the same head both fold, in either order, to the same match. merge-sim's `votes` scenario holds it (each of the four pairs of says, folded both ways; a seat's second say refused as stale; a say for one seat from the other's device refused), with two self-test mutants, each caught: `roundLimit-hashed` (the vote taken for a single seat's decision: the second say is stale) and `vote-never-closes`; and (after the review) the battle's log compared too, with a third edit, `vote-logged-as-said`.
- **The checks.** P-prop's battery judges `vote` true and false at every decision (accepted only at a round limit, where only `vote` and `concede` are), its junk (`more` as 1, `'yes'`, missing, an extra field) refused, and half its random games with a human seat play under the vote, voting more 60% of the time up to two overtime rounds (overtime reached and votes cast are counted, and required). The human-bot driver (`sim/oracle/human-bot.mjs`) answers a `roundLimit` decision through `__ts.vote(more, seat)` (`__ts.roundLimit` lists the local seats still to vote), its policies voting by temperament: aggressive one round more, random and late more by a coin up to two overtime rounds.
- What N1-N3 inherit: the panel's says come from `G.pending.votes`, so a remote seat's say shows as it folds; `Session.count` is the Folder's, which N1's store keeps. A snap past the battle's end while the vote is up (N2's refold) replaces the panel with the end screen (`snapped()`).
- **The logs that vote** (F4's second commit). Two human logs recorded on F4's code with `sim/corpus-add.mjs` and admitted as the corpus's are: `hotseat-late-vote-9` (both seats vote: more twice, two overtime rounds, then end; 6 votes) and `serpent-random-vote-1` (the serpents' seat alone votes against the AI: one overtime round, then end). The corpus is 42 battles. The PIN moved to F4's commit (the R6b note's rule, now kept by a commit that has a core), with `legacyMode` retired in the same commit (§4's PIN note). `sim/hud-check.mjs` takes the hotseat log by default and `sim/snap-check.mjs` the serpent one, so the panel, `__ts.roundLimit` and `__ts.vote` are driven in Chromium in the quick runs; the driver answers whichever seat's vote the log holds next. hud-check also snaps a log that votes at its round limit (the vote's panel up after the snap, "Round r is over", End and Auto down), and takes a battle the last say ends past its end as the driver plays that say (the end plays out in the table's next frame); its self-test gains `vote-unshown`, on the hotseat vote log. The review's `snapped()` fix has no local check: in a game played here the panel is taken down (the HUD's next refresh) before a snap reaches the end, so only N2's refold, a snap past the end with the panel still up, can tell it; N2's checks take it (an edit undoing it, `vote-blocks-end`, passed every local battle).
- **The review** (one reviewer, a skeptic per finding). Fixed: P-prop counted a round too many for a concession during the vote (it comes after the round was scored; seen at 600 games), never required a vote's junk refused (and its `extra-field` self-test edit had gone stale with `legal()`'s new line: both fixed, with a `vote-not-boolean` edit, 27 of 27 caught), play-check's `--rounds 5` lane passed a battle that ended on its rounds without asking, the driver answered the vote for the lowest seat first, and `snapped()` (above). And one the corpus's hotseat vote log found once it was in: merge-sim's peers, voting at once, folded seat 1's say first, and each say was logged as it folded, so the battle's log depended on which came first (every peer agreed: they fold one list; but the says didn't commute as §2.6 says the round limit's must). The says are now logged at the close, in seat order; both logs' traces are unchanged (nothing is traced between their two says), so no hash moved.

**N1 as built** (real Automerge in Node; no consensus change, no bump, the corpus unchanged):
- **The pins.** `@automerge/automerge` 3.5.0 and `@automerge/automerge-repo` 2.5.6 as dependencies, `@automerge/automerge-repo-network-messagechannel` 2.5.6 as a dev dependency, all `--save-exact`, the lockfile in a commit of its own. N2 adds the browser's adapters (WebSocket, BroadcastChannel, IndexedDB) when it uses them. Nothing in the page imports `net/` yet, so the shipped build is unchanged.
- **`net/automerge-store.js`.** `AutomergeStore(handle)` over a ready automerge-repo `DocHandle`, and `matchDoc()`, the new document (`{app, schema: 1, lobby: {}, log: []}`). `entries()` is the store's own array, kept in step with the document by each change's patches: an `insert` into the log at `['log', i]` is spliced in at `i`, its texts decoded once each (a `Map` from text to entry, never by place); any other change to the log (an element deleted, replaced or edited, the log put anew: never an honest peer's) decodes the list again from the document, as does a patched length that isn't the document's. `append(entry | text)` pushes `new ImmutableString(text)` in one change; `length`, `subscribe`, `close()` (stops listening), `texts()` (a log put anew as anything but a list reads as empty: every accepted entry gone, the Folder's `tamper`) and `export()` (the raw texts: N2's desync report). Subscribers are told outside the handle's own change event (the review's high finding): automerge-repo emits that event from inside its xstate machine, where a change made meanwhile is only queued, applied once the listeners return, so a Session folding there would write an entry from its own loop (a queued submit, a desync it found) and go on before it was in the list, its next entry on a stale head (an autopilot's two commands from `settled`: the second refused as stale on every peer). The store notes the change in the event and tells its subscribers after: a change its own `append` made as `append` returns, a peer's a microtask later (before any other task). A subscriber's error so reaches `append`'s caller, or the microtask's, never the handle's machinery (which caught it, rethrew it on a timer, and skipped its own bookkeeping). Verified on 2.5.6, as §2.7 asked: a local `handle.change` emits its `change` event (with the patches, `A.diff` of the heads) before `change` returns; a remote change arrives as an event between the event loop's tasks; an element pushed with `ImmutableString` from `@automerge/automerge/slim` is one of the repo's own (`instanceof`, `isImmutableString`), the repo's full entry having initialised the same module's wasm; a peer's actor id can be set (`handle.update((d) => A.clone(d, { actor }))`); and the higher actor id's concurrent insert goes first, landing before entries a peer holds. `DocHandle` reports every change with `source: 'change'`, local or remote, so a store can't tell them apart there.
- **P-peers, `sim/peers.mjs`.** Real automerge-repo repos in one Node process, a full mesh of `MessageChannelNetworkAdapter` links over ports that deliver each message after a random delay (in order per direction), the repo syncing on its own schedule (at most every 100 ms a peer). Each corpus human log is played three ways: `pair` (its seats' peers, or a vs-AI log's seat and a spectator; actor ids rising), `trio` (and a spectator more; actor ids falling, so concurrent inserts order the other way) and, for the hotseat logs, `fork` (seat 0 on two tabs of one device, each playing the log's commands, and seat 1); `auto` (as pair, each seat answering only from its sink's `settled`, as an autopilot does: the next command and, if legal already, the one after, two queued in one call, so the Session's queue writes from inside a fold over the real store); one hotseat log's `tamper` (a peer puts the log anew part way through: every peer freezes `'tamper'`); and three AI pairs (a host's start, a second spectator). Each peer acts on its own view as soon as it holds a decision, after a random pause, longer where both seats answer at once. Once the network is quiet, every peer's document is at the same heads with the same texts, every Folder agrees with every other and with a fresh single-process fold (status, accepted, rejected, stateHash), each pushed every entry once, the match is over and traces the corpus battle, every view is `project(G)`, §0.2 #3's hashes hold, no seat has two accepted commands on one head; pair, trio and auto refuse nothing (and over the run some auto seat queued two commands in one call), a fork refuses only a seat's stale, out-of-turn or inert commands (a tab's loser, or the other seat's written on the loser, sent again on the winner's head). The schedule is real time, so no two runs are alike; what is judged holds for every one. A run: 48 scenarios, 5,157 entries, 967 landing before entries a peer had folded, 538 resets, 59 s. Its `--self-test` breaks the store five ways (an insert taken for an append, the text encoded again, a change never told, a cache by place, and a peer's change told inside the handle's event), each caught.
- **The document's weight.** The corpus logs as played: 2-6 KB saved (a 214-entry fork log 6.2 KB). A synthetic 465-entry log (the start and 464 of the corpus logs' commands, as devices write them, each its own change): 11.3 KB saved, its texts 42.6 KB. §4.2.1's estimate (50-100 KB) was high.
- **`sim/fold-cost.mjs --store automerge`** runs both folds over the AutomergeStore on a repo with no network. Both are linear in time, decodes, stringifies and the fold's copies (`play`: about 610 µs an entry at 1,250 and at 5,000, Automerge's change and diff included; `reload`: about 75 µs). Automerge itself copies its document's log at every change, its wasm glue's `Array.from` of the materialized list: about 680 elements per entry at 1,250 and 2,550 at 5,000, O(n) per change, a few microseconds of time at the cap. fold-cost counts those apart and tells them, not judging them: no store can avoid them. If a large battle ever feels it, the remedy is the document's shape (a log of chunks, each a list), not the store. Its self-test with `--store automerge` breaks the store two ways (the list read off the document at every change, the whole log decoded again at every change), each caught.
- **The review** (one reviewer, a skeptic per finding; every finding confirmed). Fixed: the writes made inside the handle's change event (above, high); a subscriber's error thrown into the handle (above); a log put anew as a string, map or number, which threw in the store's listener and left its list stale (now read as empty: tamper); fold-cost's `decode-uncached` edit, which cost nothing on the path it ran (replaced, `decode-every-change`); and P-peers, which never wrote from inside a fold nor met a tamper (the `auto` and `tamper` scenarios, and the `told-in-emit` edit). Noted, not changed: the vs-AI logs' pair and trio have one writer, so they never meet a concurrent insert; the hotseat logs meet a few in the deployment and the vote, the forks hundreds.
- **What N2 inherits.** The store and `matchDoc()`; a sink's error from a peer's change surfaces from a microtask (the page's `error` event), not from a call the page made; each peer's Session made over `new AutomergeStore(handle)` once the handle is ready (`repo.find` resolves); actor ids are the repo's own (random), which P-peers sets only to order its runs. A store's `close()` when a match is left. The repo's 100 ms sync throttle is the floor of a move's round trip.

**N2 as built** (online play; consensus: a new out-of-band kind, `final`, for the closing check, and nothing else; no bump, the corpus unchanged):
- **The pins.** The browser's adapters, `@automerge/automerge-repo-network-websocket`, `-network-broadcastchannel` and `-storage-indexeddb`, each 2.5.6 `--save-exact`, the lockfile in a commit of its own. No `@automerge/automerge-repo-sync-server`: its 0.3.0 pins nothing exactly and brings express. The test rig's server is `sim/sync-server.mjs` instead, what that package runs (a repo listening on a websocket, `sharePolicy` false, in memory), made from the pinned `NodeWSServerAdapter`; `node sim/sync-server.mjs --port 3030` self-hosts one.
- **Lazy loading** (§2.7's recipe). `net/repo.js` makes the repo once per page and sync server (`openRepo(sync)`; one that failed to start is made afresh next time: the slim entries, the wasm as a file of its own through Vite's `?url`, `initializeWasm`, IndexedDB storage, BroadcastChannel and WebSocket networks). The page reaches it only through `app/online.js`, which `app/boot.js` imports for Play online or a `#m=` link, and which imports the net layer through `import()` alone (`loadNet`): `sim/boundaries.mjs`'s rules as R6b wrote them (net/ imports only core/, match/ and net/; the view reaches net/ only through `import()`), so the controller is app/'s, not net/'s as §2.7's sketch had `net/lobby.js` own the UI. `sim/bundle-check.mjs` holds the build to it: the entry chunk names no Automerge module, `index.html` preloads nothing, the online chunks and the wasm are files of their own reached by `import()`. Sizes: the entry 200 kB gz (201 before N2: the flow's and the HUD's few hundred lines); the online chunks 85.5 kB gz in seven files (§2.7 estimated 68 kB); the wasm 3.56 MB (1.12 MB gz). The repo's static server (`scripts/static-server.mjs`, `npm run preview`) serves `.wasm` as `application/wasm`.
- **Names and ids** (`net/ids.js`). A device id is 8 base36 characters in `localStorage['ts.dev']`; a tab opened with `&dev=<id>` plays as that device and keeps it for the tab in `sessionStorage` (Open second tab, and the "continue on another device" link). A display name is fitted (§4.2.10's "N2 must"): NFC, control characters and lone surrogates removed, white space one space, trimmed, then the longest prefix within 24 characters and 48 bytes of canonical JSON (an emoji counts 4, a `"` or `\` 2); the name box fits as it is typed, keeping a trailing space (the next word's). Control characters include tab and newline: "Bo\tb" is "Bob". A nonce is 16 lowercase hex characters, a guest seat's own; the host's seat and an AI's contribute `''`.
- **The seed** (`net/seed.js`). `commitOf(a)` is hex(sha256(a)), `a` 16 random bytes as hex, kept per match in the host's `localStorage['ts.a.<documentId>']`; the dice are u32be(sha256(a:documentId:nonce0:nonce1)), each seat's nonce as the start writes it. A guest's page draws its nonce as it presses Ready, and only once the log's `open` is in (Ready waits for it): so the host committed before it could know the nonce, a rematch's seat included (its copied seats carry no nonce), and the guest knows the commitment, not the secret; nobody picks the dice (the review's finding: as first built, a rematch copied the old nonces, which the host knew, so a modified host page could grind its secret). `verifyStart({ open, start, documentId, mine })` runs once, asynchronously, when the page first sees the start: the reveal against the commitment ("seed check failed: …"), the dice re-derived ("seed check failed: …"), then this device's whole seat. As built, `mine` is every lobby record this device pressed Ready on in the match (`localStorage['ts.ready.<documentId>.<dev>']`, the last eight), each with the commitment the log had opened with then; only records under this match's commitment count. The start's seat must equal one of them field for field but `ready`, a field absent on one side and present on the other a difference ("The start changed your seat (ctrl)", naming each field that differs from the last one readied), and no start seat may name this device unless it readied that seat so ("The start gave you a seat you never readied (seat 2)"). Any readied record will do, not only the last: a host whose lobby lagged a Ready behind starts from a record the guest did agree to. A failure opens the battle read-only (no seat played here) with a dialog saying why.
