A page that kept no record (another browser opened with the seat's `&dev=` link, storage cleared) has nothing to hold the seat to: it checks the seed alone and plays the seat the start gives it, with a toast saying so ("Playing seat 1 as the battle's start set it…"), rather than watching a battle that would then wait on it for ever; Leave seat forgets the seat's records.
- **The lobby** (`net/lobby.js`, `ui/screens/lobby.js`, `app/online.js`). The document is `matchDoc()` with `lobby: { host, board, terrain, rounds, overtime, seats: { s0, s1 }, next }`, each seat `{ ctrl, dev, name, race, ready, nonce }`. Play online makes it (`lobbyDoc`: the host in seat 0, the title's board and the table's races), the URL becomes `#m=<documentId>` (and `&sync=` when the page was opened with `?sync=`), and the host's Session writes the log's `open` (`Session.open(commit)`, new: before anything else is written). The lobby shows the link (Copy link, Open second tab), the battlefield (the host's to change, with New battlefield; a change un-readies both seats), each seat (who, their race, Ready or getting ready) and a status line: "Copy the link and send it to your opponent", "Waiting for Ben to get ready…", "Waiting for the host to start the battle…", "Waiting for host (their page is closed)" (the host heard from by presence in the last 15 s, or not), "Both seats are taken: you will watch the battle", "Seat 2 was taken by Cat at the same moment" (two claims at once: the map key's last writer stands everywhere, and the loser sees another device in it; the claim is told by the device id, not by `getConflicts`, which says the same), "Match not found; is the host online? (…)" (`repo.find` refused). Your own seat takes your name, race and Ready; a change of name or race un-readies it; Leave seat; a free seat offers Sit here, with the table's race for it unless the other seat took that one. Once both seats are ready, the host's page builds the setup from the lobby and writes the start through its Session (`start(setup, { a })`), only if the lobby is still the one it built from once the dice are computed (an await). A ready lobby is first asked of the rules (`createMatch` of its setup, once per lobby as it stands: a peer may write any race, battlefield, rounds or overtime into it): one they refuse says so on every page ("This lobby can't start a battle: overtime "x"…") and is never started from, and a start the log refuses is never written again from the same lobby (the review's finding: the host's page wrote one start after another until the log was full). `ready()` also requires each seat's device id and nonce in their forms. The lobby is drawn again only when what it shows changed (a picker left open stays open).
- **The battle.** When the log holds a start, the page runs `verifyStart`, closes the lobby's Session (no seats: it only followed the log and wrote the host's `open` and start) and makes the match's: the seats the start names this device for (none when the check failed), the closing check on, the flow's `onTrace`. The flow then follows it (`app/flow.js`'s `follow(session, online)`): a fresh table for the setup, snapped to the match as it stands (the Session's own fold as it was made is the quiet fold to the head), the battle log made again from the log's entries (`relog`: a quiet fold of the entries with their events kept, the last 80 `log` events written), the trace under `?debug` the match's so far (`rejoin`), and its events played from there on. The same path serves the joiner who arrives after the start (a watcher), a reload and a rematch's new match. A frozen match (`desync`, `tamper`, `full`, `skew`) opens the dialog: what happened, Keep watching, Back to the war room, and Download report, which is `session.report` with the store's raw texts, the page's URL, browser, the time, `CORE_VERSION`, `RULES_ID` and the device. (A download is a link to a Blob: the claude.ai artifact's frame blocks it, as it blocks the sync server.)
- **The closing check** (§2.7's desync note, for approval: a new out-of-band kind). Once its match is over, each seated device's Session (`closing: true`, online only) appends `final` once, from a seat played here: the head its match ended at as `p`, its `stateHash` there as `h` (decode requires both; seat -1 never). Every Folder compares it out of band (`OUT_OF_BAND` is `concede`, `desync` and `final`; `sim/data-check.mjs` pins the three): on the same head, a hash that isn't this match's is a desync by the hash at the `final`, said out of band by the Session as any other, so the device that ended freezes too (a desync still freezes a match that is over); agreeing, it is inert ("inert: the match is over, its closing hash agreeing"); on another head it is stale. It is never accepted, so the head stays where the end left it. `folder.finals` records each final folded as `device head`, so a Session made over a log that holds its own final on that head (a reload) never says it again, and one whose match a refold ends on another head says it there; a Session says it once per head whatever the Folder makes of it (`saidAt`: past the log's cap its final is inert and never recorded, and as first built it said it again for ever, the review's finding). A concession, which carries no prev, moves the head to a digest of the head before it, the head its accept makes and its id (§2.6's out-of-band note): as first built the head was the concession's id alone, so a concession raced by the other seat's move (or the same seat's from another tab) left the conceder's final naming a head whose history every other page held with the move in it, and every page, the conceder's too, froze an honest match as a desync (the review's high finding; merge-sim's new edges and its `concede-head-bare` edit hold it). This catches what the pre-state `h` can't: a drift inside the entry that ended the match, and a live peer waiting on a seat whose match is over. §4.2.10's item 9 ("no new out-of-band kinds: concede and desync only") stood for orders; a final carries none, and data-check's assertion moved with it.
- **Presence** (`net/presence.js`): `handle.broadcast({ dev, seat, name, head, n, hash, sel?, tg? })` every 5 s and whenever it changes, `n` (new beside §2.7's keys) the Folder's accepted count: a peer on the same head and count whose hash differs is "out of step" (not while a simultaneous decision is open, whose entries fold in either order). What arrives is checked field by field and the rest dropped; a peer quiet for 15 s drops from the live list. The net badge (`ui/netbadge.js`): "● online · 1 watching" (the websocket open), "◌ reconnecting…", "○ offline · your moves will sync" (`navigator.onLine` false), "⚠ out of step with Ann". The opponent's pick: a dashed ring in their colour round the unit their player holds, and a line to the unit they aim at (`view/overlay.js`'s `peer`, its three.js objects made the first time one shows, so a game played alone makes none, nor their ids' `Math.random` draws).
- **The flow online.** The HUD's hint for a human seat played on another device: "Coil of Ssithra are taking their turn…", and in the deployment, once yours is done, "Waiting for the other side to finish deploying…" (never in a game played alone: every human seat is played here). A refold that undid moves shown snaps the table, makes the battle log again and toasts "History changed: N moves undone" (`ui/toast.js`; none when only two seats' simultaneous entries changed order); a refold onto another start (two tabs of the host's device each wrote one, from another lobby) draws its table afresh first (`redraw`). The battle log is made again from the entries the Folder has pushed (`folder.pushed`). The elastic catch-up is decided once a change is folded (`sink.settled`), not after each entry's events: as first built, a snap mid-change played the rest of the change on from the entry it came at, and made the log from the store's whole list, so those entries' lines were shown twice (the review's finding); deciding at the settle, the snap is to the match the whole change leads to, the log is the Folder's, and a change of a hundred entries snaps once rather than at every entry past the threshold. There the player's backlog (`backlog()`, an estimate in game seconds: `PACE.cost` per event, a walk its path at its pace, a pause its length, a dice row its row, a banner its beat, a shot or a spell half a second) is turned into wall seconds by the page's speed and its measured game-time rate (`clock.rate`, view/stage.js: a frame steps at most 0.05 s, so a page drawing fewer than 20 frames a second runs slower than the wall clock; the lobby rig's SwiftShader pages ran at 0.42). Over 8 s it plays twice as fast (`clock.boost`), over 16 s four times, over 30 s it snaps to the match as it stands; idle, the boost is 1 again. Measured, the estimate is good: 10.7 s estimated, 11.1 s of game time played.
- **Rematch.** Over, a seated page shows Rematch: a new match (this device its host, both seats and races copied unready and without nonces), named in the old match's `lobby.next` (first come: a second asker joins the one named), and every page on the old match offers "Join the rematch", which goes there (`#m=` of the new one). Two pages that ask at once (within a sync's round trip) each make a match and name it; the old match's `next` settles to one of them on every page, and a page in a rematch's lobby keeps watching the old match until its battle begins, going to the one named (the review's finding: as first built both pages waited in lobbies of their own for ever).
- **The checks.** `sim/net-check.mjs` (Node): the names (ten cases, the caps, `nameOk`, typing), nonces and device ids; sha256 and the dice by known answers; `verifyStart` passing a start as readied (host, guest, spectator) and failing another secret, other dice, and each of the guest's `ctrl`, `dev`, `race`, `name`, `nonce` and a field only one side has (F11b's `army`), and a seat never readied; then through a real sync server and three Node repos on websockets: a guest finds the match, two guests claim one seat at once and one claim stands everywhere, concurrent edits of both seats settle to one lobby, the host's start verifies on both seated devices, a host-flipped `ctrl` fails the guest's check; and a whole battle played by both seats from their own devices with a watcher beside them, every page on the same match, each seated device's final said once and agreed everywhere. `sim/lobby-rig.mjs` (Chromium, pages in contexts of their own meeting only through `sim/sync-server.mjs`, on a fresh build): `play` (Play online, the link, Sit here, a name, Ready, the battle on both seats and a watcher, round 1 played from both pages, the watcher counted on the host's badge, a concession, finals agreed with no dialog, Rematch and Join the rematch), `names` (typed past 24 characters or 48 bytes, control characters pasted: never entered; the lobby holds the name fitted), `concurrent`, `altered` (the host's start with the guest's `ctrl`, `dev`, `race` or `name` changed: read-only, "The start changed your seat (…)"), `vote-blocks-end` (F4's leftover: a page at the round limit with its vote up, its own seat's "end" from another tab inserted before the other seat's "more": the snap shows the end screen), `history` (the page's own say, deciding the vote, undone by another tab's: the toast, the log made again, line for line the match's), `catch-up` (a watcher at a quarter speed handed a whole battle at once: the end in about 2 s, the battle log the match's, no line twice), and from the review `rematch-race` (both seated pages press Rematch at once: one lobby for both, the guest readying with a nonce of its own), `bad-lobby` (a peer writes overtime 'x': the host's page says why and writes no start) and `continue` (another browser on a seat's link after the start plays it, and says so). Its `--self-test` builds eleven broken copies, each caught by its case: the vote kept past the end, a seat check by nonce alone, no closing hash, an unfitted name box, no toast, no relog, no catch-up snap, a rematch never looking back, a nonce never drawn, the lobby's battle unchecked, and a page with no record watching. (As first written, `history`'s undone say wrote no line, so a refold that left the old log up passed it: the say now decides the vote, and the whole log is compared. A twelfth copy, the catch-up's log made from the store's whole list, went when the catch-up moved to the settle, where the list and the Folder's pushed entries are the same.) merge-sim's two `closing` drills (hotseat-late-8, hotseat-aggressive-125: the final entry's own application drifting on its author's peer, every peer freezing on a final) and five edits (`silent-final`, `final-unchecked`, `over-ignores-final`, and from the review `concede-head-bare` and `final-said-forever`), each caught; since the review every human scenario's peers say their closing hash, as online pages do (so finals race the last entries and the concessions: 116 scenarios agree), with two edges more (a concession racing its seat's own move from another tab: the final stale, the match over; a closing Session over a finished log at its cap: its final said once); P-peers likewise, over real Automerge (each seated device's final on the end head, every final agreeing or, on a head a raced entry moved, stale: one such in a fork, none frozen); data-check's out-of-band rows (the three kinds; a final's fates in a live hotseat battle: inert when its hash agrees, a desync when not, stale on another head).
- **The review** (one reviewer; every finding confirmed, by its repro or by the code, and fixed: above, each where it lies). High: a concession raced by a move froze an honest match through the closing check; a start the Folder refused made the host's page write starts until the log was full. Medium: `final()` looped for ever past the cap; a rematch let the host know every nonce before drawing its secret; the catch-up's snap showed the rest of a change's log lines twice. Lower: concurrent Rematch stranded both players; the seat check demoted a browser with no record (the continue link) to watching, leaving the battle waiting on it; the repo was made once per page whatever the sync server, a failed start-up cached; and the closing check had never met concurrency in a test (merge-sim and P-peers now run every seat with it on). Checked clean: a refold carries `finals`; two tabs of one device saying two finals; no device but the seat's can freeze anyone; peers' names and presence only ever reach the page as text; a game played alone unchanged.
- **Not built, or N3's.** Spectating's own tools (the broadside camera is F2's and serves; scrubbing, "watch from the start", the replay export), the tamper alarm across reloads (accepted ids kept in IndexedDB), and rejoin's polish are N3's (built: N3's notes, below); a reload already rejoins (the same path as a late joiner). The HUD shows races, not players' names (the lobby, the badge and presence carry names). An AI seat in an online lobby is F11b's.

**N3 as built** (spectating and recovery; consensus untouched: no bump, the corpus unchanged, a Folder given nothing to keep folds as before):
- **The tamper alarm across reloads** (§4.2's N3 note). `Folder.keep(known)`, before the first sync: the entries this page accepted in an earlier life, `[[id, sum], …]` in fold order (`knownOf(folder)`: `sum` is cyrb53 of the decoded entry, `sumOf`), are held to the list as the Folder holds the entries it accepted itself: each still there as the first good entry with its id, unchanged, and in its order; else `tamper`. Checked as the list is first folded (a list that lost one freezes before anything is pushed: no match, so the page shows the dialog and no table) and at every refold, and kept by a refold (`show()` carries it across). An honest list keeps them: an insert never moves or changes an element, and a kept entry rejected now (a concurrent insert landed before it while the page was away) is still there, as within a life. The Session takes `known` and passes it on. The page keeps them in IndexedDB (`net/kept.js`, a database of its own beside the repo's, per match and device), soon after each change of its battle settles, and only once `repo.flush([id])` has the document on disk: a kept entry the stored document lacked would read as gone, a false alarm, when the page came back offline. A log found tampered with is never kept over what was. merge-sim's edges hold it (an honest reload with an insert among the kept entries; one gone, one under another body, one out of its order; one rejected after a refold and then gone, which only the kept entries catch), with five mutants (ignored, held at the first fold only, lost by a refold, by ids alone, held only from the second sync on); three of R8's tamper mutants were rewritten for the fold's new shape.
- **Rejoin.** A page that kept something of the battle says so as it comes back: "Back in the battle: N moves since you were last here" (N from the count kept), or "Back in the battle". Each save also notes the battle in `localStorage['ts.last']` (its id, this tab's device, a self-hosted sync server, its status and round, who it is against), and the title offers Continue your online battle (`ui/screens/title.js`) for one still live within three days, by its link with `&dev=`: the seat this tab played, without having kept the link. A reload already rejoined (N2: the same path as a late joiner); this is the part a player sees.
- **Moves.** A battle's moves are its accepted entries in fold order (`Folder.acceptedEntries()`); a Folder fed only those folds to the same match (a rejected entry changes nothing: not the match, not a head, and an accepted id is never one seen before it). So the match after move k is a Session of its own over a LocalStore of the first k + 1, no seat played there, the AI playing inside its fold as it did: a move is a log entry, and an AI's whole turn is the entry that handed it over (a watched battle against the AI is one move). An online log's open comes first: the start is found by its kind.
- **The flow shows another Session** (`app/flow.js`). `battle` is the battle's own Session; `show(session)` puts another on the battle's own table (the same setup: snapped to it, its battle log made again, the end screen, a banner and the tray put away), and `showStart(session, setup)` draws the battle's table as it stood before anything happened, as `start()` does, for a Session whose store holds no start yet. The Session shown before hands over (`hand`): the battle's own goes on folding with no table, its status and what the page keeps still heard online and the bar told; a replay's is closed. Only the battle's own Session catches up (§2.7's elastic catch-up never boosts or snaps a replay) or is kept, and the opponent's ghost is drawn only on it. A new battle, a followed match and Back each close the replay first.
- **The replay** (`app/replay.js`, `ui/replaybar.js`). A bar along the bottom (over the end screen, which a replay's end puts up again): ⏮ watches from the start (the table as it stood, then each move written into the replay's Session once the table has played the last, a 400 ms rest at speed 1, the page's own ⏩ speed), ▶/⏸, a slider that scrubs to a move as it is let go of (or a quarter second after the last nudge), Live (a battle still going on: the replay comes back to it once it has caught up, moves that landed meanwhile played too; at Live the slider follows the battle's last move), 💾, and ✕ for a battle that is over or a file's (one that isn't over: back to the war room). A page watching an online battle (no seat of its own) has the bar from the start, at Live; any page gets it from the end screen's Watch the replay, and from a frozen match's Keep watching.
- **Replay files.** 💾 saves `{ replay: 'tails-and-scales', version: 1, core, rules, saved, log }`, `log` every entry's text as the store keeps it (refused entries and junk too: a fold of it is the battle, every entry held to the rules as when it was played); the title's 📼 Watch a replay file opens one (`openReplay`: a log of at most 6,000 texts of at most 4 kB, else why not), folds it in a Session with no seat played here, follows it and watches it from the start. A file from another version of the game folds read-only (skew), and says so.
- **The checks.** `sim/replay-check.mjs` (Node): app/replay.js over a stand-in flow on every corpus battle's log (the human battles' as an online log, its open first and a stale entry after the third move; the AI battles' as one played alone): a scrub to every move (40 on long battles) hashes as the battle did after it, before the start draws the start's own setup; from the start, the moves written one at a time hand on exactly the battle's events and end on its match; a replay of a battle going on, three moves landing half way, plays them and comes back to Live; the file opens again to the same texts, rejected entries and match; a Session given the battle's own kept entries folds it as before, and one that lost its last is tamper with no match; ✕ shows the battle again. `--self-test`: nine mutants (a scrub one move short, the moves every good entry pushed, a skipped move, the start taken as the first move, never back at Live, a file without its first entry, any JSON with a log opened, ✕ leaving the replay up, and from the review a replay that never checks its moves against a battle folded again). `sim/lobby-rig.mjs` gains `scrub` (a watching page's bar at Live; the slider to a middle move shows its hash; moves landing meanwhile folded but not shown; Live), `replay` (⏮ on a battle going on, moves landing while it plays, back at Live, the battle log the match's), `files` (a seated page's Watch the replay at the end, 💾 downloads the whole log, a fresh page's 📼 plays it to the same match and log) and `kept` (the toast on coming back after moves landed; Continue on the title back to seat 1; then an entry the page played deleted from the log while it was away, its own stored document set aside, is the tamper dialog with no match), with eight mutants (no bar for a watcher, a scrub that shows the battle itself, a replay that never comes back to Live, a dead Watch the replay, the file never read, nothing kept used, no Continue, and from the review Back from the tamper dialog leaving the match attached); `kept` ends with that Back: the title, no badge, no link, no Continue.
- **The review** (one reviewer; seven findings, each confirmed by the code or a repro, and fixed). Medium: Back from the dialog of a log found tampered with as the page came back left the match attached (no table had been followed, so the flow never let go: the badge, the tick and the link stayed; Back now lets go of it, and the title offers it no more); ✕ on a replay file of a battle not over showed that battle with no way back (✕ on a battle that isn't over now goes to the war room). Lower: a replay writing moves by their place stalled once the battle folded again under it (a concurrent insert before a move it had played: the move it wrote next was a duplicate, refused, nothing to play; it now checks the replay's own moves against the battle's before each and makes the replay again at its move, replay-check's `refold` and the `no-refold-check` mutant); Keep watching on a battle already being replayed reset the bar's move under the replay; a replay Session's status reached the online page's frozen dialog (only the battle's own is heard now); a change still to be kept as the page let go of the match was lost (it is noted and written then), and what a page keeps is per match and device (two tabs of one browser each say what came while they were away); the slider jumped back under a hand dragging it as the battle moved on.
- **Not built.** A scrub folds its moves from the start each time (a battle's hundred-odd moves fold in well under a second here); S6's checkpoints are the seam for Grand battles. A replay file is the log, unsigned: it plays whatever its entries say, under the same rules a peer is held to. Spectators read no names on the HUD (races, as before). An AI seat online is still F11b's.

**F6 as built** (race selection; consensus untouched: no bump, the corpus unchanged, the classic lines byte-identical):
- **The battle-setup panel** (`ui/screens/setup.js`, `#setup`). A title-screen mode button opens it rather than the battle: a line for the mode ("Against the AI: you hold the west edge", "Two players, one screen", "Watch the AI fight"), a card per seat (who plays it: You, The AI or Player N; its edge; its race in the picker), a note when both seats are one race, Back to the title and Start the battle. Its races start as the page's (`?races=`, else the classic pair) and then are the last ones chosen (`flow.races`); Start is `flow.start(mode, races)`, which refuses a race it doesn't know (a toast, the title again). The panel is the page's cards over the table, no backdrop: each seat's figure window is left clear.
- **The race picker** (`ui/screens/races.js`): a button per race (`Object.entries(RACES)`, so a new race is offered with no edit here), the race's figures, and under them the stats of the figure the pointer rests on (a tap on touch), as the unit card shows them (`ui/card.js`'s `statsHtml`, which the card now uses too). Not editable (another player's seat), it shows its race's button alone.
- **The diorama** (`view/diorama.js`): the table's own renderer draws each window after the table's frame, a scissor viewport over the element's rect (no second WebGL context, so no second upload of the template cache). One figure per unit of the race, in its army's order, the big ones in a row behind, on a felt plinth, idling as on the table, the plinth turning a little to and fro; the camera frames the plinth's width whatever the window's shape. Its rims are the seat's colour as the battle would paint it. Nothing is built until a window is first shown, so the title's first frame and its `Math.random` draws are the table's (`sim/title-shot.mjs`); it draws nothing under `?fast` (the stage skips it, as the harnesses run). A race shown again is a figure's base (the template cache); `hide` frees the figures.
- **The lobby's seat cards** (`ui/screens/lobby.js`): the same picker in each seat, its parts kept across renders (the lobby redraws a seat's card at every change). Your own seat's buttons choose your race (the `<select>` N2 built is gone); another player's seat, or a free one (the race it would bring), shows its race alone. Colours as the battle would give them (`sidesFor` over the lobby's races; a race the code doesn't know, a peer's, shows no figures). The lobby is cards over the table too, and the title is put away while it is up (`body.lobbying`).
- **R2's leftovers.** Seat names in a mirror match: `core/match.js`'s `seatName(G, s, form)` is the race's name, and in a mirror match its edge as well ("Bushtail Clans (west)"), in the roll-off's dice rows and line, the "deploy your army" lines, the end-of-round line and the vote's lines; `ui/theme.js`'s `sidesFor` names the seats so for the HUD, the banner, the card and the end screen, and the AI hint reads "Bushtail Clans (east), the AI, are taking their turn…". Only a mirror match's text changes, and the journal and the dice rows are no match state (`stateHash` leaves the journal out), so nothing bumps and the corpus, which holds no mirror match, replays byte for byte. A stronger cue on the table: the east army's base rims 2.4 times as thick (`rimOf`, through `view/models/kit.js`'s `base` and the template cache) and its unit labels filled in its colour (`body.mirror`).
- **The harnesses.** `sim/chromium.mjs` (parity `--browser`, P-browser, and self-test's mutant-title row, whose message names the panel's Start too), play-check, snap-check, hud-check and rematch-memory press `#setupStart` after the mode button, with the panel's defaults as the URL set them. No path skips the panel.
- **The checks.** mirror-check holds the names: in a mirror match the roll-off line names the winner and each round's line both seats by race and edge, in any other match by race alone (a `seatName` without edges fails five of its battles). data-check holds `sidesFor`'s names and `mirror` flag. flag-lint allows the picker's and the diorama's race tests (which button is on, a race shown again, the last race's stats put away), each presentation.
- **The review** (one reviewer; five findings, each confirmed by the code, most by a repro, and fixed). Medium: in the lobby, another seat's card left its race's button live, and its `pick` is your own seat's, so the host alone could click the free seat's race and become it (a seat not yours now shows its race's button disabled, picking nothing; lobby-rig's `play` holds it). Medium-low: a `#m=` link opened over the battle-setup panel left the panel up over the lobby or the match (its Start then dropped the online match); going online now puts the panel away. Lower: a peer's race this code doesn't know left its figure window clear onto the table (it is shut now, `.dwin.empty`); a mirror match's selected east unit lost its highlight under the filled label; a picker let go of and shown again kept the last unit's stats.
- **Not built.** The panel's terrain line (F7a), battle size (F8b) and army line (F11b). An AI seat online (F11b).

**S0-S3 as built** (scale hygiene; consensus untouched in what it decides: no bump, the corpus byte-identical, every scan the same cells in the same order with the same doubles):
- **S0, bounded scans.** `core/ai/score.js`'s `scanBox(nav, x, z, reach)`: the board's rows and columns within `reach` of a point, a cell either side to spare. A plan of at most `max` inches has no finite cell outside it (a cell's distance is the start's offset plus the path, no shorter than the straight line from where the unit stands). `bestSpot` walks its lattice only inside the plan's box, on the board's own lattice rows and columns (row `iz` a multiple of the step, its columns from its row's offset), so it scores, and draws for, exactly the cells the whole board's scan did, in their order. The fall back's scan moved out of `aiMove` into `fallbackSpot(G, u, plan)` (the same code, so the check can reach it) and visits the box's even cells. `freeSpot` visits the zone's columns, one either side to spare, row by row. `forbidMask` reads the grid's own `W`/`H`. `core/deploy.js` exports `zone` and `fits` (for the reference scan). (F7a's review: with height a ladder carries a climber farther than it costs, so the box grows by `nav.linkSave × floor(max / nav.linkMin)`, the most any link carries beyond its cost times the links a plan can take; on a board with no such link it is the box it was. P-scan holds it.)
- **S1, hoisted facts.** `bestSpot` works out once per enemy what every cell's score asks of it: `isEngaged`, `inCover`, `meleeValue(u, e)` and `meleeValue(e, u)` (`ctx.pre`); `shotValue` and `sight` take them as optional arguments (`pre`, `bCover`), and other callers still ask afresh. `p2D6` reads a table the same loop filled for a whole `need` from 0 to 13.
- **S0b, the line-of-sight broadphase** (`core/terrain/terrain.js`). Chunks are binned on a 4" grid as they join, from their bounding circle's box plus 0.01" (a chunk never moves sideways, a collapse only lowers it); `los` tests only the chunks in the bins its segment passes through (0.01" to spare), in chunk order, so a blocker still returns as soon as it is met and `obscure`, a count, is the same; with an end off the table it tests every chunk, as before.
- **S3, one mask and a plan memo.** `movePlan` builds the end's forbid mask once and uses it for the walk too, unless the unit falls back. `apply` (and `createMatch`'s first advance, where an AI battle plays itself) opens `G.nav.memo` in a `try` and shuts it in its `finally`; inside it, `movePlan` keeps the last plan it made (`{ sig, plan }`, its key and itself: one slot: those asks come one after another, and a `Map` kept every plan of an AI battle, which `createMatch` plays as one apply, up to 90 MB at Grand) and reads it back for the same unit where it stands, its base, the same extra inches, the same nav epoch (`rebuild` counts them; the lookup comes after `refreshNav`) and every live unit's place and base (`planKey`, numbers exactly, -0 apart from 0), so the AI's plan for a move and the move's own (its legality, the handler's) are made once. Nothing outside an apply sees the memo (a preview, the HUD, the Folder's `legal()` before an apply): those plans are always fresh. The memo is derived state: not hashed, null between commands.
- **The Grand fixture** (`sim/fixtures/grand.mjs`, §4.2.9): a copy of `core/`, `data/` and `match/` in `sim/.fixtures/` (gitignored), patched to 80×56 with 14" zones, 7 rounds, the grand mission's nine objectives, the classic set at pairs [24, 12] and 4,800 attempts, and the ×3 armies (21 units a side) or, `--caps`, the cap lists (every slot but Troops full, then Troops fewest models first: the Bushtails 23 units and 89 models, the Coil 24 and 84, as §4.2.1 measured). Each patch must match exactly once, or the build names its anchor.
- **The checks.** `sim/scale-check.mjs` (and `--self-test`): **P-scan** on 781 classic and 435 Grand states sampled inside AI battles (a unit at random, plans with and without extra inches): `bestSpot` returns what the whole board's lattice returned with every fact asked afresh, and leaves the dice where it did; `fallbackSpot` and `freeSpot` the cell the whole board's scan found (the reference scans, the code as it was, are `sim/oracle/scan-ref.mjs`). **P-los**: 20,000 segments on classic boards 1-500 and 6,000 on Grand boards 1-100, after random blasts, a tenth of the ends off the table: `{ blocked, obscure }` as every chunk's scan. **P-memo**: every plan an AI battle's fold reads back from its memo (521 on 12 classic battles, 361 on 2 Grand ones: the AI's plan asked for again by the move's legality check and its handler, each read watched and held to a fresh plan made with the memo set aside), each a fresh one's equal (`dist`, `prev`, both masks and their discs, `fallback`); 1,043 classic and 149 Grand plans asked by a probe inside applies (half of them the plan the fold made last: 294 and 37 read back), likewise, and asked again the same object; the 18 human logs folded with previews (plans for random units through `preview`) between their entries, trace, shadow, writes and `stateHash` as without, the memo null between entries; an apply that throws leaves it null. The reference scores as the code did before S1 (its `score` and `shotValue`, every fact asked afresh, `p2D6` counted), so P-scan judges the hoisting too. The self-test's ten broken copies (a box too tight, a lattice row's offset swapped, the fall back's odd cells, a zone's columns cut short, two facts hoisted wrong, chunks binned short, chunks met out of order, a memo key without the other units, a memo left open by a throw) are each caught; a key without the nav epoch is no fault a fold can show (nothing rebuilds the grid between the AI's plan and its read-backs), and the epoch stays in the key all the same. Parity 42/42 through the Folder, perturb (0/24 moved), property, data-check, flag-lint, boundaries, terrain-check, hooks-inert.
- **The review** (one reviewer; no input found where the new code behaves differently: 2,400 fuzzed scan probes with cramped starts and units on the edges, 144,000 line-of-sight segments along bin lines and the board's edge, every memo hit of a classic and a Grand battle checked against a fresh plan). Medium: the memo, a `Map`, was never emptied in an AI battle (one apply), 81-100 MB at Grand where the code before held 8 (the single slot now; every hit was on the last plan stored). Lower, in the checks: the reference scored with the new `score`, so a fact hoisted wrong inside it passed P-scan (35 of 42 battles differed in parity; the reference now scores as before S1, and `hoist-back` is a mutant); P-memo's probes, at trace lines, rarely met the fold's own hits (now watched as they happen).
- **scale-bench** (`sim/scale-bench.mjs`, a report): createMatch to the deployment, each AI movement phase (p50 / p90 / max) and a whole AI battle folded quietly, on the corpus's classic boards and on the Grand fixture with the presets and the cap lists, Grand against §4.2.1's budget (fails above 1.5×); `--dir` measures another copy of the code, for a before-and-after. On a quiet machine here (8 Grand boards, the medians; before is F6's commit): Grand with the presets, createMatch 40.9 → 27.3 ms, a movement phase's p90 38.0 → 34.0 ms, a battle 483 → 366 ms; on the cap lists 49.5 → 31.2, 43.7 → 46.3 and 540 → 446 ms (within 1.5× of every budget, the battle's 1.05× and 1.27×); classic unchanged (65 ms a battle). A first broadphase made a Set and sorted it on every `los` call, which cost classic a fifth of its time (68 → 82 ms a battle, the bins off: 59-66); it now marks each chunk met with a stamp and sorts a reused buffer of places in insertion order, and classic is back where it was. The fixture's first armies were the classic ones (its race module imported before its patch, so the module cache kept the classic list for its core): scale-bench and scale-check now refuse a fixture whose battles field fewer units than its lists.

**F10a as built** (group selection and one-shot group orders; client code only: no bump, the corpus byte-identical, nothing new in the log but the ordinary commands a group sends):
- **The selection** (`input/selection.js`): per seat `{ group, lead, saved, pin, note, advance }`, local to the page and never logged, so a hotseat's seats keep their own (the bar's note and +D6 too). The members are the ids still standing in the match the table shows; a unit that falls drops out of `members()` (no separate prune). Once the table has caught up after an action (the human's `idled`, whenever the record holds two or more ids), a group keeps the members still able to act (`settle`), its lead's card on them, a pin made before the action planned again from the match as it now stands (or dropped, its target fallen or fewer than two left), and a fallen target's note counting the members kept; the group's line shows on its lead's card only, a one-unit pick or a toggle clears the note, a deployment's end lets the deploying seat's group and pin go, and a new match (or a followed one) starts every seat afresh. While a group is picked the HUD's Advance button gives way to the bar's +D6.
- **The input** (`input/group.js`, `GroupInput`, handed a click, a hover, a key and the pointer before `input/human.js`'s one-unit tools): Shift-drag a box (Ctrl or Cmd too: add), the seat's own units whose centre on screen (`UnitViews.screen`, kept as `animate` projects each label) lies inside it, the box saying how many enemy units and models it covers and picking none of them; Shift-, Ctrl- or Cmd-click adds or drops one; a double click on a unit (the same unit twice) picks every one of its type on screen, a third the whole table; Q and the actions' **Ready N** every unit still to act; Tab / Shift-Tab the next or last of them, alone, the camera gliding to it (`CameraRig.glide`); Ctrl-1…9 saves, 1…9 recalls (the same twice within 600 ms: the camera to it); Space the camera to the group (Home was already the overview); Esc drops a pin, then the group. On touch, **▭ Select** sets OrbitControls' one-finger gesture to none instead of disabling the controls (a disabled control would leave two fingers nothing), and only while a seat played here may pick (else a finger orbits as ever): one finger draws the box, two still pan and pinch (OrbitControls has no two-finger pan with rotate; rotating waits for Select mode off), and a second finger lets a box or a line go, the camera free again; a finger held 450 ms on one of the seat's units adds or drops it, in Select mode or not (a 10 ms vibrate), and its lift is no click even if it wandered; no press is timed while another pointer is down, and a press that ever had two pointers down is never a click. The mouse's box and an Alt-drag hold the camera still until let go, whichever button lifts, and a cancelled pointer lets them go (the pinned formation's ghosts drawn again over an unfinished line's). The group's keys stand aside while a dialog is open or a field has focus, and leave Space to a focused button; Enter, sending a pin, is the pin's (a focused button doesn't click as well).
- **Pin, then send.** With two or more picked, a ground click in the deployment or the movement phase pins the formation (`previewGroup`'s ghosts: a ring per member, white arriving, amber falling short, and a flag, made the first time one is shown); an **Alt-drag** pins it spread along the line dragged (`slotsOf(…, line)`: the members in the order they stand along it, one rank spanning the line when the group fits, else ranks of `2 × the largest base + 0.5"` stepping back toward where the group stands). The flag (a click within 1.2"), Enter or ✓ sends it, a double click (the second click within 320 ms and 6 px of the first; a quick click elsewhere only moves the pin) pins and sends; Esc, a right click (no drag) or ✕ drops it. **+D6** in the bar makes a Move advance each member first (the preview plans the plain move and says "+D6 each"; the executor sends `advance`, then plans the member again on its roll). An enemy clicked in the movement phase pins an approach; in the shooting phase every member that may fires at it, in the AI's shooting order, stopping once it falls; in the charge phase every member that may charges it, each contact ended with the shortest move (`chargeEnd {c: -1}`). A single unit keeps today's one-click move.
- **The planner** (`present/orders.js`) is §4.2.6's (its goal fields the last 12 kept per match): a member in combat is left where it stands ("in combat": a group order never makes it fall back); members planned nearest the anchor first, each later one meeting the earlier where they were sent (`at`; core `validEnd(G, plan, i, at = null)` reads `at.get(o.id) ?? o.pos`, null being today's code, parity unchanged). A shooter's approach stays put when the target is in range and in sight where it stands (range and sight, not `shotInfo`, whose "locked in combat" another member's move can change). Fire's summary adds the models it should slay (`rules.expected`, as the tooltip's odds; blasts and spells left out) and why the rest can't.
- **The executor** (`input/orders.js`, `runGroup`) plans each member again from the session's match with the first preview's slots (and line), checks `legal`, submits, and waits for the entry to fold before the next (10 s online, then "Orders paused"). Fire and Charge send only for the members the first preview named, so the bar's "N of M fire" is what is sent; a member a blast's rubble has since given sight stays picked for the next click.
- **The bar** (`ui/groupbar.js`) shows with two or more picked: the count and models, a chip per type (only these; right-click or long-press: drop them; greyed with "N can't act now"), ⇥, the phase's verb as a hint, +D6 in the movement phase, ✓ Send and ✕ once pinned, ＋Save, Clear and the pin's summary or the last note. It sits beside the unit card on a wide screen (wrapping upward rather than over it); on a phone the card steps aside while a group is picked. The card heads its lead's lines with the group's count and models, and the hint line names the group's verb.
- **Picking far units.** `Picker.pick` falls back on the standing figure whose centre on screen is nearest the pointer, within 14 px (a finger: 24); a unit that falls loses its place on screen.
- **Online.** Presence carries the group as `sels` (≤ 120 ids, two or more; `sel` stays the lead's id); a peer's group is drawn as dashed rings in its seat's colour (at most 24, standing units only), gone with the match.
- **Not built here** (ROADMAP's F10c line keeps them): the pinned formation's own handles (move, rotate, stretch; a second ground click moves the pin, and Alt-drag makes a line, but touch has no way to make one), its faint paths, and the per-frame and 150 ms-rest scheduling of ghosts, which classic boards don't need (a whole group's preview is a few ms).
- **The checks.** `sim/macro-check.mjs` (and `--self-test`): **P-macro** over Sessions on states the human corpus logs pass through, a random group (2-6 of a seat's units) and a random target, a third of the point orders in a line and a third of the moves +D6: 240 group actions (move 59, approach 36, place 21, fire 62, charge 46; 32 in a line, 25 +D6) sent 368 commands, every one taken; 134 members landed on the cell their preview drew, 81 it left in place stayed, and the +D6 moves' 106 members each acted at most once, inside the group; no member in combat was sent a move; Fire shot only with the members the preview named, and with every one of them that could still shoot the standing target; Charge left no end open; each under 1 s, +D6 included. `--probes 400 --seed 1`, `--seed 2026` and `--seed 11` hold too (575, 527 and 510 commands). Its five broken copies (a preview that ignores the members before it, one that lets a member in combat fall back, an executor that loses the formation's slots or its line, a Fire that stops after one shot) are each caught. `sim/input-check.mjs` (Chromium, by mouse, keys and real touches through CDP) plays 23 steps from the title: the box picks exactly the units inside it, Shift-click, pin and Esc, Enter, the flag, a right click, an Alt-drag line placed member for member where its ghosts stood, a box over the enemy counted and picking none, a double click, Ready N, Tab round each unit once, the touch fallback (a touch 19 px off a far figure picks it, the mouse there nothing), Select mode (a finger's box with the camera still, two fingers moving it), a long press out and back in, the bar's verbs in three phases, a group of three whose lead moved keeping the other two once the table caught up, a lone unit's one-click move, a group move by its flag, +D6 (advance, then move), the chips greyed, Space; the seat's longest gun is left unmoved so the shooting phase is played (the engine skips a phase where nothing can act), and a group Fire whose leftovers stay picked runs when some enemy is in range of only part of the group (on its seed, none is). `sim/lobby-rig.mjs`'s `group` case places and moves a group online, nothing refused, the other page seeing the group in its presence and folding the same match (its `no-sels` mutant caught). Parity 42/42, flag-lint, boundaries, hooks-inert, data-check, present-check, property, self-test, bundle-check.
- **The review** (one reviewer, then three verifiers on its fixes and one on these notes; consensus untouched: `validEnd` with no `at` is the code as it was, and the planner runs only under the preview's lock). High: once the table caught up after a group's action, the human's `idled` picked up the lead alone (a group that fired lost its leftovers, a group move its members); now `settle`. Medium: two quick clicks apart sent a pin (a double click needs the same spot); a fallen unit's last place on screen stayed pickable; a group Move made members in combat fall back (now left in place, and P-macro holds it, with a mutant); a Fire re-planned per member shot with ones the preview hadn't named (only those named fire, P-macro holds it on four seeds). Lower: goal fields cached without bound (the last 12), a stale group line on other cards, notes and +D6 shared between a hotseat's seats, a pin outliving an advance, the deploying seat's pin left after its deployment, a selection carried into the next match, OrbitControls left disabled after a cancelled pointer, a chorded button or a second finger, a long press timed under a two-finger gesture or forgotten when its finger wandered, Select mode leaving a finger dead outside one's turn, Enter clicking a focused button too, dead units' rings online and the peer's rings left after a match.

**V1 as built** (batched playback; view only: no bump, the corpus byte-identical, the mirror folding every event in order):
- **The rule** (`present/pace.js`, pure): `batchAt(events, k, sideOf)` is §4.2.7's batch from event k: one seat's walks separated only by instant events (a focus, a pause of 0.2 s or less, objectives, status, act, log, a tray opened, an advance's dice, the match waiting on a seat, `pending`, so a batch runs across a human's entries, and ?debug's checkpoints: app/boot.js puts a `check` after each action and stop, for P-present and snap-check), the quiet events after the last walk its own up to the next unit's focus, tray or dice; two walks at least. `batchesOf` cuts a stream into steps, `playTime` times one (PACE.cost's estimate, a batch until its last walk ends), and the player's `backlog()` (the elastic catch-up's) is `playTime` of its queue, batched or not as it plays.
- **A change from §4.2.7: a wrecker's walk no longer plays alone.** With the serpents' three Brutes on the Grand fixture moving first in their movement phase, their walks played alone made a Grand AI movement phase 11.6 s, over its 8 s. Its reason was that a walker planned after a smash must not pass through a wall before it falls; so a walk that smashes holds back the walks after it in its batch until its last smash has played (`smashDone`: the walk's own timing, view/units.js's eased tween, inverted), and a stomp that smashes nothing walks like any other. Every walk still starts at least PACE.stagger (0.15 s) after the last.
- **The player** (`view/player.js`): with `batched` on, `run()` asks `batchAt` at its head (the seats from the flow's `sideOf`: the mirror holds none); a walk reaching an idle table waits a tick (`push()`), so the commands sent with it (a group order's members, submitted one after another) join its batch; a batch plays as one step (`batch()`): its advance dice in one tray row ("Advance · 5 units", "D6 each"), then its events in order, each folded into the mirror (and handed the ?debug observer) as it plays, each walk started at its `b.starts`, the first focus followed and the rest, the pauses and the per-unit trays and dice left out, instant handlers' promises (a checkpoint's pause) awaited; it is over when every walk is. The flags' owners as each walk changes them show once that walk has arrived (`View.holdOwners`, the owners held through the batch, in order, by the batch's own token; let go however the batch ends, by a snap of the page's own table, or by a handler failing), so a flag doesn't turn while its unit is still on the way. A snap mid-batch ends it (the table counter, as a handler's promise). `batches` counts what has played.
- **The setting.** The HUD's ⇉ turns batching off ("one at a time", as before V1), kept in this browser (`tails-and-scales:oneAtATime`, every access in try/catch).
- **Measured** (`sim/playback-check.mjs`, PACE's estimate; phases the table plays in one go, an AI's or a watched battle's): classic, 42 corpus battles, 397 batches of 4.7 walks (121 across a human's entries): an AI movement phase 6.0 → 2.6 s on average, the longest 13.6 → 4.7 s; a battle 218 → 185 s. Grand, 4 fixture AI battles, 56 batches of 13.5 walks (18 wrecks among them): an AI movement phase 19.5 → 4.5 s, the longest 35.5 → 7.3 s (§4.2.1's budget 8 s, its estimate 4.2 / 5.2 s); a battle 558 → 349 s, **over §4.2.1's 200 s** (its estimate 165 s): batched movement is now about 63 s of it, and the shooting alone, which V1 doesn't batch, about 165 s. The whole-battle budget stays open (a batched volley, or a faster spectator pace, is a later step's).
- **The checks.** `sim/playback-check.mjs` (and `--self-test`): the rule on eight made-up streams (two seats' walks, a charge's dice, a long pause, a wound, advance dice in one row, a wreck, a batch across entries, where a batch ends and which dice are its), then every corpus battle's stream (AI battles as createMatch plays them, human logs entry by entry) and the Grand fixture's: each batch two or more walks of one seat and nothing but walks and instant events (the check's own list), its walks 0.15 s apart (the spec's, pinned in the check) and none before an earlier wreck's last smash (the check's own timing, by bisection), the steps cutting the stream end to end in order, no phase longer batched, a Grand AI movement phase within 8 s. Its seven broken rules (batching across seats, walks let go before a wreck's smashes, a charge's dice let through, one walk called a batch, the walks started together, a batch swallowing the next unit's opening, its dice taken from past its end) are each caught. `--browser`: a watched battle in Chromium plays its batches, the player's own seat lookup names every unit's seat, and with ⇉ off the next battle plays none, no page error. P-present (present-check: the page in Node, batching on) holds the mirror at every act and checkpoint as before; snap-check holds the table at every drained queue and checkpoint, batches included; lobby-rig's catch-up holds the elastic catch-up over a batched backlog.

**F10b as built** (`pilot {m}`, the one consensus kind of F10; consensus: `CORE_VERSION` 3, the classic corpus byte-identical, `stateHash` as under 2):
- **The rule.** `pilot {m}` answers a phase decision: the AI plays the rest of that phase for the units mask m names, now, and the seat keeps its phase (`HANDLERS.pilot` is `runAI(G, seat, phase, maskUnits(G, seat, m))`; no line of its own in the battle log). Bit j is the seat's j-th unit in `G.units` order, dead or alive, so a mask names the same units on every peer for the whole battle; `core/queries.js`'s `maskUnits` (null for a bit past the seat's last unit, by exact division) and `maskOf` (a doubling bit: core/ keeps out `**`). `mayPilot`, in §4.2.6's order: a safe whole number of at least 1, no bit past the seat's units, no named unit destroyed, and one of them at least `canAct` in the phase. Whether the AI then plays it is the AI's: a shooter with no shot worth 0.4, a charge under its odds, a brawler stuck in combat, so a pilot may play nothing (and may be sent again, playing nothing new).
- **The AI under a mask.** `runAI(G, seat, phase, only = null)` and `aiPhase(G, side, phase, only = null)` pass a filter to `aiMove`, `aiShoot` and `aiCharge`, which drop the units outside it from their list before their role sort: the units kept are played as with the rest, in the same order, with the same draws between the same yields; a charge goes straight on to the shortest move (`via` 'ai', as Auto's), so no `chargeEnd` opens; a unit in combat may fall back, as under Auto. A pilot naming every standing unit, then `end`, is `auto` (P-auto, below).
- **The bump.** `CORE_VERSION` 3 (the rules take a command they refused). No match state is new, so `sim/data-check.mjs` pins version 3's `stateHash`es to 1's and 2's; no corpus battle changed (parity 42 of 42). The entry is 85-89 B on a four-letter device (`{"d":"here","h":…,"id":"here.3.0","m":127,"p":…,"s":1,"t":"pilot"}`, `h` carried: a single seat's decision); an online device's longer name counts twice (`d` and `id`).
- **The input.** The group bar's **🤖 Auto these** (`ui/groupbar.js`; `input/group.js`'s `pilot()`, through `input/human.js`'s `pilot(ids)`, the mask from the match's own `maskOf` under the preview's lock): in a phase of a seat played here, while one of the group can act ("none of them can act now" otherwise); the bar's note says so, and the members the AI left (no shot worth taking, a charge too long) stay picked and ready once the table has caught up (`settle`, F10a's). Today's 🤖 Auto, the AI playing the whole phase and ending it, keeps its place and meaning. The Controls help says both. `?debug`'s `__ts.pilot(m)` sends a mask as the button would (for sim/'s driver).
- **The checks.** `sim/pilot-check.mjs` (**P-auto**, and `--self-test`): every corpus battle's seeds as two all-human matches in step, one answering every phase with `auto`, the other with a pilot of every standing unit (when legal) and `end`; and every corpus human log played as it is and with each `auto` replaced so (an Auto part-way through a phase, after the seat's own moves and an advance's roll); the trace, `rngState` and `stateHash` the same after every phase: 42 battles, 1,263 phases, 1,258 pilots (1,143 played something, 5 phases with nobody able to act). Its four broken copies, each caught: a pilot leaving out the first unit it names, one rolling a die of its own, one logging a line, and a mask whose bits count only standing units (they shift as units die). **P-pilot** in P-prop (`sim/property.mjs`): the battery judges a pilot of every standing unit, one, a random few, one naming a dead unit, one of units none of which can act, a bit past the seat's last unit, 0, −1, 2^53, 1.5, none and an extra field; legal() may accept only a pilot naming standing units of the seat, one at least able to act, in a phase (the mask decoded by the check itself, not by the core's `maskUnits`, which a fault there would excuse); the random games send pilots (one a phase: a pilot of units the AI declines to play stays legal and does nothing again), and after each the seat's units outside the mask stand where they stood with the same flags, and the seat still holds its phase: 40 games, 121 pilots. Five more self-test edits, each caught (32 of 32): the AI ignoring the mask, a dead unit named, stray bits ignored, a pilot of units none of which can act, and a pilot that ends the phase. `sim/input-check.mjs` presses Auto these for two of the other seat's units in its movement phase: one `pilot`, its mask the group's, only they moved, the phase still that seat's. The human-bot (`sim/oracle/human-bot.mjs`) replays `pilot` entries through the hook (the gates a click has: standing units of the seat, one able to act) and gains a `pilot` policy (`random`, putting a random few of the units still to act on autopilot at most once a phase, 30% of its phases); `sim/corpus-add.mjs` takes `--policy pilot`, `--need pilot` (a pilot that played a unit in each of the three phases) and `--set pilot`, and the corpus reads log sets (`sim/lib.mjs`'s `LOG_SETS`: `human`, `pilot`; `--only pilot` picks a set).
- **The `pilot/` logs** (F10b's second commit; `sim/baselines/pilot/`). Four human-bot logs recorded on F10b's code with `sim/corpus-add.mjs --policy pilot --need pilot --set pilot` (a pilot that played a unit in each of the movement, shooting and charge phases), each admitted as the corpus's are (twice more in Node from its entries alone, then in Chromium): `hotseat-pilot-mix-1` (18 pilots), `hotseat-pilot-mix-2` (18), `bushtail-pilot-mix-2` (5) and `serpent-pilot-mix-1` (11), mixed with the seats' own moves, shots, charges, Autos and Ends. The corpus is 46 battles; the PIN moved to F10b's code commit, and `parity --pin`, parity, P-browser (`--browser --only pilot`), P-present, P-prop, replay-check, rematch-check and P-auto (46 battles, 1,384 phases, 1,379 pilots) take them; merge-sim (`--only pilot`: 16 scenarios, 1,551 entries) and P-peers (`--only pilot`: 15 scenarios, 1,388 entries) fold them on every peer to the corpus battle.
- **The review** (one reviewer; consensus untouched: no high or medium finding, `pilot` + `end` read against `auto` again, 3,256 extra pilots over the 46 setups in a scratch driver, none throwing). Four low ones, all in the checks, fixed with F10c's first commit: P-pilot held the units outside the mask to where they stood, but a piloted blast's friendly fire makes an outside unit close ranks (two of the 3,256), so it holds their flags only (what a unit played sets); the battery tried no mask between 2^32 and 2^53, so a bitwise `maskUnits` (its high bits dropped) passed every gate (now three such masks, refused, and a `pilot-bitwise` self-test edit: 33 of 33 caught); "the seat keeps its phase" compared the decision's kind and seat, not the phase, so a pilot ending only the movement phase passed when the seat's shooting came next (the phase now too; P-auto already caught it); and input-check's Auto these step counted the group members that moved without requiring one. `--only human` takes the `pilot/` logs too (the kind, not the set): noted, left so.
- **Not here.** merge-sim's bursts of 25 macro entries go with F10c, whose standing orders send them (F10a's group orders wait for each entry to fold). The play-report threshold (one army on `pilot` every phase reaching melee by round 3 in 3 of 4 Grand battles) needs F8b's Grand boards.

**F10c as built** (standing orders and autopilot; client code only: no bump, the corpus byte-identical, nothing new in the log but the ordinary commands and the `pilot`s the orders send):
- **The order book** (`input/book.js`, `OrderBook`): each seat's `{ v: 1, at, units: { [id]: order } }`, never in the match or its log, in this browser's storage under `ts.orders.<key>.<seat>` (every access in try/catch), the key the battle's start entry and seeds (app/flow.js's `bookKey`: a game played here writes the same first id every time, so a new battle opens its book fresh; an online battle followed or rejoined opens its own again); opening one lets go of all but the 12 other battles saved last (`at`). A unit that falls leaves the book at the next run, and counts for nothing before (`living`). (A seat's saved groups are the selection's, for the page only.)
- **The planner** (`present/standing.js`, pure, under the preview's lock): `covers(order, phase)`, `stepOf` (what an order does for a unit now: its own commands, `pilot`, or nothing and why), `actorsOf` (End's ⟳ badge and Go's count), `orderedUnits` (the AI's role order, reversed for shots), `doneOf` and `progressOf`, as §4.2.6's table: **March** moves toward its slot by the goal field (`legFor`; an advance first when the slot is more than a move away and nothing is in range of its gun), and in the shooting phase the AI shoots for it (`pilot`); **Attack** goes for its target (brawlers the valid end nearest it, advancing past M + 12", or M + 6" for those who may charge after; shooters `approachFor`), shoots it when the shot is on (else `pilot`), and charges it at odds of 25% (melee) or 42%, the shortest move after; **Hold** is `pilot` in the shooting phase; **Autopilot** is `pilot` in every phase. A unit in combat never falls back under March or Attack. Done: a march within **1.5"** of its slot holds ("Arrived": the planner's own reach, so a slot crowded by friends still counts; §4.2.6 said 1"), one that has gained under half an inch on its anchor two movement phases running goes back to the player ("Blocked"), an attack whose target fell goes on autopilot ("Target down").
- **The executor** (`input/orders.js`'s `runOrders`, from End, ▶ Go and Auto: never from a sink's events): March and Attack first, each unit planned again from the match as the last command left it (an advance sent alone, then the unit planned on its roll; a charge's end only if the charge opened one), then one `pilot` for every unit whose order calls for the AI and that can still act, then `end` (End) or `auto` (Auto), or nothing (Go: the phase stays open). Online it waits on each entry's fold (F10a's 10 s, then "Orders paused"). A refused command skips its unit ("N orders blocked"); none is retried. Afterwards the book is brought up to date from the match (`input/standing.js`'s `after`), with a toast for what finished.
- **Giving orders** (`input/standing.js`, `StandingInput`): the group bar's ➜ March, 🎯 Attack, ⚓ Hold, ⟳ Autopilot and ⊘ (each with how many of the group hold it), the unit card's row (a single unit's orders, on touch the only way), and the keys **G**, **T**, **H**, **P**, **X**. March and Attack arm a click (the place, each member to its slot in the formation round it, `slotsOf`; the enemy); Esc lets it go. Orders can be given whenever the selection works (the seat's deployment or its phase), so a deployment's March acts from the first movement phase.
- **What it shows.** End reads "End Movement ▸ · ⟳ 3" when the orders will act for three; ▶ **Go (3)** shows only then; **Orders N** counts the seat's ordered units and picks them up; `end.ready` (F3's lit End) counts the manual units only, a unit whose order covers the phase counting as handled; an ordered unit that can still act rings cyan, not white; each label carries its order's glyph (a `data-ord` attribute the label's style shows, so the label's HTML, which the snap check compares, is the match's); the lines of the picked units' orders are drawn (a march's to its slot, with a ghost ring there; an attack's to its target), **O** all of them; toasts say "Your orders: N units" and what arrived, was blocked or saw its target fall.
- **The settings** (the HUD's ⟳¹ and ⏭, kept in this browser). **Autopilot first**: the seat's units on autopilot play as its phase opens, answered from the Session's `settled` (a change folded whole), once per (round, turn, phase, seat), re-checking that the match still waits on that seat there. **Auto-End**: once the table has caught up (the human's `idled`), or an order changes, and nothing is left for the player's own hand with every unit still able to act under orders (End lit), a 1.5 s countdown fills End; a key, a press on the table or End itself stops it; it presses End (its orders, then the end) once per phase, re-checking the decision when it fires.
- **Online.** Presence carries the seat's orders as `ords` (a kind by unit id, at most 120; `net/presence.js` keeps only known kinds), and the other page shows them as badges on that seat's labels.
- **F10a's leftovers.** The pinned formation's handles: its flag drags it (a press that stays put is still the click that sends), a cyan knob turns it (its slots turned round the point, handed to the planner and to `runGroup`'s new `slots`), a gold knob stretches it into a line through the point (on touch the only way to make one); the knobs stay on the table. Its members' paths are drawn faintly once it is pinned (at most 24). Ghosts planned a few per frame wait for F8b's boards.
- **F10b's leftover.** merge-sim's `burst` scenario, one per log: each seat's peer writes up to 25 of its commands one after another on its own view, with junk of its own between them now and then (15%), as the orders at End send them online: every peer agrees, as in every other scenario.
- **The checks.** P-macro (`sim/macro-check.mjs`): 240 standing-order runs on states the corpus passes through (random orders for a random few of the seat's units, March groups with their formation's slots; End, Go or Auto), 398 commands, every one taken, 221 units acted, each one `actorsOf` foresaw, none for a unit without an order, and under Go no unordered unit touched; **the play-report's F10c row**, a march to a slot one to three moves away by its goal field, the other seat playing Auto: 39 of 40 arrive within three of the seat's turns (98%; 95% on another seed; 13 cut short, caught in combat or by the battle's end, are left out), against §4.2.9's 80%; Autopilot first and Auto-End over four hotseat battles (seat 0 wholly on autopilot, the countdown 0 ms): 56 autopilot pilots, each sent from inside `settled`, at most one a phase, and 56 phases ended by Auto-End. Its self-test gains `pilot-everyone`, `march-stale-roll`, `march-wrong-field` and (the review's) `auto-plays-ordered`, each caught (9 of 9). `sim/input-check.mjs`, in the other seat's movement phase: the pin's knobs turned a quarter turn and stretched into a line, nothing sent, Esc; then H and X by key, End reading "· ⟳ N" and Go "▶ Go (N)" for the N the plan counts, Go sending the march's move and one pilot with the phase still open, End lit once every unit left is on autopilot, Auto-End's countdown pressing End (the pilot, then the end), and O drawing the order lines. The lobby rig's `group` case puts a seat's units still to move on autopilot online and presses End: the pilot and the end sent and folded alike, the other page seeing the orders as `ords` (its self-test's `no-ords`, caught). hud-check's rows (End's badge, `end.ready`, Go) are input-check's here.
- **The review** (one reviewer, eleven findings, each fixed):
  - **(high) Auto-End could end a phase the player still had units for.** A press on a button didn't stop the countdown, and it fired without asking again. Now any press on the page stops it (a capture listener). An order given, or the ⏭ setting toggled, starts it over (`recount`). As it fires it asks everything again (`endable`: the same decision, the table caught up, the setting on, no orders or group order under way, no unit left in the player's hands, no dialog open). If any answer is no, it presses nothing and may count again.
  - **An armed March or Attack click outlived its decision**, and with one unit picked nothing showed it was armed. The armed click carries its decision (`sigOf`) and lapses with it: at End, at Auto, in `settled`, or at the click. It also lapses when its units are gone; an armed march whose unit had fallen used to throw at every click. One unit's prompt is a toast too.
  - **🤖 Auto with orders sent a plain `auto`**, so the AI played the ordered units too: a Hold walked in the movement phase, and a March in combat fell back. Now it pilots the units no order holds, then ends. P-macro checks the entries an Auto run writes: no plain `auto`, and in the movement phase no pilot naming a March or Hold. 84 such units were held over the 240 runs. The self-test's new edit `auto-plays-ordered` is caught (9 of 9).
  - **An Attack whose target another unit felled mid-run did nothing that phase.** `stepOf` now gives such a unit `pilot`, its Autopilot, at once.
  - **Units a Go's pilot left as they were** (no shot worth taking, a charge too long) kept Go (N) lit, and each press wrote another pilot. They now sit out the rest of that phase's runs (`declined`, by decision).
  - **The lows.** A cancelled pointer lets go of a knob drag too. The unit card's order row shows the order just given. The bar shows the group's own notes again, and the orders' note only while a click is armed. `reset()` forgets the note and the cached plan. Peer badges are each seat's own units only, every seat not played here. Orders N, `ords` and End's path count only living units. The book keeps no unused `groups`, and prunes old battles.
- **Simplified, against §4.2.6.** The cyan ring is solid, not dashed or turning; "order given" is the click sound, not a race voice and a ring pulse; "order done" is a toast, not floating text over the unit or a minimap ping (the minimap is F8b's, March from it too); the bar's line reads the counts of each order rather than "4 units await orders".

**F8a as built** (missions choose the board; consensus: `CORE_VERSION` 4, the classic corpus byte-identical, `stateHash` as under 1-3, `RULES_ID` moved by the missions' new fields; only the classic mission ships):
- **The data** (`data/mission.js`): `classic` gains `board: { W: 40, H: 28 }`, `army: 'classic'` (the preset's name, F11a's) and `sets: ['classic']`, beside its deploy, rounds and objectives. **`checkMission`** runs on every mission as the module loads (the terrain sets' pattern), refusing an odd or fractional board, a zone within 6" of the centre line, an objective under 1" inside the board, in a zone or without its point mirror, fractional rounds, a set that doesn't exist (`SETS`, prototype-free), no army's name.
- **The setup** (`core/index.js`'s `fullSetup`, the checks in §4.2.3's order, on the setup's own fields before any is copied): a field outside `SETUP_KEYS` (`board, dice, terrain, rounds, overtime, diceMode, seats, mission`) refused (`a setup takes no field "x"`), a seat that isn't a record or holds a field outside `SEAT_KEYS` (`race, ctrl, dev, name, nonce`; F11a adds `army`) refused (`seat 1 takes no field "x"`); a null field is a field left out, as ever. Then `mission` (default `classic`, filled in, so the start names it: about 20 B) must be one of MISSIONS (`no mission "raid" (there is classic)`), `terrain` defaults to its first set and must be one of its sets (`the classic mission is fought on classic, not "fortified"`), `rounds` to its rounds. `core/match.js` exports both lists and `missionOf(setup)` (`MISSIONS[setup.mission ?? 'classic']`), which `core/index.js` passes on.
- **`G.board`** (`{ W, H, deploy }`, frozen, from the mission; derived like the nav grid, never in `stateHash`): `newState`'s Terrain and NavGrid, the deployment zone and the armies' rows (`core/deploy.js`), the blast's scatter clamp (`shoot.js`). `BOARD` stays in `CONSTANTS` as classic's numbers, and data-check holds the classic mission's board and depth to it, so every classic expression computes the same doubles (parity 46 of 46, P-present, P-auto, merge-sim and P-peers unchanged). The fight guard's `max(30, 2·units + 2)` waits for F8b's bump, as §4.2.3 says.
- **The bump.** `CORE_VERSION` 4: the setup is read differently and the whitelist refuses setups taken before (a start written before F8a names no mission: read as classic, but its `CORE_VERSION` 3 opens it read-only, open question 4). data-check pins 4's hashes to 1's.
- **The view** (`view/index.js`'s `setBoard`, from the snap's `rebuild`: `project(G)` gains `board: { W, H }`, the zones' depth and the objectives read from the match): only when the board differs from the one shown (its size, depth and objectives as a key), so a classic match makes nothing over and the title's frame and Math.random draws are unchanged. Then, in place: `Table.resize` (the mat the same mesh, the pointer's ray target, with a new shape and paint: its canvas 2048 px across whatever the width, so the blots and strokes are k times as many, the strokes capped at 30,000, and 1/√k the pixels, the mottling as dense per inch; the frame; the zones, their colours kept; tufts and flowers as many again as the area, capped at 2,800 and 560, strewn anew), `ObjectivesView.place` (the old markers off the table and freed, the kit's shared materials kept), `Overlay.resize` (a texel a nav cell), the figures' run-off edge, `CameraRig.setBoard` (on a board larger than classic's the dolly reaches the overview's fit and a tenth more, the far plane `max(400, 3 × the overview's max × k)`; each preset's `max` scaled by `reachOf`, the board's diagonal over classic's, never under 1) and `Stage.fit` (the fog `70k` to `140k`; the shadow camera classic's ±27 by ±22 by 90 times k, in the sun's own view, so a larger board's corners are inside it: classic's need about ±24.4 by ±20.5, an 80×56 board's ±48.7 by ±39.2). `present/camera-presets.js` gains `boardRect` and `reachOf`; `BOARD_RECT` stays classic's default.
- **The app.** `?mission=<name>` (the plan's F8b, built here as the door the checks start another board's battles by; a name no mission has gets classic and a line on the title card), the flow's `mission`, `start()`'s setup naming it with its first set and its rounds, `showTable` and `tableOf` taking it (a battle over a battle starts on its own mission's table, so its board is made once), the title always classic's, the scoring rings at the match's own objectives, `?debug`'s `board` (`__ts.board`, the human-bot's deploy depth: 8 on older pages), `view.board()` and `view.mission(name)`. **N2's lobby** gains `mission` (`lobbyDoc`, `lobbyOf`, `setupOf`, `editBattle`; `classic` in a lobby written before); a new mission lets the old one's terrain and rounds go (the start's setup takes its first set and its rounds), and a rematch copies the battle's mission and terrain.
- **The checks.** **P-mission** in P-prop's setups task (`sim/property.mjs`, on code that whitelists its setups): eleven refusals, each with its own message in fullSetup's order (a stray field, a seat's stray field, a seat that is null or a list, an unknown mission, `toString`, a mission that is a number, a set the mission isn't fought on, the stray field before the bad mission, a parsed entry's own `__proto__` field at the top and in a seat); null fields left out and the mission named or not plays classic on 40×28; every mission as shipped held again (its objectives mirrored, inside its board, outside its zones) and a match of it on its board, grid, objectives, rounds and first set. Its self-test gains `whitelist-off`, `whitelist-after-copy`, `mission-unchecked` and `set-unchecked`. data-check: classic's board equals `BOARD`; `RULES_ID` moves on the board, the sets and the army's name; checkMission passes classic and refuses fourteen broken missions. **P-board** (`sim/board-check.mjs`, Chromium, and `--self-test`): a build of a copy with a second mission (`grand`, 80×56, zones 14", nine objectives), one page: the title classic's table (40×28, five objectives, grid 80×56, dolly 75, far 400, fog 70-140, shadows ±27/±22) though `?mission=grand`; a grand battle makes it over (80×56, zones 14", the nine objectives where the mission puts them, grid 160×112, 2,800 tufts, the camera, fog and shadows farther), a second makes nothing over, a classic one makes the classic table again exactly, a second nothing; then five round trips with renderer.info's geometries, textures and programs and the scene's objects and labels the same on every grand battle and on every classic one. Its five edits (no rebuild, the overlay unsized, the objectives or the tufts left on the table, a rebuild at every snap) each caught. camera-check: each fitted preset sees a 60×40 and an 80×56 board whole, on five screens down to a 412×915 phone, within its max scaled by the reach; classic's reach 1; the rig's `setBoard` dolly and far plane, and back to 75 and 400. The Grand fixture patches `MISSIONS.classic`'s board, deploy and rounds instead of `BOARD` and `ROUNDS` (still those on code from before F8a, scale-bench's `--dir`); terrain-check and scale-check read the board from the mission; the human-bot's deploy depth is the match's; P-present's `playedAs` reads an absent mission as classic.
- **The review** (one reviewer: classic parity and the title's objects held by its own probes; one medium finding and five lows, each fixed). (Medium) `fullSetup` copied the setup and then read the copy's keys, so a parsed entry's own `__proto__` field set the copy's prototype: a start `{"__proto__": {"board": 5, "dice": 7, "army": "x"}, …}` passed the whitelist and every page then threw at it. The whitelist now reads the setup's own fields first (P-mission's two `__proto__` cases, `whitelist-after-copy`). (Low) A lobby's new mission kept the old one's terrain and rounds; the shadow camera's ±(W/2 + 7) was in the sun's view, not the board's, and left a larger board's corners out; a larger mat came out over-painted (the canvas doesn't grow); the Grand fixture no longer built from code before F8a; and the docs still called `?mission=` F8b's and the far plane a preset's farthest.
- **Not here.** The mat's tiled detail texture (one tile per 4") and shadows fitted to the view: a larger board's mat and shadows are coarser until F8b's drawing work (§4.2.7), which is when a board other than classic's ships. Battle size on F6's panel and in the lobby's view is F8b's.

**F11a as built** (army lists in the setup; consensus: `CORE_VERSION` 5, the classic corpus byte-identical, `stateHash` as under 1-4, `RULES_ID` moved by the prices, rosters, presets and list rules; only Skirmish offered):
- **The data** (`data/races/*.js`, `data/schema.js`, `data/mission.js`).
