Every unit has its v6 `cost` (Elder 60, Oak Guard 105, Nutkin 75, Grenadiers 65, Gliders 55, Trebuchet 50: the classic list 485; Hierophant 60, Brute 100, Scaleguard 70, Spitters 65, Sidewinders 65, Venom Engine 65: 495) and every race §4.2.8.4's `roster`. `defineRace` requires `cost`, a whole multiple of 5 above 0 (no default), and a roster naming each unit once and leaving none out (`roster lists "x" twice`, `roster leaves out "x"`), the classic `army` in its order (`army is not in roster order: "a" comes after "b"`); it derives `armies.classic` from `army` (a count per roster entry, trailing zeros dropped, a count over 9 refused: `'112111'` for both races) into a frozen registry with no prototype, and takes a def's own `armies` as count strings (a key of NAME's shape, no longer than the roster; `classic` by hand refused). The normalised type gains `t.cost`. The schema exports `LIST`, frozen (a regex's `lastIndex` is state), which core/army.js re-exports: defineRace can't import army.js without a cycle at load. `MISSIONS.classic.list` is §4.2.8.3's plus `size: 'Skirmish'` (below), and `checkMission` checks it before the objectives (`checkListRules`): no field but `size`, `points`, `units`, `models`, `perKind` and `roles`; a size that is a name when given; whole points above 0, units 1-24, models 1-90, perKind 1-9; a `[min, max]` of whole numbers with `0 ≤ min ≤ max ≤ units` for each role in `ROLES` and for no other key; minimums summing to at most `units`.
- **`core/army.js`** (new; pure, draws nothing; imports data/schema.js, data/mission.js and core/util.js): `LIST`, `armyOf`, `checkList`, `listCost`, `listText`, `keysOf` and `autoList`, as §4.2.8.4 gives them. `armyOf(setup, seat)` finds the mission (`classic` when none is named) and the race by a string only (`byName`: an object's own `toString` never runs), then refuses in §4.2.8.4's order: an army that is no string (`seat 1's army is a preset's name or a list of counts, not 7`, a value shown as its JSON cut at 47 UTF-16 units, one fewer rather than halve a surrogate pair, or as its type when it has none, `bigint`); a string of NAME's shape that is no own key of the race's `armies` (`the Coil of Ssithra have no army "grnad" (there is classic)`); one `LIST` refuses; one longer than the roster; then `checkList`, its why prefixed `seat N's army: `. `checkList` judges points, units, models, then each role in `ROLES` order (Troops, Elite, Fast, Hero, Monster, Artillery), minimum before maximum, then each roster entry against `perKind` (a unit's `short`: `6 Nutkin`), so `'2'`, two Elders, reports `no Troops unit` first; its wording `no X unit` or `N X units; a Skirmish army needs at least M`, `N X units; at most M in a Skirmish`, and for a maximum of 0 `1 Vehicle; none in a Skirmish`. `autoList` draws from its own `mulberry32(seed)` only, its arithmetic exact: the first Hero in roster order if it fits, Troops drawn evenly among those that fit up to the slot's minimum, then a weighted draw (Troops `troops`, 1.5, the rest 1) among the units whose one more keeps points, units, models, the role's maximum and `perKind`, until none fits; it always ends, each pick needing `unitsIn < rules.units`. The client helpers check what only a client could hand them (`keysOf` throws, and `checkList` returns, `a list's counts are whole numbers from 0, not X`).
- **The setup.** `SEAT_KEYS` gains `army`. `fullSetup`, after F8a's checks, seats the races and controllers (`makeSeats`, its refusals moved from `newState` with today's messages), copies each seat with `army: seat.army ?? mission.army`, so the setup as written (the start's) is untouched and G.setup's seats name `'classic'` where the setup named none, then runs `armyOf` for seat 0, then seat 1. `newState` builds the units from `armyOf(G.setup, side).keys`, seat 0's then seat 1's, each in roster order (rule 6), ids from 1. Nothing new in the state, the trace or the log, and `stateHash` leaves the setup out: on board 64, dice 89 with both seats AI, no army, `'classic'` and `'112111'` each hash chz79qx8m5 (its corpus pin), with 14 units and 252 trace lines.
- **The bump.** `CORE_VERSION` 5 (the setup takes a field it refused, and the units come from the list); data-check pins 5's `stateHash`es to 1's (`PINNED[5] = V1`). `RULES_ID` hashes `cost`, `roster`, `armies` and each mission's `list` but for its `size` (the race strip already kept every field but the presentation ones, and the missions went in whole; leaving `size` out, the review's fix, is `rulesData`'s one change): 1fzfs3hifnn. Nothing pins it: the parity runner stamps the current one into a start. The start entry is as before: online-style at Skirmish its worst case (two 6-digit lists, both names at N2's 48-byte cap, the longest seeds, 99 rounds) is 598 B through `envelope.encode`, presets by name 598 and no army 564, inside §4.2.8.4's 640.

Each value is trimmed and lower-cased, as `?races=` is, then judged by `armyOf` on a trial setup of the page's mission and races, so the page refuses what the fold would, in the fold's words: a refused value plays its seat's preset (the setup names no army) and puts a line on the title card, `?armies= for seat 0: seat 0's army: 2 Hero units; at most 1 in a Skirmish, so it plays the classic preset.` (the plan's own example, `2211`, fields two Elders); a list of values not two long gets `?armies= takes two armies, comma-separated …`, and both seats play the preset. The flow keeps `armies` (null, or `[seat 0's | null, seat 1's | null]`), and `start()`'s setup names a seat's `army` only where the URL named one, so every harness URL and corpus setup is the setup it was. The panel changing a seat's race away from the table's drops that seat's list for good (a list's digits are other units in another race; F11b's army line resets the same way). `tableOf` carries each seat's army as fullSetup fills it in (no army and `'classic'` share a table) and `showTable` takes `armies`, so a battle with lists is drawn afresh on a table that fields them; the title's backdrop names none, so its 1200 ms frame is unchanged (title-shot: 0 pixels different).

The group bar's own count is as it was.
- **The human-bot** (`sim/oracle/human-bot.mjs`): `pageStart` adds `&armies=a,b` only when a seat names an army, a seat naming none given by its mission's preset's name (the values are positional); `playedAs` reads an absent army as the mission's preset and compares a named one as written (`'112111'` is not `'classic'`).
- **Choices, and why.**
  - **The size's name lives in the mission's `list`** (`size: 'Skirmish'`; optional in `checkMission`, a non-empty string when given; a list without one words its refusals as a "battle" army's), so every caller handing on `mission.list`, fullSetup, army-sim's spread copies and F11b's Muster screen, words a refusal alike. It is a name, so `RULES_ID` leaves it out, as it leaves out a race's `name` and a unit's `short`, which the refusals print too (§4.2.9's "not on a rename"). F8b gives field and grand `size: 'Field'` and `'Grand'`.
  - **Refusal #2's verb follows the count**: `(there is classic)` while a race has one preset, `(there are classic, field, grand)` from F8b, as the mission's refusal words it. P-mission and merge-sim take either.
  - **`'toString'` fails NAME** (its capital), so it is refusal #3, "neither a preset nor a list of counts", as `'__proto__'` is (its underscores); `'tostring'` and `'constructor'` reach #2, the registry having no prototype. The checks pin both, and use `'constructor'` for #2.
  - **The Grand fixture's cap lists cost more than Grand's 1,500** (1,575 the Bushtails', 1,670 the Coil's at v6 prices), so under `--caps` the fixture lifts its points to `CAPS_POINTS = 2000`, as §4.2.8.7 measured cap lists with unlimited points; the ×3 presets (1,455 and 1,485) keep 1,500. Right for the fixture, wrong for the real `grand` mission: F8b, retiring the fixture, builds its cap lists within the limit or gives scale-bench's cap rows a test mission with the limit lifted.
  - **The fit's budgets are clamped, not lifted.** §4.2.8.2 fits on budgets from 80-120% of the limit, but the fold refuses a list over the limit and army-sim patches nothing, so each side's budget is drawn from 400-600 and played at no more than 500: half the fit's lists come from 400-500 budgets and half are built at the limit, none over it (a point mass at 100%). Lists of 100-120% would need a copy with the limit lifted, as the Grand fixture is.
  - **The score gate plays lists built at the limit**, what a Random seat fields (autoList at the mission's own points). On the fit's smaller budgets the Bushtails score 53.6-53.7% against 52.2-52.4% at the limit, as §4.2.8.2's "balance depends on army size" has it.
  - **playedAs's `PRESET` table** (`{ classic: 'classic' }`, a mission it doesn't list naming a preset of its own name, as F8b's field and grand will): sim/chromium.mjs injects it into the page, so it may use only its arguments, never data/mission.js. A mission whose `army` differs from its name needs a row.
- **army-sim** (`sim/army-sim.mjs`, plain JS, no dependencies) plays AI-against-AI battles headless through createMatch, both seats `ai`, each seat's `army` `listText(autoList(race, { ...mission.list, points }, seed))`, the pair's races swapping seats every other battle, the first race's score (a win 1, a draw 0.5) read from `G.turn.result`. Every battle is seeded from ``mulberry32(cyrb53(`<seed>:<stream>:<i>`))`` (the seed 1111 by default; streams `score:<pair>:<set>`, `score-again:…` and `fit:<pair>`), so `--jobs N` (2 by default: child processes playing chunks of 20, read back in battle order) changes nothing: `--jobs 1` and `--jobs 3` print the same report. `--check`'s gates, for every race pair on every set the mission offers (one of each today): (c) each classic list within the limit; (d) the mission's preset legal for every race (`armyOf`, the fold's own refusal); (a) the score gate, N 1,500, holding when |score − 50| ≤ 4, a failure played again once on its own fresh stream and that run counting; (b) the per-unit gate, a 2,400-battle fit, each unit's fitted value within max(2 SE, 20%) of its cost, a unit whose count never varies over the fit's lists (the hero) exempt. `--fit` is the report: a quasi-binomial logistic model fitted by IRLS (an intercept, the seat ±1, both sides' unit counts, the second race's negated; the Pearson dispersion scaling the covariance), then §4.2.8.2's steps (the exchange rate from the classic lists; each value by the delta method through it; the heroes split about today's mean of their two prices by the intercept; prices to 5; a classic list over the limit losing 5 at a time off the unit priced furthest over its value). `--self-test` (the review's) runs `--check` at N 300 / 600 on three copies: the sound table holds every gate, a Nutkin at 30 fails the score gate and the per-unit gate on the Nutkin, a Brute at 125 (the Coil's classic list 520) fails (c) and (d); each mutation an exact anchor, failing loudly when gone; about 175 s. A bad command line, or a count that is no whole number above 0, exits 2.
- **Measured** (v6 on seed 1111; no retune, every `cost` as proposed). The score gate: the Bushtails 52.4% ± 1.2 (1,500 battles, 144 draws), 2.4 points from even. The fit: 53.6% ± 1.0, dispersion 0.897, IRLS in 4 steps, 14.0 logits per 1,000 points; fitted value ± SE (cost) Oak Guard 115 ± 6 (105), Nutkin 80 ± 5 (75), Grenadiers 64 ± 4 (65), Gliders 48 ± 4 (55), Trebuchet 52 ± 6 (50), Brute 97 ± 7 (100), Scaleguard 62 ± 4 (70), Spitters 63 ± 4 (65), Sidewinders 64 ± 5 (65), Venom Engine 71 ± 6 (65); the hero difference −15 ± 42 points to the Bushtails (exempt); every unit inside its band, SEs of 4-7 points (§4.2.8.2's 5-9). Seed 2222: 52.2% ± 1.2, the hero difference +36 ± 38, every unit inside. The Skirmish fits agree with §4.2.8.2's (Brute 97-108, Trebuchet 52-55, Venom Engine 70-71). The table `--fit` proposes moves about an SE between seeds (Elder 55 or 80, Hierophant 65 or 40, Oak Guard 115 or 100): a direction for a retune, not a table to ship. On 4 CPUs shared with other work, `--jobs 2`: 65-95 ms of CPU a battle, the whole `--check` (3,900 battles) 170 s. autoList on seeds 1-1,000 always legal, spending 445-500 points (the Bushtails) and 450-500 (the Coil). The review checked the fit analytically (the design matrix, the dispersion, the delta method's derivative) and on 200 synthetic replications, the model's SEs within 5% of the empirical spread.

(Medium) A mission list's `size` was hashed into `RULES_ID`, so renaming it moved the hash (2qtp535ufi → 19u7prjcs9s), against §4.2.9's "not on a rename": `rulesData` now leaves it out (data-check's size-rename control; version.js's ALLOW entry). (Low, fixed) `shown()` cut a refused value's JSON at 47 UTF-16 units, which could halve a surrogate pair (both reviewers); the client helpers took bad counts and names (`keysOf` threw a RangeError on a fraction, `checkList` concatenated strings, `armyOf` let a value's `toString` throw: now the whole-number refusal and `byName`; none reachable from the fold, fullSetup having judged them); army.js's header now says "imports only" means its own, which is what PURE holds; army-sim had no `--self-test`, an unknown option exited 1 and `--n abc` quietly ran the default (now its self-test and exit 2); data-check's `army/` row would have passed a seat naming no list while saying "N lists checked"; flag-lint's one-reader rule missed a spaced dot and a destructuring across lines (a formatter's shape); armiesPick's comment said each value was judged as the fold judges it, though it lower-cases first (kept, as `?races=` does, the comment saying so; the bundle byte-identical). (Answered) `CAPS_POINTS` 2000 and the fit's clamped budgets: "Choices, and why", above.
- **Not here.** F11b's army line on F6's panel (**Army: Classic ▾ · Build…**, Preset / Random for an AI seat), the Muster screen, saved lists, the hotseat's pass screen and the lobby's lists (`army` in N2's seat records, `verifyStart` over it, courtesy sealing); the deployment's points banner and the result screen's totals; the cost on F6's race picker (`ui/screens/races.js`'s card shows the role alone) and points in the group bar's own count; `?armies=` as a standing check of its own (the door's cases ran from a scratch script: a list fielded unit for unit, `2211` refused with its note, `zzz`, one value, none, a mirror, a race change dropping one seat's list). Open: if pairs.json ever holds fewer than 24 pairs, scale-bench and scale-check could take `army/` logs, which have no `job.seed`.

**F7a as built** (climbable fortifications: decks, stairs, ladders and platforms, the works; consensus: `CORE_VERSION` 6 (5 is F11a's, landing beside it), the classic corpus byte-identical, `stateHash` as under 1-4, `RULES_ID` moved by the new set, the `climb` flag and the mission's sets; classic and every board before it build no floor):
- **The pieces and recipes** (`core/terrain/recipes.js`). `deck`, `stair`, `ladder` and `post` carry the piece table's fields (`surface`, `link`, `on`, `supports`; `hp: Infinity` all, F7c's posts excepted); stairs rise `STAIR_SLOPE` 0.5"/" and are 4.5" wide; a ladder's link runs from a foot `LADDER_OUT` 2.25" out from its face to a top on its deck's centreline, its cost `2·h` the nav's. `rampart`, `bastion`, `watchtower`, `platform` and `keep` as the recipe table, each centred on its bounding box with its front at local −z, each making its draws in a fixed order and recording them in `look`. The point mirror of a fortification is built from the first copy's frame with every place negated and every yaw plus π (`fortFrame`), so the halves' floors, links and gates are each other's negation bit for bit; a feature's copy is turned by π as ever (classic's). `gatesOf(name, frame, seed)` dry-builds a recipe into a scratch terrain: no board draw. Parapets are F7b's: a comment block, and each recipe says where its own go. The watchtower's two ladders share one top, the deck's centre (on a 4.5" deck only the middle reliably hosts r 1.22), so a cell may be joined to two feet: `nav.link` names the first, `linkMore` the rest.
- **Footprints, decided.** The recipe table's 7.1, 6.3 and 4.3 are each reach plus 0.25" to the nearest tenth (the rampart reaches 6.884", the bastion 6.058", the platform 4.056"), not rounded up as the table's rule says; F7a keeps the table's radii (raising them to 7.2, 6.4 and 4.4 would move the placement rates the prototype measured) and data-check holds `FOOTPRINT ≥ round₀.₁(reach + 0.25)` and every gate inside, on seeds 1-500 (`reachOf`). That measurement cost 120-200 ms at every import, so it is data-check's row; checkSet at load refuses only a `fortKinds` radius under its recipe's `FOOTPRINT`.
- **The `fortified` set** (`core/terrain/sets.js`) exactly as §4.2.4 lists it, and scatter's three branches, each reached only for a set with its field: the centre `keep` (its yaw, then its seed; it records r 8.6), the works (up to 8 tries, z then the seed; both copies' 2.2" aprons must fit, and are pushed into the placed list, so nothing later stands in them), the fort phase before the ordinary pass (its tests and the facing yaws as listed) and `scale: 'area'` (s = W·H/1120; classic's lines untouched). checkSet allows the eight optional fields and refuses every malformed one. `MISSIONS.classic.sets` is `['classic', 'fortified']`: classic stays every mission's default.
- **Measured** (terrain-check, seeds 1-500): the works on 486 of 500 Skirmish boards (97%; the prototype 193 of 200) and 500 of 500 Grand; the keep on 251 of each; fort pairs besides the works 0 / 0.17 / 1 on Skirmish (only platforms, 66, and watchtowers, 18: a rampart or bastion never fits between the zones there; the prototype 0.3) and 2 / 4.06 / 6 at Grand (6 on 9 boards, the prototype's max 5 on 200); chunks 9 / 27 / 70 and 85 / 142 / 210 (F7b's parapets not yet among them). So terrain-check judges Grand's pairs at least 2, at most the 7 the rule can ask for, on average 3.5-4.5, rather than the prototype's 5.
- **The height layer** (`core/nav.js`): `STEP` 0.4, `STAIR_SLOPE` 0.5, `LADDER_MUL` 2, `CLIMB_R` 1.22. `hasHeight` is set only when an alive chunk has a surface or a link, and only then are the height arrays allocated: classic runs the code it always ran. `rebuildHeight` follows §4.2.4's order: the floor raster (each ramp lerped along its axis, quantised to 1/64"; a 1e-6 slack takes both mirror copies the same way at a cell centre on an edge or a height on a half 64th, so the floor is exactly point-symmetric), the links (`link`, `linkCost`, `linkMore`; `linkCostOf(i, j)`), the ledges and `field(ledge, null, cliff)`, the levels (numbered by their first cell) and `gates` in chunk order, then the hard, soft, difficult and cover rasters, each only within STEP of its chunk's `base`. `standable` (cliff ≥ r − 0.06), `reachHeight` (|Δfloor| ≤ STEP onto a standable cell; a climber takes a link onto a standable end at its cost; a burrower keeps to the ground and takes no ladder until F5a's field), `pathHeight` (cut at each link, the foot and top kept as vertices, the top marked `climb` with the link's `cost`) and `walkableHeight` (the cliff, Δfloor, an enemy's disc only at its own level) are the height branches. Cost at Grand (scale-bench, the fixture's 8 fortified boards): nav.rebuild with height 2.1 ms on average (max 2.7) against §4.2.4's 3 ms, the layer itself 0.9 ms; reach (r 1.06, 8") 0.256 ms a plan with height against 0.295 ms on the same table flat, 13% less (the estimate was +10% more). (The review: that flat table is the board without its works, more open ground to search, so it is no measure of the height branch; scale-bench now times the same table with its decks, stairs and posts as hard blocks too, and against it reach with height costs 5-16% more, in two runs at load 6-9: 0.19-0.21 ms against 0.18.)
- **Height in the rules**, each behind `G.nav.hasHeight` as its own path: `HIGH` 1.2, `floorAt`, `groundY`; `sight` from the floor where the shooter would stand and each model's chest on its own floor (one internal `look` shared with the new door `sightInfo`, whose `{ok, block, obscure, cover, high}` F7b's ray reads; `Terrain.los` gained a `why` to report the chunks met); `engagedWith`, `controlOf` (the keep's objective is held from its top) and `levelDist`; `forbidMask`'s level test and its discs' floors; `climbs(u)`, the only reader of `t.climb`, handed to reach by `movePlan` and `chargePlan`; charge spots within HIGH of the target's floor; `blastLands` at `land.y` with hypot3 for its victims and `Terrain.blast(…, { y: land.y + 0.5 })` (classic passes nothing: 0.5); `smashAround` skips chunks off the sample's level; no pile-in onto a cell that isn't standable. `data/schema.js` derives `climb = !big && !fly` (overridable; F9a's `!vehicle` has its comment). With height a move's log line counts a climb at its cost (`walkCost`), not its span; classic's line is unchanged.
- **The AI** (rule 10): `levelDist` replaces the straight line in the objective and approach terms, and shooters and artillery take `+0.25·min(4, floor)`. No tuning was needed: play-report passes on both rows (below). (The review: it passed only with the units deployed onto the works counted; judged by a move, the AI was tuned, under "The review" below.)
- **Events and mirror.** With height `unit.move` carries `path: [{x, y, z, climb?}]` and `to: {x, y, z}`, `unit.place` carries `y`, and so does `unit.formation`'s `pos` (a pile-in can move a unit along a stair: the spec didn't list it); each event keeps one emit, so present-hooks' mutants still bite. Mirror units gain `y` (0 without height), and P-present holds it to `project(G)` over `fort/`.
- **The view** (`view/terrain.js`, `units.js`, `overlay.js`, `objectives.js`, `effects/`; `input/picking.js`; `ui/card.js`). Decks, stairs, ladders and posts built from `look` with no Math.random, each piece's parts merged into a geometry per colour (a few draw calls a piece; made at the first fortification, so a classic table makes nothing new): earth and stone decks a banded body, a rim and a planked or flagged top; the timber platform a slab on its four braced posts; stairs solid steps with pale chevrons up them; ladders two rails leaning out with rungs. Each walkable top carries an invisible quad: `surfaces()`, `tops()`, `ladders()`, `floorAt()`. `defOf` carries the height fields from its own copy of the list (`HEIGHT_FIELDS`: the view can't import terrain.js), and terrain-check holds the copy to core's. Figures, rings, hit cylinders and labels stand at the mirror's `y`; a walk follows the path's heights, and a segment marked `climb` plays as a ladder, the figures in file 0.9" apart; a raised unit (over STEP) gets a drop line and "▲2"" on its label, its card "▲ high ground, 2" up". The reach overlay tints every deck and ramp top (the overlay's texture sampled by world x, z: one draw call per top while it shows) and glows at a climbed ladder's foot ("⤒ 4"", "⤓" going down); the path, ghost and range ring sit at the floor. The objectives' markers stand on their tops (`raise`). The picker casts at unit cylinders, then the tops, then the board. Shots fly from and to the figures' heights, and a template is marked, lands, explodes and scorches on the top it falls on (`Shots`' `floorAt`).
- **The app.** The battle-setup panel's terrain line (a button per set the mission offers), `?terrain=` at boot (the panel's default; a set the mission isn't fought on gets its first and a line on the title card), `flow.terrainOf()`, `start(mode, races, terrain)`, `?debug`'s `view.terrain(set)` and `group.pick`'s `y`, and the lobby's terrain select (the host's; `editBattle` takes `terrain`). **The title stays on the classic table** (§4.2.3): `showTable` takes the mission's first set whatever the panel chose, and `start` draws the battle's own table, so title-shot is unchanged and Back from a fortified battle shows the classic title. `pageStart` adds `&terrain=` only for a set that isn't its mission's first, so every classic URL is the one it was.
- **The checks.** **P-climb** (terrain-check section 7) on 1,000 fortified boards: 6,706 decks (2,714 a stair rises to, 3,992 only ladders reach), each reached by a climber (r 1.22) from seat 0's zone, every stair deck by the big walkers (r 1.05, 0.95) and no ladder-only deck by them; 7,612 ladders climbed over their links and 3,216 stairs walked up from their gates; every top hosts r 1.22 and the fliers' r 0.886; 11.2 million cells' floors and links exactly point-symmetric (cell i against N−1−i), the cliff within 1e-4; the works on 486 Skirmish boards and 500 Grand of 500. Section 6, the fortified set on Skirmish and Grand, seeds 1-500: every board built twice with Math.random made to throw; every add's def carrying the chunk's height fields and equal to the view's `defOf`; every deck, stair, ladder and post exactly point-symmetric (13,684 mirrored pairs, and 502 decks their own mirror; 56,416 other chunks), every other chunk within 1e-9; every corner, foot and gate inside its footprint; the works' front faces on the zone edges, the ladders' feet 2.25" out; facing pieces toward the other zone (±0.3), the keep's stairs toward the zones (±0.2); the rates on 100 boards or more; the view's rows (a synced table the adds' table, one quad per top, every mesh taken back). terrain-hooks gains five edits for them, each caught: `fort-mirror-turned`, `fort-look-random`, `fort-def-link`, `works-off-edge`, `facing-ignored`. **P-height and P-level** in P-prop: two random games in five fortified, the ledge, engagement and sight rules after every command, no ladder for a non-climber and `y` exactly where the board has height in every event batch; the `height` task (classic flat, standable never on a ledge's band, reach's every step, ladders climbed by exactly the climbers, pairs across a ledge neither engaged, forbidden nor charged, `levelDist` a reference Dijkstra on 24,000 pairs over 12 boards); five more self-test edits (42 of 42). data-check: checkSet passes `fortified` and refuses 20 broken copies, classic has none of the new fields, each footprint holds its reach, every climber's r ≤ `CLIMB_R` (the others big or flying), `stateHash` pins 5 and 6 to 1's. scale-bench's fortified rows (Skirmish and the Grand fixture's `--fortified`, presets and cap lists) and the height layer's row. **play-report** (`sim/play-report.mjs`, new) over the `fort/` AI pairs, its counts read off the match as it is folded (`sim/height-probe.mjs`, through foldJob's new `probe`: never the trace, which has no floors): a unit on a deck by the end of round 3 in 6 of 6 battles, the keep's objective held from its top in 2 of the 3 it stands in; 29 units deployed onto decks, 20 ladders taken (every one down), 7 moves onto a deck (by stairs) in 3 battles, a fight on a deck in 1. No tuning: the AI reaches decks by their stairs and takes the works' ladders down into no-man's land, not up. Before the corpus, a seeded sweep of 24 fortified AI battles: a unit on a deck by the end of round 3 in 24 of 24, the keep's objective held from its top in 5 of the 7 keep battles; 108 units deployed onto decks, 85 ladders taken (4 of them up: units deployed on the works go down their ladders into no-man's land), 22 moves onto a deck in 13 battles, deck fights in 4.
- **The `fort/` logs** (F7a's second commit; `sim/baselines/fort/`), recorded on F7a's code and admitted as the corpus's are (twice more in Node from the entries alone, then the same trace and battle log in Chromium on a build of the PIN code, started from the title with `?terrain=fortified`): the AI pairs `watch-fort-1`, `-2` and `-3` (the keep standing: held at 5, 1 and 0 round ends) and `watch-fort-7`, `-8` and `-9` (no keep), each with the works (`corpus-add.mjs --mode watch --terrain fortified --set fort --need works,keep`, then `works,nokeep`, three each); and two hotseat human-bot logs, `hotseat-aggressive-climb-8` (a ladder climbed up, from its foot to its deck: `--need climbup`, the only one of 24 aggressive games that did; three ladders taken in all) and `hotseat-aggressive-deckfight-1` (ten blows struck with a unit on a deck: `--need deckfight`). A first pick of the climbing log, `climb-1`, was the same battle as `deckfight-1` (the same seeds under another tag) and climbed only down: it was dropped before the commit, and `climbup` added. `sim/corpus-add.mjs` gains `--terrain`, `--set fort`, `--mode watch` (an AI pair as a log with no entries) and the needs `deck`, `climb`, `climbup`, `deckfight`, `works`, `keep` and `nokeep`, each read off the match by `sim/height-probe.mjs` as the candidate is folded again on the PIN code; `sim/lib.mjs`'s `LOG_SETS` gains `fort`, a log whose seats are both AI coming back as kind `ai` (parity's `--record` saves such a pair as its log). The corpus is 54 battles; the PIN moved to F7a's code commit.
- **Run** (every standing check of ROADMAP's rules, Node and Chromium, each exiting 0, on a machine shared with two other teams at load 6-36 on 4 CPUs): before the code commit, all of them on the 46-battle corpus; after the corpus commit, again those that read the corpus (parity, `--page`, `--pin`, `--browser --only fort`, self-test, mutation and `--core`, perturb, data-check, mirror-check, P-present, replay-check, P-auto, playback-check and `--browser`, P-macro, rematch-check, P-prop, merge-sim, P-peers, snap-check and `--only fort`, hud-check, play-report). present-check's self-test ran its 53 edits in two parts (the runner's 7,000 s limit stopped the first after 43, all caught; the other 10 caught on their own), and its move edits again after the port below; rematch-memory's self-test lost its Chromium mid-run under load once (the page closed: no verdict) and passed when run again. scale-bench and fold-cost (both stores, and their self-tests) ran alone, at load 5-7: every Grand row within 1.5× of its budget, the fortified cap lists' movement p90 the closest (1.31×).
- **What turned up.** The fake DOM had no `measureText`, so the overlay's ladder tags threw the moment a human-bot unit on a fortified board was picked: it returns 0 wide now (the page in a browser was never affected). present-hooks' `no-rolloff-row` was anchored on `raceOf(G, 1).short`, gone from core/engine.js since F6, so present-check's self-test failed at HEAD; it is anchored on `seatName(G, 1, 'short')`, as F11a's commit has it. flag-lint's allowed line for the template's explosion follows its new height argument. With `fort/` in the corpus two checks needed a port: P-present's event order held a move's line to its walk's ground length `L`, while with height the line says what the walk cost (a climb at its link's cost: 4" for a 2" deck, against 4.5" of ground), so the rule now sums the path's climbs at `LADDER_MUL` times their height (the code's own constant and `hypot`), and classic's walks are held as before; and rematch-check's third battle, on the same page, keeps the page's `?terrain=` as it keeps its dice and races, so the setup it is held to names that terrain too.
- **The review** (two reviewers; 13 findings, each reproduced by its probe or read in the code, and all 13 fixed, one by its second remedy). Medium: a ladder costs `2·h` over more ground than that (0.5" more for a rampart's or a platform's, 0.75" for a bastion's), so a climber's plan reached cells outside S0's `scanBox` on Grand-sized boards (80 of 12,096 plans from ladders' ends on 40 of them, none on Skirmish): the ladder's cost is the rules' (§4.2.4: "twice the height in inches") and stays, and the box grows by `nav.linkSave × floor(max / nav.linkMin)` (the most a link carries beyond its cost, cell centre to cell centre, 0.5-1.1"), so it holds every finite cell again; the same shortcut made `levelDist` miss a deck crossed between two points below it, so neither it nor P-level's reference was exact on Grand (228 of 80,000 pairs on 20 Grand-sized boards): it now takes the gate graph's own shortest ways between gate ends (`gateGraph`: Floyd's over the gates' ends, once per nav rebuild, kept on the nav as `gateMemo`; on a board with no shortcut the closed forms to the bit), and P-level runs on 12 Grand-sized boards as well (48,000 pairs in all); P-scan's reference had none of F7a's height terms (20 of 178 fortified states mismatched): ported, and P-scan runs the `fort/` AI pairs, the Grand fixture's `--fortified` and the box itself (its two new edits, `height-term` and `box-no-climb`, caught). Several height rules had no property check: P-height's `height` task gains its scenes (the keep held from its top, a deck unit not holding a ground objective beside it, a template on a deck sparing the ground below, a smash skipping a raised piece, a pile-in onto a ledge's band refused, a charge's spot kept beside an enemy below), each with a self-test edit (`control-ignores-height`, `blast-flat`, `smash-any-level`, `pile-in-anywhere`, `charge-others-flat`, with `leveldist-no-stair` and `leveldist-no-shortcut`). The keep's foot can't hold its objective by geometry alone (a ground model stands 0.6" or more past `OBJECTIVE_RANGE` and its base), which is why a `controlOf` without its height test passed play-report; the scene that parts them stands on Grand-sized boards, where the works' fronts are 2" from (±24, 0). High: play-report's round-3 row passed on the units deployed onto the works whatever the nav allowed (a nav that never steps up passed it 6 of 6): `sim/height-probe.mjs` now counts a unit on a deck only where it got there by a move of its own (seen at the trace lines, as an AI battle's events arrive only after its last), and the keep's row only a round held with a model of the holder on the keep's top. Judged so, F7a's AI met the row in 2 of the 6 `fort/` battles (and 26-32 of 48 in three seeded sweeps: about 85% where the keep stands, 30% where it doesn't); so the AI was tuned (rule 10, within F7a's bump): the charge term and the brawlers' danger term measure a walker's way by `levelDist`, as the objective and approach terms do. The exact graph and the two terms first cost a fortified Grand movement phase's p90 2.2× its budget; `levelSlack` (the most any shortcut takes off the straight line) lets `score` skip, exactly, the enemies and objectives a straight line already puts out of a term's reach, and the pairs that are no shortcut of their own are pruned from `short` (P-scan's reference measures every one): scale-bench passes, the fortified rows' p90 1.17-1.19× (1.31× before the review). Lower: a point partway up a stair took its deck's level, so `levelDist` sent it round by the stair's top (8.5" for a walk of 2.69"): a cell whose floor a stair's ramp gave (`nav.rampOf`) also walks straight down to the stair's foot; fliers were measured over the walkers' gate graph (the straight line now, their move a circle); a charge's spot was barred by another enemy within 1" horizontally whatever its height, unlike engagement and forbid (now only within `HIGH` of its floor: met on a stair, by a big squad below); the group planner's goal fields never climbed (`goalField` takes `climb`, `q.climbs`, in its key); a walk between two vertices lerped the figures' height, sinking or floating them by up to 0.95" where a segment ran off a deck down its stair (the table's own `floorAt` under a walker now, a flier as before); scale-bench's height row compared reach with the table without its works (more open ground) and the notes read it as the height branch's cost (now against the same table with its pieces as hard blocks too: 5-16% more, above); rematch-memory had no fortified run (`--terrain fortified`, in the standing list) and the migration row's by-hand items went unrecorded and named a bastion Skirmish never fits (reworded to a rampart's stair; the three by-hand rows were not played by hand: this team has no hand, and the climbing human log and P-height's scenes stand in for them). The fixes move how the `fort/` AI pairs play (the stair walk-down above all, then the tuning); the six were re-recorded on the fixes' code (the two human logs unchanged), the PIN moved to it, and classic is untouched (46 of 46, boards 1-500). After it: `fort/`'s AI pairs put a unit onto a deck by a move by round 3 in 4 of 6, take 2 ladders up (none before), and hold the keep from its top in 3 of 3.
- **Not here** (F7b and F7c). Parapets and level-aware cover; the LOS ray with `sightInfo`'s reasons, the move tooltip's climbing cost (`linkCostOf` is ready), cliff rims, see-through occluders and Alt; `blast.land` carries no `y` (the view reads the floor from its own tops); the timber platform is drawn as an open slab on posts while its deck's line-of-sight body is solid from the ground (the piece table's `y = h/2, hy = h/2`), so the view shows a gap no shot passes: F7c, which makes the posts breakable, should give a timber deck a thin body (or the view enclose the space). F7c's posts at `hp: 3`, the cascade, `settle` and `unit.fall`. The ground-vehicle rules of P-height and `standable` are comments until F9a gives a unit `vehicle`; burrow's deck rule waits for F5a's field. army-sim's Skirmish gates on `fortified` (the F7a migration row's) wait for F11a's `sim/army-sim.mjs`, which lands beside this; its "every set the mission offers" will take `fortified` as it merges.
**F8b as built** (Field and Grand battles; consensus: `CORE_VERSION` 7, after F7a's 6, landing beside it; the classic corpus byte-identical, `stateHash` as under 1-6, `RULES_ID` moved by the new missions, the `open` set and the prices; this block stands on its own, whatever F11a's and F7a's notes beside it say):
- **The missions** (`data/mission.js`). `field`: 60×40, zones 12", 6 rounds, seven objectives (the centre, classic's two pairs pushed out to ±11 by ±10, a pair at (0, ±14)), 1,000 points, at most 18 units and 70 models, 5 of one unit, Heroes 1-2, Troops 2-10, Elite and Fast 0-3, Monster and Artillery 0-2. `grand`: 80×56, zones 14", 7 rounds, nine objectives (the centre, (±14, ±14) both ways, (±24, 0), (0, ±20)), 1,500 points, 24 units, 90 models, 7 of one, Heroes 1-3, Troops 3-14, Elite and Fast 0-4, Monster and Artillery 0-3: §4.2.3's and §4.2.8.3's numbers, unchanged. Each is fought on `open` alone (F7a's merge makes it `['open', 'fortified']`, and the refusal then reads "fought on open or fortified"). Every race's `armies` gains `field: '224222'` and `grand: '336333'`, the classic list twice and three times over. fullSetup's refusals name the three missions through F11a's plural ("no mission "raid" (there are classic, field, grand)", "the grand mission is fought on open, not "classic""); only its comment changed.
- **The `open` set** (`core/terrain/sets.js`): classic's feature table and spacing rules but `objectiveGap` 2.6 and `gap` 3.2 (the starting value, which passed: no tuning was needed), and `scale: 'area'`, a field no other set has: scatter's branch of its own (F7a's code verbatim, `areaScale`) scales the pair counts and attempts by the table's area over classic's (×2.14 at Field, ×4 at Grand: 13-18 and 24-35 pairs), so classic's line and its draws are untouched; `checkSet` takes `scale` as its one optional field, `area` its one value. **One deviation from §4.2.3: its centre is `[['rockbox', 0.8]]`, not classic's tower-and-rockbox rule.** The ruined tower ring's doors are about 1.25" wide, so no squad (r 0.89-1.18) walks in, and the nearest an r 1.18 one stands is 4.6-4.8" from the centre objective, past the 4.18" control needs: with the tower the connectivity rows failed on about 55% of boards and no `gap` fixed it; with the rock box they pass on every board at the starting gap. (Classic has the same property: a squad controls every objective on 217 of 500 classic boards, reported, never judged: its draws are frozen.)
- **Connectivity** (terrain-check, every set a Field or Grand mission offers, seeds 1-500, boards built as newState builds them): from the standable cell nearest each zone's middle, the nav's own reach for a round hull disc (r 1.5, ground only) and an r 1.18 squad must cross to the other zone, and the squad must reach a standable cell within `OBJECTIVE_RANGE + r` (4.18") of every objective. On seeds 1-500 every row holds on all 1,000 Field and Grand boards (6,000 reaches in 24 s); classic, reported and never judged, has the hull crossing on 497 of 500 boards and the squad on all 500. Chunks per board (§4.2.3 expected 250-300 at Grand): classic 40-136 (mean 77), Field 84-192 (median 128, mean 130), Grand 178-376 (median 256, mean 259); data-check's capacity check, on seeds 1-200, finds the worst at 130 chunks on classic, 190 at Field and 362 at Grand (within 450). Its `--self-test` plants two controls in the grid, a wall across the centre line and a ring round one objective, and each fails a row.
- **The fight guard** (`core/actions/fight.js`): `max(30, 2·units + 2)`, so a Grand melee of 42-48 units plays out; it is 30 for every classic battle (14 units) and for every army/ battle (12-14). A Skirmish list may field 10 units a side, so a battle of 20 would have 42, never reached: AI play makes at most 7 alternations. The bump is the guard's, the new missions' and the set's: `CORE_VERSION` 7; data-check and P-prop pin 6's and 7's `stateHash` to 1's.

- **What the retune turned up.** The Grand fit is weakly identified: an exchange rate of 3.5 logits per 1,000 points, a race-level edge of 409 ± 882, standard errors of 20-83 points a unit, so the per-unit gate passes partly because its bands are wide (the Sidewinders fit 170 ± 45 against 80, at the band's edge). The odd-looking Grand prices (Hierophant 10, Venom Engine 15, Trebuchet 15) keep the Coil's ×3 preset under 1,500 while its big units are priced up. Bushtail autoLists at Grand spend 1,120-1,480: the unit and model caps bind, not the points, against §4.2.8.3's "points must be what binds". The Field score swings about 10 points between nearby tables (42.9 → 47.2 on a re-run; round 4 58%). Human play will tell; the prices are data, a retune moves `RULES_ID` with no bump.
- **Drawing at scale** (§4.2.7 items 1-4; every one keyed on a board larger than classic's, so classic's table, title and terrain shots are drawn exactly as before). **Terrain tiles** (`view/terrain.js`): one mesh per 8" tile and material class, each chunk's own meshes merged in world space with vertex colours; each chunk keeps its own mesh in the group, hidden, so `sync`, `clear`, spares and `state()` keep their contract; a hurt, destroy, collapse or a tree felled promotes the chunk out of its tile (the tile merged again at once) and `settle()` puts it back as it rests; rubble, fallen logs and shared items are never tiled; `tileCheck()` holds every tiled chunk's drawn vertices and colours to its own mesh, read independently. About 64 tiles and 108 terrain draw calls at Grand. **Shadows fitted to the view** (`view/stage.js`): once the camera has rested 8 frames, the shadow camera bounds the view's ground footprint clipped to the board, never per frame; classic keeps ±27/±22 (and `fit()` resets `near` too). **The mat's detail texture** (`view/table.js`): a tile per 4", a material of its own made the first time a larger board shows and kept, painted from a fixed hash, never Math.random; the box under a larger mat sits 0.05" lower (it z-fought the mat in stripes from a phone's overview, 150" away). **Figure LOD** (`view/models/cache.js` `lodOf`, `view/units.js`): one low-poly stand-in per (unit, seat colour, rim), vertex-clustered at 0.07", one shared material, past 60" (back under 57"), no idle animation; dying, fleeing and flinching figures keep full detail; off under `?fast`. **Semantic zoom** (`present/zoom.js`: `pxPerInch`, `tierOf` with 2% hysteresis, `clusters`, `glyphOf`; `ui/chips.js`): the Tactical labels and the Strategic hiding are CSS on `#labels[data-tier]` and each ring's `material.visible`, so the labels' HTML and the rings' state, which snapDiff and hud-check read, are untouched; chips are 22 px discs with a glyph, a count and the order badge, bordered in the ring's colour, stacking into ×N within 18 px ((F8b's review) 28 px on a coarse pointer, the size its chips are drawn there), a tap a click on the unit and a cluster's a zoom onto it (the rig's `frameOn`); a label is written only when it moved half a pixel. A Grand overview at 1280×800 is Tactical (11.3 px per inch); Strategic comes on a portrait phone's overview (4.2-4.5).
- **The minimap and the roster.** `view/minimap.js`: 160×112, bottom-left, rising above the card; folded to 🗺 on a portrait screen, and on classic until toggled (🗺 or M; (F8b's review) the 🗺 is the map's own, on its corner, not one of the tools, and on classic it shows only once M has brought the map up). Terrain footprints cached offscreen, the zones, the objectives in their holder's colour, the order lines, unit dots sized by r with the selection outlined, the camera's ground trapezoid, pings read off mirror diffs; polled at 10 Hz, redrawn only when its signature changes. A click or a drag pans; a right-click or a long press pins the group's move or place there, else gives a March; an armed March's click takes it (F10's March from the minimap, through boot.js's `ground`). `ui/roster.js`: your units with their acted, ordered and in-combat state, both armies' worth (Σ price × alive / models); a row picks the unit up and glides to it; ☰ or R, open by default on a larger board but on a phone ((F8b's review) the ☰ left the tools: the roster's header is its toggle).

The Grand frame: the camera 97" out, 11.3 px per inch (Tactical), 156 of 156 figures their stand-ins, 268 chunks in 62 tiles, the shadows fitted once.

On Field and Grand `behind` fits the seat's own half (its zone to the centre line). **Deviation: held to 45-46", not 45-60".** Measured in Chromium at 1280×800 the army's figures stood a median 14.3 px tall at 60" and 17.5 px at 48", under §4.2.3's 18-22 px; where the half can't fit that near (Grand's needs 61-77" on a laptop), the target slides toward the seat's own edge until the edge sits at the foot of the view, so the whole army shows (the opening at 46": figures 18.9 / 19.4 / 23.9 px, p10 / median / p90). **F14 as built** (the camera follows a human opponent, from the October playtest; view only: no bump, the corpus byte-identical, no event added or moved):
- **The gap.** Only the AI's own actions (core/ai/policy.js) and the fights (core/actions/fight.js) emit `focus`, and a batch takes two walks or two attacks at least (V1, F8b), so a human seat's lone move, shot, template or charge, an online opponent's every one, moved the camera not at all: online, in a watched online battle, in its replay.
- **The cue** (`present/camera-presets.js`, pure). `cueAt(events, k, posOf)` is the action that opens at event k: from its opening (a focus, the turn to face, its tray) or its first deed (a walk, a volley, a template aimed or thrown, a spell, a charge's verdict, a blow) through its `act`, or its `pending` (a charge that reached waits for its spot: the walk there is the next entry's action), or up to the next action's opening, or a phase, round, stage or end; none for a run with no deed in it (an advance's roll, a morale test, a placement). It returns where the action ends, its actors (`pointsOf`: the units its events name, where the table shows them before it plays, the places they go to, a template's aim and landing; the player's `frame` gathers a batch's members with it now, the aim and landing new to it), where the camera glides if they are all on screen (the action's own focus, the AI's or a fight's; else its first walk's end; else its actors' middle, as the AI's own focus on a shot or a charge is) and `own`, whether it carries a focus.
- **The player** (`view/player.js`). Every action no batch takes is cued once as it opens, the handlers' `cue` (the view's: `view/index.js`) told `{ points, x, z, own }`, and its focus events are folded but not followed: one move of the camera per action, as per batch. With ⇉ off too, and for every seat, so an AI's lone action (a turn's last walker, a lone fight) is now framed when off screen where its focus glided 60% toward it: a watched battle and a replay get what a human opponent gets, by the same path. A player made without a `cue` handler plays as before.
- **The rig** (`view/camera.js`). `cue` makes the move: an action with its own focus by `frames` (the follow policy, as ever), a seat's command by `cues`; then `frameAll` (`frame`'s framing, `framePose` round `circleOf`, now shared by the two) if any actor is off screen, else `focus` toward (x, z) (60% of the way at the same distance; none within 6"). `followed` counts every move the follow policy makes (a batch or an action framed, a focus glided to), which `?debug`'s `view.camera()` reports.
- **Whose actions** (`cues`): as `frames`, but never an action of a seat played here, unless its orders after its End. So in hotseat neither player's own moves are chased (the follow policy follows every hotseat turn, which before F14 only the fights met); the fights there, with their own focus, are followed as ever.
- **Not followed: placements.** An online deployment is simultaneous, so following the opponent's placements would swing the camera while you place your own; and `follows` is the battle's only.
- **The bookmark kept** (a change to F8b's). Every phase begins with a `phase.start`, a fight or a morale phase with nothing in it too, so the bookmark of a turn's last End (its charges) was spent at the seat's own fight phase, and its next turn never came back from the opponent's, which F14 now follows. `resume(seat)` glides back only once something has taken the camera away since that End: the follow policy (the orders at End framed, an opponent's turn followed) or, in hotseat, another seat's phase begun here (the other player's own camera); till then it keeps the bookmark, and a camera the player moved by hand after End stays where it is (F8b glided back regardless). The orders-at-End window (`ending`) still closes at the seat's next phase, so a seat's own fights are not framed. (The wave's integration) A bookmark kept to a battle's end, nothing having taken the camera away since its End, outlived the battle: `marks` were cleared only by `toTitle`, so the next battle started from the same page (input-check's aim case after its main run, `__ts.start`) glided its first phase to the old battle's pose, its enemies off screen. `setViews`, which every battle's opening calls, now clears `marks` and `ending`: a battle's bookmarks are its own (camera-check's case).
- **The checks.** camera-check (608 checks, from 560): `pointsOf`; `cueAt` on the core's shapes (a human seat's move, shot, scattered template, charge and its walk, the AI's move with its focus, a fight up to the next or to its phase's end; none for an advance's roll, a morale test, a placement or a walker the table doesn't show); `cues` beside `frames` in every mode; and the rig's `cue`: an opponent's walk off screen framed exactly as `frame` frames those members, one on screen near the look left still, one far glided to as a focus is, nothing for the seat played here, a hotseat seat's own walk or with 🎥 off, a hotseat fight framed, a seat's orders after End framed but not glided to, and the bookmark kept through the seat's own fight and morale phases and coming back after the opponent's turn. present-check: in its parent process, the page's own player and rig play a corpus battle's first human move as the other seat's page plays it: one glide (toward the walk's end on the opening view; framed as a batch of its ends is with the camera zoomed off), one for a watching page, none on the mover's own page, in hotseat or with 🎥 off; and the AI's first turn one at a time, each action cued once, no focus followed on its own. lobby-rig's `follow`: once the host has pressed End, the guest's lone move swings the host's camera once and the guest's own not at all, and the host's next phase brings its camera back to its bookmark; its two mutants (the cue handler gone, the bookmark spent as F8b spent it) are caught.

**F12 as built** (local undo, open question 28; client code and a derived record in the Folder: no bump, the corpus byte-identical, nothing hashed or logged changed):
- **The record** (`match/fold.js`). Beside `accepted`, `placed` (each accepted entry's place in `pushed`) and `dice` (the match's `G.rng.n` after it, 0 before a start), pushed in `accept()`, where the entry is always the last pushed: a number each, O(1) an entry (fold-cost unchanged), carried over by a refold's show() with the rest of the Folder. Derived, never hashed, never in the log; `match/` reads the counter off `G.rng` and imports nothing of `core/rng.js` (§1.2).
- **The rule** (`present/hud-model.js`'s `undoable(session)`): the entry undo takes back is the last accepted, of a live match played here alone (`playedHere`: a `LocalStore`, every human seat in `localSeats` and played from this device), a `place`, `move` or `chargeEnd` (`UNDOABLE`) of the seat `decisionFor()` names, so in hotseat each seat its own, with `dice[k] === dice[k - 1]`. End, Begin battle and any entry that rolled commit: an advance, a shot, a charge's declaration, Auto, a pilot, the last Begin battle (the roll-off), an End that ran a fight, morale or the AI. No kind undo takes back rolls today (a walk's smash draws nothing), so the counter's test guards what may come (a deck settling under a wrecker's walk: §4.1 rule 17); replay-check holds it on a stand-in Session. One press takes back one entry; pressed again, the one before, down to the last commit point.
- **The mechanism** (`app/undo.js`'s `rewind`, the flow's `undo()`). Never by cutting the store (the Folder's tamper freezes the match). A Session over a new `LocalStore` of the log's texts up to the entry (`store.export()` cut at `placed[k]`), with the battle's device, `localSeats` and `rand`, folded quietly as it is made (the flow's `onTrace`, the card's facts and `?debug`'s trace, hears its lines only from then on: the snap makes both again); then `flow.battle = ses` and `flow.show(ses)`: `hand()` closes the old Session (no longer the battle), the snap draws the table, `relog` makes the battle log again (the line of the move taken back gone), and the HUD, the card and the selection are derived again from it (the unit picked up is put down first, `human.select(null)`). The Session numbers its entries from its log's length, and in a log one device writes an entry's number is its place, so the move made again is written as the same text as the one taken back. Deviation from the brief's "a LocalStore of the first k accepted entries": the log's own texts up to the entry, refused ones included (a fold refuses them again: a rejected entry changes no match, no head), so an id the new Session writes is never one its log holds, and its replay file keeps what was refused, as N3's files do. The order book is keyed by the start entry and the seeds (`bookKey`), with which the new log begins: the standing orders stand.
- **When.** `flow.undo()` refuses online (`flow.online`), while a replay or a scrub is up (`flow.session !== flow.battle`, or `replay.battle`), while the player plays, a group sends or the orders run, and when nothing is undoable (a match over included); it returns why, or null.
- **The page.** `#undo` (↶ Undo) first in `#actions`, before `#readyN`; the HUD model's `undo` slice `{ show, busy }`: up with End (the deployment, a seat's phase, never the charge's pick) where `playedHere`, disabled while the table plays or nothing is undoable; `ui/actions.js` puts it on the page, and `app/boot.js` wires its click and Ctrl-Z or ⌘-Z (not in a field, not under a dialog, not a repeat) to `flow.undo()`. One sentence of help under Controls. Online, watching, in a replay or a scrub it is hidden: there is no seat's decision on the table, or the game isn't played here alone.
- **The checks.** replay-check's `undo`: over each of the 28 human battles played alone, after every entry `undoable()` is the rule read off the match (the kind, the seat deciding, `G.rng.n` before and after) and the Folder's record is the match's; at four of the entries it would take back (spread over the battle; 1,308 such entries over the 28 battles, 112 taken back) `rewind` gives the match after the entry before, live, and the same command sent again folds to the trace, match and texts of the log with the move made once; and the rule where the corpus doesn't reach (a stand-in Session whose last move rolled; seat 1 placing while seat 0 deploys). Its self-test gains four mutants, each caught (`undo-past-dice`, `undo-any-seat`, `dice-unread`, `rewind-keeps`). `sim/undo-check.mjs` (new, Chromium; hotseat, seed 4242, dice 1, `?debug&lowfi&fast`): Undo up and disabled in the deployment, a placement taken back by the button and by Ctrl-Z; Undo up and disabled as the movement opens; a move taken back (the unit where it stood, not moved, put down, End Movement up, its line gone from the log); an advance leaves nothing to take back, and the advanced unit's move is taken back to it. Its `--self-test`: `undo-unwired` and `undo-keeps-battle` (the new Session shown, the old one still the battle) caught. lobby-rig's `play`: neither seated page shows Undo in its deployment (mutant `undo-online`).
- **Not built.** Redo; a group's move taken back as one press (it is its members' `move` entries, one a press: open question 18 stands for online play); undo online (an `undo` command in the rules would be a step of its own, §5).

**F15 as built** (the battle log scrubs, open question 33; client code only: no bump, the corpus byte-identical, the battle log's written stream unchanged):
- **The stamp** (`app/flow.js`). The sink stamps each entry's `log` events with `k = ses.accepted.length - 1`, the entry the Session has just accepted (the moves' own numbering: online the `open` is move 0), and `relog` stamps the same from its own fold of the list from its start; the `log` handler hands it on. `ui/log.js` writes it as `data-k` (and a title) on the line, never in its class or HTML, which P-browser's `written` stream records.
- **The click** (`ui/log.js`'s `wire`, `app/replay.js`'s `before(battle, k)`): `scrub(k - 1)`, the match before the entry, paused; ▶ plays the entry first, then on. A bar already over the battle (a watched online battle, a replay file, the end screen's replay) scrubs as its slider does; else `open(battle, { live: status !== 'over' })`, and over a battle not over the bar is a **peek** (`replay.peek`): Live, ✕ (shown beside it) and a replay reaching the battle's last move put the bar away and show the battle as it stands (`close({ back: true })` comes back to the battle, never the war room). The deployment's lines, logged by the start, show "Before the battle" (the table as it stood); the roll-off's, logged by the last Begin battle, the deployment just before it. Against the AI an AI turn's lines are the End that handed it over (a move is an entry), and every line of a watched battle played here is its start's.
- **While scrubbed** the table's Session is the replay's (`dev: 'replay'`, no `localSeats`): no seat's decision is on the table, so End, Auto, Undo and the tools are down, the keys find no seat, a command is refused (`seat -1 is not played on this device`), and Undo refuses (`session !== battle`). The battle's own Session goes on folding with no table (N3's `hand()`; a game played here alone gets nothing meanwhile). Live shows the battle again, its seat able to act.
- **The page.** `#logList .entry[data-k]`: a pointer, a hover tint. The help's sentence on Undo says it too.
- **The checks.** replay-check's `logs`: over all 70 battles, every line the page's sink hands on (the real flow's, with nothing drawn) names a move that logged it (the trace after the move before it short of the line's `at`, after its move reaching it; a traced line the trace's own line there), `relog` writes the last 80 alike, six clicks a battle spread over its lines show the match after move k − 1 (its hash and trace), or before the start for the deployment's; and a peek at move 4 of a battle going on comes back to the battle at Live and at ✕. Its self-test gains four mutants, each caught (`log-k-next`, `relog-unstamped`, `click-after`, `peek-stays`). undo-check: a click on a move's line shows the unit where it stood on the bar, End, Auto and Undo down, Ctrl-Z and a command refused; Live, ✕ and ▶ each come back to the battle; the deployment's line shows "Before the battle" (its `--self-test`: `log-unwired`, `peek-stays` caught).
- **Not built.** Scrubbing inside an entry (an AI's whole turn, a watched battle played here, is one move); a line's own place in the trace (the scrub is to the eve of its entry, open question 33's "before that move").
- **Checks run** (F12 and F15 together, on the final tree; the machine shared with other runs, its load average 20-37 on 4 cores): `node sim/parity.mjs` 70 of 70 byte-identical, nothing re-recorded; `boundaries`, `flag-lint` (each with `--self-test`) and `data-check`; `fold-cost` linear (as on the base commit, `--ref`; one run at load 30 read ×4.8 and passed again after) and its `--self-test` 3 of 3; replay-check over the 70 battles and its `--self-test` 17 of 17; undo-check and its `--self-test` 4 of 4; hud-check; present-check over the 70; play-check's `hotseat` and `bushtail` lanes; lobby-rig's `play` with the new check, and `--self-test --only undo-online`. Left as the WIP merge of F8b left them, none of them reading code these steps changed: `self-test.mjs`'s one wrong verdict (its `spin` mutant's text isn't in the PIN's `fight.js`) and `mutation.mjs` inconclusive (the PIN doesn't reproduce the `scale/` battles); lobby-rig's `size` (its `#lobbySize` never visible, on the base commit's build alike) and `catch-up` (a drawn page not loaded within 30 s, on both builds, under the load), its other 15 cases passing (`history` on a second run). `title-shot --ref` the base commit: exit 3 twice (its screenshot timed out, 120 s and 500 s: no verdict; the title's `#undo` is `display: none`).

**F17 as built** (lobbing from height; consensus: `CORE_VERSION` 8, the classic, army/ and scale/ corpora byte-identical, `stateHash` as under 1-7, `RULES_ID` unchanged: the formula has no constant, so it is code, not rules data):
- **The rule** (`core/actions/shoot.js`). `lobbed(w)`: a weapon with `blast` or `indirect` and no `spell` (the Trebuchet's Flaming pinecone, the Venom Engine's Acid globe, the Grenadiers' Blasting acorns; not the Elder's Thornburst, a blast spell erupting under its target, nor the Hierophant's gaze). `rangeOf(G, u, tg = null, from = u.pos)`: without height (`!G.nav.hasHeight`, every classic and open board) or for a weapon that doesn't lob, `w.range` itself, the classic expression (§4.1 rule 18); with height, h = `floorAt(from) − groundY(tg)` (with no `tg`, the ground: h is the shooter's own floor) and the reach `√(R² + 2hR)`, R exactly where h is 0, and 0 where `R² + 2hR ≤ 0` (firing up more than half the range: no deck is that tall). It is the farthest a projectile launched at the speed that carries it R on the flat lands from h higher, at its best angle (R = v²/g, the range from h being (v/g)·√(v² + 2gh)): scale-free, so the table's inches serve, and `Math.sqrt` is exact on every engine (boundaries.mjs allows it). Pure, and a door of `core/queries.js` (boundaries' list names `rangeOf` and `lobbed`).
- **Where it is read.** `shotInfo`'s range test (`gap > rangeOf`), whose refusal prints the reach to a tenth where it isn't the printed range (`out of range (38.2" / 37.9")`; classic's text unchanged), and whose result carries `reach` beside the gap `range`; the AI's `shotValue` (`core/ai/score.js`), measured from the cell scored (rule 10: the bump's); `sim/oracle/scan-ref.mjs`'s reference takes the code's `rangeOf` (a rule, as the reference takes the code's rules). No AI scan is bounded by a weapon's range: S0's boxes (`scanBox`) bound the move's plan, `levelSlack` the charge, objective and danger terms, so nothing widened; P-scan holds the scans to the whole board's on the `fort/` pairs as before. `core/ai/policy.js`'s Advance rule (`nearest > range + M + 3`, a shooter with nothing to shoot) keeps the printed range: a heuristic beside `pick.canShoot`, which is `shotValue`'s, and the reach's 2" sits inside its 3" margin. Client code left as it was: `present/orders.js`'s approach (`can`: the gap against `w.range`) and `present/standing.js`'s `targetInRange` still read the printed range, so the planner and the standing orders are a lob's 2" conservative on a deck (they decide nothing the match takes without `shotInfo`).
- **What it gives** (terrain-check's lob rows, bit for bit against `Math.sqrt(R*R + 2*h*R)` on every deck of terrain-check's 1,000 fortified boards; the roadmap's numbers to a tenth): the Trebuchet's 36" is 37.9" from a 2" rampart or bastion (√1440) and 38.4" from the keep's 2.5" (√1476), 33.9" firing up at a 2" deck (√1152); the Venom Engine's 30" is 31.9" from 2" (√1020); the Grenadiers' 12" is 13.9" from 2" (√192) and 14.7" from the watchtower's 3" (√216), which only climbers reach (the big guns take no ladder, so the Trebuchet's best is the keep's 2.5"). About a drop's worth farther, as open question 30 foresaw: the Trebuchet's base range stays.
- **The view.** The range ring (`input/human.js`'s one line) is `rangeOf(G, u)`: the reach to the ground under the shooter, so a gun on a deck shows the larger ring, drawn at its floor as F7a draws it. The tooltip prints the gap against the reach to that target, `30.2" / 37.9" (36", lobbed down)` (or `lobbed up`; classic `12.3" / 18"`). The help's line-of-sight paragraph gains a Lobbing line.
- **The checks.** terrain-check's P-climb: the lob rows (every deck's centre against the first ground cell, every lobbed weapon both ways, the ring, direct fire and spells at their printed range, a board without height at the printed range; on the 1,000 Skirmish and Grand-fixture boards of seeds 1-500, 46,942 rows on 6,706 decks, every one of the roadmap's six numbers met), each row a P-climb failure. P-height's `lobPairs` on its 12 fortified boards: every ranged unit on 40 random cell pairs (raised and ground) against an enemy, `rangeOf` the physics restated to the bit, `shotInfo` out of range exactly past it, the AI's `shotValue` 0 past it (5,280 pairs); the scenes only the lob decides, a shot from a deck at the ground past the printed range taken (36) and valued by the AI for an indirect weapon (24), a shot up at a deck within the printed range refused (36); three self-test edits, `lob-flat`, `lob-direct`, `lob-ai-flat`, each caught. data-check's PINNED and P-prop's PINNED_UNDER take 8 (shadowState prints nothing new). `sim/height-probe.mjs` counts shots (a `unit.face` then its volley, first template or cast), those from a deck, those from a deck the shooter walked onto in the battle, those past the printed range (the gap between the bases as the events place them) and those up at a raised target; `sim/play-report.mjs` gains F7b's row on them (§4.2.9's threshold), sharing one fold of the `fort/` AI pairs with F7a's.
- **The corpus** (its own commit, b0dbba0; `parity --record --only fort`): of `fort/`, watch-fort-3, -8 and -9 play differently and were re-recorded; watch-fort-1, -2, -7 and both human logs replay unchanged, hash for hash. No `scale/` pair is on `fortified` (the WIP merge recorded none there: all ten are on `open`), so none moved. The PIN moved from 90bd7c8 to F17's code commit (1917303), so `parity --pin` passes all 70 again (the WIP merge's PIN had no Field or Grand mission and failed the ten `scale/` battles).
- **Play** (play-report on the `fort/` pairs, before → after): F7b's row, a shooter fires from a deck in 6 of 6 battles both ways; shots from a deck 28 → 36, from a deck the shooter climbed to 8 → 11; F7a's row 4 → 5 of 6, the keep held from its top 3 of 3 both ways. Not one shot past its printed range in the six, before or after. On a 24-battle sweep (`--sweep 24`, seeds from 7000): shots from a deck 102 → 100 in 22 → 21 battles, from a climbed deck 25 → 25, past the printed range 0 → 1, up at a raised target 86 → 79; F7a's row 10 → 12 of 24. So the AI doesn't climb to lob: the reach adds about 2" over a 36" weapon, the guns already climb for the height term, and firing up costs a little more than firing down gives (2.1" against 1.9" for the Trebuchet at a 2" deck). Both rows pass; no tuning.
- **What turned up.** terrain-check's connectivity rows fail on 320 of the 2,000 Field and Grand boards on `fortified` (seeds 1-500): where the keep stands, the centre objective sits on its 2.5" top and no squad on the ground is within 4.18" of it at its level. That is the WIP merge's (F8b's rows were written for `open`, and F7a's keep holds its objective from the top by design), not F17's: the same rows fail on the same boards on F17's parent (28 of 120 on seeds 1-30, a copy of 2983543), and F17 touches neither the terrain nor the nav. A rule for it (connectivity judging the keep's objective from its top, or by its stairs) is the merge's follow-up. mutation.mjs's first run here came back inconclusive at a load of 46 on 4 CPUs (four Field and Grand page runs of the PIN timed out at the 60 s `ORACLE_TIMEOUT_MS`: the same four replay on the PIN's page in 13-19 s at a load of 17, and mutation and `--core` passed when run again with a 300 s timeout). terrain-check's self-test had a stale edit at the parent already (`spare-height`, anchored on the sync line F8b's tiles rewrote): ported, with a `lob-flat` edit beside it; while the connectivity rows fail, every edit's run prints MISMATCH whatever it breaks, so both were held by hand to their own rows.
- **Run** (F17's code and corpus, and the tooltip's fix, on a machine shared with three other teams at load 13-46 on 4 CPUs; each exiting 0 unless said): parity, 70 of 70, and `--pin`, 70 of 70 (and before the re-record, 67 of 70: the three `fort/` pairs named above); self-test; mutation and `--core` (on their second run, What turned up); perturb `--fn hypot` and `--fn sin,cos,atan,atan2`; dmath-check; data-check; flag-lint and `--self-test`; boundaries and `--self-test`; terrain-check, every row but the connectivity rows above (exit 1 on those alone), and `--self-test` (with the caveat above); property (70 corpus battles and 32 random games; P-height's lob rows as above; 1,510 s) and `--self-test` (all 58 edits caught, `lob-flat`, `lob-direct` and `lob-ai-flat` among them); scale-check and `--self-test` (12 edits); play-report, every row (F7a 5 of 6 and the keep 3 of 3, F7b 6 of 6, F10b 4 of 4 with its control 0 of 4); mirror-check; replay-check (70 battles); pilot-check; merge-sim; macro-check; playback-check; army-sim's Skirmish gates (`--check --mission classic --jobs 2`: classic 52.4% ± 1.2, as ever, `fortified` 49.1% ± 1.2, per-unit in band; 471 s). In Chromium 153: parity `--browser`, 70 of 70 (66 in the run at `PARALLEL=2`; the four whose page didn't load within 30 s at load 35, again alone); hud-check; present-check (70 battles, 392 s); play-check (its watch, bushtail, serpent, hotseat and grand lanes played; its layout lane fails as it fails on a build of F17's parent, 2983543: on a Grand board at 1280×800 and 1366×768 no unit's card shows after clicks on six units' labels, the WIP merge's, which the card's two new lines play no part in). Not run: army-sim's Field and Grand gates (15-20 minutes with `--jobs 2` on a quiet machine; F17 moves no price and none of `scale/` is on `fortified`, but a Field or Grand battle on `fortified` lobs as a Skirmish one does), the timing checks (scale-bench, fold-cost, render-bench: this machine was never quiet), P-peers, and the rest of the Chromium list (snap-check, rematch-memory, title-shot, terrain-shots, lobby-rig, input-check, board-check): the step touches the view only in the ring's radius, a shot tooltip's words and the card's lines.

**The tooltip's reason as built** (the October playtest's fix; view only: no bump, the corpus unchanged). The Scaleguard (T4, Sv4+) and the Brute (T6, W9, Sv4+) are their numbers alone, with no armour rule; the tooltip now says so by giving each need its reason. `ui/tooltip.js`'s `oddsText` prints `wound 6+ (S3 vs T6)` (`woundWhy`: the weapon's S against the target's T, and `poison N+` only where the poison lowers the table's need) and `save 4+ (Sv4+ AP0)` (`saveWhy`: the target's save and the weapon's AP as the card writes it, AP0 or AP-1, and `, cover` where cover helps; `save — (Sv6+ AP-2)` when none is left). `ui/card.js` was to add, under each weapon with a strength, what it wounds on against every toughness a unit of any race has (`wounds T3 4+ · T4–5 5+ · T6 6+`, runs of one need together: the card knows no target, so the reason for all of them at once); built, and taken out again at the wave's integration: the card stood two lines taller, and on a 1280×800 screen the lead's open card (F10a's group line over it) then covered a figure that `sim/input-check.mjs`'s Shift-click lands on, so the click never reached the table (the check now picks a member no panel of the HUD covers, by the panel test its `clear` already made). The card is as it was; the reason is the tooltip's, at the moment it matters. sim/hud-check.mjs holds no tooltip text (its rows are the HUD's buttons, the charge's spots and the end screen), so nothing needed porting; play-check's hovers (`/hit|Mesmerize|template|shots/` for a shot, `/models|wounds/` for a unit's line) still tell them apart, a shot's tooltip saying "wound", never "wounds".

**F13 as built** (touch aim: a hover for a finger; client code only: no bump, the corpus byte-identical, nothing new in the log but what a click sends; open question 29's answer, both the long press and 👆 Aim, the lift committing with no second tap):
- **The long press** (`input/group.js`'s `holdFrom`: 450 ms, the finger within 6 px). On one of the seat's own units it adds or drops it, as F10a built it. Held anywhere else on the board while there is something to aim (`Aim.ready()`: a unit or a group of the seat's picked up in its deployment or its phase, or a charge's end to pick), it becomes an aim drag, with a 10 ms vibrate and the click's sound; a box the press began in ▭ Select gives way to it.
- **👆 Aim** (`#aimMode`, right after ▭ Select in `#actions`; shown, as ▭ Select, under `pointer: coarse` while `body.playing`). While it is on, a finger pressed on the board aims from the start, whenever there is something to aim: OrbitControls' one-finger gesture is then set aside (`touches()`, as Select mode's), and otherwise a finger orbits as ever, never dead; two fingers still pan and zoom. A press on a pin's handle is still the handle's drag. **The rule with ▭ Select: they take turns**, switching one on switches the other off (`Aim.set`, `GroupInput.setSelectMode`), both lit from the HUD model's `aim` slice (`ui/hud.js`). Not "Aim wins while a unit is picked up": with both on a box could never be drawn round a new group while one was picked up, and the lit buttons would no longer say what a finger does.
- **The drag** (`input/aim.js`, `Aim`; `input/human.js`'s listeners hand it the pointer after the group's). The camera is held by `controls.enableRotate = false` for the drag's length, not `enabled = false`: a disabled control ignores the second finger's pointerdown, so after the abort two fingers would turn the camera by the first; with rotate alone set aside, the second finger is OrbitControls' two-finger pan and zoom at once. Under the finger runs the mouse's own hover (`pointed()`: the move's path, inches and ghost; a shot's or a charge's odds; a charge's end spot; a group's formation, through `GroupInput.hover`, ghosts a few a frame on a larger board as ever), the tooltip 96 px above the finger, out from under it, and the hint line saying what the lift will do (the HUD model's `aimVerb`). The lift is `click(pick, e, true)` where the finger leaves the glass, which is the last move's point (Chromium plays a pending move before the pointerup), so what is sent is what the preview showed: the move, the shot, the charge, the charge's end spot, a group's pin (or, on its flag, its send), a placement. A second finger, a cancelled pointer, or the finger off the board (no ground under it) calls it off: the preview goes (a pinned formation drawn again, `GroupInput.unhover`), nothing is sent, and off the board the hint says so until the lift.
- **As far as it goes** (`input/tools/move.js`'s `aimCell` and `farthest`: read only over the plan, under the preview's lock; no core change, no new query). With `far` (a finger's aim; the mouse with Alt held, its hover and its click), where the pointer lies beyond the unit's reach (the plan has no distance at its cell, or no valid end within nearestValid's 2.4"), the move goes to the valid end farthest along the ray from the unit through the pointer, and no farther than the pointer: of the cells the plan reaches whose centre lies within a cell (0.5") of the ray (a strip an inch wide, so every column of the grid it crosses holds one), the one farthest along it that `validEnd` takes, ties nearer the ray, then the lowest index, measured with `core/dmath.js`'s `hypot` as the charge-end tool's. The tooltip adds "· as far as it goes". In the movement phase the far preview shows over an enemy too, since a click there takes the move branch. The command sent is still `move {u, c}`. Within the reach, and for the mouse without Alt, hover and click are what they were: a plain click beyond the reach still does nothing.
- **The checks.** `sim/input-check.mjs`'s aim cases (`--only aim` plays them alone), on a fresh classic hotseat battle, by real touches through CDP: a long press on the ground with a unit picked up shows its path, its inches and its ghost under the finger with the camera still (within 0.02", once an earlier gesture's damping has run out), and the lift moves it to the ghost's cell; a second finger calls a long press's aim off, the preview gone and nothing sent; a group of two's long press draws its ghost rings and the lift pins it, nothing sent; ▭ Select and 👆 Aim switch each other off; with 👆 Aim a plain one-finger drag shows the move at once with the camera still and the lift moves the unit to the ghost's cell; dragged beyond a unit's reach (its M + 7" ahead) the ghost stands on a valid end on the ray with none farther along it, the tooltip says "as far as it goes", and the lift lands it there; with the mouse a plain click at such a point sends nothing and an Alt-click goes as far as it goes; in the shooting phase a long press on an enemy in range shows the shot's odds and the lift fires (the Trebuchet's blast played at ⏩ 4×). The harness waits two frames after a slide: Chromium hands the page a move at its next frame, a second or so under SwiftShader. Parity 70/70 with no re-record; boundaries (and its self-test), flag-lint (and its self-test), macro-check (and its self-test), present-check, and hud-check (and its self-test) pass; the whole input-check, 43 steps. `node sim/self-test.mjs` passes but for its spin mutant, which looks in the PIN's `core/actions/fight.js` for F8b's `guard < guards` where the PIN (90bd7c8) still has `guard < 30`: that predates F13 and touches nothing here. play-check's watch, serpent, hotseat and grand lanes pass, bushtail on a second run (its first found no click that placed a unit); its layout lane fails here as it does on the commit F13 starts from (no unit's card after clicks on six units on Grand at 1280×800 and 1366×768). title-shot is inconclusive in this container (its screenshot times out, at 400 s too); nothing of F13 shows on the title (👆 Aim shows only while a battle is played).
