- **Not here.** An input-check case for the charge phase's aim (its odds and its end spot are the same hover and click as the shot's and the move's, which the cases hold), and a check by hand on a phone. An armed March or Attack (F10c) takes a finger's lift as it takes a click, but the preview under the finger is the plain hover's (the mouse's is too: an armed click has no hover of its own).

**F16 as built** (the courtesy fog of war, open question 32's answer; view only: no bump, the corpus byte-identical, nothing new in the match, the log or the setup; §5's "no hidden information" stands as a rule of the core, and this hides in the view, as the sealed army lists of open question 20 do, on the trust the dice rest on):
- **Where the flag lives.** Never in the core, the fold or the setup: no `SETUP_KEYS` entry (the roadmap's sketch had one the core ignores; as built the start of a fogged match is byte for byte an unfogged one's, so the corpus, P-merge and the Folder never hear of it). Online it is the lobby's `fog` (net/lobby.js: `lobbyDoc({ fog })`, `lobbyOf` reading it as `fog === true`, so a lobby written before F16 is off; `editBattle({ fog })` the host's, un-readying both seats as any change of the battle does, so the two Readys are the agreement), shown to the guest beside the battlefield before its Ready as the size and the terrain are (ui/screens/lobby.js's switch, made once as `#lobbySize` is, disabled but for the host), read by each page as its battle begins (app/online.js's `begin`: `flow.follow(session, { …, fog })`) and kept by a rematch. Against the AI it is the battle-setup panel's Fog line (ui/screens/setup.js, made in code as the size line is, so index.html's markup is untouched: a switch, and "You see only what your units see of the other army, and the scenery as you last saw it. The AI sees everything."), shown for the two modes against the AI (`FOG_MODES`) and never for hotseat (one screen) or a watched battle; its default the flow's `fogPick` (?fog on, ?fog=0 off, else `localStorage['tails-and-scales:fog']`, in try/catch, written as the switch turns), handed to `Flow.start(mode, races, size, terrain, fog)`. The flow keeps `fog = { seat }` for a battle under it: a mode against the AI, or an online page playing exactly one seat; a watcher, a page read-only after its seed check, a replay file and hotseat keep none.
- **The model** (`present/fog.js`, pure; the header says it whole). A seat's fog `F` is `{ seat, over, foes, seen, fell, last, known, table }`: the enemy units its living units see now, those that fell in sight in the last step, each enemy as last seen (a mirror unit's record; a seen one's as it stands, an unseen one's its ghost), each one's models as last known (the roster's), and the scenery as last seen (`table`, each chunk's `{ alive, y }`; null until the first step takes the board as it stands, which both seats see). `fogStep(F, M, sideOf, sees)` moves it an entry on: an enemy seen is recorded; one that falls while seen as the entry opened fell in sight (no ghost, counted 0); a ghost whose place is seen goes ("seen to be gone": the unit isn't there, or it would be seen); a chunk seen is recorded as it stands; with the battle over the fog lifts (everything seen, no ghost, the scenery live). `fogView` (the units hidden, the ghosts), `fogOpen` (while an entry plays), `fogReveal` (the chunks whose record a step changed), `fogChunks` (the chunks as the seat's table draws them), `fogStale` and `fogEvents` (below) read it; none touches the fog it is handed.
- **Seen.** `fogSight(G, q, ask, cache)`, run inside the Session's preview (the dice locked, as input/ asks its questions), asks the core's own `sight` (any living friendly unit, its eye, to any model's chest: S1's broadphase through `G.terrain.los`), never a copy of the rule: an enemy is seen when any friendly unit's `sight(...).visible`; a ghost's place, a stale chunk and a template's landing by a stand-in, a unit as `sight` reads one (a ghost: the unit's type, its record's place and models; a chunk: one model at its top centre, 0.1" up; a landing: one on the floor there, 0.5" up), its cover never asked. Answers are cached per pair, keyed by both units' places and their models' slots, the whole cache let go when the scenery's state moves (`terrainKey`: the broken chunks, their count and a weighted sum of heights). A chunk is "seen" by the first of the two rules F16 offered: the ray from a friendly eye to its top centre unblocked, through the same `los`; asked only of the chunks whose live state isn't the record (a few after a blast; none before), so the cheaper rule was not needed. A chunk the eye stands below has its own face in the way: from there it is not seen (a gap where a wall stood never is: a broken chunk blocks nothing). A fallen log and the tree it was are seen together (one mesh draws both), so the record never holds the one fallen and the other standing.
- **Per entry, two fog events.** The flow's sink (`fogEntry`, after the ?debug checkpoints) asks the sight of the match the table will show once it has played the entry (the Session's G after the entry: `sink.events` is told after each entry is folded), steps the fog, marks the events and puts `{ t: 'fog', at: 'open', live, hide, ghosts }` before them and `{ t: 'fog', at: 'close', F, hide, ghosts, reveal }` after (the chunks seen again with their defs, `view/terrain.js`'s `defOf`, and a fallen log's tree's). While an entry plays an enemy is live only if seen at both its ends, or seen as it fell (its fall plays); one leaving sight becomes its ghost as the entry opens, where it last stood, so its walk away is never shown, and one coming into sight appears as the entry closes; so the AI's whole turn, one entry, shows an enemy seen at its start and its end. `present/pace.js` counts `fog` among the instant events (`INSTANT`, `IN_ATTACK`), so no batch waits on it or breaks at it (a group order's members run across entries). The mirror ignores it, and a mark changes no field the mirror folds (a collapse's drops not to play are named in `unseen`, its `drops` untouched): the mirror is still the match (P-present, held under the fog too).
- **What the marks say** (`fogEvents`, by reading the entry as core/actions/ emit it: an action opens with a focus, its turn to face or its tray, its deeds name its actor `u` and target `tg`). An action's tray, dice rows and lines are its actor's: shown when the actor is the seat's own or an enemy seen as the entry opened or closed; else, aimed at one of the seat's units, shown with the actor unnamed (the tray "Unseen → Oak Guard · Acid globe", the line "<b>Unseen</b> shoot Oak Guard: …", the rows as they are: you are being shot) or in full for a fight it is in; else hidden. A line or tray whose action names no unit (an advance's roll played alone, a morale test held) is read by the name it starts with: hidden when every enemy unit of that name is unseen (flag-lint's one allowed name test in present/, said so there). A held-back destroyed line is the unit that fell's, in the order they fell. A template's victims (each wound row from its landing on, its save row, its line) and its "…scenery wrecked" line show when its landing is in sight, a victim's when it is the seat's own (damage to your own units always shows); its landing's explosion likewise; its aim, scatter and throw as its shooter's figure. The scenery's events (a walk's smashes too) for a chunk stale as the entry closes, or from a template landing out of sight or a walker unseen, play nothing. Lines of nobody's (the round's end) and of the seat's own always show. The flow's handlers never hear of an event marked hidden (`VEILED`: the log, the tray, the scenery's events, a template's); the battle log's line keeps its `data-k` (F15).
- **The view.** `view/units.js`'s `veil(ids)`: a unit veiled has no figure drawn (a falling or fleeing figure goes on as it was), no ring, no hit cylinder (the picker returns no unit for it, so no tooltip, card or pick), no label, no drop line, no place on screen (a box and the picker's fallback skip it) and no chip; what its events would say over the table (a wound's number, a death's cry and gore, "flees!", "destroyed", a charge's shout, a stomp, a smash's shake, a volley's shots, a spell's sound, a gaze, the thorns' motes at the caster) says nothing, and a fight with it unseen at both ends makes no sound. `view/fog.js`'s `Ghosts`: a grey translucent figure per model then standing (the unit's own miniature, every mesh under one shared material made the first time a ghost stands), and a dashed "last seen" label with its models or wounds. `view/terrain.js`'s `reveal(list)` brings a chunk seen again up to date (a broken one off the table, no debris; a dropped one at its height; one never seen before built as `sync` builds it), and a snap draws the scenery as last seen through `sync(fogChunks(...))`. The minimap (`fog()`): no dot for a unit veiled, a grey ring for a ghost, the footprints as last seen, no ping for either; the roster (`fog()`): the other army's worth as last seen (each unit seen now as it stands, each other at its models as last known, whole if never seen), greyed, its title "As last seen". The player's `veil` (the flow's, while anything is veiled): the camera cues no action whose actor is veiled and frames no batch of veiled members (their focus left out too), and a batch of veiled walkers shows no advance row. The card on a unit as it is veiled closes, and the pointer's hold on one lets go.
- **Snaps, peeks, Undo, the end.** A snap (an online battle followed, a refold, the catch-up past 30 s, a scrub or a peek shown) is followed by `relog`, which already folds the battle's entries from its start: under the fog it walks the fog with them, an entry at a time as the sink does (a cache of its own), leaves out the lines the seat can't see, and the table shows the fog it ends at (`refog`): the ghosts and the scenery as last seen come back. A peek at a battle under the fog (F15's log click, the bar's ⏮) is fogged for the battle's seat while the battle lives; Undo (F12) swaps in a Session that relog walks the same way. The battle's last entry lifts the fog as it closes (the end screen shows the whole table); a replay of a battle over sees all, and an entry of another Session after it lifts a fog still kept.
- **?debug.** `__ts.view.fog()` (not promised): the seat, the fog the sink has walked to (`last`: seen, ghosts, known, the chunks stale) and the one shown (`shown`: hidden, ghosts, stale; `table`, its record of the scenery), each unit's figures, ring, label, hit cylinder and pick, the ghosts standing, the chunks the table draws standing, the minimap's dots, the roster's model and the chips (each standing unit given a place on screen for the asking). `__ts.view.fogFor(seat)` (not promised) keeps the next battle started here under the fog for that seat whatever its mode (`Flow.start` takes a seat's number for `fog`; the panel only ever hands it true or false, and never offers it in hotseat): present-check's hotseat battles. The real match is the ?debug block's as ever.
- **The cost** (measured in Node, the machine shared with other runs, its load average 20-28 on 4 cores, so every maximum is a stall's): on the `scale/` pilot log's Grand board (80×56, 40 units, 277 chunks) an entry's whole pass (the projection, the sight with its cache, the step and the marks), over its 222 entries in three runs, p50 0.6-0.8 ms and p90 about 5 ms; the sight alone p50 0.3 ms and p90 1.4-2.0 ms with the cache, p50 0.6-0.8 ms and p90 5-6 ms without; the first passes of a run (the code not yet compiled) and the stalls 25-110 ms. The whole board asked at once (about 20 units a side standing, warm, medians of 30): 0.4-0.9 ms cold and 0.1-0.3 ms cached, against 3-9 ms for every pair (an enemy seen by one friendly unit asks no other) and 0.1-0.25 ms for the projection; at the cap (24 a side, every enemy unseen, so every pair asked) that is about 6-13 ms, the worst a pass can cost. No coarsening (a single ray to a unit's centre, a distance pre-check) was needed. relog's walk after a snap: the Grand log's fold of 871 ms becomes 943 with the fog's pass (222 entries), a Field log's (29 units, 186 chunks, 281 entries) 307 ms 477.
- **The checks.** `sim/fog-check.mjs` (new, Node; 75 checks): the units' transitions, the scenery's record, the marks over made-up entries (an AI turn, a morale phase, a template), the mirror untouched by any mark, and over every entry of four corpus logs (classic, fortified, Field, Grand) and both seats the sight pass held to the brute force over every pair of the core's sight, with the cache and without, a stand-in for an unseen enemy where it stands never seen, the dice never moved, and the marked events folding to the match. present-check's F16 case: the eleven battles against the AI (the human set's nine, pilot/'s two) played on the page under ?fog, each the corpus's battle (trace and shadows; the log the page writes is the fog's) and the mirror the match at every checkpoint, and after each entry's closing fog event the page held to a fold of its own that asks the core's sight over every pair: the enemies veiled exactly those unseen, none of them drawn, dotted or chipped, every one seen labelled and pickable, the ghosts the fold's where it says with its models' figures and a minimap ring each, the roster's other army as last seen; every line and tray the page writes that starts with an enemy's name names one seen at either end of its entry, a line hidden never written, every other written as marked; every chunk drawn standing exactly when the seat's record says so, and none kept as last seen while the fold's core sees a stand-in at its top centre; the fog lifted at the end. No battle against the AI loses sight of scenery it saw change, so four hotseat battles that do (hotseat-aggressive-125 and -lists-3 for seat 1, -140 and -field-1 for seat 0) are played too, that seat under the fog by `view.fogFor`: 155 chunk-entries kept as last seen over them. Over the set some enemy hidden, some ghost, some line and some chunk (hand mutations caught: a label drawn for a veiled unit, no ghost drawn, a hidden line marked shown, the handlers' veil gone, `reveal` doing nothing, rubble added out of sight drawn anyway). The case's first run caught the battle's last entry marked as lifted (the AI's last turn named units still veiled): it is marked by what the seat sees as it ends, and only its close lifts the fog. lobby-rig's `fog`: the host's switch, off; on battlefield 8 (each seat's deployment leaves two enemies unseen) the host turns it on after the guest readied, the guest's lobby shows it on and un-readied; both ready, the start names no fog; each seated page keeps the fog for its own seat and, whenever its table has caught up, hides exactly the enemies its seat's units can't see (the core's sight through the page's own Session), drawing none of them, through the deployment and the turns played with Auto to round 2; a watcher keeps none; two mutants (`fog-unread`, `fog-unwired`), each caught.
- **Not here, and what the fog does not hide.** The objectives' flags and the score still show who holds each objective (an unseen enemy on one shows as its holder's colour, as the score must); the move's reach still bends round an enemy you can't see (the rules know where it stands, and the planner's forbid mask is theirs); 🤖 Auto and the standing orders choose with the whole match, as the AI does, so your own unit's line may name a target its seat can't see; an attack batch's tray still counts its units ("Shooting · 3 units"); an unnamed shot's tray still names its weapon, and a template's wound row its victim (the seat's own, or one under a landing in sight). A snap mid-battle draws the fog from the battle's start (relog's walk), so the ghosts and the scenery as last seen survive a rejoin, a refold and the catch-up. The battle's last entry is marked, and played, by what the seat sees as it ends; only its close lifts the fog. No vs-AI log at Field or Grand is in the corpus, so the page's case runs the eleven classic ones; fog-check holds the pass itself on Field and Grand logs. Not done here: a check by hand on a phone.
- **Checks run** (the machine shared with other runs, its load average 13-34 on 4 cores): `node sim/parity.mjs` 70 of 70 byte-identical (nothing under core/, match/ or data/ changed, nothing re-recorded); `boundaries` and `flag-lint` (each with `--self-test`) and `self-test.mjs`; fog-check's 75 checks; present-check over the 70 battles (P-present on every one with the fog off, then its F16 case over the eleven against the AI and the four hotseat battles), and `--self-test` on one battle with three mutations, each caught; replay-check over the 70; macro-check; hud-check, snap-check and undo-check in Chromium; lobby-rig's `fog`, alone (its first run, under a load of 28, timed out loading the watcher's page; alone it passed) and `--self-test` of its two mutants; the whole lobby rig, 18 of its 19 cases passing (`play` and `group` among them, the lobby's new field beside theirs), `size` failing as on the base commit (its `#lobbySize` never visible: another step's, not touched here). input-check stops at its box step's Shift-click ("Shift-click on 6 left the group [1,5,6,7]") on this branch and on a build of the base commit (26ecab9) alike, so its later cases went unrun but `--only aim`, which passes. `title-shot` exit 3 (its screenshot timed out: no verdict). Not run: rematch-memory (50-80 minutes), play-check, board-check, terrain-shots and render-bench (none reads what the fog changes with it off), and the core's own (mutation, perturb, scale-check and -bench, army-sim, merge-sim, peers: no core, match or data change).

**Inherited failures as built** (the WIP merge of F8b's three, each reproduced on 26ecab9; checks and a note only: no core, view, input or UI line changed, no bump, the corpus byte-identical):
- **lobby-rig's `size`: the rig's race, not the page.** The case pressed Ready on both seats and only then set the host's `autoStart` off, and `app/online.js` starts the match on the host's page as soon as its lobby has both seats ready. Whenever the guest's Ready reached the host's page before the host's own press, that press was the start: the lobby hid, and `selectOption('#lobbySize')` waited 30 s on a select no longer shown ("element is not visible": the select there, its three sizes offered). Which lands first is timing: alone the host's press won, in the full run it lost every time. With the guest's Ready waited on before the host presses, the old case fails so on every run and the new one passes. The case now opens its lobby with `lobbyPair({ autoStart: false })`, as `altered` does. `ui/screens/lobby.js` shows the select (made once in the seed row, the host's to change, the guest's disabled) as the case wants; the self-test's two size mutants are still caught.
- **terrain-check's connectivity rows: right, and failing on the tower ring, not the keep.** The 320 failing boards of seeds 1-500 (160 Field, 160 Grand) are exactly those whose centre draw lands in [0.5, 0.8), where `fortified`'s centre rule (F7a's `[['keep', 0.5], ['tower', 0.8]]`) stands the ruined tower ring: its doors are about 1.25" wide, no squad walks in, and on every one of them no r 1.18 squad reaches a cell within 4.18" of the objective (what F8b measured of the ring on `open`, and why `open`'s centre is the rock box alone). On all 502 keep boards an r 1.18 squad walks up either 4.5" stair and holds the objective from the keep's top, within HIGH of its floor, and the 178 boards with open ground at the centre pass. (F17's notes read the failures as the keep's: the failure line said only "no ground within 4.18" of the objective at (0, 0)".) The fix is consensus: `fortified` gains a `largeCentre`, the rule scatter reads in place of `centre` on a table larger than classic's, the rock box under 0.8 where the ring stood, from the same one draw, so the keep and open ground stand on the same boards and the Skirmish's fortified boards (and `fort/`) are untouched. It was proposed, not landed, in `sim/notes/keep-connectivity.diff` (it moves boards and `RULES_ID`, and the core and the corpus are another step's this wave): applied and measured, terrain-check exits 0 with connectivity 2,000 of 2,000, parity 70 of 70 byte-identical (no corpus battle is a fortified Field or Grand one) and data-check passes. The check now says what it judges: with height the hull keeps to the ground (it walked the works' and the keep's stairs; ground-only, it still crosses on all 1,000 fortified Field and Grand boards), and the squad holds an objective only from a cell within HIGH of the objective's floor (controlOf's rule, §4.2.9's "at its level"); a failure names what stands round the centre objective and the MISMATCH counts the failed boards by it ("the ruined tower ring 320"). A connectivity failure no longer stops the run before the tiles' rows (exit 1 at the end), the self-test's edits must fail a row of their own (while these rows fail every run printed their MISMATCH, and the tile edits were caught by it alone), and its two controls run on seeds 7-9, boards with no ring. The rows failed until the patch landed. **Landed with F19a** (its own commit, 8469817, before F19a's; the note deleted with it; `CORE_VERSION` 10 is F19a's bump and covers it): `fortified` has `largeCentre: [['keep', 0.5], ['rockbox', 0.8]]`, which scatter reads in place of `centre` on a table larger than classic's (`areaScale(T) > 1`), from the same one draw; `checkSet` checks it as it checks `centre` (an optional field, `OPTIONAL_FIELDS`), and data-check refuses five broken copies (no list, a piece that doesn't exist, a threshold above 1, thresholds that fall, an entry without its threshold), holds classic to having none, and moves `RULES_ID` on it (a threshold, the field dropped). terrain-check exits 0: connectivity 2,000 of 2,000 on seeds 1-500, the 320 tower boards now the rock box's, every other Field and Grand board and every Skirmish board (`fort/`'s among them) built as before; parity 70 of 70 byte-identical.
- **play-check's layout lane: the lane read the labels mid-swing.** On a Grand hotseat board it read seat 0's labels a fixed 4 s after Begin battle showed. The camera's swing onto the broadside is 1.4 s of game time and a frame steps at most 0.05 s of it, so under SwiftShader (a Grand frame a second or more, the clock's rate 0.2-0.6) it runs about 25 s: 4 s in, the camera still near the title's orbit (at (−26, 13, 14), looking at (−5, 0, 0)), every one of seat 0's labels projected far off the screen, the lane's filter kept none and nothing was clicked. On classic that pose happens to frame seat 0's half, so its lanes never met it. The picker, the card and the figures' LOD were never at fault: once the swing ends the first click shows the Elder's card. With the camera waited on, a second reading surfaced: 1.9 s after the click the card was still 20 px low in its slide and the minimap's 10 Hz tick hadn't run, so the map read as covering it. The lane now waits for each to rest (`settle`: no box moving 2 px across a tick and two of the page's frames, three times running), and so does every other lane's `rest()`, whose two readings 800 ms apart fell inside one frame on a loaded machine: at a load of 20-27 the serpent lane twice hovered seat 1's labels mid-swing ("no unit placed by a click (0 clicks on the ground)", the page stepping some 0.03 s of game time a wall second) and the hotseat lane once, on the base's code as on this; with `settle` the serpent lane plays at that load; at 1280×800 the card stands 521-790 px, the minimap raised to 391-511 and the roster above it, and a build whose minimap is never raised (`view/minimap.js`'s lift held at 10, a scratch copy) still fails the lane, the map at 670-790 over the card.
- **lobby-rig's `group` and `catch-up` under load** (both failed in one run of the two alone at a load of 12-15 on 4 CPUs; `group` passed in both full runs here, at 6-10 and at 25-29, and `catch-up` in the first and alone). `catch-up` opens a drawn page (not `?fast`): its `page.goto` waits for the load event within Playwright's 30 s default (the run that failed timed out there), then the page has 60 s to begin and its catch-up is held to under 15 s of wall clock, which a SwiftShader page starved of frames misses. `group` presses End on the mover's page, once its orders show in the other page's presence, without waiting for that page's table to be idle: `?debug`'s endPhase then refuses ("no phase of a seat played here to end now") while the player still plays the group's move, as under load it may; an `until(mover, () => window.__ts.player.idle …)` before it, as the deployment's loop has, would close that. Its other waits are wall-clock bounds on presence (sent on a change, polled by online.js's 2 s tick, a 5 s heartbeat, a peer live for 15 s after it last spoke): 20 s for the host's group and for the orders to show. Neither changed here.
- **Checks run** (on a machine shared with other teams' runs, its load 5-29 on 4 CPUs; each exiting 0 unless said): parity 70 of 70 byte-identical, nothing re-recorded, the PIN unmoved; boundaries and flag-lint, each with `--self-test`; terrain-check exit 1 on the connectivity rows alone (320 of 2,000, all "the ruined tower ring"), every other row passing and the tiles' 48 of 48 run after them, and its `--self-test` with every edit and both controls caught, each by a row of its own; with the proposed patch applied (and taken out again), terrain-check exit 0, parity 70 of 70 and data-check. lobby-rig on 26ecab9's code: 17 of 18, `size` failing; with the fix a full run at load 25-29 passed 16 of 18, `size` among them, `history` and `catch-up` failing at a page's 30 s `goto` and each passing alone; `--self-test --only size`, 2 of 2 caught. play-check, every lane: `watch` (a first run, at load 20-27, in which `serpent` and `hotseat` failed as above), then `serpent`, `hotseat` and `layout`, then `bushtail` and `grand`, all passing with `settle`. Not run: input-check and hud-check (no input or UI line changed) and the rest of the standing list (nothing they read changed).

**F18 as built** (shooting into a fight; consensus: `CORE_VERSION` 9, `stateHash` as under 1-8 (shadowState prints nothing new), `RULES_ID` unchanged: the rule is code and moves no rules data; open question 31's answer, the exposure-weighted miss built, the cone kept as the alternative):
- **The rule** (`core/actions/shoot.js`, `core/queries.js`; §4.1 rule 27). `shotInfo` no longer refuses a target locked in combat, for any ranged weapon, at no modifier; the shooter itself still may not shoot while engaged (`canShoot`, unchanged), and a spell was never refused. Its result carries `fight`, `fightOf(G, u, tg)`: the shooter's own units engaged with the target (`engagedWith(G, tg)` filtered to u's side, G.units order), F their living models, T the target's, `onto` the one with the most living models (a tie keeps the first) and whether it is in cover; null when none of u's is in the fight. A plain volley (neither `blast` nor `spell`) into a fight: the whole hit roll as ever, then one `draw(G.rng)` per miss in the order of the hit dice, a miss straying when its draw is under F / (F + T); then the target's wound roll, save roll, `damage` and log line as ever; then, when any strayed, `strayHits`: the strays rolled to wound against `onto`'s T and saved on its Sv (cover as `inCover`; the dice roll with no save to make, rule 5), in rows of their own after the target's (`⚠ Oak Guard: 3 stray hits · wound 5+`, `Save 5+`), `damage` and its events as ever, and the line `Friendly fire! 3 stray shots hit Oak Guard: 1 wound, 1 unsaved — 1 slain.` With F = 0 nothing is drawn (rule 11's own branch). A template (the Trebuchet's, the Venom Engine's, the Grenadiers'; and the Elder's Thornburst, which erupts where the target stands) lands as it always has, and `blastLands` hits whoever is under it, the ⚠ row and "Friendly fire!" as before: the scatter is its risk. `shotInfo` also carries `under` for a blast weapon, `friendsUnder(G, u, tg)`: who of u's side (u among them) a template landing square on the target would catch, by `blastLands`' own victim test (now `modelsUnder`, shared, the same arithmetic: parity holds it). `fightOf` lives in `queries.js`, a door of its own; `friendsUnder` is shoot.js's and not re-exported (score.js imports it from the action, the tooltip reads it off `shotInfo`), so boundaries' door list is unchanged.
- **Why the share, not the cone.** It reads right on the table: the more of yours in the fight, the riskier the shot, and a melee your squad has swamped is one you shoot into at your squad's peril (a Hierophant alone against five Oak Guard: 5 in 6 of the Nutkin's misses stray, and the AI still took that shot in one corpus battle, the Hierophant being worth the risk); it needs no geometry the players can't see; and it costs one draw per miss, where the cone (each miss's line through the melee by `dmath`'s angles, the first base it crosses hit) would put a ray test per miss in the consensus code for a difference no one sees at card size. What the share does not see: a model is a model, so the Brute (one model, a 0.95" base) counts one against ten of your Nutkin (10 in 11 of the misses stray at a Brute your squad has swamped), and a lone hero is hard to pick out of a crowd. If the table finds that harsh, the lever is a base-weighted share (Σ base² for each side), still one draw a miss; the cone stays the documented alternative.
- **The AI** (`core/ai/score.js`; rule 10, it bumps with F18). `shotValue` no longer zeroes an engaged target. A volley is valued net of `strayCost(n, need, w, fight)`: n·(1 − p(hit))·F/(F + T) strays, each a hit on `onto` (rules.js's `expected`, hitting on 1+, against its T, Sv and cover), the same odds `doShoot` rolls. A template (a blast spell's too) is valued net of `ownUnder(G, u, e)`: each friend under it by `expected` over its models there, a big one's D3+1 hits as 3, as the target's own are counted; for every target, not only one in a fight, since a friend 1.5" off a target is under a 3" template all the same (five corpus battles changed by that alone: 8-21, 64-89, 2231-561374, 58021-588511 and watch-fort-8). So a shot whose friendly fire outweighs its haul is worth less than nothing, and the AI never prefers to shell its own Brute. The policy's scatter cost (aiShoot's "own lads", for a template that misses) is as it was; `bestSpot` hoists `fight` and `own` per enemy where it hoisted `engaged` (S1), each asked only of the weapon whose value reads it, and P-scan's reference (`sim/oracle/scan-ref.mjs`) asks the code's `fightOf`, `strayCost` and `ownUnder` afresh at every cell. No draw moves: `shotValue` draws nothing, and the lattice's draws are where they were. On 300 classic AI battles (seeds 5001-5300, the races swapping seats), 209 of 3,696 volleys went into a fight: 632 misses, 264 of them strayed, 126 enemy models slain by those volleys against 31 of the shooter's own; 55 of 3,385 templates were thrown at a target in a fight, killing 14 enemy models and 10 of the thrower's own (a template's scatter is the policy's heuristic's, which the AI weighs lightly).
- **The tooltip** (`ui/tooltip.js`'s `riskText`, a line of its own under the odds): a volley into a fight `⚠ into a fight: 3 of yours in it, a miss strays 1 in 3 (≈0.4 of yours slain)` (F, the share in lowest terms, and `strayCost`'s arithmetic as kills); a template with any of yours under it `⚠ friends under the template: Gliders ×4, Brute` (the count of models where the unit has more than one); nothing for a clear shot or the gaze. **The help**: the Shooting bullet says a unit in combat can't shoot but you may shoot into a fight, each miss striking your own unit there with the odds of your share of its models (3 of yours against 6 of theirs: 1 in 3), wounded and saved as any hit; the Blast paragraph that a template dropped into (or scattering into) a fight can catch your own, and the odds name any under it.
- **The checks.** P-prop's **P-fight** (`fightTask`, code with `fightOf`): on six classic boards each way round, a hotseat match to the first turn's movement phase, every other unit taken off and a scene set before End, for each of the active seat's ranged units: the fight (a friend 0.4" from an enemy, the shooter clear of both, placed until `shotInfo` takes it; any refusal but sight or range fails at once): `legal()` takes the shot and `shootTargets` offers it, for every ranged weapon of both races; the shot played through `apply()` and its dice held draw for draw to a copy of the stream (the hit dice, a draw per miss, the strays the misses under the share and the ⚠ row's count, the target's wound and save dice, the friend's, nothing else drawn; the target's rows and line first; every wound after the ⚠ row the friend's); a template or a spell straying nothing; the clear shot (the friend 4" off) drawing no stray die; the tie (each army's two Nutkin or Scaleguard round the enemy) striking the first in G.units order, and the second once the first has lost a model; the AI's value of each shot into the fight less than without the friend, a template's less with a friend under it; and the Venom Engine at an enemy locked with (and under the template with) the Brute: `ownUnder` > 0, the value less than without the Brute, and where it is at or under the AI's floor (0.4) the AI's shooting phase fires nothing (it held its fire in all six such scenes). Every ranged unit type of both races must meet the fight and the clear shot, both armies the tie, and a stray be rolled. Nine self-test edits, each caught by P-fight's own failure: `fight-barred`, `stray-draws-clear`, `stray-per-hit`, `stray-share-flipped`, `stray-after-wound`, `friend-rows-first`, `stray-tie-last`, `ai-ignores-strays`, `ai-ignores-own-template`. P-height's lob scene that wants the AI to value an indirect weapon now also wants none of its own under the template. data-check's PINNED and P-prop's PINNED_UNDER take 9: hotseat-late-8 and serpent-random-2 hash as under 1 at every pin, and 64-89, which plays another battle, ends at its new hash (`V9`). `sim/corpus-add.mjs --regen <ids>` plays named human-bot logs again by their own bots (setup, policy and seed) on the PIN code, admits them as any candidate, and writes each over itself, all or none.
- **The corpus** (its own commit, 6b12ba4; the PIN from F17's code, 1917303, to F18's, 15f42ef). 38 of the 70 battles played differently: 28 AI battles (16 classic pairs, army/'s watch-lists-swapped-102, fort/'s watch-fort-1, -7, -8 and -9, scale/'s watch-field-1, -2, -swapped-101, -swapped-102, watch-grand-1, -2 and -swapped-102), re-recorded with `parity --record --only` (their files alone rewritten; watch-fort-1 and -7 take the recorder's one-line `"entries": []`); and ten human-bot logs whose AI seat, Auto or pilot now shoots into a fight, eight of them reaching a command the new battle refuses. No log was edited by hand: eight were played again by their bots (`--regen`: human/bushtail-aggressive-3, -4, bushtail-random-6, hotseat-late-5, serpent-aggressive-1, serpent-random-1; pilot/hotseat-pilot-mix-1 and serpent-pilot-mix-1, `--need pilot`), and the two that no longer showed what they were made for were replaced as corpus-add made them, from the same arguments and `--from 1`: pilot/bushtail-pilot-mix-2 (no longer a pilot in each of the three phases) by bushtail-pilot-mix-6 (10 pilots), and human/hotseat-late-vote-9 (no overtime now) by hotseat-late-vote-11 (6 votes, two overtime rounds, as -9 had; `sim/hud-check.mjs` takes it). R0's coverage list (corpus.mjs's NEED) is still met in full, and 19 battles now hold a stray, six of them human-bot logs (serpent-aggressive-1's among them, a bot's own Scaleguard straying onto its Hierophant). The other 32 replay unchanged, hash for hash.
- **Balance** (army-sim's Skirmish gates, `--check --mission classic --jobs 2`, 285 s): classic 53.5% ± 1.2 (52.4% at F17), `fortified` 51.7% ± 1.2 (49.1%), each within its 4-point band; every unit's fitted value within its band (the Trebuchet 59 against its 50, within 14; the Sidewinders 74 against 65, within 13). No price moves. Field and Grand (`--check --mission field,grand --jobs 2`, 930 s; the Field again on F17's code, 26ecab9, on the same seeds, and both on a second seed, `--seed 2222`): the Field's score gates hold, 46.1% ± 1.6 on `open` and 47.3% on `fortified` (48.5% and 49.2% on F17's code), and on the second seed 47.1% and 48.8% (48.7% and 49.2%): the Bushtails a point or two lower, within the 5-point band. Its per-unit gate fails on the default seed on the Glider Wing alone, fitted 30 ± 12 against its Field price of 60 (band 24; 55 ± 11 on F17's code), and on the second seed on the Nutkin (46), the Brute (175) and the Sidewinders (97), the Glider Wing then in band (56); but F17's code fails it too on the second seed (the Nutkin 48, the Trebuchet 20), so at N = 900 the Field's per-unit gate moves with the seed, and no unit is out on both. What F18 changes for a melee unit is real all the same: locked in combat it could not be shot before, and now it can (at the shooter's own risk); the Glider Wing, a raider that lives in melee, is the unit to watch. A Field price for it would be a retune (data only, `RULES_ID` moves), the user's to slot, not F18's. The Grand's gates are reported, not judged (its rebalance is the roadmap's): 44.6% ± 1.9 on `open`, 41.1% ± 1.9 on `fortified` (outside its band of 6), every unit inside its band.
- **What turned up.** macro-check (P-macro) held the standing orders to act only for the units the count named as the run began (`actorsOf`, the preview behind Go's number). On a state the corpus never passed through before, hotseat-pilot-mix-1 as its bot played it again (entry 29), a Trebuchet's Attack on a target locked with the Oak Guard wrecks nine pieces of scenery and opens the sight a held Nutkin lacked, and the run's pilot plays it: the count was right about the table it saw, and the table changed under it. An order that wrecks scenery or fells a foe could always do that (and since F18 a shot into a fight can free the unit locked there), so the check is ported (c0da8e6), not the client: a unit the count left out may act only if it could not act at all as the count was taken (`q.canAct`), never one that could; one was freed in its run. The client's count stays a preview of the table as it stands.
- **Run** (F18's code and corpus, on a machine shared with other teams at a load of 10-29 on 4 CPUs; each exiting 0 unless said): parity, 70 of 70 (32 of 70 before the re-record), and `--pin`, 70 of 70; self-test; mutation and `--core`; perturb `--fn hypot` and `--fn sin,cos,atan,atan2`; dmath-check; data-check; flag-lint and `--self-test`; boundaries and `--self-test`; property (70 corpus battles and 32 random games, P-fight as above; 1,273 s) and `--self-test` (all 67 edits caught, the nine of P-fight among them; 2,909 s); scale-check and `--self-test`; replay-check (70 battles); pilot-check (74 battles); play-report, every row (F7a 5 of 6 and the keep 3 of 3, F7b 6 of 6, F10b 4 of 4 with its control 0 of 4); mirror-check; macro-check (after its port, above) and `--self-test` (9 faults); playback-check; rematch-check; camera-check; merge-sim; army-sim's Skirmish gates (above), and its Field and Grand gates (above: exit 1 on the Field's per-unit gate alone, as F17's code on another seed). In Chromium 153: parity `--browser`, 70 of 70 (68 in the run at `PARALLEL=2` and a load of 25-29; the two whose page never loaded, hotseat-random-4 and serpent-late-1, neither touched by F18, again alone); hud-check and `--self-test` (on hotseat-late-vote-11, every edit caught); present-check (70 battles, 180 s). Not run: terrain-check (F18 touches no terrain or nav, and its connectivity rows fail as F17 found them), the timing checks (scale-bench, fold-cost, render-bench: the machine was never quiet), P-peers, net-check, bundle-check, and the rest of the Chromium list (snap-check, rematch-memory, title-shot, terrain-shots, play-check, lobby-rig, input-check, board-check, undo-check): the step touches the view only in the tooltip's one line and the help's words.

**F19a as built** (the powder keg, the October playtest's first hazard; consensus: `CORE_VERSION` 10, `stateHash` as under 1-9 (shadowState prints nothing new), `RULES_ID` moved: the hazards, the `keg` set and mission, and with them the tower ring's fix before it, `fortified`'s `largeCentre`, which the same bump covers):
- **The keg** (`data/hazards.js`, `core/terrain/recipes.js`, `core/terrain/sets.js`; §2.8, §2.9). A chunk of kind `keg` at the table's centre on every board of the `keg` set and on no other: soft, no sight or cover, 2 hit points; its profile, data like a weapon's, in `HAZARDS.keg` (S5 AP1 D2, a 3" blast, scenery 4), hashed into `RULES_ID` less its name and look. The terrain breaks it as a crate and never sets it off: what broke, a blast's list or a wrecker's walk's, carries it out to the rules (`kegsIn`).
- **The rule** (`core/actions/shoot.js` `kegsGoOff`, `landing`; `core/actions/move.js`, `charge.js`, `damage.js`, `core/commands.js`; §4.1 rule 28). blastLands' body is now `landing`, which returns the kegs its blast broke, and blastLands sets them off: the line "The powder keg goes up!", `keg.fuse`, then the keg's blast landed by the same `landing` at its place with the keg's profile, so everything a template's landing does (its victims friend and foe, the ⚠ rows, the "Friendly fire!" lines, the scenery, the nav) a keg's does, by the same code. A keg its blast breaks joins the end of the line (breadth first, chunk order within a blast); a keg breaks once, so none goes off twice. A wrecker's walk collects the kegs it smashed (`smashAround`'s `broke`) and `resolveWalk` and `doMove` return them, and the move's handler and `finishCharge` set them off once the walk has ended: move.js can't import shoot.js (damage.js imports move.js), so it hands the kegs up rather than setting them off. `damage` takes `from`, where "nearest" is measured from (the attacker's place, as it was, by default): a keg's wounds go to the models nearest the keg, while the setter-off stays the attacker, so the fallen are its (`unit.slain`'s `by`) and "friendly" is its side. Nothing new is drawn but the blasts' own dice.
- **Why these choices.** *After the walk, not at the sample.* A walk is one `unit.move` with its smashes' events captured per sample and the unit placed at its end (§2.3's `resolveWalk`); a blast mid-walk would put dice, wounds, slain models and a nav refresh inside it (and could slay the walker mid-stride). Going off as the walk ends keeps the walk whole and catches the walker where it stops, which is where a Brute that walks through a keg usually stands. *Wounds nearest the keg.* The thrower may be 30" off; "nearest the attacker" would have the keg's wounds land on the far side of a squad from the blast. *The setter-off credited.* Whoever broke it owns what it does, the setter-off's own included ("Friendly fire!"), as a template's thrower does.
- **The profile, tuned.** The roadmap's sketch (S6 AP2 D2) killed 69% of a squad standing on it on average (by `rules.js`'s `expected`, every model under it); S5 AP1 D2 kills 52%, about half, which data-check now holds to a 40-60% band: Nutkin 4.0 of 6, Grenadiers 2.8 of 5, Oak Guard 1.7 of 5, Gliders 2.2 of 4, Scaleguard 2.7 of 6, Spitters 2.8 of 5, Sidewinders 2.2 of 4; of the big and the heroes' wounds the Trebuchet 2.0 of 7, the Elder 0.9 of 5, the Brute 1.3 of 9, the Venom Engine 1.0 of 7, the Hierophant 0.7 of 5. Two hit points against `blast`'s damage model (the full scenery damage within 0.6 of the radius, half rounded up beyond): the acorns' template (1) only cracks it, a second one breaks it; the Thornburst (2, 1) sets it off from its core, within 1.25" of the keg's box; the pinecone (3, 2) from 3.0", the acid globe (4, 2) from 2.5", another keg (4, 2) from 3.0"; the Brute's smash (99) always.
- **The mission** (`data/mission.js`; §4.2.3). Classic's Skirmish (board, zones, rounds, 500 points, list rules, the classic preset) on the `keg` set alone, its four objectives 2.5" from the keg, each in its blast. On the panel and in the lobby by its own name, "Powder keg" (`sizeName`), with a line saying what it is about; `?mission=keg`.
- **The AI** (`core/ai/score.js`; rule 10, it bumps with F19a). Three modest terms, each skipped where no keg stands (every board but the keg set's scores to the bit as it did), none drawing (bestSpot's draws are where they were). *Fear*: while any enemy could set a keg off (a blast weapon or a wrecker standing: `kegDanger`), a cell is worth less by what a template of the keg's profile would take of the unit there (`kegFear`, `expected` over the models within the blast; ×`KEG_FEAR` 0.12, between the danger term's weights). *The guns*: an artillery unit's template is worth, on its hit, the kegs it would set off landing square on the target (`kegGain`: `Terrain.blastDamage` at least the keg's hit points left), each keg by what it takes of the enemy less of its own side (`kegValue`, as `ownUnder` counts a template's friends). *The wrecker*: a walk that ends within the smash's reach of a keg is worth that keg's value with the walker where it ends (`kegWalk`, ×`KEG_SMASH` 0.3); a keg on the way is left out, because the nav's wreck mode pays double through soft ground, so the path goes round a lone keg. `bestSpot` asks the kegs, the danger and each enemy's gain once a scan (`pre.keg`, `ctx.kegs`), and P-scan's reference asks the code's own terms afresh at every cell.
- **The view and the page.** `view/terrain.js`'s barrel (lathed staves, two iron hoops, a red band, a lid, a fuse with a glowing tip), broken as a crate with a puff of black powder; `keg.fuse` fizzes its fuse a beat, then the blast's `blast.land` (fx 'keg') plays `fx.kegBlast` (the explosion in a powder palette, a shock ring, a column of sparks, black smoke, the staves flung, a deep scorch, a harder shake) and a hot ring the size of the blast. The minimap draws the keg as a red dot; the attack batches take the fuse as a hold (`pace.js`), the camera's `pointsOf` as a place, the courtesy fog as its blast's landing (shown or hidden with it). The help's paragraph under the blast templates. No tooltip line warns that a shot would set the keg off: a template's odds still name only the units under it.
- **The checks.** data-check's section 13: `checkHazard` and eight refusals, `RULES_ID` moving on each of the keg's numbers, the set's spacing, the mission's objectives and the keg dropped, staying on its name and look; only the keg set stands a keg, at (0, 0), the first chunk, with its hit points; the mission classic's Skirmish on its own set alone, its objectives 2.5" off and inside the blast; the per-unit table above and the 40-60% band. PINNED and P-prop's PINNED_UNDER take 10 (V9's hashes: no pinned battle changed). terrain-check's keg rows (500 keg boards: built twice alike, the keg its own mirror, the view's defs and sync, the keg gone from both once broken; the objectives' nearest and farthest held cells, 1.77-1.90" and 5.93-6.60" from the keg; what sets the keg off, by `blast`'s own model at 0.25" steps; a wrecker's smash; the chain, two kegs beside one, each breaking once) and connectivity's keg row (reported: 500 of 500), three self-test edits (`keg-off-centre`, `keg-tougher`, `blast-rim-full`). P-prop's **P-keg** (`kegTask`): no keg on 240 boards of the other sets, one at (0, 0) on 40 keg boards; 8 templates setting the keg off once (8 again on the spot, setting nothing off), the setting-off blast's victims and scenery before the keg's line, fuse and blast, 24 victims' rows held die for die to a copy of the stream in G.units order, the fallen the setter-off's; 8 chains of four kegs going off in the line's order, each once; 4 wreckers' walks setting it off once the walk ended; 12 AI keg values and 8 cells in the blast feared; five self-test edits (`keg-twice`, `keg-depth-first`, `keg-walk-dud`, `keg-on-classic`, `keg-ai-blind`), and the anchors of `quiet-smash` and `nav-dirty` ported. scale-check's P-scan takes the `keg/` AI pairs' boards with the code's keg terms. present-check holds a keg's fuse straight after its line and its blast straight after the fuse, there, in the keg's look; playback-check holds the fuse as a throw; lobby-rig's `size` wants the Powder keg offered by its name, board and points; flag-lint allows the view's `fx === 'keg'`; corpus-add's `--need keg` and LOG_SETS' `keg`; the human-bot's preset and first set for the keg mission; play-report's F19a row.
- **The corpus** (its own commit, 74df14f; the PIN from F18's code, 15f42ef, to F19a's, 3b52833). No existing battle plays differently (no board of theirs has a keg; the tower ring's fix changes no corpus board), so nothing is re-recorded. `keg/` holds two AI pairs (`corpus-add --set keg --mission keg --mode watch --tag keg --need keg --count 2`: watch-keg-1 and -4) and a human-bot hotseat log (`--mode hotseat --policy aggressive`: hotseat-aggressive-keg-2), each admitted twice more in Node and once in Chromium. The keg went off in 19 of the 24 watched candidates and 17 of the 24 hotseat ones. In watch-keg-1 the Venom Engine's acid globe at the Oak Guard sets it off (one wound on them, saved); in watch-keg-4 the acid globe again, the keg's blast slaying the Oak Guard's last model; in hotseat-aggressive-keg-2 the bot's Trebuchet lobs a pinecone at the Scaleguard and the keg goes up under the Elder (a "Friendly fire!" wound), the Hierophant and the Scaleguard (two slain). pairs.json takes nothing (it holds classic's seed pairs; the keg mission's AI pairs are watch logs, as fort/'s and scale/'s are). snap-check's default selection takes watch-keg-1.
- **Balance** (army-sim, `--check --mission keg`, 267 s): the keg mission's Skirmish gate fails, the Bushtails 37.6% ± 1.2 and on fresh seeds 38.4% ± 1.2 (N = 1,500 random legal lists at the limit; band 4 round 50%), and its per-unit gate on five units (fitted against cost: the Oak Guard 127 against 105, the Nutkin 57 against 75, the Grenadiers 48 against 65, the Brute 128 against 100, the Sidewinders 86 against 65). The keg is not what moves it: on 400 AI battles each with the presets, the races swapping seats, the keg mission scores the Bushtails 36.6% (the keg off in 211), the same mission with no keg (the keg set's centre left open) 39.1%, and classic 51.9%. What moves it is the mission's layout, its four objectives clustered at an open centre, where whoever holds the middle holds all four (most likely the Coil's Brute, Sidewinders and Scaleguard holding a middle better than the Bushtails' shooters do; the keg's own −2.5 points is inside two runs' noise at N = 400). A mission retune (its objectives, data only: `RULES_ID` moves) is the user's to slot; F19a leaves the mission as the roadmap drew it.
- **What turned up.** The tower ring's fix (the commit before F19a's) changed the Grand-sized fortified boards from its tower draw on, and scale-check's box-with-height control lost both its shortcut ladders on seeds 1-40 (31 and 34): it runs on 41-80 (42 and 61). In the play-report's sweep and the corpus no wrecker walked through the keg (the path goes round it, as the AI's term expects), and the keg killed few (the fear term keeps units out of its blast while an enemy could set it off): it is mostly the artillery's to set off, the Venom Engine's acid globe most of all.
- **Run** (F19a's code and corpus, on a machine shared with other runs at a load of 1-16 on 4 CPUs; each exiting 0 unless said): parity, 73 of 73 (70 of 70 on F19a's code before the corpus), and `--pin`, 73 of 73; self-test; mutation and `--core`; perturb `--fn hypot` and `--fn sin,cos,atan,atan2` (44 AI battles, the keg pairs among them); dmath-check; data-check; flag-lint and `--self-test`; boundaries and `--self-test`; terrain-check (connectivity 2,000 of 2,000, the keg rows, the tiles' 48 of 48) and `--self-test` (28 edits, the three keg edits among them, and both connectivity controls, each caught); property (73 corpus battles and 32 random games, P-keg as above; 242 s) and `--self-test` (all 72 edits caught, P-keg's five among them; about 56 minutes: `keg-on-classic`'s first failure is P-army's shadow fold of hotseat-late-8, which applies the log's entries without `legal()` and crashes on one the keg's board no longer fits, while P-keg fails on it in its own words, "the classic mission's classic board 7 stands 1 powder keg(s)"); scale-check (P-scan's keg board 124 states) and `--self-test`; replay-check (73 battles); pilot-check (77 battles); play-report, every row (F7a 5 of 6 and the keep 3 of 3, F7b 6 of 6, F10b 4 of 4 with its control 0 of 4, F19a 2 of 2); fog-check; camera-check; macro-check; army-sim's keg gates (above: exit 1, reported). In Chromium 153: parity `--browser`, 73 of 73 (at `PARALLEL=2`, 1,442 s); hud-check; present-check (73 battles, the keg's fuse and blast held on the three keg battles; 162 s); snap-check (its default selection with watch-keg-1, and the Grand row); board-check; lobby-rig `--only size`; playback-check; mirror-check. Not run: the timing checks (scale-bench, fold-cost, render-bench: the machine was never quiet), P-peers, net-check, bundle-check, merge-sim, rematch-check, hud-check's `--self-test` and the rest of the Chromium list (rematch-memory, title-shot, terrain-shots, play-check, input-check, undo-check, the rest of lobby-rig): F19a's view is the keg's piece, its effects and the setup panel's size line, which present-check, snap-check, lobby-rig's `size` and a watched keg battle in a page (no page error, the keg drawn, broken in the match) cover.

### 4.1 RNG-order rules

Each rule gets a comment at its new site. The parity gates (P-ai, P-human and P-browser: trace, shadow and battle log) enforce rules 3-11. Rule 1 is enforced by `sim/boundaries.mjs` (imports: (R6b's fixer, round 2) the core's surface and its doors, §1.2) and by parity (a stray draw shifts every later die; the only check of a draw wrapped in a door's function, on the paths the corpus runs), rule 2 by P-prop, rule 12 by the envelope decoder and P-merge, and rule 13 by `boundaries.mjs` and P-peers.

1. **Only consensus code draws, and only through `G.rng`** (`d6(G)`, `roll(G,n)`, `draw(G.rng)`). The view, presenter, input, UI, match and net layers never import `core/rng.js`, (R6b's fixer, round 2) nor any module that draws, nor `rules.js`'s `d6`/`roll` (§1.2's surface). Cosmetic randomness stays on `Math.random` in the view.
2. **`legal`, previews (`oddsText`, hover `chargePlan`/`movePlan`, reach overlays), `hudModel` and the AI-legality assertion run under `rng.lock`.** A draw throws.
3. **Statement order inside each action is frozen.** Each `await` is replaced *in place* by an `emit`. No logic moves across an emit. Building an event never draws or mutates.
4. **These orders must be kept exactly:**
   - `blastVolley`, per template (712-721): break if the shooter's own unit is dead (33946a4), then break if the target is dead and `k > 0`; aim angle `rng()`, then offset `rng()`; then the hit `roll(1)`; on a miss, scatter `roll(1)[0]+1`, then the angle `rng()`.
   - `blastLands` (799): all victims are collected first, in unit order. Per victim, a big target's `d6()` comes before the wound roll.
   - The mesmerize D3 comes after the cast (828).
   - The roll-off is `do { a = roll(1); b = roll(1) } while (a[0] === b[0])` (1208-1213).
5. **The no-save rolls still roll.** `roll(wounds)` runs even when `sn > 6` (653, 807, 1077).
6. **Iteration orders are behaviour:**
   - units in `G.units` order (seat 0's army, then seat 1's);
   - chunk order: `smashAround` walks the live array, `blast` a copy (553, 548);
   - morale walks `units` (1106);
   - fight alternation keeps its guard of 30 (1090);
   - `damage` tie-breaks with `<` (849-855);
   - `relayout` sorts by `atan2` (320);
   - the AI's lattice scan, with its odd-row offset, draws only for cells passing `isFinite(res.dist[i]) && validEnd` (ai.js 127-135);
   - the AI's role sorts are stable: ascending for move and charge (59, 264), reversed for shoot (231).
7. **Walk:** the final position is the k=1 lerp, not `pts.at(-1)`. A path under 0.05" moves nothing and smashes nothing (519). Smash samples are taken every 0.25" plus the end point, in order.
8. **Journal quirks:**
   - `doAdvance` writes no `act` line;
   - destroyed-unit lines are flushed through `write` and are not traced (917, 1284, 1653); the corpus's battle-log stream (`written`) pins where they land;
   - the "deploy your army" lines are logged in seat order at `createMatch`;
   - unit ids restart at 1 per match;
   - the trace format is unchanged (`toFixed(3)`, alive chunk count, vp, `rngState`).
9. **`refreshNav(G)` runs at exactly today's sites.** Nav is never dirty at a command boundary.
10. **AI code is rules code.** Draws stay between the same yields. Any AI change bumps `CORE_VERSION` and re-baselines.
11. **New behaviour draws only inside its own branch** (`if (t.swarm)`, deck `settle`). New terrain kinds go only in new sets. `deploy`, `vote` and `chargeEnd` draw nothing.
12. **Commands carry integers and booleans only.** Fair-dice reseeding (N4) may happen only at a command boundary.
13. **No module-level mutable state in consensus code.** Two matches in one process must not interact; the peer tests rely on it.

14. **`pilot` is the AI for a subset.** It calls `runAI(G, seat, phase, only)`: the same generators, the same role sort and the same draws, filtered by `only`. `only = null` is today's path, so P-ai stays byte-identical. `pilot` over every unit followed by `end` plays exactly `auto`'s phase (P-auto).
15. **Masks.** Bit `j` is the seat's `j`-th unit in G.units order; G.units is never spliced, so the order is stable. A mask is decoded by exact division (`m % 2`, `(m − r) / 2`), never with 32-bit operators.
16. **Bail-out** (F9a), at a transport's destruction inside `unitDestroyed`, in this order:
    1. The wreck chunk is added, then `refreshNav`.
    2. For each rider in G.units order: its spot (no draw; the nearest landing cell of any of the hull's discs, ties to the lowest index), then `roll(G, alive)`, then `damage` for the 1s (mortal: no saves).
17. **Settle** (F7c). After the `refreshNav` that follows terrain destruction (the end of a blast, a move or a charge), for each dropped deck in chunk order, and each unit on it in G.units order: its spot (no draw; ties to the lowest cell index), then one D6 for the D3, then `damage`.
18. **Height.** Every height-dependent computation sits behind `G.nav.hasHeight`, which is false on `classic` and `open` boards. It is a separate code path, never "+0". Floors are quantised to 1/64" as they are rastered, so every comparison with `STEP` (0.4") is between exact Float32 values.
19. **Riders.** An aboard unit is off the table for every spatial rule, friendly ones included (§4.2.5). `moveUnitTo` carries riders in G.units order and draws nothing. The deployment's autoload (F9a) boards riders in G.units order and draws nothing.
20. **New `refreshNav` sites:** the wreck's (16), settle's (17), and the embark walk, which ends through `doMove`'s own tail (§4.2.5). Each is reached only in its own branch. Nav is still never dirty at a command boundary, and `terrain.dropped` is empty there (P-prop checks both).
21. **Derived caches never decide.** Each returns exactly what the full computation returns: the LOS bins (S0b, checked by P-los), the plan memo (S3b, P-memo) and the hull memo (F9b, P-lattice). The height layer (`floor`, links, `cliff`, `level`, gates) is derived from the chunks like today's clearance fields. None of it is hashed. The plan memo lives inside one `apply`, opened and closed in `try/finally`, and is gone between commands. The bins, the height layer and the hull memo are rebuilt (or cleared) with the terrain they index; the hull memo may be filled during `legal()` or a preview, which is harmless because it returns exactly what the full test returns.
22. **Client macros are not rules.** Group commands, standing orders and autopilot runs reach the log only as ordinary entries: `place`, `advance`, `move`, `shoot`, `charge`, `chargeEnd`, `embark`, `disembark`, `pilot` and `end`. Peers replay the entries, never the client's choices, so a client may change how it chooses with no bump.
23. **A list is data, never a draw** (F11a). `seats[i].army` is fixed in the start. `newState` expands each seat's list in roster order, seat 0 first (rule 6), and the classic preset expands to exactly `race.army`. `autoList` draws from its own `mulberry32(seed)`, runs only in a client before the start, and never runs in the fold. Validation is integer arithmetic in a fixed order, so every peer refuses the same setups with the same text.
24. **Footprints** (F9b). A footprint's per-heading disc offsets and pivot sweep samples are tables built at load from exact constants:
    - axis headings use 0 and ±1, and diagonals `Math.SQRT1_2`;
    - the 15° and 30° sub-steps use sqrt-only `cos` and `sin` (`(√6 ± √2)/4`, `√3/2`, `½`);
    - they are rounded to the 0.5" grid by `sign(v)·Math.round(|v|/cell)`, and data whose `|v|/cell` falls within 1e-9 of a half is refused.

    No trig runs at play time. The tables are point-symmetric exactly (heading h+4 is the negation of h).
25. **The lattice** (F9b). `hullReach` relaxes forward, reverse, pivot right, pivot left, in that order, from each popped state. Ties in the heap pop as `nav.reach`'s. With `f` absent, a command takes the valid heading with the least distance, ties to the lowest index. Facing changes draw nothing. The AI's `bestSpot` draws once per lattice **cell** that has a valid heading, as rule 6 says for cells.
26. **Footprint branches** (F9b). Every footprint site is `if (t.fp)` (either unit's). Two round units keep today's expression literally, never "the disc formula with k = 1" (`hypot(…) < o.r + u.r + 0.08` and `hypot(…) − o.r − u.r < 0.08` round differently), so classic, `fort/`, `scale/`, `army/` and War-Cart battles are byte-identical through F9b.
27. **Shooting into a fight** (F18). A plain volley (a ranged weapon with neither `blast` nor `spell`) at a target engaged with any of the shooter's own units (`fightOf`, at the shot's start: F those units' living models, T the target's, and `onto`, the one with the most living models, ties to the first in G.units order), in this order:
    1. the whole hit roll, `roll(n)`, as ever;
    2. one `draw(G.rng)` per miss (a hit die under the need), in the order of the hit dice, the miss straying when its draw is under `F / (F + T)`;
    3. the target's wound roll, its save roll (rule 5), `damage` and its log line, as ever;
    4. when any strayed: `onto`'s wound roll for the strays (its T), its save roll (its Sv, cover as `inCover`; rule 5), `damage` and the "Friendly fire!" line.

    With none of the shooter's units in the fight (F = 0) nothing is drawn: the classic expression, its own branch (rule 11). A template (and a blast spell) draws as rule 4 says, whoever it lands on; the gaze as ever. The AI's value of such a shot reads the same odds and draws nothing (rule 10).
28. **The powder keg** (F19a). A keg (a chunk of kind `keg`: only the `keg` set stands one, at the centre, on a board without height) breaks as any chunk does, by a blast's damage or a wrecker's smash, and the terrain only reports it broken; the rules set it off (`core/actions/shoot.js` `kegsGoOff`). In this order:
    1. whatever broke it finishes first: a template's blast (a thrower's, acid's, an eruption's) its victims, dice, `damage` and lines as rule 4 says, its "…scenery wrecked" line and its `refreshNav`; a wrecker's walk (a move's or a charge's) the whole walk, the unit placed at its k=1 end (rule 7), the walk's `objectives` and `status` and its `refreshNav`;
    2. then each keg it broke, in the order they broke (a blast's in chunk order, `blast` walking a copy; a walk's sample by sample, each sample's in the live chunk order: rule 6), and after them, at the end of the same line, each keg a keg's blast broke, in that blast's chunk order (breadth first, so the first keg's victims and scenery all come before the second keg's line). Each keg: its traced line "The powder keg goes up!" (the setter-off's side), `keg.fuse`, then its blast, landed as a template's at the keg's place with the keg's profile (`data/hazards.js`): `blast.land`, its victims collected in G.units order, per victim a big target's `d6()` before the wound roll, then the save roll (rule 5), `damage` (the wounds to the models nearest the keg; the fallen the setter-off's), its line (with "Friendly fire!" for the setter-off's own), then the scenery and its `refreshNav`;
    3. then the command goes on as it would have: a volley's next template or the shot's end; a move's `finishAction`; a charge's `finishAction` after `chargeEnd`, or the AI's charge after `declareCharge`.

    A broken chunk is past every blast, so no keg goes off twice, and nothing is drawn but the blasts' own dice. The setter-off is the unit whose template or walk broke the first keg, for every keg in its line. A board with no keg takes none of these branches (`if (kegs.length)`, rule 11), so every classic, open and fortified battle is byte-identical. New `refreshNav` sites (rule 20's list): one per keg's blast, each in its own branch; the nav is still never dirty at a command boundary.

Rule 10 ("AI code is rules code") covers F7's AI terms (`levelDist` and the height term bump with F7a) and F9b's (the room term and the charge prefilter bump with F9b), and (F19a) the keg terms (`kegFear`, `kegGain`, `kegWalk`: they bump with F19a). It does not cover `autoList`, whose output is recorded (rule 23).

### 4.2 Large battles (S0-S3, F7-F11, V1)

The user asked for larger maps with fortifications and platforms to climb, large vehicles with firing platforms, and, for large battles, drag-selecting a group to order it to move or attack or to put it on autopilot. They then asked for online play first, three battle sizes with a points-based army builder, and a vehicle shape per race. This section is that design (written after R8, against R8b; revision 3, then the user's decisions of 2026-10-22).

It grafts three competing designs onto one base:
- **Base: the scale-and-performance design.** It contributes S0-S3, the size envelope, the measured budgets, V1, the rendering plan, `pilot {m}` and the client macros.
- **From the controls design:** the whole player layer. That is the selection model, the group bar, ghost formations, "leftovers stay selected", the End/Go timing, semantic zoom, the minimap, height and vehicle readability, and group deployment as a macro. It also gives `legal()`'s `opt`/`bools` schema.
- **From the rules-engine design:** the rules for missions, fortifications and vehicles, the setup whitelist, `checkMission`, the fight guard, `RULES` `k` as a list, and its core standing orders as the documented fallback.

**Evidence.** The figures quoted below were measured with throwaway prototypes written during the design (`sp/`, `f7proto/`, `army/`, `hulls/`, `rev3/`); they are not in the repo. All are desktop Node 22 CPU time, the minimum of 3 interleaved runs unless stated. Phone figures are about 4-5× desktop and were **not measured**. Battle scores are AI against AI over seeded boards and dice with seats swapped every other battle; "score" is wins plus half of draws, and "±" one standard error.

#### 4.2.1 Size envelope and budgets

**Size envelope.** data-check's **capacity check** holds every mission, preset, list rule and set inside this table; a set's chunk count is checked on its worst board over seeds 1-200. A mission that wants more must move the table and re-run the budgets.

|---|---|---|
| Board | ≤ 80×56 | Readability and the camera, not the core. The core copes with 120×84: a rebuild takes 2.4 ms and an 18" reach 0.9 ms. |
| Nav cell | 0.5" on every board | The smallest base (0.3), STEP and ledges. A coarser grid would move every classic battle. |
| Cell index `c` | ≤ 17,919 | Stable within a match: every peer builds the grid from the setup. |
| Points a side | 500 / 1,000 / 1,500 by mission (F11) | The builder's limits; prices are tuned against them (§4.2.8). |
| Units a side | ≤ 24 (a Grand list's cap; the Grand presets hold 21; the Bushtails reach 23 under the model cap, the Coil 24) | AI cost. Measured: a Grand AI battle with lists at the caps costs 1.07× one with the presets (below). `pilot`'s mask would allow 53. |
| Models a side | ≤ 90 (a Grand list's cap; the Grand presets hold 72-84) | Draw calls and LOS rays. |
| Vehicles a side | ≤ 2 in Field and Grand (the builder's `Vehicle` slot), 0 in Skirmish; capacity ≤ 12 | Lanes, draw calls and AI cost. Long hulls cross zone to zone on only 75-100% of Skirmish boards (§4.2.5). |
| Footprint (F9b) | 2-3 discs; r 0.5-1.6; a body disc at the pivot; snap error ≤ 0.15"; connected at every heading; each disc's pivot gap ≤ 0.06"; bounding R ≤ 3.5 | Lanes, the sweep's sampling and the lattice's cost (§4.2.5). |
| Headings (F9b) | 8 | The nav grid's neighbour steps. |
| Climber disc | r ≤ `CLIMB_R` = 1.22 for any unit that uses stairs or ladders (squads today: 0.89-1.18) | The fortification sizes (§4.2.4). |
| Chunks | ≤ 450 (fortified, measured: Skirmish 26-72, Field 63-146, Grand 142-223) | `sight` costs 2.6 µs at 148 chunks and 9.4 µs at 440 without S0b. |
| Rounds | 5 / 6 / 7 by mission | The log budget below. |
| Entry | ≤ 1,024 B; the largest new one is `pilot`, 125 B with a 53-bit mask (`embark` 119 B; `move` with a heading ≈ 108 B) | R8's `MAX_BYTES`. |

N2 normalises a display name and caps it at 24 characters and 48 encoded bytes, and fixes the nonce at 16 hex characters (§3's additions). |
